The tweet can be seen here . The tweet was posted by Kalyani Ganesh Wagh (@kalyaniwagh8400), and the profile detail suggested she was a member of Shiv Sena from Sambhaji Nagar. Below is the screenshot of the tweet. Subsequently, the Desk tried to find the details of the party worker who tattooed his back with the images of the Thackerays on YouTube. We first searched with the keyword 'Sanjay Raut Tattoo' on YouTube and didn't get anything about the party worker in the search results. Then, we searched with the keyword 'Uddhav Thackeray Tattoo' and found the first video by news channel TV9 Marathi on August 28. The video's headline was in Marathi; so we used Google Translate to change the text into English. The English translation of the Marathi-language headline read: "Uddhav Thackeray Tattoo | Ramanna Jamadar, a Shiv Sainik of Solapur, got a tattoo of Thackeray father and daughter (son) on his back." Below is the screenshot of the YouTube video The Desk thus inferred that the person who tattooed his back was Ramanna Jamadar, and he was a Shiv Sainik from Solapur. In the YouTube video, the TV9 Marathi journalist was seen talking to Ramanna, and, in the video, the Shiv Sainik showed his tattoos with the faces of only the Thackerays. The video can be seen here . The Desk also searched Ramanna Jamadar's name on Facebook and found a page title 'Aditya Sahab Thackeray.' On this page, Ramanna Jamadar posted the same photo of his tattoos on August 31. Here is the Facebook page link , and below is the screenshot. Jamadar has posted the same photo on his profile page , also. In the last part of the investigation, the Desk contacted PTI's Mumbai-based special correspondent Prashant Rangnekar to verify that the viral image was edited. Rangnekar reached out to Chandrakant Khaire, Shiv Sena leader and former party MP from Aurangabad, who was seen in the picture along with Uddhav Thackeray. Khaire told PTI's Rangnekar that he was present at Matoshree - Uddhav's home -- when the photo was shot, and he had seen pictures of Uddhav Thackeray and his son Aaditya Thackeray tattooed on the back of the man. "This is the love of Shiv Sainiks due to which they have tattooed the photos of Aaditya and Uddhav Ji on their back," Khaire said. When asked about the picture of Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut tattooed on the man's lower waist, Khaire said: "I have not seen it."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Wrestler in video shared on social media is not Bajrang Punia; viral claim is misleading
content: New Delhi, September 10 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Social Media users have shared a video of a wrestling match claiming one of the wrestlers is Bajrang Punia, the bronze medal winner of 2020 Tokyo Olympics. PTI Fact Check Desk has found in its investigation that the wrestler's name is Mosam Ali, and he is from Punjab. The social media posts claiming the wrestler to be Bajrang Punia misleading. Claim PTI Fact Check Desk noticed a video of a wrestling match posted by many users on Facebook and Twitter claiming that one of the wrestlers was Indian Olympian Bajrang Punia. The text in one of the Facebook posts published on September 7 read: "All-time gem from our ace Wrestler Bajrang Punia." In the 21-second-long video, one wrestler was seen defeating the other wrestler, using quick techniques in a local-level wrestling match. The Facebook post can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post- Many other users shared the same video clip claiming that one of the wrestlers was Bajrang Punia. The posts can be seen here and here also. Below is the combination image of the screenshots of bith the posts - Investigation Bajrang Punia is a well-known Indian freestyle wrestler from Haryana. Punia won a bronze medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. In August this year, Punia clinched gold in the men's 65kg freestyle wrestling in Commonwealth Games 2022. This was Bajrang's third Commonwealth Games medal in as many events. He had won silver in his maiden CWG in 2014 and then bettered the colour four years later in Gold Coast by winning gold. Punia is the only Indian wrestler to have won three medals at the World Wrestling Championships. Punia's participation in a local-level wrestling match is a piece of big news. So, the Desk searched for the details of any such matches that in the recent past. However, nothing showed up to this effect in Google search. To verify the video, the Desk further used the InVid tool to get keyframes and then conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes to check the origin of the video clip. In the Google Reverse Image Search results, the Desk found a report suggesting the viral clip is a part of an old video available on the Internet since 2019. Then, we scanned the comments section of one of the social media posts, and found one user's comment that the wrestler who was seen defeating his opponents was Mosam Ali. We found profile pages of Mosam Ali (a wrestler from Punjab) on YouTube , Facebook , and Instagram through a Google Search. Subsequently, we searched YouTube for the original video and found it published by a channel on October 28, 2019, with the headline, "Mosam Ali Vs Tiger, मोसम अली ने धोया टाइगर पहलवान को डरके चढ़ गया पेड़ पर". The 11.30-minute-long YouTube video has more than 5 Lakh views and 4000 likes, and the clip shared on Twitter and Facebook starts 9.12-minute onward in the video. It can be seen here , and below is the screenshot of the video. In the next part of the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk contacted PTI's Deputy Chief of Bureau (Sports) Amanpreet Singh who said: "I have covered Bajrang Punia for some years now. The wrestler in the video is tall and burly while Bajrang is short and weighs only 65kg. Certainly, this wrestler is not Bajrang."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, white goat seen at King Charles III's proclamation was not for sacrifice; claim in social media posts is fake
content: New Delhi, Sept 18 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook post has claimed that the white goat seen at the crowning and declaration of Prince Charles as King of England was intended for sacrifice. The PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the white goat amid soldiers dressed in red uniforms is the mascot of the Royal Welsh. The viral claim that the white goat was brought for sacrifice is fake. Claim On September 14, a Facebook user posted a photo of a white goat with the soldiers in Red uniform on the occasion of the proclamation of Prince Charles as King of England. The post reads: "This is the British carrying a white ram (intended for sacrifice) for the crowning and declaration of Prince Charles as King of England. This is their ancient tradition and culture." The Facebook post can be seen here . And here is the archive link of the post. Below is the screenshot of the post- While scanning the social media for similar claims, the Desk found that a user with the same name (Chuka Nduneseokwu) has posted a thread of three tweets with the same image and claims. Here is the link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The same image and claim were shared by many other users on Twitter and a website. The Twitter post can be seen here . The website called NairaLand Forum has published the same information and image. Here is the link to the page. Below is the screenshot of the page- Investigation The Desk started the investigation by doing a Google Reverse Image Search on the image used in the Facebook post to find the details of the animal walking with the men in red uniforms. Google Reverse Image Search helps users quickly discover visually similar images from around the web. We searched with the keyword "White goat and British Crown proclamation." The search results led us to a video posted by the Independent with the headline, "Royal Welsh regiment led by a goat in Cardiff march for King Charles's proclamation." In the 32-second clip, the white goat was seen walking with the soldiers while people were standing on both sides of the road. The video can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the video- The Description of the video reads, "The Royal Welsh regiment was led through the streets of Cardiff by the Goat Major as the Welsh capital proclaimed King Charles III on Sunday, 11 September. Thousands watched as the procession marched from City Hall to the castle, where the UK's new monarch was proclaimed in a ceremony." According to the description, the name of the white goat is Goat Major, and Royal Welsh have adopted goats as their mascots since the 1770s. The Desk further did a Google Search to find the details of the Goat Major and to know why Royal Welsh have adopted goats as their mascots since the 1770s. We found an article published on the website Royal Welsh Museum with the headline, "A Brief History of The Regimental Mascot." The first paragraph of the description reads, "Within many regiments, there is a history of having a mascot which for The Royal Welsh is a goat. The different antecedent regiments typically use the traditional names of Dewi, Taffy, Shenkin, and Sospan. Official mascots have a regimental number and rank; they can be promoted and demoted like human soldiers and even receive a salary! For the goat mascot, this salary goes towards his uniform, accommodation (which often includes a radio and a sofa), and food." The article can be read here . Below is the screenshot of the lead image used in the article- The Desk read the post to know why and when the Royal Welsh adopted goat and found one paragraph that reads, "The Royal Welsh and its predecessor units have been adopting goats as their mascots since 1775, each with their own unique story of how they were acquired. At the Battle of Bunker Hill, during the American War of Independence (1775-1783), it is thought that a wild goat came onto the battlefield and led the colour party from the field. The Royal Welsh Fusiliers then adopted the goat as their mascot as it brought them good luck." The post further says, "When a mascot dies, the regiment writes to the Queen (or King) informing her of the loss and to request permission to recruit a new mascot, continuing the tradition that begun with Queen Victoria. The next kid goat is selected and trained by the Goat Major, who develops a close bond, with the kid accepting the Goat Major as the alpha." The Desk found another article with an image in which the white goat was seen kneeling in front of HRH Princess Elizabeth II on May 27, 1948. The article can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the image- Another report published on the news18.com website said, "the present mascot of the Royal Welsh regiment is Lance Corporal Shenkin IV." As per tradition, different regiments have different names for their respective goats. Shenkin, the goat, is the official mascot for the Regimental Mascot of the 3rd Battalion, The Royal Welsh. The regiment participated in the historical event of King Charles III's proclamation last week. In the tweet here and in the image below, the goat can be seen preparing for the regiment's participation in the proclamation.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: King Charles did not sign proclamation on US elections, and note atop Queen's coffin did not mention Trump; viral claims are fake
content: New Delhi, Sept 22 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A claim has gone viral on social media platforms that King Charles III signed a proclamation stating that Donald Trump won the 2020 US Presidential election and was the rightful President by Law. Also, an image of a note with the text 'Trump won 2020' atop Queen Elizabeth's coffin is also being shared by many social media users. PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the claim that King Charles III signed the proclamation is fake, and the image with the 'Trump won 2020' note on the Queen's coffin is edited. Claim While scanning the social media platforms, PTI Fact Check Desk noticed two different claims related to former US President Donald Trump shared by users of Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. The first claim is from a user who published an image of King Charles III signing some documents on Twitter and wrote: "King Charles III signs a proclamation stating that Donald Trump won the 2020 Presidential election and is the rightful President by Law. Warns Biden and Kamala to vacate the premises within 48 hours or a state of war will exist between America and England." The tweet can be seen here , and here is the archive link of the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the image- The same claim was shared by a user on Instagram also. Below is the screenshot of the post- The second claim is about an image of a note with the text 'Trump won 2020' placed on the coffin of Queen Elizabeth. Many users have shared the photo on Facebook and Twitter. The posts can be seen here , here , here , and here . Below is the combined image of all four posts that appeared on Facebook and Twitter with the same photo showing the note on the coffin- Investigation To verify the first claim that King Charles III signed a proclamation that Donald Trump won the 2020 Presidential election, the Desk searched with the keyword 'King Charles III proclamation on Trump 2020 US elections' in Google Search. We could not find any report on King Charles signing such a proclamation on Trump or US elections 2020. A Google Reverse Image Search on the image in the post led the Desk to an article published by People.com with the headline, "King Charles's Inkpot, Gifted by His Sons, Causes a Viral Moment During His Proclamation Ceremony" The article's first paragraph reads, "Following the death of Queen Elizabeth on Thursday, the Accession Council made the official proclamation of King Charles, 73, in the State Apartments of St. James's Palace in London at 10 a.m. local time Saturday - and in a historic first, the rite was televised." We can see that King Charles was in the same attire (as in the viral photo) in the video attached to the article. The video can be seen here . And Below is the screenshot of the clip- The Desk found another article by HullDailyMail.co.uk with the headline, "Hull and Beverley proclamations of King Charles III details confirmed." The lead image in the article showed King Charles signing the oath during the Accession Council at St James' Palace in London. The report can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the photo in the article- It has been proved that King Charles did not sign any proclamation on Trump winning the 2020 US elections, and the photo used in the viral post is from the occasion when he was at St James' Palace in London during the Accession Council. The second claim also had an image of a note atop the Queen's coffin that said," Trump won 2020". The Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search and came across an article on Foxla.com with the headline, "What did the note atop Queen Elizabeth's coffin say?" The report had an image showing a clear view of the note on the coffin. Below is the screenshot of the image used in the article- One of the paragraphs in the article reads, "On a wreath atop the coffin, a handwritten note read, "In loving and devoted memory," and was signed Charles R - for Rex, or king." Here is the article link . The video of the occasion can be seen here . It's clear from the findings that the image of the note atop the coffin in the social media posts is edited.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi did not meet the 'pro-Pakistan slogan' girl during his Yatra in Kerala; viral claim is fake
content: New Delhi, Sept 26 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi walking with a girl during the party's Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kerala is being shared with the claim that the girl was Amulya Leona Noronha, who was arrested for shouting a pro-Pakistan slogan at a Bengaluru event in February 2020. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the girl with Gandhi in the social media posts was Miva Jolly from Kerala. Miva is the general secretary of the Kerala Students Union (KSU) for the Ernakulam district in the state. The viral claim that the girl with Rahul Gandhi was Amulya Leona is fake. Claim On September 21, Rahul Gandhi visited Ernakulam in Kerala during the Congress party's 'Bharat Jodo Yatra' and was seen walking with a girl for some time. As soon as the photo and videos were shared, many users on social media platforms started posting claims that the girl with Rahul Gandhi was Amulya Leona Noronha. Amulya hails from Karnataka and was arrested by the Bengaluru police on charges of sedition for raising pro-Pakistan slogans during a protest against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), held at Bengaluru's Freedom Park on February 21, 2020. Many politicians from the BJP also shared the same claim. Some of them deleted the post later, but the claim went viral on Twitter and Facebook. The posts with the viral claims can be seen here , here , here , and here . The same post was shared by a user on Facebook also. Here are the archive links of the tweets which have 290 retweets , and 990 retweets . Below are the screenshots of some of the viral posts- On September 24, a website published an article on the same claim. Here's the archive link of the article and below is the screenshot of the story- Investigation To investigate the claim, the PTI Fact Check Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo to know the details of the girl who was seen walking with Gandhi during the Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kerala on September 21. The search results led us to a photo published on Rahul Gandhi's Facebook page on Sept 21. However, the photo shared on the FB page had no details of the girl whom Gandhi was seen hugging and walking with. The photo can be seen here . And, here is the link to the Facebook post which has a total of 13 images. Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post - While scanning the search results, the Desk found a report by Telegraph India saying the girl's name was Miva Jolly, and she was from Kerala. Since the Telegraph India report suggested the girl was Miva Jolly and the viral claims said the girl was Amulya Leona, the Desk then scanned Twitter and Instagram to find their profiles or any information on either's meeting with Gandhi during his yatra in Kerala. During the search, we found a Twitter handle, Facebook account, and Instagram account in the name of Amulya, but none of these accounts were verified and not even regularly updated. There was no information regarding Amulya's meeting with Gandhi. The Desk also searched with the keyword 'Amulya Leona Noronha meets Rahul Gandhi' on Google and found no report on her meeting the Congress leader on any occasion in the past. Now, we searched for Miva Jolly's profile on social media platforms to know if she shared anything about her meeting with Rahul Gandhi and found her Instagram account . On her profile page, Jolly has shared her photo and the video with the Congress leader during his yatra in Ernakulam district in Kerala. The desk found that another user has tagged her in the video in which she was seen walking with Gandhi. The post can be seen here . She has posted her photo with Gandhi in another post . Below is the screenshot of the video post- Subsequently, the Desk also found a tweet by Rajya Sabha MP and Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal (@kcvenugopalmp) saying the girl in the photo and video with Mr. Gandhi was KSU Eranakulam District Secretary Miva Jolly. In his tweet, Venugopal also attacked BJP leaders for spreading false information about the girl. Here is the link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to Miva Jolly on Instagram for her reaction to the photo and video being shared with the false claim. She said: "I am Miva Jolly from Kerala. I am a state padyatri of Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra. I am also the state's district general secretary of NSUI (KSU). I met Rahul Ji when the yatra reached Ernakulam district. I ran towards and hugged him when I saw him in the yatra. He asked about me and I introduced myself as a Congress follower. I can't forget that moment in my lifetime."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Anupriya Patel's 3-year-old video shared as recent; Apna Dal (S) calls viral social media posts fake news
content: New Delhi, Sept 28 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Some social media users have shared a video of Anupriya Patel claiming that the Apna Dal (Sonelal) leader snapped ties with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and supported Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video is from 2019 and is being shared now in social media posts with the fake claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the PTI Fact Check Desk noticed a video of Anupriya Patel being shared with the claim that the Apna Dal (S) leader has ended her party's alliance with the BJP and supported Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra. The video clip was first published on the Nation TV's Facebook page and then shared by two users on Twitter. Here is the link to the Facebook page , the archive link of the page can be seen here. Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post- The tweets can be seen here and here , and the archive links are here and here . Below is the combined image of the screenshot of both tweets- Investigation Since the viral post was published on Nation TV's Facebook page on September 13, and the tweets were posted on September 16, the Desk decided to scan Anupriya Patel's Twitter handle to see if she had posted anything similar to her remarks in the viral clip in September. Patel currently serves as Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry in the Government of India and has been very active on Twitter. We went through the tweets posted by the minister's handle(@AnupriyaSPatel) in September and couldn't find any post against the BJP or in support of Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra. We noticed a series of tweets posted by Patel's Twitter handle about the minister attending official events organised by her ministry on September 13, the date when the Nation TV's Facebook page published the video in which the minister can be seen making remarks against BJP. Below are the screenshots of two of the tweets posted on Sept 13 from the minister's Twitter handle- Subsequently, the Desk did a Google search with the keyword 'Anupriya Patel supported Rahul Gandhi'. It didn't find any report as claimed in the viral post that Patel has supported the Congress leader and his yatra. Now, to check the origin of the video, the Desk used the keyframe analysis in the InVid Tool, and the Image search led us to a video with the headline, " क्‍या बीजेपी को झटका देंगी अनुप्रिया पटेल ?" posted by NDTV Hindi website on Feb 22, 2019. Here is the link to the video . The Desk noticed Anupriya Patel's outfit and the Boom microphones of the channels were the same as in the viral video. We found another video of Patel with the same bytes published by ABP News' YouTube channel on Feb 22, 2019. Here is the link to the video . The Desk noticed that the first 30-second of the viral video, 35-second onward footage in the NDTV video, and 40-second onward clip in the ABP video are the same. The news channels' boom microphones placement was the same in all three videos (the viral video shared now and the videos published by the NDTV website and ABP YouTube channel in 2019). She can be heard making the same statement in all three clips: "Some differences cropped up with the BJP, and we gave them time till February 20 to answer our questions. But they did not have any answers. So it appears the BJP is not interested in listening to or answering the complaints of their allies. Apna Dal is independent to make its own decision. We have called a party meeting, and we will do what the party decides; whatever will be decided in the meeting, we will let you know.". The screenshot below has one image taken from the viral video ( Right ) and another from the ABP video published in 2019 ( Left ). When searching in Google News to know why Patel, an ally of the BJP, made a statement against BJP in 2019, we found an NDTV article with the headline, "Apna Dal's Anupriya Patel Threatens Exit Just As BJP Calms Other UP Ally" published on Feb 22, 2019. The first paragraph of the article reads: "Union Minister Anupriya Patel of the Apna Dal, a crucial ally of the BJP in Uttar Pradesh, has threatened to quit the National Democratic Alliance over being not heard by the BJP on issues that it had raised." Here is the link to the NDTV article. The findings made it clear that Anupriya Patel's video clip in the viral social media posts is a part of an old video of her media interaction ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to PTI's Lucknow Bureau for a response from Apna Dal (S) on the veracity of the claim in social media posts. Rajesh Patel, the National Spokesman of Apnal Dal (Sonelal), told PTI that the information in the viral social media post is fake news and should be ignored.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Patanjali doesn't sell 'beef biryani'; Image in viral social media posts is morphed with fake claim
content: New Delhi, October 3 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Some social media users have shared an image of a beef biryani recipe pack claiming yoga guru Ramdev's Patanjali is selling the product in the Indian market. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image of the food product is morphed. National Foods, a kitchen & food solution provider multinational company, sells the spice mix product shown in the image in the Pakistani market. The viral claim that Patanjali sells beef biryani is fake. Claim On Sept 29, PTI Fact Check received a tweet on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 requesting to verify the claim in an image that Ramdev's Patanjali was selling beef biryani in India. The photo showed a packet of the product with the names of Ramdev and Patanjali. The tweet can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk, while scanning the social media platforms, found a few more posts shared with the same image and the claim. The posts can be seen here , here , here , here , here , and here . Investigation Since all the posts had the same image, the Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo. On the search result page, we found images similar to the ones shared in the viral posts but without the name of Ramdev and Patanjali printed on them. Then, The Desk checked the company's name on the pack in one of the screengrabs and found that it's the product of National Foods, which is a US-based company . Subsequently, the Desk searched for the same product on an eCommerce site and found the same product on the website of National Foods with the description, "National Foods is a multinational company celebrating 50+ years of bringing families together through innovative food products embraced by millions across the world. We are the most diverse Pakistani Kitchen & Food solution provider operating across 13 categories. We have expertise in creating the perfect blend of spices that allow you to easily prepare delicious & authentic meals." The details can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the page- Now, the Desk compared the photo of the product with the one shared in the social media posts; it could see the difference as the company name was changed from 'National' to 'Ramdev,' and Patanjali was printed in the white space in the original photo. The edited part can be seen in the combination image below- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Tijarawala SK (Spokesman, Swami Ramdev) to verify the image in viral social media posts. Tijarawala told PTI fact Check Desk: "This is a disgusting conspiracy to defame Patanjali by putting our 'logo' on the viral image. This is not our product. It's a fake photo. We cannot even think of making beef masala or biryani products in our dreams. We are strong supporters of vegetarianism. We have always demanded a ban on beef. Under the conspiracy, contrary to our principles and different from reality, such fake posts and material are being deliberately put to defame the 'Patanjali' group and its guide Swami Ramdev and Acharya Balkrishna Ji. It is our humble request to everyone, including the media, to be alert to such acts against us on a daily basis. We are taking strict legal action against these conspirators and all media platforms and groups that allow the use of such fake content. Right now, we have started proceedings against hundreds of individuals and organizations."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of IUMYL flags in procession to support Congress' Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kerala shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Some social media users have shared a video claiming that Pakistani flags were carried in a procession organised to support Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra in Kerala. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the flags seen in the shared video belong to Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) and Indian Union Muslim Youth League (IUMYL). The viral claim that Pakistani flags were seen in the procession is fake. Claim The PTI Fact Check Desk received a tweet from a user on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 with a request to verify the claim in the post. The tweet was posted with a 29-second video in which some people and a boy were seen carrying a green-colour flag showing crescent and star. The tweet reads: "This is Bharat Jodo Yatra. But, which flag are they waving? Congress' new flag or Pakistan's". Here is the link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post- When the Desk scanned social media platforms, it found similar claims with the same video shared by many other users. One such tweet was posted with the Hindi text: "दूसरा पाकिस्तान बनाने _____ यात्रा निकाली है". Here is the link to the tweet. This post quoted another tweet shared by Suresh Chavhanke of "Sudarshan News" with the same video. Chavhanke's tweet reads: "यह #भारत_जोड़ो_यात्रा कौनसे इस्लामी देश में पहुँची हैं? @RahulGandhi @digvijaya_28". The tweet was retweeted 4017 times and liked by 7047 users though he didn't name any country in his tweet but mentioned 'Islamic country' in his tweet. Here is the link to Chavhanke's Tweet , and the archive link can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of his tweet- The Desk found similar posts shared by many other users claiming that people seen in the video were carrying Pakistani flags. The posts can be seen here , and here , here and here also. Investigation Since the posts claimed that the flags in the video were the Pakistan flag, the Desk started the investigation, searching the details of the procession, the people participating in the rally, and the flags. When the Desk watched the 29-second video, it noticed that people also carried a banner with the photo of Rahul Gandhi and the text which reads: "Rahul Ji, Leader of Democratic India, Welcome to Pallakad, IUML Pattambi Mandalam Committee." Below is the screengrab of the video- We cropped the image of the flag from the screengrab of the video and did a Google Reverse Image search with the keyword 'IUML' to know the details of the flag. The search results led us to the official Facebook and Twitter pages of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML). The Desk noticed that the logo on the IUML social pages has two images - the flag showing crescent and star and a picture of a ladder. Below is the combination image of the screengrabs of both pages- Later, the Desk searched the details on the Election Commission Website and found that IUML was registered as a state party in Kerala with 'Ladder' as the symbol reserved for the party. The details can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the Election Commission notification issued on Sept 23, 2021. Further search on Google with the keyword 'IUML Flag' led the Desk to the website of the Indian Union Muslim Youth League (IUMYL), which has a logo similar to the image shown on IULM's social media page and in the viral video also. According to the IUMYL website, Muslim Youth League is the youth wing of the Indian Union Muslim League. Here is the link to the website, and below is the screenshot of its homepage- The Desk further scanned IUML's Facebook page and found one video of a party meet posted on October 5. The video shows the photo of the ladder and the green flag with star and crescent in the backdrop on the podium of the party's event. The video can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the video- Now, we compared the Pakistani flag, which has a white ribbon on the left with star and crescent on the green flag, with the screengrab of the flags seen in the viral video. Below is the combination image of the photos of the Pakistani flag and the IUML/IUMYL flag- It can be seen that there was no white ribbon in any of the flags in the video shared on social media. The Pakistani flag has a white stripe on the left side. The Desk also found that the Muslim Youth League Guruvayur's Facebook page posted the same video on Sept 26. Here's the link to the post and below is the screenshot of the post- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted PTI's Special Correspondent in Kerala to verify the claim and check the authenticity of the video shared in social media posts. Biju confirmed with the IUML's unit in Kerala and told the Desk that the video was shot during the procession organised by the IUML at Koppam Gram Panchayat at Pattambi in the Palakkad district of Kerala on September 26. "IUML Koppam Panchayat Committee had organised this procession to greet Congress' Bharat Jodo Yatra at Koppam junction in the evening on September 26 when Rahul Gandhi-led Bharat Jodo Yatra reached there. IUML is a key partner of Congress-led UDF in Kerala," An IUML leader told PTI. "The boy carrying the IUML flag in the video was the son of Koppam Panchayat Muslim League President Thiyyattil Riyas," he told PTI. He shared a photo of the procession where the same boy and people can be seen carrying the IUML/IUMYL flags.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das being shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, October 10 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Some social media users have shared a video of RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das claiming he talked about how to block digital payment apps in case someone had installed them on a phone that got lost. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the RBI governor's video is edited, and the claim shared in the social media posts is fake. Claim While scanning social media platforms for potential fake information, the Desk found a tweet with a video of RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das, speaking about ways to block digital payment apps installed in a lost phone. The Tweet text read: "How to block your active apps/ wallet when your phone is lost/ stolen. Please see this video of the RBI Governor for public awareness. Save it. @Bankers_We @UFBUIndia @officialAIBOC @DFS_India In the video, Das was seen advising about the steps to keep digital wallets safe and secure if anyone has payment apps like GooglePay (GPay), PhonePe, and PayTM in a phone, which has been lost. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk found Tweets with similar claims here , here , and here . Investigation Google Pay (GPay), PayTM, and PhonePe are the Unified Payment Interface (UPI) apps for online transactions. If your phone has any of these apps connected to the bank account, losing the phone may cause money loss if the user is not aware of the steps to be taken quickly to secure the digital wallet. Das was seen giving the details of the customer care numbers of these payment apps and about the steps to take to block them in a lost phone. Here, the question arises why the RBI Governor would release such a video about the customer care numbers of the payment apps when the RBI has a separate department for such communications. The Desk watched the 47-second video and noticed the audio was imposed, and a few frames of foreign currencies and customer care executives were also used. To check the authenticity of the 47-second video clip in the social media posts, the Desk used the InVid tool and found that the clip was a part of the RBI Governor's press conference on May 5, 2021. The 29.08-minute video was posted on YouTube from the Reserve Bank of India channel, and we noticed the background in the video and the colour of Das's suit and tie were the same as in the social media clip. The similarity can be seen in the image below - The YouTube video can be seen here - It's clear that it is not Shaktikanta Das' voice in the video that was posted on social media. Subsequently, the Desk searched Google to find the origin of the audio and frames of customer care officials. The search results led the Desk to a Reel posted by digital creator Mausam Nagpal on his Facebook page. When the Desk oversaw the Reel, it noticed that the reel audio was similar to the audio in the viral video. The Desk also found that the footage of the two people appearing as customer care officials was the same in Nagpal's reel. The reel can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the reel in which the digital creator is seen talking about the steps that can be followed to block payment apps uploaded in a lost phone. Also, below is the combined image of the screenshots showing the same people as customer care officials in both videos. The screenshot from the video posted on social media (L) and the screengrab from the reel (R) . The details gathered made it clear that the video in which Das was seen speaking was edited. The voice of digital creator Mausam Nagpal from one of his reels was imposed on Shaktikanta Das' press conference video to make it look like the RBI Governor was talking about safety tips relating to payment apps. The Desk also noticed that the customer care numbers of GooglePay, PhonePe, and PayTM highlighted in the 47-second were authentic and similar to the numbers mentioned in the reel posted by the digital creator. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted RBI for its response to the edited video shared on social media with fake claims. The CGM's Secretariat at the RBI's Department of Communication responded to the mail and shared a link to an article by a media house that had debunked the information saying it was a fake video.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Kejriwal didn't hold bow and arrow in reverse direction at Dussehra event; Morphed image being shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, October 13 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Social media users shared an image of Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal holding a bow and an arrow in the reverse direction, claiming the Aam Aadmi Party leader was pointing the target toward himself, and not the effigy of Ravana, at a Dussehra event. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image in the social media post is morphed and shared with a fake claim. Claim The Desk received a Facebook post on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 with a request to verify the authenticity of the image and the claim with which it was shared. In the picture, Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal was seen holding a bow and an arrow at a Dussehra event. The photo showed the bow and the arrow in the reverse direction, pointing toward Kejriwal, not at Ravana's effigy. The Text on the Facebook post reads: ""देश का दुर्भाग्य कि तीर चला नहीं वरना कल्याण हो जाता । अफसोस, कि तीर चला नही है। हम तीर की कड़ी निन्दा करते हैं। उसे चलना ही चाहिए था। इतिहास मे पहली बार ऐसा हो रहा है की एक रावण, दूसरे रावण को तीर मार रहा है " The Text reads in English: "It's the nation's misfortune that the arrow didn't shoot, or else, there would have been a beneficial outcome. Regret that the arrow didn't shoot. It should have. We strongly condemn the arrow. This is the first time in history that one Ravana is shooting another Ravana with an arrow." The post can be seen here . Here is the link of the archive link . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post image which was published in a Facebook group titled '"मोदी है तो मुमकिन है" (It's possible if there is Modi) which has 87,000 subscribers. When the Desk searched Twitter, it found a tweet with the same image and a similar claim as was in the Facebook post. Here's the link to the tweet . Here's the link to the archive post . Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation by doing a Google Reverse Image Search on the image in the tweet and the Facebook post. The search results led the Desk to a PTI report published by a news website Business Standard with the headline, "Vice-President Dhankar, Delhi CM Kejriwal attend Dussehra celebrations." The article's lead image showed Kejriwal standing with some people and holding the bow and the arrow in the right direction, pointing at Ravana's effigy. Here is the link to the report . The Desk compared the image in the social media posts with the one published in the Business Standard article and found Kejriwal's dress, the people standing with him on the dais, and their outfits to be the same. The only difference was the direction of the bow and the arrow in Kejriwal's hand, as highlighted in the combined images below- The Desk also noticed the caption of the BS article image, which reads: "CM Arvind Kejriwal during Ramlila celebrations on Dussehra eve at Red Fort (Photo: Twitter)." Since the BS website gave the image credit to Twitter, the Desk scanned the micro-blogging site to search for the image's origin and found a tweet posted by Kejriwal himself on October 5. Here's the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post in which Kejriwal was seen with the actors playing the role of Lord Ram, Lakshman, and Lord Hanuman at the Dussehra event at Ramlila Ground in Delhi. When the Desk watched the 2.07-minute video, it noticed that Kejriwal was holding the bow and the arrow for 4-5 seconds between 1.47-minute and 1.50-minute duration before shooting the arrow toward Ravana. Below is the screenshot of the frame paused at 1.50 minutes in the video in Kejriwal's tweet. We could also notice all the people and their dresses looked the same as they were in the morphed image shared with fake claims on social media. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Aam Aadmi Party's Saurabh Bharadwaj for his response to the morphed image of Kejriwal shared on social media. Bharadwaj told PTI Fact Check Desk: "BJP's IT Cell is continuously circulating fake pictures of Arvind Kejriwal and disseminating false claims about him. This is one of such fake pictures of Arvind Kejriwal."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Yogi Adityanath didn't disrespect Mahatma Gandhi; social media posts shared with fake claim
content: Lucknow, October 17 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Some social media users shared a video claiming Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath disrespected Mahatma Gandhi and left the event venue within 30 seconds after offering flowers to his statue. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video in the tweet was a small clip of a more extended version of a footage in which Yogi was seen attending the prayer meeting also near Gandhi's statue. An image tweeted by the BJP MLA from Lucknow East showed Yogi bowing his head with folded hands while paying his tribute to Gandhi. The claim in the shared social media post that he didn't pay respect properly with folded hands and left the event in 30 seconds is fake. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a 17-second video of Yogi Adityanath shared in a tweet claiming the Uttar Pradesh CM didn't pay respect with folded hands after offering flowers to Gandhi and leaving the place in just 30 seconds. Here is the link to the tweet and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Further, the Desk searched for more such claims and found a few posts with the same claim in the same video. The posts can be seen here , here , here and here . Investigation Since all these social media posts were shared after Gandhi Jayanti on October 2 this year, we uploaded the video in the InVid Tool to find its origin and context. The Desk found the keyframes of the video and did a Google Reverse Image Search on the keyframes to know the source of the video. The search results led the Desk to a PTI report published on the Times Of India Website on Oct 2 with the headline: "UP CM Yogi Adityanath pays tributes to Mahatma Gandhi, Lal Bahadur Shashtri." Here is the link to the story . The TOI article had embedded two tweets from the handle of Yogi Adityanath posted on October 2. In one tweet, Yogi was seen offering flowers to former prime minister Lal Bahadur Shashtri and praying with folded hands while standing in front of his statue. October 2 is also the birth anniversary of Shri Lal Bahadur Shashtri, India's second prime minister who served the country between 9 June 1964 to 11 January 1966. In the second tweet, Yogi can be seen offering flowers to Mahatma Gandhi's statue and praying with folded hands in front of Gandhi's statue. Here are the tweets posted by Yogi's Twitter account. 1. Paying tribute to Shashtri 2. Paying tribute to Gandhi Below are the screenshots of the tweets- When the Desk compared the screenshots of the video in the social media post with the image of Yogi offering flowers to Gandhi in the tweet from his handle, it noticed that the UP CM wore a mask in the posts shared by the social media users. In contrast, in the video posted by Yogi, he can be seen without a mask. It can be seen in the combination image of the screenshots of the social media post and Yogi's tweet- It was clear that the social media posts published after October 2 this year were not related to the Gandhi Jayanti celebration event Yogi attended in 2022. Continuing the investigation, the Desk searched Google with Keyword 'Yogi Adityanath Mahatma Gandhi' and found a YouTube video by the news agency ANI on Jan 30, 2022. The video's headline reads: "CM Yogi Adityanath pays floral tribute to Mahatma Gandhi on his death anniversary in Lucknow." In the 1.04-minute video, Yogi was wearing a mask, offering flowers to Gandhi's statue, and then sitting for a prayer song performance by school children near the statue of Gandhi. As the social media posts claimed, he didn't leave the venue in 30 seconds. The 17-second clip was cropped from the longer video posted by the news agency. Here is the link to the YouTube Video . Below is the screenshot of the video. Further search with the same keyword on Twitter led the Desk to a 7.04-minute video posted by CM Office's handle on Jan 30. The handle had posted the video of the same event on Jan 30 in Lucknow. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the video. It's clear that the video in the social media post was shot on January 30, 2022, and Yogi didn't leave the event venue in 30 seconds. As we know that 30 January each year marks Gandhi's death anniversary, and the nation celebrates the birth anniversaries of Mahatma Gandhi and Lal Bahadur Shashtri on October 2. Now, the Desk started investigating the second part of the claim that Yogi didn't offer prayers to Gandhi's statue with folded hands. To verify the claim, we searched for the details of the people visible with Yogi at the same event in the video tweeted from the CM's handle. We found that one of them was Ashutosh Tandon, BJP MLA from Lucknow East, as highlighted in the screenshot below- The video also showed Tondon sitting with Yogi at the same event. As seen in the screenshot above, Tondon posted three images on Jan 30, and one of the images showed Yogi wearing a mask and bowing his head with folded hands in front of Gandhi's statue. Here is the tweet posted by Tondon. Below is the Yogi's image posted by Tondon in his tweet- In the social media clip, when Yogi bowed down after offering flowers to the statue, the focus of the video camera was probably not on him, so he was not seen paying tribute with folded hands. This image, clicked from a still camera from another angle, shows him paying respect to Gandhi. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk tried to contact Ashutosh Tandon to verify the claim. We will update the article once he replies to the Desk's query.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Former PM Manmohan Singh doesn't have a Twitter account; social media post shared in his name is misleading
content: New Delhi, October 17 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user has shared a screenshot of a tweet claiming former prime minister Dr Manmohan Singh tweeted in favour of the Popular Front of India (PFI) and against the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the tweet shared in the Facebook post is not from a verified handle, and Manmohan Singh doesn't have a Twitter account. The Facebook post showing the tweet in the name of Dr. Singh is misleading. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 a Facebook post requesting to verify the claim that Dr. Manmohan Singh posted a tweet in favour of PFI and against RSS. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post. Below is the screenshot of the post- Investigation The Desk started the investigation by checking the tweet shown in the Facebook post. We searched with the handle @Mr_ManmohanSing on Twitter and found an unverified handle. Here is the link to the handle . The profile's bio read: "He is an Indian economist and politician who served as the 13th Prime Minister of India from 2004 to 2014. (Parody account) Not affiliated to Manmohan Singh." It's clear from the bio that it is a parody account created in May 2022. The parody account has used Manmohan Singh's image in the profile photo and his photo with Rahul Gandhi in the banner image. Below is the screenshot of the handle- Continuing the investigation, the Desk scanned the 'tweets & replies' on the Twitter handle and found the tweet - shared in the Facebook post - was published with a video on September 30. Here is the link to the tweet , which was retweeted by more than 5,000 users and liked by 11,000 others. Below is the screenshot- It is clear that the handle doesn't belong to Manmohan Singh. Later, the Desk searched Google to find if Dr Singh made any statement on the recent ban on the PFI, but could not see any news agency or website report n the same. In the next part of the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk contacted Supriya Shrinate, the head of the social media department and spokesperson of the Congress party, and shared the Facebook post and the tweet with her to verify. Shrinate said: "Former prime minister Dr Manmohan Singh does not have a Twitter account. Any claims to the contrary are mischievous and deliberately done to create controversy. These are not his quotes or views either. We will raise this with the platform for appropriate action." Subsequently, the Desk searched Twitter to check if more handles were active in the name of Manmohan Singh or showing his image as the profile photo. We found two more Twitter handles with thousands of followers using Dr Singh's name and photos in their bio. One handle with more than 180,000 followers mentions in its bio that it is a 'Parody Account'. The other account with 66,000 plus followers describes itself as a 'Fan Account'. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both profile pages- The PTI Fact Check Desk suggests that readers check the profile details carefully to see if the names and photos of politicians, celebrities, or influencers have been used in unverified social media accounts.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited photo of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman buying onions shared with misleading claim
content: Chennai, October 18 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): An image of Nirmala Sitharaman was shared on Twitter, claiming she bought onions while visiting a vegetable market in Chennai. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image shared in the tweet was digitally morphed. The finance minister visited Chennai's vegetable market on October 8 and bought some vegetables. But the image used in the tweet showing her buying onions is edited. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 two tweets posted by the verified Twitter handle of Maharashtra Congress Sevadal requesting to substantiate the claim in the tweets. Both tweets showed the same image of Sitharaman purchasing onions in a vegetable market. The first tweet was posted at 12.19 PM on October 11 with the text: "ये प्याज क्या पड़ोसियों के लिए खरीदी जा रही है?" (Are onions being bought for neighbours?) Here's the link and archive link to the post. The Second tweet was published at 10.26 PM on the same day. The text read: "संसद में सुना था कि @nsitharaman प्याज खाती ही नही है।" (Had heard in Parliament that @nsitharaman didn't eat onion) The link and archive link to the post can be seen here and here . Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both tweets- While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found another tweet and a Facebook post with the same image and similar claim. The Tweet and the FB post can be seen here and here . Investigation The Desk started the investigation by doing a Google Search with the keyword "Nirmala Sitharaman in the vegetable market" and found a Mint Website report published on October 9 with the headline - "Watch: Nirmala Sitharaman buys vegetables from Chennai local market." A paragraph in the Mint report read: "The finance minister was in Chennai for a single day (On Oct 8). Later, she unexpectedly stopped at Mylapore vegetable market where she spoke with vendors and locals." Now, the Desk scanned the Twitter handles of Sitharaman's office to find if any images or videos were posted on her visit to the local vegetable market in Tamil Nadu's capital city. We found a 1.30-minute video posted from @nsitharamanoffc published at 8.23 PM on Oct 8 in which the finance minister was seen talking to a shop owner and buying vegetables at a vegetable market. The text in the tweet read: "During her day-long visit to Chennai, Smt @nsitharaman halted at Mylapore market where she interacted with the vendors & residents and also purchased vegetables." Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk watched the video to check, finding a frame similar to the image shared in the viral tweet. We noticed that onions were not there in the finance minister's basket, as claimed in the photos shared by the Maharashtra Congress Sevadal Twitter handle. Below is the combined image of the screenshot captured from the video and the photo shared in the tweet- The combined photo above established that one screengrab from Sitharaman's video was copied and edited to share on social media platforms with a misleading claim. This is not the first time Sitharaman became the target of misinformation for her 'Onion' remarks she made in Parliament in 2019. During a debate in the Lok Sabha in December 2019, MP when Supriya Sule asked a question on the rising onion prices, and someone else from the Opposition also asked a direct question, Sitharaman replied: "I don't eat much garlic and onions, so don't worry. I come from a family where onions and garlic are not used that much." After the statement, many unverified claims started floating on social media platforms, and even the Opposition leaders also targeted the minister for being 'insensitive.' Later, the minister's office posted a full video of her statement claiming a shorter clip was used out of context to spread misinformation against her. Below is the screenshot of the video, and the tweet by Sitharaman's office can be seen here .

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo and video of chopper accidents being shared on social media after Kedarnath helicopter crash
content: New Delhi, October 19 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users, including leaders from the major political parties, shared a photo and a video of helicopter crash incidents in their posts on the Kedarnath helicopter incident that happened on October 18. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image and the video shared in the tweets are not related to the helicopter that crashed in Kedarnath. The Tweets are misleading. Claim While scanning the social media platforms for potential fake information on the helicopter crash incident in Kedarnath, the Desk found an image and a video of burning helicopter used in a series of tweets posted after the Kedarnath helicopter crash incident. Seven people were killed when a helicopter carrying pilgrims went down minutes after taking off and broken into pieces in Kedarnath on October 18. We found a tweet by P.N. Pathak, BJP MLA from Kushinagar in Uttar Pradesh, showing three images. One of the images showed a helicopter in flames while flying, and two photos showed broken pieces of the machine on the ground. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Similarly, we found a post by Indraj Gurjar, Congress MLA from Viratnagar and a member of the Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee as described in his bio, showing three pictures and one of them shwed a flying helicopter into flames. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Rahul Gurjar, the National Social Media charge of @BJP4OBCMORCHA, also shared the same image and the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. A user who described herself as a journalist with a media house also posted the same image in her tweet on the Kedarnath crash. Her tweet can be found here, and here is the link to the archive link to the post. The Desk noticed that all four tweets mentioned above were posted from the verified Twitter handles. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the tweets - Later, the Desk found many other users also shared the same photo in their tweets on the Kedarnath crash. The links to the tweets can be found here , here , here , and here . Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the tweets - We noticed that Dainik Jagran's Hindi news website used the same image in one of its articles on the Kedarnath crash, and later changed it. Here is archive link to the report. When the Desk searched in Google, it found that multiple media houses used the same image in their previous reports on chopper crash incidents in the last four years and mentioned 'representation image' in the photo caption. The reports can be seen here , here , here and here . We also noticed that one user shared a video in the tweet claiming it was shot when the helicopter in Kedarnath also. Here is the link to the tweet showing the video. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation by doing a Google Reverse Image Search on the image in the tweet by the leaders of BJP and Congress and found that the same image was published on the iStockPhoto website. iStockPhoto published the same photo on March 24, 2015 with credit to Giocalde. Here is the link to the iStockphoto website where the photo was published. And here's the link to the page of the photographer to whom the credit was given on the iStockPhoto website. Below is the screenshot of the iStockPhoto page- The Google Reverse Image Search results proved that the same photo was there on the Internet since 2014. Now, the Desk started investigating into the claim of the 17-second video shared in one of the tweets. We used InVid to find the source of the footage by uploading the clip into the video verification tool. With the Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes in the InVid tool, we found a more extended version of the same video on YouTube. According to the description, the video showed Mi-8 Crash during an air show in Gelendzhik in Russia on September 5, 2014. Here is the link to the YouTube video . Below is the screenshot of the YT Video- It's clear that the image of the helicopter shown in the tweets has been over the Internet since 2014 and used in multiple media reports filed before October 2022. The image in the series of tweets has nothing to do with the recent Kedarnath chopper crash on Oct 18 this year.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Twitter accounts of Donald Trump and Kangana Ranaut still suspended; tweets from parody and fan accounts shared as real
content: New Delhi, Nov 11 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Soon after Elon Musk took control of Twitter after finalising a $44bn deal, the micro-blogging site was flooded with multiple posts claiming former US president Donald Trump and Bollywood star Kangana Ranaut got access to their suspended accounts. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral tweets were misleading. Twitter handles of Trump and Kangana are still under permanent suspension. Musk has yet to decide on the accounts suspended for violating Twitter Rules. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91 - 8130503759 two screenshots and tweets that claimed former US President Donald Trump and Bollywood actor Kangana Ranaut returned to Twitter after Elon Musk took over Twitter in October this year. Here's the link and the archive link to the first tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The second tweet, shared by Twitter handle @TheKangnaRanut, claimed the actor returned to Twitter and thanked Elon Musk, the new owner of the social networking site. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Twitter search and found a few more posts claiming Trump was back on Twitter. Below are the screenshots of those posts- Continuing the investigation, the Desk did a Google Search with the keyword 'Donald Trump Back on Twitter' and did not find any report. Subsequently, we checked Trump's original Twitter handle, @RealDonaldTrump and found it permanently suspended. Here is the link to his suspended Twitter handle , and below is the screenshot of the page- A Twitter blog posted in January 2021 detailed why Trump's account was permanently suspended. Below is the screenshot of the post- While searching the Internet, the Desk came across a 'press note' announcing Trump's decision to join Twitter again. The 'press note' was later found fake, and many fact-checker journalists tweeted about it. BBC World journalist Shayan Sardarizadeh was one of them who tweeted about the fake press note. Here is the link to his tweet , and below is the screenshot of the post- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched for reports on Kangana returning to Twitter. The handle @KangnaRanut posted the tweet we received with a request for verification. We noticed that the actor's name was misspelled on the Twitter handle. The account was opened just a month back, in October 2022, with two tweets published on Nov 1 and 2. The bio of the handle read: "Official Twitter Handle Team - Kangna Ranaut - Deshbhakt - Actress." Below is the screenshot of the tweets- Kangana Ranaut's Twitter account was permanently suspended in May 2021 for repeated violations of Twitter rules. An Indian Express report published on the day her account was suspended quoted a Twitter spokesperson saying: "We've been clear that we will take strong enforcement action on behaviour that has the potential to lead to offline harm. The referenced account has been permanently suspended for repeated violations of Twitter Rules, specifically our Hateful Conduct policy and Abusive Behaviour policy." The Report can be seen here . Here is the link to Ranaut's suspended Twitter account , and below is the screenshot of the page- The actor applauded Elon Musk via her Instagram Stories when he took control of Twitter in the last week of October, but there was no report that she returned to Twitter as claimed in the viral tweet. However, an NDTV report published on Oct 29 quoted Kangana saying: "I'm happy that I'm not there on Twitter. But if my account is revived, then you will definitely get a lot of 'masala.' If I come back on Twitter, people's lives will become sensational, and my life will become problematic because cases are filed against me in different states. I was on Twitter for one year, and Twitter couldn't tolerate me for even a year. I completed one year on Instagram in May, and I have already received three warnings. So I said I would not use Instagram. My team has taken over, and now everything is good. Nobody has a problem with it." The report can be seen here . The investigation suggested that the Twitter accounts of Donald Trump and Kangana Ranaut were still under permanent suspension, and parody handles and fan account posted the viral tweets. However, Musk, after taking over Twitter, indicated having a clear process to allow the handles which violated Twitter rules in the next few weeks. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot- Musk also mentioned highlighting 'parody' in the handles of the parody accounts in one of his tweets posted on Nov 11. The thread of tweets read: "Going forward, accounts engaged in parody must include "parody" in their name, not just in bio." "To be more precise accounts doing parody impersonations. Basically, tricking people is not ok. " The link to the thread can be seen here . Below is the screenshot- The PTI Fact Check Desk requests that users check Twitter handles' bio carefully to verify such accounts' authenticity and tweets.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Kharge didn't mention Gehlot or Pilot in Shimla speech; Facebook post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Nov 11 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A recent Facebook post shared a video of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's speech during an election rally in Shimla with the text quoting him as saying Sachin Pilot would replace Ashok Gehlot as chief minister of Rajasthan. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that Kharge made no such announcement in the video and at the rally he addressed at Banuti in Shimla Rural. The claim in the Facebook post, which received one million views and 43,000 likes, is false. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 a link to a Facebook post and a screenshot requesting that the claim be verified. The video showed Kharge addressing a public rally with the text in the post reading: "खड़गे ने किया शिमला में बड़ा ऐलान सचिन होंगे मुख्यमंत्री गहलोत को मिलेगी बगावत की सजा " (Kharge made a big announcement in Shimla. Sachin Pilot will be the new Rajasthan CM. Ashok Gehlot will be punished for his revolt") Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, which created a flutter with its claim on the Gehlot-Pilot friction that has long played out in public and been the centre of endless debate. Below is the screenshot of the page- Investigation A close watch of the 22.33-minute video to verify if the Congress president indeed said something about Gehlot and Rajasthan revealed that he had not. Kharge's November 9 speech at Banuti in the Himachal Pradesh capital focused on his election as party president and highlighted the issues of BJP governments in the hill state. While addressing the people in the run-up to assembly elections in the state, Kharge attacked the Narendra Modi government for rising inflation and declining job opportunities across the country. He listed the achievements of the previous Congress-led UPA government at the Centre and praised Sonia Gandhi's leadership. The Congress president also targeted the BJP government in Himachal Pradesh and appealed to the voters to give the Congress a chance to form the government in the state. Kharge's Banuti rally was organised by the Congress party's Himachal Pradesh. A screenshot of the video (below) shows the rally details printed on the background banner on the stage. As the next step of its investigation, the Fact Check Desk scanned the Congress' social media handles to search for the source of the Facebook clip. It found a 1:12-hour video of the same rally uploaded by the party's YouTube channel on November 9. In the YouTube video, Kharge is seen addressing the rally from 00:49:40 onwards. He doesn't talk about Rajasthan during his speech. The YouTube video can be seen here. The combined image (below) of the screenshots of the Facebook post video and the Congress' YouTube video indicated both the videos were of the Congress rally in Banuti on November 9. A subsequent Google Search with the keywords 'Kharge Banuti Shimla Rally' also found no report on Kharge talking about Gehlot, Pilot, or Rajasthan in his Banuti rally speech. In the next part of the investigation, we reached out to Congress spokesperson Gurdeep Singh Sappal. Sappal rebutted claims made in the viral Facebook post and said, "The Shimla speech was on Himachal Pradesh elections. It had nothing to do with Rajasthan or any other state."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Golden Dragon lit-up boats from China shared as Deepotsavam in India; Claim in viral video is fake
content: New Delhi, Nov 15 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users shared a video of interconnected lit-up boats sailing in a river claiming that 240 lit-up boats were sailing on a river near Sri Mahankaleshwara Devalayam to celebrate Deepotsavam in Kerala. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that it was an old video of interconnected boats from the Golden Dragon show in China. The claim with the video shared in tweets and YouTube channels is fake. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91 - 8130503759 a tweet and a YouTube video showing lit-up boats sailing in a queue with the claim that it was the footage of 240 lit-up boats sailing on the occasion of Dev Deepavali in Kerala on November 7. The text in the tweet read: "Deepotsavam in the river with 240 boats in Kerala." The text, along with the video, reads: "Sri Mahankaleshwara Devalayam, Miralam Mandi." Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Here is the link and archive link to the YouTube Shorts video. Below is the screenshot of the Shorts- While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found many other Twitter handles shared the same video and the claim. The posts can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here . Investigation The Desk started the investigation with the InVid Tool Search on the video shared multiple times in different posts on social media platforms. The InVid results showed the detail of the tweet and a keyframe with an option to do a Reverse Google Image Search. The Google Reverse Image Search on the keyframe led the Desk to a video posted by Twitter handle @tianmumedia on May 23, 2022. The Twitter text read: "Dragon lantern parade on Yulong River of Guilin's Yangshuo. #AmazingChina #festival #Romance". Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk found another tweet with the same video posted by the handle @DiscoverGuangxi on May 20, 2022. The text in the tweet read: "Every year in #Yangshuo, there will be a golden dragon performance in the Yulong #River, the local people singing and setting lanterns on the river to pray for good wishes.#Guilin #Happy520Day #travelgram" Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the post. The Desk searched with the keyword 'Golden Dragon Yangshuo' on YouTube and found many similar videos of boats sailing as a dragon on the rivers. The video description suggested the event was organised on the Yulong River in Yangshuo in Guangxi in China in May this year. During the search, the Desk found the same YouTube Shorts video, shared with the claim of Kerala's Deepotsavam celebration on social media platforms. Here is the link to the YouTube Shorts video . Below is the screenshot of the Shorts- The Desk also compared the frames (Below) of both videos- The original videos of the Golden Dragon sailing boats organised on the Yulong River in Yangshuo in Guangxi in China in May 2022 can be seen here , here , here , here , and here . The viral tweets claimed the video was captured at Sri Mahankaleshwara Temple, Miralam Mandi, in Kerala. We did a Google Search to check if the temple is located in Kerala and if it celebrated Dev Deepavali this year. The search results led us to the Facebook page of the temple. The temple is located in Hyderabad, not Kerala, as claimed in the viral posts. Here is the link to the Facebook page of the temple, and below is the screenshot of the page- The video shared in viral tweets was captured at Guilin near China's Yulong River in May this year. In the video, the Golden Dragon boat, comprised of 88 interconnected bamboo rafts illuminated with lanterns forming a dragon's tail, was seen cruising on the Yulong River in south China's Guangxi.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Sukhant Funeral didn't open stall at Delhi's International Trade Fair; Photo shared by social media users, news websites with false claim
content: New Delhi, Nov 23 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users have shared an image of a stall offering funeral services claiming it was set up at this year's International Trade Fair in Delhi to promote its business. The PTI Fact Check Desk has found in its investigation that the company offers funeral services in a few cities in Maharashtra. The viral photo was captured at a business fair organised in Thane. The claim that the company opened its booth at Delhi's International Trade Fair was false. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found an image of a stall offering funeral services widely shared on Facebook and Twitter, claiming the company opened its counter at this year's India International Trade Fair in Delhi. The Desk received the same image requesting to verify the claim on its Fact-Check WhatsApp Number +91 - 8130503759 . Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post- Below is the screenshot of the post- Here is the link and archive link to the tweet sent to PTI Fact Check WhatsApp number. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk found many news websites also published reports on the social media posts that claimed the company opened a stall at this year's trade fair in Delhi. Here's the link and archive link to the Zee News report: Below is the screenshot of the article headline - Here's the link and archive link to the TV9 report. Below is the screenshot of the article headline - Here's the link and archive link to the Prabhat Khabar report. Below is the screenshot of the article headline - Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search to find the source of the viral image. We found that a few news websites also published reports claiming the company's stall was at Delhi's International Trade Fair. Here's the link and archive link to the India Today report. Below is the screenshot of the India Today article- Here's the link and archive link to the First Post report: Below is the screenshot of the First Post article- Here's the link and archive link to the English Jagran report. Below is the screenshot of the article headline- During the investigation, the Desk found that most news reports quoted a tweet posted by @AwanishSharan . The bio of the handle read: "IAS 2009 Batch. Chhattisgarh Cadre" The post, published on Nov 20, was retweeted 431 times and received 4131 likes in two days. Below is the screenshot of his profile on Twitter- Here is the link and archive link to his tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post- However, Sharan didn't mention in his tweet that the photo was from this year's Delhi International Trade Fair. Instead, he asked a question in his tweet: "Why would there be a need for such a 'start-up'?" Continuing the investigation, the Desk requested its Video journalist Madhur Khanna to go to the trade fair venue to check if there was any such stall. On Nov 22, Madhur visited almost all the stalls at the fair and couldn't find the 'Sukhant Funeral' booth as claimed in the viral image. The Desk contacted PTI journalist Vishu Adhana, who was reporting from the trade fair venue this year. Vishu talked to the senior manager of the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) Vivekananda Vivek, to verify the claim. The ITPO senior manager told PTI: "There is no stall by the said start-up. You can check it yourself. Several media organisations have carried the news. It is fake news. The photos being circulated are from some other place as the ceiling is quite low, which you can check is not the case in any of our halls." The Desk subsequently scanned the start-up 'Sukhant Funeral's social media handles ionGoogle and found its account on Twitter . Below is the screenshot of the page- The Desk contacted Sanjay Ramgude, founder & director of Sukhant Antim Sanskar Seva, by dialling the phone number mentioned in the Twitter Bio. Ramgude, while talking to the Desk over the phone, said that the stall photo in the viral social media posts was not from Delhi's International Trade Fair. Ramgude said: "The photo shared in the social media posts was captured when the company installed the booth to promote its start-up at the Maharashtra Business Jatra trade fair in Thane in on Nov 11-12 this year. I request the people not to share the photo with false information." "The Business Jatra provides a unique platform to new entrepreneurs. My company opened the stall at this year's Business Jatra Trade Fair to make people aware of our services in Mumbai, Pune, Thane, and Nasik," he added.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi's translator didn't leave stage in middle of his speech; Claim in viral video is misleading
content: New Delhi, Nov 29 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users, including politicians, have shared a video of Rahul Gandhi claiming that his translator left the stage in the middle of his speech at a public rally because he could not understand and translate it. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the people at the rally told the translator to let Gandhi continue his speech in Hindi. The translator conveyed the same to Gandhi and returned to his seat. The claim that the translator walked out while Gandhi was addressing the people was misleading. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91 - 8130503759 a tweet requesting to verify the claim that Rahul Gandhi's translator walked out in the middle of his speech. The tweet read: "Unable to understand and translate; the translator walks away; Rahul Gandhi does it again!" Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- While scanning the Internet for similar posts, the Desk found many tweets with the same video and the claim. The tweets can be seen here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , here , and here . Investigation The Desk started the investigation by searching YouTube for the original video of the clip shared in the tweets. We came across a full video of the same public rally in Surat shared by the Congress party's YouTube channel on Nov 21.
