Rahul Gandhi can be seen in the video addressing people at his party's political rally in Surat on Nov 21. The headline of the YouTube video read: "Shri Rahul Gandhi addresses a public rally in Surat, Gujarat." Here is the link to the video . Below is the screenshot of the video- When the Desk watched the original video, it found that Gandhi started his speech at 25:20 minutes, speaking in Hindi, and the translator translated it into Gujarati. While watching the video, the Desk noticed that Rahul Gandhi's speech in Hindi and its translation in Gujarati by the translator continued uninterrupted till 38:05 minute. At 38:05 minute in the video, Rahul started talking about a story of his conversation when he was 5-6 years old with his grandmother, the late prime minister Indira Gandhi. When the translator started telling the story in Gujarati, a few people from the stage and the audience asked Gandhi to continue speaking in Hindi only. In the video, the translator can be seen accepting people's demands and suggesting Gandhi continue speaking in Hindi. He told Rahul: "It will work if you speak in Hindi." People cheered for Rahul when he asked, "Will it work?" The translator was also heard saying, "It will work. They understand your Hindi." By the time Rahul asked the translator if he didn't want to translate, he had left the stage to return to his seat. Later, people clapped for Gandhi for telling his story in Hindi, and he continued his speech uninterrupted till 47:55 minutes, as showed in the video. Subsequently, the Desk searched the translator's details; he was Bharat Solanki, the former president of the Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee. While scanning Twitter, we found Solanki's video in one of his tweets, which detailed what had happened on the stage. In the video posted from his official handle, he said: "People at the rally said they were ok with Rahul Gandhi speaking in Hindi. I stopped translating his speech, conveyed the message, asked him to continue in Hindi, and returned to my seat." The tweet can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the post-

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: None of these 14 Twitter handles belongs to Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu; New Himachal CM doesn't have official account on micro-blogging site
content: New Delhi, Dec 12 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Newly-elected Congress MLA Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu took oath as the 15th chief minister on Sunday after the party's victory in the recently concluded assembly elections in Himachal Pradesh. Many social media users shared congratulatory messages for the new CM on Twitter. The PTI fact Check Desk found 14 Twitter accounts sharing posts in the name of the new CM. The Desk investigated and found that none of them was verified and authentic. CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu doesn't have an official Twitter account yet. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a Twitter handle in the name of the new Himachal CM, Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Since the account was not verified, the Desk searched Twitter to check If Sukhu had an active and verified Twitter account. The Twitter search led the Desk to a list of 14 Twitter accounts showing Sukhu's photo in the profile image or his details in the bio of the handles. Below is the list of a few handles the Desk found on the search page on Twitter- The handles can be seen here- Twitter Handle 1: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu- @SukhuSukhvinder Twitter Handle 2: Sukhvinder sing Sukhu @Sukhvinder_Inc Twitter Handle 3: Sukhwinder Singh (Sukkhu) @Indian28124530 Twitter Handle 4: Sukhwinder Singh Sukhu @Sukhvindersuke Twitter Handle 5: Sukhwinder Singh Sukhu @Sukhwininc Twitter Handle 6: Sukhwinder Singh Sukhu @ThaleshSingh2 Twitter Handle 7: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @Sukhu_Sukhvindr Twitter Handle 8: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @Sukhvindrsingh_ Twitter Handle 9: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @SukhuINC Twitter Handle 10: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @sukhusukhvender Twitter Handle 11: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @SukhuSukhwinder Twitter Handle 12: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @_Sukhvindersuk Twitter Handle 13: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @SukhvinderHM Twitter Handle 14: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu @yadavhardik_761 Investigation Staring the investigation, the Desk reviewed all the handles, their URLs, usernames, profile photos, banner images, and bio details and checked If any of the 14 handles were verified by Twitter. Almost all handles showed the new Himachal CM's photo as the profile image but used different spellings of his name in the URLs and usernames. Some handles wrote 'Himachal CM' or 'Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh' in the bio; some did not have the updated details. The combined Image of all Twitter handles can be seen below- None of these handles was verified by Twitter. Continuing the investigation, the Desk contacted PTI's Associate Editor Sanjeev Chopra to reach out to the office of the Himachal Pradesh CM to know which one was the original Twitter handle of the new chief minister. The CM's office told PTI: "New Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu does not have an official Twitter account so far."

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, undated videos and 12-year-old photo shared with misleading claims after Dec 9 Tawang clash
content: New Delhi, Dec 14 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Social media platforms flooded with videos of clashes between Indian and Chinese Armed Forces after the reports of the Tawang scuffle in which Indian troops thrashed and pushed back the Chinese PLA at the Line of Actual Control (LAC) on Dec 9. The PTI Fact Check Desk came across two videos and one photo claiming they were related to the recent Tawang scuffle. The Desk found in its investigation that both videos were available on YouTube and published a year back. The photo shared in one of the tweets was published in a report in 2010. The social media posts sharing these videos and photo are misleading. Claims While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found two viral videos claiming they were from the recent Tawang scuffle between Indian and Chinese troops. We also found a tweet with a photo of coffins claiming they were of the Chinese soldiers who lost their lives in the recent Tawang clash. The Desk investigated the videos and the photo, and here is what we found- Claim 1 The caption in the first tweet read: "Proud of Indian Army how they handled the Chinese in #Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. Chinese Expansionists thinking won't work towards India." Here is the link and the archive link of the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet: The Desk found videos with the same claim shared by many other social media users. The posts can be seen here , and here . Investigation The Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on a keyframe of the video and found a video posted on YouTube in June 2020. The video description read: "Indian Army smashing Chinese at Sikkim border 2020." The YouTube video can be found here. Below is the screenshot of the video. Taking a cue from that, we conducted a keyword search and found a news report by NDTV from 2020 that carried the video. It's evident that the video was old, but it was unclear when it was shot. The NDTV report said the video emerged when India and China held top military talks on the Chinese side of the border to discuss the Galwan face-off and other points of dispute in 2020. The similarities in the videos can be seen in the combined image below- Claim 2 Another tweet claimed around 100 Chinese soldiers and 30 Indian soldiers were injured during a recent clash in Tawang. The tweet read: "Around 100 Chinese soldiers were injured, while the number of injured soldiers of the Indian Army is less than 30. Today China must have understood in pure language. Bharat Mata ki jai. Proud of you #IndianArmy #ArunachalPradesh #Tawang" Here is the link and the archive link to the video. Below is the screenshot of the tweet - Investigation The desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on a few keyframes of the video and found similar footage in a YouTube video posted in 2021. The video description read: "WATCH: Galwan Valley Clash Video." The YouTube video can be seen here. Below is the screenshot of the video- The similarities in the frames can be seen in the combined image of the screenshots of the Twitter video (Shared on Dec 12) and the YouTube video (Published in 2021). The investigation so far proved that the video shared in the tweet above was old and unrelated to the recent Tawang clash. Claim 3 A Twitter handle, @defence_360, posted an image of coffins in its tweet. The text read: "INDIA & CHINESE TROOPS CLASH IN TAWANG SECTOR, More than 50 Chinese soldiers were injured, and 20 Chinese troops were eliminated, as per Chinese social media Weibo. Indian & Chinese troops clashed in the Tawang sector of the India-Tibet border on Dec 9. Injuries on both sides." Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with Google Reverse Image Search on the photo in the tweet. The results led us to a report with the same image published on a Chinese website on Dec 7, 2010. Using the Google Translation tool, the Desk changed the report's language to English to check the detail of the photo published in the report. The report's headline read: "Remains of 15 firefighting heroes arrive in Kangding, Sichuan (Photos)". The photo story caption read: "On December 7, the coffins of the 15 martyrs who died in the bush fire in Daofu County, Sichuan Province arrived in Kangding, where a mourning hall was set up in the Kangding Gymnasium for the public to carry out mourning activities. It is reported that the family members of the officers and soldiers who died have all arrived in Kangding, and the memorial service will be held on December 9. The picture shows the coffins of 15 martyrs arriving in Kangding. Photo by Liu Zhongjun issued by China News Agency" Here is the link and the archive link to the report. Below is the screenshot of the image in the report of the death of 15 firefighters in a grassland fire in Sichuan on Dec 7 - Here's what Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told Parliament on December 13 on the Tawang clash: "On 9 December 2022, PLA (People's Liberation Army of China) troops carried out an incursion across the LAC in the Yangtse area of Tawang sector in Arunachal Pradesh and unilaterally changed the status quo. The Chinese attempt was contested by our troops in a firm and resolute manner. The ensuing face off led to a physical scuffle in which the Indian Army bravely prevented the PLA from transgressing into our territory and compelled them to return to their posts. The scuffle led to injuries to a few personnel on both sides. I wish to share with this House that there are no fatalities or serious casualties on our side." The defence minister's complete statement can be read below- The Video of his statement made in Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha can be seen here.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi was not dressed as a monk in Bharat Jodo Yatra; Edited photo shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 17 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra, which started from Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu on September 7, has covered eight states as it completed its 100 days on December 16. During the ambitious foot-march, which aims at covering 3,570 km in 150 days, the Congress leader became the target of misinformation on various occasions. Just before Gandhi's Yatra completed 100 days, a Facebook post went viral in which he was shown dressed as a monk. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral image was edited. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found an image of Rahul Gandhi dressed as a monk, shared by a user on Facebook. The post read: " कोंग्रेसी इस 52 साल के बच्चे से क्या क्या करवायेंगे ? ये कौन सा वेश है ? " (What will Congressmen do to this 52-year-old child? Which costume is this?) Here is the link and the archive link of the post. Below is the screenshot of the post- Moreover, the Desk found another post with the same photo and claim on Twitter. Here is the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo shared on social media. The search results led us to a news report by The Indian Express published on Dec 3. In the article's feature Image (a PTI image), Rahul Gandhi can be seen with 'Computer Baba' at the Bharat Jodo Yatra in Madhya Pradesh. The headline read: "MP: Controversial godman 'Computer Baba' takes part in Bharat Jodo Yatra, interacts with Rahul; BJP targets Congress." Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot of the article- The Desk also compared the viral image with the original one and noticed that image used in the tweet was morphed. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the Image in the viral tweet and the original photo- The self-styled baba participated in the Bharat Jodo Yatra and walked along in Mahudiya village of Madhya Pradesh on December 3, 2022.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Ronaldo's photo in recent social media posts not from FIFA World Cup 2022; Old picture shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 20 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users shared a photo of Portuguese Football player Cristiano Ronaldo watching the FIFA World Cup 2022 final match between Argentina and France on Dec 18. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the picture of the footballer was from the UEFA Champions League, Turin, Italy, in 2018. The claim in the social media post was shared with misleading claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a Facebook post claiming the photo of Cristiano Ronaldo watching the FIFA World Cup Final match between Argentina and France in Qatar. The Desk also received a Facebook post on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 requesting to verify the claim in the post. The Facebook post read: "Ronaldo watching Argentina vs. France in Qatar." Here are the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post - We also came across two Facebook posts with the same image and claims. The links to the posts can be found here and here . Investigation The Desk started the investigation with Google Reverse Image Search on the image and found an image from GettyImages posted on October 2, 2018, with the caption "Juventus v BSC Young Boys - UEFA Champions League Group H." The image's description read: "TURIN, ITALY - OCTOBER 02: (L-R)Georgina Rodriguez and Cristiano Ronaldo look during the Group H match of the UEFA Champions League between Juventus and BSC Young Boys at Allianz Stadium on October 2, 2018, in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images)" Here is the link to the website : Below is the screenshot of the page- Taking a cue from this, we did Google Search with the keyword "Ronaldo attending FIFA World Cup 2022 Finals in Qatar". We didn't find any authentic reports on the claim. According to the GettyImages' description, this photo was from the UEFA Champions League from Italy in 2018.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Modi was not with Amit Shah in this 1993 photo; Social media posts shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 20 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, dating back to 1993, and claimed that the person standing next to him was Amit Shah. In its investigation of the viral post, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the person with Modi in the photo was not Amit Shah. The person seen with Modi in the picture was RSS leader Dr. Sanjiv Oza. He accompanied Modi during his visit to Germany in 1993. The claim relating to Amit Shah in the photo in the social media posts was false. Claim While searching the social media posts, the Desk found a tweet with a photo of Modi claiming the other person with him in the image was Amit Shah. "Little did they know that in 1993, they would be the all-powerful men in India by 2014," the Twitter user captioned the photo he posted on Dec 17, 2022. The text on the Image claimed the person with Modi was Amit Shah, and the photo was clicked in 1993. Here is the link and the archive link of the post. Below is the screenshot of the viral post- The Desk also found in a Twitter search that Bollywood film director Ram Gopal Verma tweeted the same photo in May 2022. Here is the link and the archive link of the post. Investigation The Desk started the investigation and searched Google whether Modi visited Germany in 1993. The Google Search and the Reverse Image Search on the photo led the Desk to a report by the NDTV website published on May 4 this year, confirming that Modi had visited Germany in 1993 while returning from a trip to the US. Modi, along with the person claimed as Amit Shah, was standing near the statue of Charlemagne, the medieval emperor in Western Europe who founded the Holy Roman Empire. The photo was clicked in Frankfurt, where Modi had halted briefly while returning to India from the US. At the time, he was a BJP worker. Here is the link to the story. Below is the screenshot of the report- While it could not be initially ascertained who the other person in the photo was, during our investigation on Twitter, we came across a comment on one post that claimed he was Dr. Sanjiv Oza, an RSS leader from Gujarat. Here is the link to the comment on a Tweet by another user who shared the same image in May this year. Below is the screenshot of the comment- However, to further verify the claim that the person standing next to Modi was Dr. Oza, the Desk searched Google and found a person with the same name, the former Vice Chancellor of Gujarat Ayurved University. Here is the link to the Senate page on the Ayurved University website. Below is the screenshot of the page in which Dr. Oza's name was mentioned as 'Ex-VC of the University- Subsequently, the Desk found his photo in a Facebook post published in April this year on the ABVP Gujarat page. According to the details in the banner of the Facebook post, Dr. Oza is an Ayurvedic Doctor. He was also former Organising Secretary of the Gujarat Unit of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). Here is the link to the Facebook post . Below is the screenshot of the post- Continuing the investigation, we searched Google to find Home Minister Amit Shah's photo clicked in the 1990s. We found Shah's photo clicked in 1997 on his website and compared his photo with Dr. Oza's photo clicked in 1993 in Germany. Below is the combined image of both photos- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Dr. Oza over the phone to confirm from him that the person standing next to Modi in the photo was him. Dr. Sanjiv Oza told PTI Fact Check: "I was sent to Europe in 1992 by the Sangh, and Modiji (as a BJP worker) had gone to the United States in 1993 to join the centenary year celebrations of Swami Vivekananda's 1893 speech at the Chicago Parliament of Religions. He had known me for a long time, and he halted in Germany on his way back from the US. This photo was clicked back then." The photo went viral in May this year when Prime Minister Narendra Modi was on a three-nation Europe tour.

author: Pratyush Ranjan/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Sanjay Raut shared 5-year-old video in his tweet to counter Fadnavis' 'Nano Morcha' remark; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 22 (Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) leader Sanjay Raut shared a video of a huge procession in Maharashtra on Twitter to counter Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis' claim that the protest march held by the opposition was a "Nano Morcha". Raut's tweet was to counter Fadnavis' remark over the MVA's Halla Bol rally held on Dec 17, 2022 in Mumbai, which the latter had termed as a "Nano Morcha". The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that it was an old video of Maratha Kranti Morcha held in 2017 demanding reservation in jobs for the Maratha community. Hence, Sanjay Raut's tweet in which he shared a 5-year-old video was misleading. Raut's tweet came after the Halla Bol rally carried by the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) on December 17 between Richarson and Cruddas at Mazgaon and CSMT at Fort. The video, however, was not of the MVA rally, but of the Maratha Kranti Morcha held in August 2017. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91 - 8130503759 a tweet by Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut with the claim that the MVA procession which Fadnavis had termed as 'Nano Morcha' was indeed quite massive, joined by the people of the state. The text in the tweet read: " देवेंद्र फडणवीस ज्यास नॅनो मोर्चा म्हणून हिणवत आहेत तो हाच ! महाराष्ट्र प्रेमी जनतेचा बुलंद आवाज . देवेंद्र जी .. हे वागणे बरे नाही . जय महाराष्ट्र !" ("This is what Devendra Fadnavis is calling as Nano Morcha! The loud voice of the loving people of Maharashtra. Devendra ji..this behaviour is not good. Jai Maharashtra!") Here is the link and the archive link of the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found another post on Facebook with the same claim with visuals. The posts can be seen here . Investigation The Desk started the investigation with the InVid Tool Search which provided us with a few keyframes, and a Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to a video posted by a Facebook user on Aug 9, 2017. The post read: "J. J. Flyover Mumbai Maratha Sagar." Here is the link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the post- Taking cue from this, The Desk searched on social media platforms and found a tweet by TOI official handle. The tweet read: "#MarathaKrantiMorcha: The community members chanting slogans as they pass-by the JJ flyover. Video by Raju Shinde." The description suggested that the video was from the Maratha Kranti Morcha organised in August 2017. Here is the link to the tweet: Here is the screenshot of the tweet- Taking the investigation further, the Desk searched Google with the keyword 'Maratha Kranti Morcha' and found a report by The Indian Express published on Aug 10, 2017. The headline read: "Maratha Kranti Morcha: South Mumbai halts for 3 lakh marchers". Here is the link and screenshot of the report: Description of the report read: "The 3-kilometre stretch from Byculla to Azad Maidan turned into a sea of saffron phetas (turbans) and flags by mid-morning Wednesday, as the Maratha Kranti Morcha staged its 58th and final 'muk-morcha' or silent demonstration, in Mumbai. The JJ flyover, an arterial connection from south-central Mumbai to south Mumbai, was closed for traffic as demonstrators walked across it." This proves that the video is not from the recent MVA rally.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited photo of PM Modi's visit to Banaras railway station shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 21 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A social media user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to a railway station with a claim that the image was clicked at 04:20 AM, as shown in the digital clock in the picture. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo was edited and shared in the tweet with a false claim. The original image was clicked at 01:13 AM when the PM visited Banaras railway station and inspected the developments works at the platform. Claim While scanning the social media platforms, the Desk found an image of Modi standing under a digital clock of a railway station that showed the time as 04:20. The tweet read: "What an apt capture किसी को कुछ दिखा तो कमेंट करे !! ("What an apt capture. Please comment if anyone saw anything.") Here is the link and archive link of the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet While searching for similar claims on Twitter, the Desk found another tweet with the same photo and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared on social media. The search results led us to a news report by the Times of India published on Dec 14, 2021. The report was about PM Modi's visit to Varanasi in December last year and surprise midnight visit to the Banaras railway station on the intervening night of Dec 13 and 14. The report's headline read: "PM Modi visits Banaras railway station, makes midnight inspection of key development works in Kashi." The lead image in the report showed the same picture that was shared in the social media posts. The digital clock in the photo published in the TOI report confirmed that was clicked at 01:13 AM. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot- Other reports with similar images can be found here and here . Taking a cue from this, we scanned PM Modi's Twitter account to check the claim's veracity and found the original image uploaded with other photos. The photos were uploaded on Modi's Twitter handle around 01:23 AM on Dec 14. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the tweet The Desk also compared the viral image with the original one and noticed that image was morphed to change the timing in the digital clock. Below is the combination of the image shared in the social media posts and the photo shared from Modi's Twitter handle-

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: BJP leader tweeted 3-yr-old video of two Sikh motorcyclists pushing ambulance in Delhi; News websites carried clip as recent
content: New Delhi, Dec 22 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Delhi BJP leader Tajinder Pal Singh Bagga tweeted a video claiming that two Sikh motorcyclists pushed an ambulance, which broke while carrying a critical patient in Delhi. While Bagga did not mention when the incident occurred, it went viral and was carried by a couple of news websites when he posted it on Dec 21. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video posted by Bagga on Twitter was three years old and previously posted on Facebook and YouTube by different users in 2019. The news reports claiming the incident as recent are misleading. Claim The Desk received a message on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number, +91 - 8130503759, requesting to verify the claims in the video Tajinder Pal Singh Bagga tweeted on Dec 21. "While transferring a critical patient from DDU Hospital, Hari Nagar, Delhi to RML Hospital, the Ambulance broke down & was pushed by Two Sikh Motorcyclists for about 12 km at midnight," wrote Bagga in his tweet dated Dec 21, 2022. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with the InVid Tool Search, which provided a few keyframes of the video in the tweet. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to a Facebook post dated October 25, 2019. The post included the same video, describing it as an incident when two Sikh motorcyclists pushed an ambulance, which broke while on its way to DDU Hospital. Here is the link to the Facebook post . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post published in 2019- Continuing the investigation, the Desk searched YouTube and found the same video posted by a user on Oct 25, 2019. Here is the link to the YouTube video . Below is the screenshot of the video posted in 2019- The Desk searched the InVid Tool to know the exact publishing time of both videos, and we found that the video was first published on Facebook and then on YouTube on the same day in 2019. Below are the screenshots of the InVid descriptions of both Facebook and YouTube Videos- Description of the Facebook Video posted in 2019- Descreiption of the YouTube Video published in 2019- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched Google for any similar incident reported in the national capital recently. A Google search with the keyword "two Sikh motorcyclists push ambulance" led us to two media reports, one by Free Press Journal and the other by News18 Tamil, carrying the news based on the tweet by Bagga. Here is the link and the archive link to the report by Free Press Journal. Below is the screenshot of the report- Here is the link and the archive link to the report by News18 Tamil website. Below is the screenshot of the report- When we changed the language of the page from Tamil to English using Google translate tool, the page appeared like this- Here is the link and the archive link to the Inshorts report. Below is the screenshot of the report- The Desk compared the screenshot of the video posted by Bagga in his tweet and the video posted by a user on YouTube in 2019. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos-

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Bhojpuri song was not sung at concert attended by Rahul Gandhi to celebrate 100 days of Bharat Jodo Yatra; Edited video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 23 (Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A WhatsApp user shared a video of Rahul Gandhi claiming that the Congress leader attended an event where a Bhojpuri song was sung by the singers performing on the stage. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video, which was 'forwarded many times' on WhatsApp, was edited. The Bhojpuri song was imposed on the video clip to share it with a false claim. Claim The Desk received a message on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91 - 8130503759 requesting to verify the authenticity of the video of Rahul Gandhi listening to a Bhojpuri song at an event. Below is the combined image of the four screenshots of the video shared multiple times on WhatsApp. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Search with the keyword 'Rahul Gandhi attending musical show.' The search result led us to a PTI report filed on the Outlook website on Dec 17. The headline of the report read: "Live Musical Performances On 100th Day Of Rahul Gandhi-Led 'Bharat Jodo Yatra'" The opening paragraph of the report read: "Live performances were given on Friday night in a musical concert organised here to mark 100 days of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi-led 'Bharat Jodo Yatra.' Gandhi and Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot, AICC general secretary K C Venugopal, and state in-charge Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, attended the concert at Albert Hall here. Playback singer Sunidhi Chauhan and other singers gave performances at the event. Gandhi reached the stage and shared his experience of the yatra during the function. He said the people of India have unlimited intelligence and love." The PTI report gave a clue that the musical concert was organised to mark 100 days of Rahul Gandhi-led 'Bharat Jodo Yatra.' Gandhi, Gehlot, and other Congress workers attended the show at Albert Hall in Jaipur on Dec 16, as the report was filed on Dec 17 morning. Playback singer Sunidhi Chauhan was the lead performer at the event. Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot of the PTI report published on the Outlook website- Continuing the investigation to check if the singers sang a Bhojpuri song as claimed in the viral video, the Desk searched Twitter with the keyword 'Rahul Gandhi Sunidhi Chouhan Jaipur concert.' We found a tweet, a promotional poster of the event showing Sunidhi Chouhan's face, and other details. Below is the screengrab of the poster- The Desk subsequently found a video of the same event posted by a user at 10:45 PM on Dec 16, the day the event was organised. When we compared the video shared on WhatsApp with the video posted on Twitter, we found that both the clips were the same. However, Sunidhi Chauhan was singing one of her popular Bollywood songs in the Twitter video, not a Bhojpuri song as claimed in the viral WhatsApp forward. Here is the link to the tweet : Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk noticed many other users posted the same video on Twitter on the same day. Here is the link to another tweet that showed Sunidhi singing a Hindi song at the same event. Now, the Desk used the InVid tool to compare the keyframes of both videos to confirm that the videos were the same. Below is the combined image of the keyframes of both videos- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk spoke to Lokesh Sharma, Officer on Special Duty (OSD), to Rajasthan CM Ashok Gehlot. He told PTI that no Bhojpuri song was sung at the event, which was organized to mark 100 days of Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra. The Desk also contacted singer Ravindra Upadhyay who was with Sunidhi Chouhan at the same event in Jaipur. "I was present throughout the event, and no such song was sung or played there," Upadhyay confirmed.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: PM Modi's photo in traditional Khasi outfit from his Shillong visit shared with edited image and false claim on Twitter
content: New Delhi, Dec 23 ( Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi claiming that the dress he wore was for women. The user posted a female model's image in the same tweet to indicate that the same dress was available at an online merchandise outlet. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the model's photo was edited and shared in the tweet to spread misinformation. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk noticed a user posted a tweet claiming Modi wore the same dress that a female model promoted on a merchandise portal. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post- When we searched on Twitter for similar posts, we found a screenshot of a tweet by Trinamool MP Kirti Azad. Below is the screenshot of the post tweeted by Azad- The Desk searched their Twitter handle of Azad but couldn't find the tweet on his profile page. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google search to know when PM Modi wore the dress shown in the tweets posted on Twitter. Since the users' tweet was posted on Dec 18, we included the date in the search keyword and found a video of PM Modi's visit to Shillong in Meghalaya uploaded on Modi's YouTube channel on Dec 18. When the Desk watched the first 5 minutes of the video, it noticed that PM Modi wore the same attire (As shown in the tweet) when he was on the dais with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and other leaders. The backdrop on the dais indicated that the PM attended the Golden Jubilee of the North Eastern Council (1972 - 2022) as the chief guest with the home minister and other party leaders from the north east region on Dec 18. Here is the link to the YouTube video . Below are the two screenshots that showed Modi's wearing the same dress and the event details highlighted in the backdrop on the stage- When we searched about the dress Modi wore, we found a report on IndiaTVNews website. The report read: "PM Modi wore a traditional Khasi outfit along with a conventional Garo hat in Shillong - to convey his respect for the culture of both the critical tribes of Meghalaya. Meghalaya has three major tribes - the Garos, the Jayantias, and the Khasis. Shillong is predominantly known to be populated by Khasis, with a sizeable number of people from the other two tribes. Garo hills and Jayantia hills have Garos and Jayantias in the majority population." Here is the link to the report . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched for the dress the female model wore in the photo shared in the tweet. The Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found an advertisement by Shoreline Wear, an online apparel store based in the US. Here is the link to the website . Below is the screenshot of the page- Continuing the investigation, the Desk cropped the photo of the dress and compared it with the image shared in the tweet. The combined image of the screenshots indicated that the image shared in the tweet was morphed- While searching for more information on PM Modi's dress on Twitter, we found a tweet by Himanta Biswa Sarma, Kirti Azad, and his party Trinamool Congress. Below are the links and the screenshots of the tweets- 1. Tweet by Himanta Biswa Sarma 2. Tweet by Trinamool Congress 3. Tweet by Kirti Azad in reply to Himanta Biswa sarma's tweet -

author: Pratyush Ranjan/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Messi's placard message was not about Zelensky; 8-year-old photo morphed and shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 22 (Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a photo of Argentine football champion Lionel Messi holding a placard with a comment on Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky. The viral post claimed that Messi asked Zelensky and Ukrainian refugees to leave Europe at the FIFA World Cup opening ceremony. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that it was an 8-year-old photo first posted on Messi's Instagram page, and it was morphed and shared in recent social media posts with a false claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a Messi photo showing him holding a placard with text written in the Russian language for Zelensky. While speaking at the inaugural event of the football World Cup in Qatar, the tweet claimed that Messi asked the Ukrainian President and the country's refugees to leave Europe. The tweet read: " Yesterday, at the opening of the World Cup in Qatar, Messi expressed his thoughts about refugees from Ukraine and directly about Zelensky's actions: "I'm tired of looking at this senseless war! Zelensky, take your people and get out of Europe; we know the truth!"Футбол Италии!" Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk also came across a Facebook post with the same image and claim. The link to the post and the archive post can be found here. Below is the screenshot of the post- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found the same image on Messi's official Instagram page, posted on May 22, 2014, supporting a child with cancer named Luca Senatore. The post read: " #fuerza Luca." (#strength Luca) Here is the link to the post . Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk compared both photos and found that, except the text on the placard, everything visible in the pictures was the same. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the viral post and the Instagram photo posted in 2014- In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched Google to find if Messi had ever spoken about Zelensky, but it couldn't see any report.

author: Pratyush Ranjan/Amisha Airen
title: PTI Fact Check: 31-yr-old photo related to 1991 USSR economic slowdown shared in recent social media posts to claim Russian banks in trouble
content: New Delhi, Dec 26, (Pratyush Ranjan / Amisha Airen, PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared an image of a crowd claiming that the situation in Russia is terrible, and people were standing outside banks possibly to withdraw their savings. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo was an old picture clicked in 1991. The social media users shared the old image to claim that banks in Russia were in trouble. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a tweet with a photo showing people standing in large numbers outside a building. The user posted a hashtag - # RunOnRussianBanks - to claim that the crowd was outside a bank. The tweet read: "USSR is back. No, this photo isn't from 1982. It's from 2022 #RunOnRussianBanks". Here is the link and the archive link of the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched Twitter and found another tweet with the same image claiming Russians thronged banks to withdraw their savings in the wake of the reports of the falling economy in the country. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk found a few more tweets with the same image and claim. These posts can be seen here , here , and here . Continuing the investigation, the Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared on social media. The search results led us to a report by a website named 'Russia Beyond' published on Apr 14, 2021. The report's headline read: "What was Russia like in 1991 (PHOTOS)". The Desk noticed the report had the same image the social media users shared in recent posts. The photo's caption read: "A line to a food store in Moscow." Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page- Taking a cue from this, the Desk searched Google with the keyword "Food shortage in Russia Economic slump 1991". The search results led us to the same photo with the name of the photographer, Alexander Makarov, on the Sputnik Media Bank page. The photo caption read: "Muscovites lining up to get foodstuffs as the country was hit by the economic slump in 1991". Here is the link to the page . Below is the screenshot of the image - The combination image of the picture published on the Sputnik Media Bank page and shared in the recent tweets can be seen below-

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Ayodhya's Ram Temple inauguration not scheduled on Jan 1, 2023; Facebook post viral with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a post claiming Ayodhya's Ram Mandir will be inaugurated on January 1, 2023. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral post is false. The temple trust confirmed to the Desk that the construction works would be completed next year. The claim in the post shared on Facebook was false. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk came across a viral post on Facebook claiming that the Ram Mandir in Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya will be inaugurated on January 1, 2023. The Facebook post read: " खुश खबरी 1 जनवरी 2023 को राम मंदिर का उद्घाटन होगा , जानकर जिनको खुशी हुई तो # जयश्रीराम " (Good news, Ram Mandir to be inaugurated on 1 January, 2023, #JaiShriRam if you like it). Here are the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the viral post- Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google search to check the Ram Temple's inauguration date and found a PTI report published by The Economic Times on Dec 18 this year. The report headline read: "After construction of Ram Temple in Ayodhya, tourism will increase by ten times: Yogi Adityanath." The report quoted Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath saying that the temple construction will conclude in 2024. "When the construction and development work of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya is completed in 2024, tourism to the city will increase by ten times," the report quoted the CM as saying. Here is the link to the Economic Times report . Below is the screenshot of the report- The Desk next came to cross a news report by Mint titled: "Ayodhya Ram temple: Construction underway for sanctum sanctorum | PICS." The report carried the latest photos of the temple construction, which indicate that it is nowhere near completion by December 31, 2022. Here is the link to the report : Below is the screenshot of the report: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to the Ram Mandi Temple Trust. While talking to the Desk, General Secretary of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, Champat Rai vehemently refuted the claim in social media on Ram Temple's inauguration date. "This is completely false. We should not heed any such claim by any random person," Rai told the PTI Fact Check desk.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Amisha Airen
title: PTI Fact Check: 2-year-old video of PM Modi announcing 'Janata Curfew' shared as recent; Social media posts viral with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 27, (Abhinav Gupta / Amisha Airen, PTI Fact Check ) : A video has been making rounds on social media recently in which Prime Minister Narendra Modi can be seen talking about the steps taken by the government to curb the Covid-19 Pandemic. Several users shared the video on Facebook as if PM Modi's announcements were made recently. The PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the video, dating back to March 2020, was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk came across a Facebook post in which a video shared as Live showed PM Modi addressing the nation over the Covid-19 Pandemic and listing out the steps to curb the spread of the virus. The Facebook post read: " प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने अचानक अपने लोगों के लिए खुशखबरी का ऐलान किया। " (Prime Minister Narendra Modi suddenly announces good news for his people.) Here is the link and archive link to the post: Below is the screenshot of the post- While searching social media platforms, the Desk found another post with the same claim as a live-streamed video. Here is the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared on social media, which took us to a report by The Hindu Business Line published on Mar 20, 2020, when PM Modi announced the 'Janata Curfew' amid the first wave of COVID-19. The report's headline read: "PM Modi calls for 'Janata curfew' on March 22 from 7 AM-9 PM". Here is the link to the article : Below is a screenshot of the article: Subsequently, the Desk did Google Search with the keyword "PM Modi on coronavirus Janata Curfew" and found a video on the official YouTube handle of Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) posted on March 19, 2020. The video showed PM Modi addressing the nation over the COVID-19 Pandemic and announcing the 'Janata Curfew' on March 22. The headline of the YouTube video read: "PM Shri Narendra Modi's address to the nation on COVID-19 | #IndiaFightsCorona." Here is the link to the YouTube video of BJP . Below is the screenshot of the YouTube video: In an advance search, The Desk also found an article on the official website of PIB posted on the same date (March 20, 2020), which mentioned the same announcements made in the viral video. Here is the link to the article : Hence, the Desk concluded that the video in the viral Facebook post, shared as recent, dated back to March 2020 when PM Modi announced the 'Janata Curfew,' which was subsequently followed by the announcement of the first lockdown in the country.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 11-month-old photo of traffic snarls on Manali highway shared as recent in social media posts, news reports
content: New Delhi, Dec 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Thousands of Tourists thronged Manali's tourist city in Himachal Pradesh to celebrate Christmas, year-end, and the new year in the last weeks of December. This unprecedented footfall has led to severe traffic jams on the roads leading to Manali and other connected places in the hills of Himachal Pradesh. Meanwhile, a photo was shared across social media platforms showing massive traffic congestion stretching to several kilometers near Manali. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the photo to be old and the claim in the viral post as misleading. While the high footfall of tourists in Manali has led to significant traffic jams, the viral image has yet to be clicked recently but dates back to January 2022. Claim Scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a viral photo on Twitter that purportedly showed colossal traffic congestion in Manali in Himachal Pradesh. The viral Twitter post read: "Time of the year when 99% of the population is in Manali. Joke apart, there is huge traffic congestion at Manali towards the Atal Tunnel stretch. Follow all traffic rules." Here is the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the viral post: IFS Dharamveer Meena tweeted the image on Dec 26 and captioned it as: "There are limits to how many tourists the hill infrastructure can support. Above that, it's quite risky." Click here to view the tweet and here for an archived link . The viral image was also picked by news portals Editorji and TV9 Hindi to report the traffic condition in Manali on Dec 25, 2022. Here are the link and the archive link to the Editorji report. Below is the screenshot of the report on the Editorji news portal: Here is the link and the archive link to the TV9 Hindi report. Below is the screenshot of the article- The TV9 Hindi report gave the image credit to Twitter handle @OptionsGurukul. The Desk scanned the Twitter handle and found the same image with the same claim posted there on Dec 26. Investigation The Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo and found a Facebook post with the same picture, published on July 11, 2022. The image credit in the Facebook post was given to Yash Handa, whose watermark was there on the image in the post by the page Raid De Himalaya. Here is the link to the Facebook post . Below is the screenshot of the post- In the next step of the investigation, we searched for the profile of Yash Handa and subsequently found his Instagram account, in which he has described himself as a "digital creator" and a "travel freak." Scanning the public account, the Desk found the same photo posted by Yash Handa on Jan 27, 2022. He also wrote in the comment box that he "took this photo on 2nd Jan 2022". Here is the link to his Instagram post . Below is the screenshot of the post- Since the photo was posted in January this year, it is clear that the viral post, in which the image has been shared as recent, is misleading.

title: PTI Fact Check: 7-yr-old video related to Gorkha earthquake in Nepal shared as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Amisha Airen PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of panic-stricken people running on a street claiming it from a recent earthquake in Nepal. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video dated back to 2015. The old video was shared by the social media user with a false claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a tweet with a video showing people running on a street to claim two earthquakes of magnitudes 4.7 and 5.3 hit Nepal's Baglung district on Dec 28. The tweet read: " नेशनल अर्थक्वेक मॉनिटरिंग एंड रिसर्च सेंटर (NEMRC), नेपाल के अनुसार , बुधवार तड़के नेपाल के बागलुंग जिले में 4.7 और 5.3 तीव्रता के दो भूकंप आए। " (According to the National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Center (NEMRC), Nepal, two earthquakes of magnitude 4.7 and 5.3 hit Nepal's Baglung district in the early hours of Wednesday.) Here is the post and the archive link of the post. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with search on Twitter and found many tweets with the same video with similar claims. Here is a tweet and the archived link to it. Here is another post and the archived link to the post. The Desk then searched on Google to verify the veracity of the claim in the post that two earthquakes hit Nepal on Dec 28. It came across a news article by Mint which reported that three earthquakes, of magnitudes 4.7, 5.3 and 4.0, hit Banglung in the early hours of Wednesday (Dec 28). Here is the link to the Mint report . Below is the screenshot of the news report - Continuing the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool search on the video, which provided with a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to a YouTube video dated May 22, 2022. It described the video as an Earthquake of magnitude 6.9 recorded in Peru, Bolivia and Chile. Here is the link to the video . Below is the screenshot of the video- When we went through the comments, the Desk noticed that a comment stating that the video is of a 2015 earthquake in Nepal. Here is the screenshot of the comment - Taking a cue from this, the Desk searched Google with the keyword "Nepal earthquake 2015", which led us to the YouTube video by Selton Video posted on Jun 15, 2015. The video was posted with the headline "Nepal Earthquake CCTV footage Darbar Marg Kathmandu 25 April 2015." On April 25, 2015, a 7.8 earthquake also known as Gorkha earthquake shook Nepal. The video description read: " CCTV footage of Darbar Marg Kathmandu on 25 April 2015". Here is the link to the video . Below is the screenshot of the video The Desk compared the screenshot of the video posted in the viral tweet and the video posted by a user on YouTube in 2015. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos -

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Rahul Gandhi reading National Herald newspaper shared in social media posts with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Amisha Airen PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a photo of Rahul Gandhi claiming the Congress leader was reading a Kannada language newspaper. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image was from the commemorative launch of National Herald newspaper held in Bengaluru on June 12, 2017. The post claiming Rahul Gandhi reading Kannada newspaper was misleading. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 a Facebook post requesting to cross-check the claim that Rahul Gandhi was reading a Kannada newspaper. The text in the post read: " जिसको ठीक से हिंदी पढ़नी नही आती वो कन्नड़ का अखबार पढ़ रहा है . मनोरंजन में कोई कमी नही छोड़ता ये चमचो का वभुचक " ("The one who does not know how to read Hindi properly is reading Kannada newspaper. This chamcho ka vabhuchak leaves no stone unturned in entertainment.") Here's the link and the archive link of the post: Below is the screenshot of the post- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with Google Reverse Image Search on the image. The search results led us to a report by The Financial Express from June 12, 2017 containing the same picture as in the claim. The headline read: " Rahul Gandhi slams BJP at National Herald commemorative edition launch, says government forcing everyone into silence" Here is the link of the report . Below is the screenshot of the report- The news report confirmed that Rahul Gandhi visited Bengaluru to attend the launch of the commemorative edition of the National Herald newspaper, which was held on June 12, 2017. Subsequently, the Desk searched Google with the keyword "Rahul Gandhi at launch of National Herald" and found a tweet from ANI reporting the same image with similar claim as the media report. The tweet read: "Karnataka: Rahul Gandhi at launch of the commemorative edition of the National Herald, in Bengaluru" Here is the link and below is screenshot of the tweet- In the next step of investigation, the Desk searched for the details of the commemorative edition dated June 12, 2017 of the newspaper. The e-paper edition of the said date was found in the official website of National Herald. Here are the screenshots of the first two and last two pages of the 52-page edition: The contents of the inside pages, as mentioned on Page 2 of the e-paper, mention that the articles on those pages were in English language. Only the first and last page of the edition were in Kannada language, which were advertisements. The Desk also did advance search on the official website National Herald website and found that it is published in only 3 languages - English, Hindi and Urdu. This means that they don't have any Kannada edition of newspaper. Below is a screenshot of the website's About Us page: Subsequently, the Desk came to the conclusion that the claim made in the viral post is misleading.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi never said he would stop Bharat Jodo Yatra; Misleading tweets shared by BJP leaders
content: New Delhi, Jan 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Delhi BJP leader shared a video of Rahul Gandhi claiming the Congress leader said he would stop the Bharat Jodo Yatra if it didn't work. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that Rahul Gandhi's remark was unrelated to his Yatra. The tweet shared the 9-second clip of Rahul Gandhi's video in which he responded to a query on wearing a half-sleeve T-Shirt in the winter. The video shared on social media platforms was in the wrong context. Claim Scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a 9-second video clip shared by Delhi BJP general secretary Kuljeet Singh Chahal in which Rahul Gandhi was seen saying, "As long as it is working… when it does not work, we will stop it". Chahal claimed that the Congress leader's remarks were on his Bharat Jodo Yatra. The text in the tweet read: " जब तक चल रही है … जब नहीं काम करेगी तो रोक देंगे … For Rahul Gandhi, Bharat Jodo Yatra is timepass." (As long as it is working… when it does not work, we will stop it… For Rahul Gandhi, Bharat Jodo Yatra is timepass). Here is the link and the archive link of the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk also found the same video and the claim shared by several other BJP leaders on Twitter. Here are the links to the tweet and archive link to the post by BJP leader Harsh Chaturvedi. Another BJP leader Dr Mahesh Sharma also tweeted the same video with the same claim. Here are the links to his tweet and its archived post . Investigation The Desk started the investigation by searching for the video's keyframes using the InVid Tool. Continuing the investigation, the Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes it found in the Invid Tool. The search results led us to a tweet posted by a journalist on the News18 India news channel on Dec 28 last year. The tweet read: " टी शर्ट पहनकर हवा के झोंको के बीच कांग्रेस स्थापना दिवस के मौके पर पार्टी मुख्यालय पहुंचे @Rahul Gandhi, बोले " टी शर्ट ही चल रही है " (Wearing a T-shirt, reached the party headquarters on the occasion of Congress Foundation Day amid gusts of wind @Rahul Gandhi, said " only the T-shirt working.") While watching the 12-second video, we noticed the question about him wearing the T-shirt in the winter. Whatever he said was his reply to the question about him wearing the T-shirt-the people asking questions did not mention his Yatra or Rahul Gandhi himself in the video. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the tweet- While scanning Twitter, the Desk found a tweet posted by Congress Rajya Sabha MP Imran Pratapgarhi. He posted a 16-second clip in which Rahul Gandhi can be seen answering a question about him wearing the T-shirt. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post- Hence, the Desk concluded that the 9-second video of Rahul Gandhi was shared on Twitter in the wrong context.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal not arrested in any case; Satirical website story shared as real
content: New Delhi, Jan 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A Twitter user shared a screenshot of a story claiming former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal was arrested in a child porn case. The post in the screengrab also claimed that Agrawal was nabbed after a tip-off by the company's new owner Elon Musk. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the screenshot in the post shared on Twitter was a part of an article published on a satirical website. The claim in the post shared by the Twitter user was false. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a tweet with a screenshot of an article claiming the arrest of former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal in an alleged child porn case after a tip-off by Elon Musk. Here is the link and the archive link of the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk also came across several Facebook posts with the same image and claim. Here is the link to one such Facebook post . Here is the archived link to the post: Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Here is another Facebook post with the same claim. The archived post can be viewed here: Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google search on the keyword "Parag Agrawal arrested for child porn" and could not find such reports on any news websites. The Desk noticed the purported tweet mentioned 'Vancouver Times' with a publishing date of Dec 23, 2022, in the screenshot. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a Google search for the keyword 'Parag Agrawal Vancouver Times.' The search results led us to the website article about the former Twitter CEO. The report's headline read: "Former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal arrested for child porn." Here is the link and archived link to the report. Below is the screenshot of the article: As the screenshot went viral, Vancouver Times added an update to the story, emphasising that it was a satire article. It also wrote that a note regarding the same was added to the bottom of the story. The Desk went through the report and found a note stating: "This is a satire article. For more information on our website, go to the About Us section or read the Disclaimer." The Desk then checked the website's "About Us" section, which categorically labels its content as "satirical stories." It states, "Vancouver Times is the most trusted source for satire on the West Coast. We write satirical stories about issues that affect conservatives." Below is the screenshot of the About Us page:

title: PTI Fact Check: No, WHO didn't term Covid-19 common flu; 2020 World Doctors Alliance video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 03 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video claiming the World Health Organisation (WHO) termed Coronavirus as the common flu in a recent announcement. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the footage dated back to 2020 and was shared as recent with a misleading claim. Claim The PTI Fact Check Desk received a tweet on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +81-8130503759 with a request to verify the claim in the video shared in the post. The tweet read: "Breaking News: WHO accepted its mistake and took a complete U-turn and said that Corona is a seasonal virus, it's a cough, cold and sore throat that occurs during the change of weather, there is no need to panic." Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk submitted the tweet URL in the InVid Tool to check the details of the video and find its keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to a video by ACU (Außerparlamentarischer Corona- Untersuchungsausschuss) dated Nov 13, 2020. The video headline read: "A better normal, not a new normal! Foundation of the WDA - World". The video was of a panel of the World Doctors Alliance doctors who gathered in Berlin in Oct 2020 to discuss the coronavirus pandemic. When the Desk watched the entire 18:17-minute video, it noticed that the clip shared in the tweet was a small chunk of the original video. The original video showed the same footage (As shared in the recent tweet) between 16:35 - 17:21 minutes in which Heiko Schöning, a doctor from Germany, said: "Yes, so these are the statements of experts, doctors, and other scientists and activists all over the world. And we have this good message: we see no evidence of a medical pandemic. So, it looks like a plandemic. And we all together say: we don't want this "new normal," certainly. And we don't want to go back to the old normal because the old normal created this situation of "new normal. We want a better normal, and we want it together with you! Thank you very much indeed!" The English transcript of the video suggested that the people in the video were doctors from different countries participating in the WDA. They gathered in Berlin to announce the World Doctors Alliance under the roof of ACU2020.ORG on October 10, 2020. Here is the link to the video : Below is the screenshot of the video- Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos- In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk scanned the WHO's official website and social media handles but could not find any report or video as claimed in the tweet shared recently. Also, had the WHO made any such announcement, it would have grabbed the headlines across news websites. However, we could not find any authentic media report on the claim made in the viral tweet. Also, we could not find any such statement or announcement made by the WHO on its official website and Twitter handle . While going through the website, the Desk found an article by WHO Director-General dated March 3, 2020, which claimed that the 'Coronavirus is not SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome), it's not MERS (Middle-East Respiratory Syndrome), and it's not influenza. It is a unique virus with unique characteristics. Here is the link to the article , and below is the article's screenshot. We also found that the WHO website advised people to get vaccinated, maintain social distancing, wear face masks and follow other Covid-19 guidelines to keep safe and curb the spread of the virus. Here is the link and screenshot of the website: With the details gathered, the Desk concluded that a 2020 video of WDA was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, WEF didn't issue public order to bathe once a week to save the planet; Social media post shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 04 (Pratyush Ranjan /Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a report claiming the World Economic Forum (WEF) had ordered the public to bathe only once a week or even less as part of an effort to combat climate change. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the WEF never made any such statement on climate change. The tweet was shared with a false claim. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 a tweet requesting to cross-check a claim that the WEF issued an order directing the public to bathe once a week or less as part of an effort to combat climate change and save the planet. The text in the tweet read: "WEF Orders Public To Bathe 'Once a Week or Less' To Save the Planet. You're pushing." Here's the link and the archive link of the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The desk also found another tweet with a similar claim. Here are the links to the tweet and the archive post . Below is the screenshot of the tweet: Investigation In the first step of its investigation, the Desk went through the article tweeted by the Twitter user. The article's headline, published by News Punch on Dec 29 last year, read: "WEF Orders Public To Bathe 'Once a Week or Less' To Save the Planet." Here is the link to the article and the archive link to the post: Below is the screenshot of the website The Desk found that the article did not carry any official statement by either the WEF or agency officials. It also found that the hyperlinked YouTube video in the article was not from any official channel and included an animation representation of what it termed "WDR lists the advantages of showering/bathing once a week." Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk did an advance search on the News Punch website and found its 'Terms of Use' page which says the organisation does not stand behind the accuracy of its reporting. Below is a screenshot of the website's Terms of Use page: To further verify the claim's veracity in the article, the Desk scanned the organisation's official website and social media handles but couldn't find any such announcement. The Desk also conducted a Google search for the keyword "WEF public bathing order" but couldn't find any authentic news coverage regarding the claim. Had the WEF made any such announcement, it would have made the headlines across countries. While searching the Internet, the Desk found a report by Treehugger.com on water use for showers published on Sept 19, 2021. The report headline read: "Shower Less to Help Save the Planet." Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot of the page- The report's first paragraph said: "The World Economic Forum consistently lists water crises as a top-five risk in its annual Global Risks Perception Survey, and the United Nations calls water "the primary medium through which we will feel the effects of climate change. Regardless of expert advice and cultural norms, it's clear that daily showers aren't conducive to conservation in an era of widespread water scarcity." The Desk found a link to the WEF_The_Global_Risks_Report_2021, highlighting the water crisis as a 'Top Global Risk by Impact.' Based on the World Economic Forum Global Risks Perception Survey 2020, the report put chemical, food, mineral, and water crises at the top of the global scale because of human overexploitation and mismanagement of critical natural resources across the world. Nowhere in the report has the WEF suggested the frequency of bathing for the public as a step to save water or climate. Here is the link to the PDF of the WEF report . Below is the screenshot of one of the pages of the report- The Treehugger report mentioned the recommendations by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) suggesting taking showers instead of bathing to reduce your water usage significantly, but it didn't connect it with climate change, which was highlighted in the tweet. The Desk found a United Nations report on ' Water Facts ' on its website. The report's opening paragraphs read: "Climate change is primarily a water crisis. We feel its impacts through worsening floods, rising sea levels, shrinking ice fields, wildfires, and droughts. However, water can fight climate change. Sustainable water management is central to building the resilience of societies and ecosystems and reducing carbon emissions. Everyone has a role to play - actions at the individual and household levels are vital." The report highlighted multiple sustainable, affordable, and scalable water solutions and water management steps. Still, the common people's bathing frequency was not mentioned anywhere in the report as a solution to control the water crisis or save climate change. Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot of the page- However, the Desk came across a tweet by United Nations Foundation posted on August 21, 2019, which suggested taking a 5-minute shower every day for the whole year as a step to reduce the carbon emission. The tweet was posted with a link to the UN page and a 6-second-long video suggesting taking action against climate change. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot- When we tried to check the link shared in the tweet, it opened the page with the message - "The requested page "/en/climatechange/take-action.shtml" could not be found." The Desk subsequently concluded that the claim made in the tweet that WEF ordered the public to bathe once a week or less was misleading.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, FIFA will not keep football legend Pele's feet in museum; Social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 05 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared Pele's photo in a post claiming that FIFA will keep the feet of the soccer legend who passed away on Dec 29 last year in a museum for display with the permission of his family. The PTI Fact Check Desk contacted FIFA to verify the information shared in the Facebook post. In an email to the PTI fact Check Desk, the international organisation that controls the sport of football refuted the claim in the Facebook post. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk came across a Facebook post, which included Pele's photo claiming FIFA will keep legendary Brazilian soccer player Pele's feet in the museum with the permission of his family members. "Breaking. FIFA will keep Pele's feet in the museum. Pele's family has given the permission," read the text in the image shared in the Facebook post citing "TNT_SPORTS_BRAZIL," a Brazilian sports outlet. The Facebook post read: "Okay, we don't know what to think about this. Just a day ago, the FIFA boss wanted to ask every single country in the world to name a stadium after Pelé. Some African countries didn't like the idea but cutting his legs and putting them in a museum is a different story." Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post. Below is the screenshot of the post- We found another social media post sharing the same image and claim. Here is the Twitter post and the archive link to it. Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google search with the keyword "Pele's feet to be kept in a museum", and couldn't find any report on the search result page. Owing to the popularity of the late football legend, who passed away on Dec 29 last year, any such announcement by FIFA would have grabbed the headline across global media. The Desk scanned the official website and Twitter handle of FIFA but couldn't find any such announcement by the organisation. We also searched TNT Sports' website and Twitter handles to check whether it made any such claim but could not find any such report. The Desk then conducted a Google search with different keywords related to Pele's demise and came across a BBC article reporting the soccer player's funeral procession . Pele was laid to rest in Santos, where he moved to play for Santos FC at age 15. Here is the link to the BBC report , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk emailed FIFA to verify the claim shared in the Facebook post. In the email reply to the PTI fact Check Desk, the organisation's spokesperson vehemently refuted the claim, saying no such move was ever planned by FIFA. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim shared by social media users carried incorrect information.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 'misleading' video claiming rule change in banking services shared as recent in social media posts
content: New Delhi, Jan 05 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users recently shared a video clip of a news channel claiming that some significant changes in banking services were announced effective from Jan 20, 2023. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video dated back to 2018 and was shared as recent with a false claim. Notably, even back then, the claims made in the video were found misleading. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a Facebook post with a video where the news presenter was seen explaining that free banking services will be discontinued from January 20 this year. The post read: " Changes in Banking Rule from 20.01.2023." Here are the link and the archive link to the post: Below is the screenshot of the post: The Desk found the same video and the claim shared by another user on Facebook. Here is the link and archive link to the post- Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk noticed that the 2:48-minute video showed a logo of Zee Business and DNA money in the background screen. Taking a cue from this, we started our investigation with a keyword search on "Banking rules to change from Jan 20, Zee Business". The search results led us to a tweet by the official Twitter handle of Zee Business with a more extended version (3:49 minutes) of a video posted on Jan 5, 2018. The video shared on Facebook was a small part of the full video (from 01:02 minutes to 3:49 minutes). The anchor in the original video posted in 2018 explained additional charges that would be levied on customers during transactions. The video claimed that the changes in banking rules would be effective from January 20, 2018. The tweet read: " #DNAMoney| 20 जनवरी से महंगी हो जाएगी बैंकिंग ! देखिए , किस काम के लिए कितना चार्ज लगेगा ? " ("#DNAMoney| Banking will become expensive from January 20! See, how much will be charged for which work?") Here is the link and archive link of the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Changes in banking rules from Jan 20". The search results led the Desk to a report by India Today published on Jan 11, 2018. The report's headline read: "Government denies any move to discontinue free banking services." Here is the link and screenshot of the report: While going through the report, the Desk found two tweets of the then financial services secretary Rajeev Kumar posted on Jan 10, 2018. The tweets were in response to the media reports claiming the discontinuation of free banking services from Jan 20, 2018. The tweets by Rajeev Kumar can be viewed here and here . Below are the screenshots of the tweets Rajeev Kumar tweeted a circular by the Indian Banks' Association, which labeled these news reports as baseless and false. According to an official statement by Indian Banks' Association, "There is neither a move by banks for a blanket removal of free services nor such a thing is being contemplated: Indian Banks' Association over reports in social media that free services of public sector banks will be ceased by January 20." "However, banks looking at its commercial and operational costs would constantly examine and revise charges as the case may be," the statement added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2018 video of Zee Business was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post on UP's Sania Mirza, who cleared NDA exam, shared with false claim, wrong photos
content: New Delhi, Jan 4 (Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user posted a tweet with two photos of a woman fighter pilot claiming Sania Mirza, daughter of a TV mechanic from Uttar Pradesh's Mirzapur district, has become India's first Muslim fighter pilot. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that 17-year-old Sania has secured All India Rank 63 and AIR 10 in the girls' category in the 149th course of the National Defence Academy (NDA). She was not yet commissioned as a pilot in the Indian Air Force. The photos used in the tweet were of Mawya Sudan, the first female fighter pilot from Jammu & Kashmir and the 12th woman officer in India. The tweet posted on Dec 24 was shared with a false claim and wrong photos. Claim The Desk received a tweet on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +81-8130503759 with a request to verify the claim made in the post. The tweet read: "Sania Mirza became the country's first Muslim fighter pilot. Sania is a resident of Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh; the father is a TV mechanic." The tweet also included a photo carrying the same claim, allegedly posted by The Mooknayak, a verified Twitter handle. Here is the link to the tweet and the archived link of the post: Below is the screenshot of the tweet: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google search on the keyword "Sania Mirza India's first Muslim fighter pilot." Several reports claimed Sania Mirza was set to become the country's first Muslim fighter pilot. Meanwhile, on the search result page, the Desk found a report by the India Today website, which clarified that while Sania had cracked the NDA exam, reports on many websites carrying the news missed crucial information on the selection process to become the fighter pilot in the Indian Air Force. The India Today report carried the official statement by the IAF: "A candidate takes four years to be commissioned as a pilot in the Indian Air Force.
