The IAF further stated that during four years, the candidate has to complete the designated training for the flying branch." Here is the link to the India Today report . Below is the screenshot of the report- The Desk also found another report by The Hindu website, which carried the official statement by the IAF, which clarified that Sania Mirza would have to undergo training and tests for the next four years, which will subsequently decide on her commissioning as a pilot. Here is the link to the report by The Hindu , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the recruitment website of the IAF, which clearly states that "Candidates, short-listed for Indian Air Force after the initial selection procedure, go through a rigorous three-year training regimen at the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla, followed by specialised training at one of the AF Training Establishments. On successful completion, they are Commissioned as Permanent Commission Officers and posted as officers at any of the Air Force Stations". Here is the link to the website , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the Twitter handle of The Mooknayak, whose alleged photo was attached to the viral claim. While we couldn't find the same in its Twitter handle, we found a related tweet that quoted former Wing Commander Anuma Acharya saying that it will be too early to predict whether Sania Mirza will become a fighter pilot. " सानिया मिर्ज़ा पर गर्व है कि उन्होंने NDA क्लियर किया . क्या वे फ़ाइटर पायलट बनेंगी , ये अभी से कहना ठीक नहीं ! 3 साल के NDA प्रशिक्षण के बाद शायद हम यह होते देख सकेंगे . उम्मीद है कि वे एक अच्छी अधिकारी बनेंगी . बहुत बहुत शुभकामनाएं (Proud of Sania Mirza that she cleared NDA. Will she become a fighter pilot, it is too early to say! After 3 years of NDA training maybe we will see this happening. Hope she turns out to be a good officer. many many congratulations)," read the tweet by The Mooknayak, which mentioned former Wing Commander Anuma Acharya. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the same: Since the tweet received by the Desk to verify the claim's authenticity had two photos of a fighter pilot, the Desk did a Google Reverse Image Search on both images. The search results led us to a tweet by a Twitter handle named Defence squad, which had four images of Mawya Sudan (12th woman officer inducted as a fighter pilot in IAF in 2021) The tweet read: "Touch The Sky with Glory. Meet Flying Officer Mawya Sudan, who became the first female Fighter Pilot In Indian Air Force from Jammu and Kashmir, Rajouri District. She has become the 12th Woman officer to be inducted as a fighter pilot. #ProudMoment #IndianAirForce #IAF (Sic)". Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk compared the photos shared in the tweet we received to verify and the images tweeted by the Twitter handle above. We noticed that the pictures were the same in both tweets- The Desk also found a Hindustan Times report on Mawya Sudan published on June 21 last year. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page- Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the tweet was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of Telangana CM KCR calling himself PM Modi's best friend shared on social media as recent
content: New Delhi, Jan 06 (Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A social media user recently shared a video of K Chandrashekar Rao claiming the Telangana chief minister called himself Prime Minister Narendra Modi's best friend. The user claimed that KCR said this because his daughter was questioned in the liquor scam. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video shared in the tweet was an old video dated back to 2018, and it was shared in the tweet with a misleading claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a tweet with a video of Telangana Chief Minister K Chandrashekar Rao claiming he called himself Prime Minister Narendra Modi's best friend after his daughter K Kavitha was questioned in the Delhi liquor policy scam case. The tweet read: "Daughter caught in liquor scam. Papa suddenly is a changed man. He has become Modiji's fan and best friend." Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet posted on Dec 27, last year. Below is the screenshot of the post: The Desk found a few other social posts carrying the same video and similar claims. The tweets can be seen here and here . The archived links to the tweets can be viewed here and here respectively. Below are the screenshots of the tweets: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the 28-second video clip to get a few keyframes of the footage. A Google Reverse Image search on the keyframes with the keyword 'KCR PM Modi best friend' led us to a YouTube video published on Mar 4, 2018. Responding to a query by a journalist in the 1:36-minute video, KCR can be heard saying: "I have nothing against Mr. Modi. I have all respect for him. As the Honourable Prime Minister of India, I have all respect for him. Another important thing I am telling you is that I am his best friend also. People hardly know what friendship we have between us. The kind of matters we discuss, people hardly know it. Telling it on record." The video was posted by YouTube channel Xporer India on March 4, 2018. The caption of the video read: ""I am Modi's Best Friend" - CM KCR on his relationship with PM Modi." Below is the screenshot of the YouTube video: The Desk subsequently conducted a Google search with the keyword "KCR PM Modi best friend," The search results led us to a Times of India report published on the same date as the YouTube video - Mar 4, 2018. Here is the link to the Times of India report , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk used relevant keywords to look for any recent statement by KCR about PM Modi after his daughter Kavitha's questioning in the Delhi liquor policy scam. However, it could not find any news report on the same. The search results and the old YouTube video dating back to 2018 concluded that the claim about KCR shared in social media posts was misleading.

title: PTI Fact Check: 5-year-old video of argument between doctors during surgery shared as recent
content: New Delhi, Jan 07 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of an alleged verbal spat between doctors inside an operation theatre, claiming it was from Chandigarh. Meanwhile, Pakistan-Canadian journalist Tarek Fatah shared the same video and claimed it was from a hospital in Pakistan. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video related to an incident at a hospital in Rajasthan's Jodhpur in 2017 was shared as recent with a false claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a video shared by a Facebook user on Jan 3 showing doctors involved in a heated argument during surgery in the operation theatre of a hospital. The post read: " बेचारे मरीज़ का क्या हाल हो रहा होगा ! जाने कितनी बार मर मर कर जिया होगा ! डाक्टर साहिबान थोड़ा रहम कीजिए . ये वीडियो #PGI , चंडीगढ़ का बताया जा रहा है . कबीर सिंह मत बनो यार लो reel थी , OT पर real मरीज़ है . (What must be happening to the poor patient? I don't know how many times he must have lived after dying! Doctor, sir, have some mercy. This video is being told of #PGI, Chandigarh. Don't be like Kabir Singh; it was a reel; there is an actual patient in the OT.) Here is the link to the Facebook post and its archive link . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Pakistan-born columnist Tarek Fatah also shared the same video on Jan 4 and claimed it was an incident in Pakistan. The tweet read: "How does one country produce so many xxxxxxx? How does Pakistan do it? Here surgeons in an operation theatre get into a heated argument with the nursing staff." Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Fateh's tweet received more than 2 lakh views, 2700+ likes, and was retweeted 762 times. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool search and found a few keyframes on the result page. We conducted Google Reverse Image Search on one of them and found a tweet by the Deccan Herald website posted on Aug 30, 2017. The tweet read: "WATCH: Doctors fight in operation theatre in Jodhpur hospital, new-born dies." Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the tweet- The Desk then compared the two videos and found they were the same. Below is a comparison of the screenshots from the two videos: Subsequently, the Desk found an article by The Hindu published on Aug 30, 2017, with the same video. The headline read: "Doctors fight during surgery of pregnant woman." Here is the link to the article , and below is the article's screenshot. According to The Hindu report, a doctor named ML Tak and gynecologist Ashok Nainwal got into a heated debate that apparently lasted for around 30 minutes. We also found a report by BBC on the incident, which countered the claim made by several media reports that the woman pictured on the operating table gave birth to a baby who did not survive. The BBC report quoted the Superintendent of Umaid Hospital in Jodhpur, Dr. Ranjana Desai saying, "By the time I saw the video and conducted an internal inquiry, the media had already reported that this baby had died." BBC also mentioned that "a baby did die, but not the one media reported." "A few feet away, on another operating table within the same room, a different woman gave birth to a stillborn baby. "These two incidents are not linked," Dr. Desai told BBC. Here is the link and screenshot of the report- According to a report by Hindi daily Patrika published on September 6, 2017, Jodhpur District Collector Ravikumar Surpur held doctors Ashok Nainwal and M L Tak guilty under the code of medical ethics for committing such actions and recommended disciplinary action on both of them. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2017 video was shared as recent with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo, video of Kolkata slum shared in name of Haldwani encroachment in social media posts
content: New Delhi, Jan 09 ( Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Social media users shared a photo and video of people allegedly living near railway tracks claiming they were related to the Haldwani railway land encroachment case. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo and video were old and not from anywhere in Haldwani. The old image and video from Kolkata were shared in social media posts with false claims. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk came across a tweet, which included a photo showing people living on railway tracks. The user posted the tweet with the hashtag #HaldwaniEncroachment. The tweet read: " This is What the Supreme Court has legitimized. And Our Govt has become Coward, Just Not taking any action, Bogus HMO. (Sic)" Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched Twitter and found another tweet by Major Surendra Poonia with the same image using hashtag #HaldwaniEncroachment. Major Poonia tweeted: "Dear Friends, Don't buy land anywhere .. just unite with your community in large numbers and capture any Govt/Defence/Railway land; Milord will legitimise it. And if you raise your voice against this, you are endangering the country's secularism #HaldwaniEncroachment (Sic). Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Further scanning Twitter, the Desk came across a video in a Twitter post, claiming the visuals were of the alleged land encroachment by Rohingyas near railway tracks in Haldwani. The tweet read: "Here's a glimpse of the illegal Encroachment done by Rohingyas near Haldwani. And now they are playing the victim card like Shaheen Bagh through upfronting the ladies and child's. Even railway have the map of track on which ilg houses present. (Sic)" Here is the link and archive link of the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet: In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk first took up the photo shared on social media and conducted a Google Reverse Image search. The search results led us to an image with the name of the photographer, Samir Hussein, on Getty Images posted on December 12, 2013. The photo caption read: "The Slums And Homeless Of Kolkata." The image's description stated: "KOLKATA, INDIA - DECEMBER 12: People get on with their lives in a slum on the railway tracks as a commuter train goes past on December 12, 2013, in Kolkata, India. Almost one-third of the Kolkata population live in slums, and a further 70,000 are homeless." This suggested that the image was old and was from Kolkata. Here is the link to the page Below is the screenshot of the image - Below is the combination of the image shared on the social media and the photo on Getty Images: Hence, it is clear that the image was not of the alleged encroachment of railway lands in Haldwani, as mentioned in the claim. Continuing the investigation, the Desk took up the video and the claim made in the tweet along with it. It submitted the tweet URL in the InVid Tool to check the details of the video and found its keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to an extended version of the video on YouTube posted by Sukamal Chakraborty on Jan 12, 2017. The caption read: "KOLKATA RAILWAY TRACK GRAB BY THE POOR PEOPLE (INDIAN PEOPLE LIFE WHO LIVES IN RAILWAY TRACK). The description read: "Kolkata railway track grab/occupied by the poor people. Railway track like people's bathroom, kitchen, roof, club, playground, etc." Here is the link to the video . Below is the screenshot of the video While watching the video, the Desk noticed that the clip posted on social media was a small chunk of the original video posted in 2017. Below is the comparison of the screenshots of the video posted in the tweet this year and the video posted o YouTube in 2017: This proved that the video was not related to the recent incident of alleged encroachment in Haldwani. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that old photos and video of the encroachment of railway lands in Kolkata were being shared on social media as recent claims were from Haldwani.

title: PTI Fact Check: Medical experts believe 'insufficient evidence to link artificial sweeteners and cardiac deaths'; Social media post shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 09 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a screenshot of a report claiming artificial sweeteners were responsible for the recent spike in sudden deaths due to cardiac arrests. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the claim in the report cited in the social media post was misleading. Speaking to medical experts and scanning several studies, the Desk found no conclusive evidence backing the claim made in the social media post. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a Facebook post with a screenshot of a report which quoted 'experts' claiming artificial sweeteners were the cause of the increase in deaths due to heart attacks. The post read: "Ahhh yes, that makes sense. Thank you, Mr. Bergman! (Sic)" Here are the link and the archive link to the post, which was published on Dec 30 last year. More than 1500 users liked the post, and 200+ users reshared it. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google search with the keyword 'Artificial sweeteners behind the spike in sudden deaths, heart attack'. The search results led us to the article by Slaynews, published on Dec 24, 2022. The Desk noticed that the screenshot of the same report was shared in the Facebook post later. Here is the link and archive link to the article. Below is the screenshot of the article: The Desk went through the report by Slaynews and found that it quoted a study in the British Medical Journal to back its claim on artificial sweeteners. "A new study claims that artificial sweeteners may increase the risk of cardiovascular disease and "should not be considered a healthy and safe replacement to sugar," the Slaynews report read. Below is the screenshot of a portion of the article: Continuing the investigation, the Desk clicked the hyperlink in the report that led us to the research article in the British Medical Journal published on Sep 07, 2022. The title read: "Artificial sweeteners and risk of cardiovascular diseases: results from the prospective NutriNet-Santé cohort." Here is the link to the research article , and below is the screenshot of the same: The BMJ's large-scale cohort study resulted from a survey of 1,03,388 participants and was prepared based on their dietary intakes and consumption of artificial sweeteners. In its 'Conclusions' part, the BMJ study stated: "The findings from this large scale prospective cohort study suggest a potential direct association between higher artificial sweetener consumption (especially aspartame, acesulfame potassium, and sucralose) and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Artificial sweeteners are present in thousands of food and beverage brands worldwide. However, they remain controversial and are being re-evaluated by the European Food Safety Authority, the World Health Organization, and other health agencies." Below is the screenshot of the summary of the study: The cohort study by the BMJ stated in its conclusion that higher consumption of artificial sweeteners "might be associated with increased risk of CVDs. Further well-designed, large-scale prospective studies need to confirm these results, and experimental studies should be conducted to clarify biological pathways." Below is the screenshot of the same: The BMJ report also cited a 2022 report by the World Health Organisation (WHO) on the health impacts of artificial sweeteners, which "notably observed associations between consumption of beverages with artificial sweeteners (used as a proxy) and some intermediate markers of CVD." In the next step of the investigation, we spoke to four medical experts for their views on the claim in the Slaynews report. Speaking to PTI's Special Correspondent Payal Banerjee, Dr. Richa Chaturvedi (Senior consultant, Endocrine at Delhi's Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals) said: "There is insufficient evidence to link artificial sweeteners and cardiovascular diseases, as of now. However, excessive use of artificial sweeteners should be discouraged. Moderation, as per doctor recommendation, should be followed." Dr. Mukesh Goel (Senior Consultant, Cardiothoracic and Heart Surgery at Delhi's Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals) echoed similar sentiments, pointing out that the BMJ study was a "prospective study with the control group." "There have been many studies in the past which documented increased incidence of worsening of indirect markers of heart disease like hypertension, increased bad cholesterol levels with artificial sweeteners. All these studies were mainly observational. This study published in BMJ is a prospective study with a control group. It has shown an increased incidence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases with artificial sweeteners. These sweeteners are used extensively by food companies and propagated as low calories alternatives to regular sugars," Dr. Goel said. Meanwhile, Dr. Varun Bansal, Senior Consultant, Cardio-Thoracic Surgery at the same hospital, pointed out that the BMJ study was based on the survey done on French participants, majorly educated women who had access to such food products and did not represent the entire population. "The study published in BMJ states that the population consuming artificial sweeteners is at risk of higher BMI, are more likely to smoke, have a sedentary lifestyle, have diet low in nutrients/fibers and high in salt. Contents of the Slaynews report should be read and interpreted carefully before coming to any conclusion or making a decision which has widespread impact." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the social media post was not supported by enough evidence.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video clip of Asaduddin Owaisi's speech shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video of All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief Asaduddin Owaisi claiming he cited a Hindu religious hymn during his speech. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was edited to make him look like he was chanting the hymn. The Desk watched the original video of his speech and didn't find him chanting any religious song. The Instagram post was shared with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user, who goes by the name Perfect Whistler, posted a reel on Instagram on Dec 18 last year which showed Asaduddin Owaisi chanting a Hindu religious hymn. The user captioned the reel: "Owaisi is now a Hindu priest." Here is the link and the archive link to the Instagram post, which was liked by more than 2.5 lakh users. Below is the screenshot of the Instagram reel: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool for the details and the keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led it to a 3:17-minute-long YouTube video posted by Aaj Tak on Oct 9 last year. The video description suggested Owaisi was addressing a public rally on Oct 9, 2022. The AIMIM leader was not found singing any religious song in the video. Here is the link to the YouTube video . Below is its screenshot of the page: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the video clip shared on the Instagram reel and the one found on YouTube. Below is a comparison of the screengrabs of the video posted on Instagram and the other from YouTube: The Desk subsequently searched Google with the keyword 'Owaisi attacks BJP Oct 9, 2022' and found a report on the India Today website , which suggested the AIMIM chief, while speaking at the event, trained guns on the BJP after some men were tied to a pole and flogged with canes for allegedly throwing stones at a Navratri Garba event in Gujarat last year. Nowhere in the report was it mentioned that Owaisi chanted any religious hymn during his public rally. The Desk found another report on the ABP News website , but nothing on Owaisi singing any religious song was mentioned in it. In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk used the Advance Search feature on Twitter with the keyword 'Owaisi Oct 9 video' and found footage of the same event posted in a tweet by Owaisi's official Twitter handle on Oct 8 last year. The tweet's caption suggested the video was of an event named Jalsa Rahmatul lil aalameen, Darussalam, in Hyderabad. Owaisi started his speech at 4:23 hour and ended at 5:42 hour in the 5:46-hour-long video of the event. In his 1:19-hour-long address, the Desk didn't find him chanting any religious hymn. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the same: The link to the event's live broadcast was posted by AIMIM's Twitter handle and shared by Owaisi's handle later. Here is the link to the tweet posted by AIMIM's handle . In the next step of its investigation, the Desk scanned the Instagram profile of 'Perfect Whistler' and found several digitally altered videos on his page posted in the past. title: PTI Fact Check: 5-year-old video of accident due to dense fog on Yamuna Expressway shared as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video of several vehicles colliding with each other due to dense fog and claimed the incident took place in Rajasthan recently. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video shared in the Instagram post was old and related to an incident where 18 cars collided on Yamuna Expressway in Uttar Pradesh in 2017. The Instagram post which shared the 5-year-old video as recent was misleading. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a video posted by an Instagram user on Jan 3, 2023, which showed several vehicles colliding with each other, leaving several injured. The user claimed the accident took place in Rajasthan. The post read: " राजस्थान में ज्यादा धुंध या ओस की वजह से। एक्सीडेंट का खतरा ज्यादा बड़ गया इस लिए कृपया करके वाहन या साधन को धीरे चलाएं। आज का एक वीडियो एक्सीडेंट सामने आया है इस तरह से एक्सीडेंट का कारण ज्यादा बनता है जरूर यह वीडियो देखें " (The danger of accidents has increased due to fog and dew in Rajasthan. So, please drive your vehicle slowly. A video of today's accident has surfaced and such accidents happen more due to these reasons. You must watch this video.) Here is the link to the Instagram post and its archive link . Below is the screenshot of the post: The Desk found a Facebook post with the same video on Jan 3. The post read: " घने कोहरे के कारण कई वाहन आपस मे भिड़े, लाइव तस्वीर, वीडियो हुआ वायरल " (Many vehicles collided with each other due to dense fog. Live picture, and video went viral.) Here is the link and the archive link to the post: Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk used the InVid Tool to find the details and the keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a YouTube video posted on Nov 8, 2017. The caption of the YouTube video read: "Horrific video: 6 cars collide due to smog on Yamuna Expressway | Delhi Fog | Viral on WhatsApp |" The description read: " The smog on Wednesday caused a pile-up on the Yamuna Expressway when speeding cars rammed into each other due to low visibility." Here is the link and archive link to the video Below is the screenshot of the video- The Desk then compared the two videos and found they were the same. Below is a comparison of the screenshots from the two videos: Subsequently, the Desk found another video from the official YouTube channel of Aaj Tak posted on Nov 8, 2017. The headline read: " Vehicles Collide on Yamuna Expressway Due to Dense Fog, Video Goes Viral." The description read: "Eighteen cars rammed into each other on the Agra-Noida Yamuna Expressway due to low visibility. Speeding cars rammed into one another while people on the footpath were shouting and requesting the drivers to slow down." Here is the link to the video , and below is the screenshot of the video: Continuing the investigation, the desk did a keyword search on 'Vehicles collide on Yamuna express highway'; we found a report by the India Today website with the same video on Nov 8, 2017. The headline read: "Watch: 18 cars collide on Yamuna highway due to Delhi-NCR's dangerous smog" Here is the link and screenshot of the article: In the later part of the investigation, the Desk searched Google with the keyword 'Yamuna Expressway accident Jan 2023' and found no report of any such incident on the expressway on the days the social media posts were shared. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2017 video of an accident was shared as recent with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of 2008 Miss India Universe riding rickshaw shared by social media users as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of a woman riding a rickshaw with an older man sitting as the passenger, claiming she was a police officer and the man, a rickshaw puller, was her father. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the woman was Miss India Universe 2008 Simran Kaur Mundi, and the older man was not her father. The photo was shared in the social media post with a false claim. Claim The Desk received a Facebook post on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91 - 8130503759 requesting to verify the claim in the photo shared in the post. The user shared a picture of a woman peddling a rickshaw with an older man sitting as a passenger behind her. The text in the Facebook post read: " ਬਾਪੂ ਨੇ ਰਿਕਸ਼ਾ ਚਲਾ ਕੇ ਕਮਾਏ ਪੈਸੇ ਨਾਲ ਆਪਣੀ ਧੀ ਨੂੰ ASI ਬਣਾਇਆ , ਸਲੂਟ ਹੈ ਇਸ ਬਾਪੂ ਦੀ ਸੋਚ ਨੂੰ. " (Father made his daughter ASI with the money earned by driving rickshaw. Salute to this father's thinking.) Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post published on Jan 4 and received more than 800 likes. Below is the screenshot of the post - While scanning Facebook, the Desk found another social media post sharing the same image and the claim. Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post, which more than 1200 users liked. One hundred thirty-six other users shared the post published on Jan 3, thinking it was real. Investigation While checking the photo carefully, the Desk noticed that the older man carried a placard on which the text read: "Follow Star Masons." Starting its investigation, we did a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found an Instagram post by Star Masons Entertainment on Jan 15, 2016. Here is the link and archive link of the post. Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk noticed that the post was reshared by someone named 'Simran Kaur Mundi.' Taking a cue from this, the Desk found her profile on Instagram and noticed that she had posted the same photo on Jan 15, 2016. The post read: "Aaja meri gaadi mein baith ja (Come, sit in my vehicle) and #FollowStarmasons #starmasons#badshah#bangalore @starmasons." Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the post - The Desk found that she posted the photo shared in a recent Facebook post to promote her production house Star Masons. The Desk subsequently conducted a Google search with relevant keywords related to Simran Kaur Mundi and Star Mason and found another Instagram post by her last week. She shared a screenshot of the viral Facebook post in post, calling it "#fakenews." The post read: "Please don't believe everything you read on Facebook and Instagram school! 114 comments, out of which the majority are congratulations. This is proof that people these days blindly believe anything and everything they read on Facebook/WhatsApp/Instagram school!! And this is apparently a "news portal" #FactCheck anyone? He is not my father and i am not ASI #fakenews". (Sic) Here is the link to the Instagram post and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a tweet from her official Twitter account sharing the same screenshot and refuting the claim made in the post. Here is the link to the tweet and below is its screenshot: Mundi's Instagram bio shows that she is an actor, Femina Miss India Universe 2008, and a sports presenter. We found her profile in an Indiatimes report , which confirmed she was crowned Miss India Universe in 2008. Below is the screenshot of the page- The Desk subsequently concluded that the 2016 photo of the actor was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 3-year-old photo of Deepika Padukone wearing saffron-colour shoes shared on social media as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a photo of Deepika Padukone wearing saffron-colour footwear claiming the Bollywood actor wore it to mock the people who protested against her wearing a saffron-colour bikini in one of the songs in Pathaan. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that it was a three-year-old photo and recently shared it on social media with a misleading claim. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +81-8130503759 a tweet containing the photo of Deepika Padukone wearing a blue-white striped pantsuit with saffron-colour shoes. "अब क्या होगा दीपिका भक्तो को जलाने से बाज नही आ रही है!! (What will happen now, Deepika is not desisting from making fun of the bhakts)," read the caption of the tweet, which came with the hashtags #DeepikaPadukone and #Orange. Here is the link to the tweet posted on Jan 4 which has received almost 1,000 views so far. The archive link to the post can be viewed here. Below is the screenshot of the tweet: The Desk came across another post on Facebook, which carried the same photo and claim. Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post, which was published on Jan 5 and reshared by 78 users. More than 1100 users liked the post guessing it was recent. Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the photo. The search results led to several media reports carrying the actor's picture, stating that it was from the Cannes Film Festival in 2019. A report by the Times of India, published on May 17, 2019, carried the same photo. The report's headline read: "Cannes 2019: Deepika Padukone's hottest looks". The article captioned Deepika's photo in a striped suit and saffron-colour shoes as 'Deepika Padukone stuns in a pantsuit on Day 2 at Cannes'. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page: The Indian Express also carried the same photo in its report published on May 21, 2019. The report's headline read: "Best photos of Deepika Padukone at Cannes 2019". Here is the link to The Indian Express report , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search for the keyword 'Deepika Padukone Cannes 2019 Striped Suit, ' which led us to an Instagram post by the actor's stylist Shaleena Nathani. Nathani posted the same photo on May 17, 2019, using #Cannes2019 as the hashtag. Here is the link to Nathani's Instagram post , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that the photo of Deepika Padukone wearing saffron-colour footwear was recently shared with a misleading claim. Pathaan has been making news and facing boycott calls after releasing its song Besharam Rang featuring Deepika Padukone and Shah Rukh Khan.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, person with Nirmala Sitharaman was not her father; Social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a video of Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman with an elderly man claiming she was with her father at her ancestral home. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the Dec 2022 video was of her visit to Kashi, and the person she met was the great-nephew of famous Tamil poet Mahakavi Bharathiyar. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a video shared by a Facebook user on Jan 10 claiming that the video showed the finance minister meeting her father at his "simple" home. The post read: "केन्द्रीय वित्तमन्त्री निर्मला सीतारमरण अपने पिताजी के साथ, कितनी सादगी, सरलता और संस्कार. निम्न मध्यम वर्ग जैसा रहन सहन, सरकारी बाबू, पटवारी, सिपाही, सरपंच भी इससे अधिक ठाठ बाट से रहते हैं. भ्रष्ट RTO, INCOME TAX OFFICERS, थानेदारों, तहसीलदारो के मकान लाखों करोड़ों के होते हैं - एक नहीं कई. धन्य हैं निर्मलाजी और उनके पिताश्री जो सादगी, ईमानदारी और हिन्दुत्व की मिसाल हैं. #sitaraman" (Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman with her father, so much simplicity, simplicity and culture. Living like lower middle class, Government Babu, Patwari, Constable, Sarpanch also live with more glamor than this. The houses of corrupt RTO, INCOME TAX OFFICERS, Thanedars, Tehsildars are worth lakhs of crores - not one but many. Blessed are Nirmalaji and her father who are an example of simplicity, honesty and Hindutva. #sitaraman (Sic) Here is the link to the Facebook post and its archive link . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: The desk found several other social media posts carrying the video with a similar claim. They can be viewed here , here , and here . The archive posts can be viewed here , here , and here . Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool and found a few keyframes of the video. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Facebook post with the same video posted on Dec 5, 2022. The caption of the post in Tamil read: " மகாகவி பாரதியாரின் பேரன் ஸ்ரீ K V கிருஷ்ணன் அவர்களிடம் நமது நிதி அமைச்சர் ஆசி பெற்ற பொழுது " The Desk used Google Translate to change the Tamil text to English. It read: "When our finance minister received blessings from Sri K V Krishnan, the family member of Mahakavi Bharathiyar." Here is the link to the post and archive link : Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk then compared the different frames of the videos and found that both were the same. Here is the combination of the screenshots of both videos- In the next step of its investigation, the Desk scanned the social media handles of Nirmala Sitharaman to check the details of the place he visited and who was the person she met during the visit. The Desk came across a Facebook post on the finance minister's official page published on Dec 3, 2022. The post read: "Siva Madam is the place where Mahakavi Bharathiyar stayed during his visit to Varanasi in the 1900s. #KashiTamilSangamam" Here is the link to the Facebook post , and below is its screenshot: We also found an Instagram post on her official account on Dec 4, 2022, with the caption: "Visited Siva Madam in Varanasi yesterday and interacted with the family members of Mahakavi Bharathiyar, including his 96-year-old great nephew Shri K. V. Krishnan. #KashiTamilSangamam". Here is the link for the Instagram post and below is its screenshot: Sitharaman's official Twitter handle shared the same video and photos after her visit to Kashi. Below is the screenshot of the video tweeted by Sitharaman: In a Customised Google search, the Desk found a Dec 2 press release by the Press Information Bureau, stating that the finance minister planned to visit key Tamil influence places in Varanasi, including Siva Madam, on December 3. Here is the link and screenshot of the press release: Who was Mahakavi Bharathiyar C. Subramaniya Bharathiyar, popularly known as Mahakavi Bharathiyar, was a poet, freedom fighter, and social reformer from Tamil Nadu. His songs on nationalism and freedom of India helped to rally the masses to support the Indian Independence Movement in Tamil Nadu. He was born on Dec 11, 1882, in Tamil Nadu. At the age of seven, he started writing poems in Tamil. In June 1897, Bharathi went to Kashi and stayed with his aunt Kuppammal and her husband, Krishna Sivan, for the next two years. His participation and activities in the Benaras Session (1905) and Surat Session (1907) of the Indian National Congress impressed many national leaders with his patriotic fervour. Bharathi died on September 11, 1921. (Source: PIB Release ) The Desk subsequently concluded that the elderly man in the video shared in social media posts was not Sitharaman's father. The video was shared in Facebook posts and tweets with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: YouTube video claiming 'Elon Musk bought Google' not authentic; 'Fictive entertainment' content by 'fan channel' sparked rumours over social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 12 (Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A YouTube video claiming Twitter CEO Elon Musk allegedly bought Google sparked rumours over social media where many users asked questions about its veracity. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video clip was created by a 'fan channel,' which makes content for 'fictive entertainment.' The claim in the YouTube video was purely baseless. Claim The Desk received a YouTube link on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91 - 8130503759 requesting to verify the 'Musk bought Google' claim in it. Here is the link and the archive link to the video, which was posted by a channel named 'Elon Musk Zone' on Jan 9 this year and received more than 6.5 lakh likes. Below is the screenshot of the video page- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a search on Twitter, and found two users asking questions if the claim was valid or true. The tweets can be seen here and here . Below is the screenshot of the tweets- Continuing the search, we tried advance Twitter search with the keyword 'Elon Musk bought Google' but didn't find anything on the result page. Below is the screenshot of the search result page- The Desk did a similar search in Google and couldn't find such reports on any authentic news website. Since there was no such report on Twitter and Google, the Desk scanned the profile page of the YouTube Channel which posted the video. We noticed that the channel named 'Elon Musk Zone' had a verified logo with over 970K subscribers. The Desk went through the 10:11-minute-long video and saw the footage's voiceover discussing "Google as the new game-changer" for Musk. The clip further alleged that Musk fans "seem to know his big next move" in the tech industry. But nowhere in the video, any authentic source was mentioned. The Desk subsequently went through the 'About' page to learn more about the channel. The description read: "The Official Elon Musk Zone YouTube Channel - The Elon Musk YouTube channel covering the latest Elon Musk news! We transform the original content from shows, podcasts, and keynotes with Mr. Elon Musk, to provide the viewers with a more immersive experience. We also make the messages of Elon Musk more accessible to people that are suffering from hearing disabilities by applying professional transcription to the majority of our videos. We amplify the content's original message by making it more cinematic and easier to understand by the end consumer. This way, we hope to reach more people and thus educate more people with Elon Musk's valuable messages. We only use third-party copyrighted content under Fair Use." We noticed a disclaimer was also mentioned just below the description. It read: "Disclaimer: This is a fan channel made for fictive entertainment, and not affiliated with Mr. Musk, SpaceX, Tesla, Neuralink, The Boring Company, Neuralink, NASA, Blue Origin, etc." Below is the screenshot of the 'About' page of the channel - It was concluded that the YouTube video, which eventually sparked rumour on social media that "Elon Musk bought Google", was an imaginary content without any verified source of information.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this woman is not India's first female railway porter; Social media posts shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user posted a photo of a woman porter claiming she was Sandhya Marawi, India's first woman porter, working on a railway station in Katni in Madhya Pradesh. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the name, photo, and details of the woman porter were correct in the tweet, but the claim that she was India's first female porter was incorrect. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of a woman porter claiming she was the first 'lady coolie' of India. The tweet posted on Jan 13 this year read: "31y old lady coolie Sandhya Marawi, badge No 36. Her husband died in 2016, so she took up her husband's job to feed her three kids & her mother-in-law! She works at Katni Railway Station in Jabalpur. She is the first Lady coolie." (Sic) The user tagged Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and the Prime Minister's Office in his post, using the hashtag #womenempowerment. Here is the link and the archive link to the post: Below is the screenshot of the tweet that has received more than 100 views. The Desk found another tweet with the same claim and photo posted on Jan 6 this year. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet, which garnered over 15000 views and 440 likes so far: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found three social media posts on Sandhya Marawi shared in 2020 and 2019, and even in 2018. The tweets and the Facebook post can be viewed here , here , and here . The archive link to the same posts can be seen here , here , and here . The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword 'Sandhya Marawi' and found a report by the Indiatimes website published on Mar 12, 2018. The report's headline read: "Meet Sandhya Marawi, India's 1st Woman Coolie Whose Breaking Stereotypes To Earn For Her Family". Here is the link and the archive link to the report. Below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk found another report by Dainik Bhaskar posted in 2017 which quoted Sandhya Marawi saying the she started working as a porter at Katni Junction in the year 2017 after her husband Bholaram Marawi passed away in October 2016. Here is the link to the report and below is the screenshot of the same: A customised search on Twitter led us to a tweet by Railway Ministry's official handle on March 4, 2020, which showed three women working as porters on different platforms. The tweet read: Working for Indian Railways, these lady coolies have proved that they are second to none! We salute them! Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post- Continuing the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword 'India's first woman coolie'. The search results led us to a report by The Economic Times published on May 18, 2018. The report's headline read: "Life of first woman coolie at Jaipur railway station." Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk found another report by The Indian Express, posted on May 28, 2018. The report's headline read: "Meet Manju Devi, the first woman porter of North-West Railways in Jaipur." According to the report, "Manju was the first woman for the entire North Western Railway region to take up the job of a "coolie" (porter)." She started working at the Jaipur railway station in 2013, it claimed. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: Another report by the Femina website, posted on Oct 9, 2019, reported Manju Devi being the first woman porter of North-West Railways and said she started working in 2013 as the sole breadwinner of her three children. The report's headline read: "Meet Manju Devi, the first woman porter at Jaipur railway station." Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a YouTube video by NDTV posted on Mar 20, 2013, reporting about Manju Devi. The video's headline read: "Manju, Rajasthan's first woman coolie (porter)." Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is the screenshot of the same: While it cannot be claimed that Manju Devi was India's first woman porter (coolie), but it was confirmed that she started working as a woman porter in 2013, way before Sandhya took up the job of porter in 2017. The Desk subsequently concluded that Sandhya Marawi could not be termed India's first woman porter. The social media posts were shared with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 5-year-old photo of Peru landslide shared as recent from Joshimath in social media posts
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (PTI Fact Check): A Facebook user shared a picture of a landslide in a mountainous area claiming the photo was from Uttarakhand's Joshimath, which has been affected by severe land subsidence recently. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo shared in the Facebook post was dated back to March 2018 from a landslide in the Cusco region of Peru. The satellite images and photos from the Joshimath region have indicated that the town is at risk of collapse due to cracks in hundreds of houses, hotels, and roads due to severe land subsidence. Social media users have shared many photos from the region, and a few of those images are found to be unrelated to Joshimath. Claim A Facebook user shared an image of cracks in land in a hilly area, claiming it to be from Uttarakhand's Joshimath. The text in the image read: "600 families of Uttarakhand's sinking Joshimath to be shifted to safer locations, plea in SC to declare it 'national disaster.' Construction works around hills halted, PMO takes charge." Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post : Below is the screenshot of the photo shared in the Facebook post: Another Facebook user shared the same photo and captioned: "Save Joshimath." Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post : Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the photo, which led it to an article posted by Smithsonian Magazine on September 4, 2018. The article's headline, which included the same photo as its thumb image, read: "New Software Can Predict Landslides Weeks Before They Happen." The photo caption read, "A landslide in the Cusco region of Peru destroyed more than 100 houses in March 2018". Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search for the image with the keyword 'Cusco Peru landslide,' led the Desk to a tweet in the Spanish language by the official handle of the Ministry of Defence of Peru posted on Mar 16, 2018. The English translation of the text read: "Minister of Defense Jorge Kisic, together with the regional governor of Cusco, @EdwinLiconaGRC, carries out an inspection overflight in the area affected by landslides in the district of Cusco, Cusco. (Sic)" Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a report by Daily Star published on Mar 5, 2018. The article's headline read: "Huge cracks devastate a community and destroy buildings as families forced to FLEE." The Desk noticed that the photo, which was shared in the name of Joshimath in recent social media posts, was one of the images in the Daily Star report published in 2018. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: Below is the combined image of both photos - the one found in the 2018 report and the other shared in recent social media posts- Evidently, the photo shared in the Facebook post was an old one from Peru. The Facebook post had three other claims as well: 1. 600 families of Uttarakhand's sinking Joshimath to be shifted to safer locations 2. Plea in SC to declare it a 'national disaster.' 3. Construction works around the hills halted, PMO takes charge The Desk subsequently started investigating the first claim with a Google search using the keyword '600 families shifted to safer places, Joshimath' and found a PTI report published by The Economic Times on Jan 6 this year. The report's headline read: "Dhami orders immediate evacuation of 600 families in Joshimath". Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: The first claim with the photo in the Facebook post was valid. We did another Google search with the keywords 'plea in SC to declare Joshimath national disaster' and found a report by The Indian Express published on Jan 11, 2023. The report's headline read: "Joshimath crisis: No urgent hearing, Supreme Court lists case for January 16". "Almost a week after cracks appeared on many roads and in hundreds of houses in Uttarakhand's Joshimath, authorities on Sunday declared it a landslide and subsidence-hit zone. The plea by Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati urged the court to declare the situation in Joshimath a national disaster and direct the National Disaster Management Authority to aid and assist the residents," read a section of The Indian Express article. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: On Jan 11, the Supreme Court agreed to examine a plea on January 16, seeking its intervention to declare the crisis in Uttarakhand's Joshimath as a national disaster. The second claim in the post was also found to be correct information. Investigating the third claim, the Desk did another Google search with the keyword 'construction work halted in Joshimath.' The search results led us to a report by Live Mint with the headline: "Joshimath: Uttarakhand government halts all construction projects." Here is the link to the article , posted on Jan 7, 2023, and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk came across another report by the Times of India published on Jan 8, 2023. The report's headline read: "PMO holds high-level meet on Joshimath subsidence: Key Points." Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that while the claims in the Facebook post were accurate, the image was of a landslide in Peru in 2018.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited photo of Rahul Gandhi and meme on entrepreneur Vineeta Singh shared as real on social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi having food with a 'plate of chicken' and a 'glass of alcohol' on his table. Another user shared a photo of Sugar Cosmetics CEO Vineeta Singh claiming she played the role of mother in a Bollywood movie, '3 Idiots'. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that Rahul Gandhi's photo was edited and shared with a false claim. Similarly, the claim in the social media post shared with Vineeta Singh's photo was incorrect, as an actress named Amardeep Jha played the mother's role in the movie '3 Idiots'. Claim 1 A Facebook user shared a photo of Rahul Gandhi with a 'glass of alcohol' and a 'plate of chicken' on his table at a Dhaba or restaurant. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post: Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Investigation While a first look at the photo indicated that it was altered, the Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image search and found that several other Facebook users shared the same photo with the same claim. The Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archive posts can be viewed here , here and here . The Desk did an advance search on Twitter and found a tweet by journalist and documentary filmmaker Paranjoy Guha Thakurta posted on Jan 7, 2023. Guha posted the same photo, saying he met Rahul Gandhi at a Dhaba near Karnal in Haryana while traveling to Punjab. The tweet read: "It was a sheer coincidence: traveling to Punjab this morning, I crossed the Bharat Jodo Yatra. With some difficulty and a scuffle, I was able to meet Rahul Gandhi while he was eating at a Dhaba a few km from Karnal. We discussed politics, economics and India's richest men." (Sic) Here is the link to the tweet and below is the screenshot of the same: In the photo, Rahul could be seen with a glass of tea/coffee and plates of dry fruits on his table. The Desk compared the two photos - one shared on social media, and the other tweeted by Guha - and found the first picture was edited to replace the glass of tea/coffee with a 'glass of alcohol.' Similarly, one of the dry-fruit plates was changed to a 'plate of chicken' on his table in the edited photo. Below is the combined image of the screenshot of the original and the edited photos: In the subsequent investigation, the Desk contacted Guha, who confirmed that he clicked the photo at Dhaba near Karnal when he met the Congress leader on Jan 7. We also reviewed the comments on Guha's tweet and noticed a user asking the journalist if he shot the photo. Guha replied to the comment by saying "indeed." Here is a link to the comment and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, a Google search with the keyword 'Rahul Gandhi, Bharat Jodo Yatra, Karnal' led us to a 1:17-minute video published by News 24's YouTube channel on Jan 7. The video headline read: "पहले किया नाश्ता फिर देखा मैच, Bharat Jodo Yatra से सामने आईं Rahul Gandhi की अनदेखी तस्वीरें ।" (First had breakfast, then watched the match, unseen pictures of Rahul Gandhi from Bharat Jodo Yatra) The video shows Rahul Gandhi with a glass of tea/coffee and dry-fruit plates. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is the screenshot of the page: Claim 2 An Instagram user shared a photo of Sugar Cosmetics CEO Vineeta Singh with the actor who played the mother of a character named Raju in a superhit movie, 3 Idiots. The post read: "CEO of Sugar Cosmetics, Vineeta Singh, didn't feel ashamed or nervous and proudly played the role of a poor mother in 3 Idiots #Respect." Here is the link and the archive link to the Instagram post: Below is the screenshot of the Instagram post posted on Jan 9, which has so far garnered over 6,600 likes: Investigation The Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image search on the photo and found multiple social media users shared the same photo with the same claim. The posts can be seen here , here and here . The archive links to the posts can be viewed here , here , and here . The Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword 'Raju's mother in 3 Idiots' and found the list of actors and actresses who worked in the film on the IMDb website. IMDb is an online database platform that provides information related to video content released globally. On the website, the name Amardeep Jha was mentioned as the actress who played the role of the mother of the lead character Raju Rastogi in the 2009 film. Here is the link to the IMDb page on Amardeep Jha and below is the screenshot of the same: Continuing the search, the Desk found a video in March 2022 tweet by Vineeta Singh responding to the memes in which she was shown as Amardeep Jha, who played the role of mother in '3 Idiots'. "All is not well! Stop with the photoshopping, Team @trySUGAR," read the tweet posted on Mar 12, 2022, which has garnered over 182K views and 2500 likes. Here is the link to the tweet and below is the screenshot of the same:

title: PTI Fact Check: 11-year-old airplane accident photo shared in name of Pokhara plane crash by social media users, news portals
content: New Delhi, Jan 15 (Amisha Airen, Abhinav Gupta, Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a photo of an airplane accident, claiming it was of the Pokhara plane crash that happened on Jan 15. At least 68 people were killed after a 72-seat passenger aircraft belonging to Yeti Airlines crashed upon landing at Pokhara International Airport on Jan 15. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo was of an 11-year-old airplane crash that happened in Kathmandu in September 2012. Social media users, a news agency, and several news websites carried the 11-year-old picture in their posts and reports related to Jan 15 Pokhara plane crash incident. Claim The Desk received a tweet on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 a photo of a plane crash requesting to verify the claim that it was of the Jan 15 plane crash in Kathmandu. The tweet read: "72 passengers were on board. Plane crash at Pokhra International Airport. Prayers for Nepal crash. #Nepal #NepalPlaneCrash". (Sic). Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post- Another user shared the same photo in its tweet on the plane crash incident on Jan 15. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Investigation The Desk started the investigation by doing Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found the same photo shared in a tweet by news agency ANI on Jan 15. The tweet read: "Passenger aircraft crashes on the runway of Pokhara Airport in Nepal. #Nepal #PokharaAirport #Runway #planecrash" (Sic). The tweet also carried the story link of its report. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the image- The search results led us to reports by several news websites, which carried the same photo in their reports on the Pokhara plane crash after ANI posted the image in its tweet. 1. A Facebook post by India TV News was posted on Jan 15, 2023. The post read: "नेपाल विमान हादसे में अबतक 36 लोगों की मौत.. तकनीकी खराबी की वजह से हादसा #Nepal #PlaneCrash #YetiAirlines #Kathmandu #Pokhara" (So far 36 people have died in Nepal plane crash.. Accident due to technical fault #Nepal #PlaneCrash #YetiAirlines #Kathmandu #Pokhara). Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post : Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post by India TV News: 2. Continuing its search, it found another social media post by DNA India, carrying the same photo while reporting the plane crash on Jan 15, 2023. "A flight in Nepal has crashed in a fiery explosion, and the 72 people on board are currently feared dead. Kathmandu-bound plane flying out from Pokhara crashed on the runway of the Pokhara International Airport in Nepal," the tweet read. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post by DNA India: Below is the screenshot of the tweet: 3. Navbharat also carried the same photo to report Pokhara's plane crash, giving ANI the image credit. Here are the links to the article and its archive post . Below is the screenshot of the page: 4. The thumbnail of a video posted by JagranTV also used the same image in its report on the plane crash. Here is the link and the archive link to the video. Below is the screenshot of the page: The Desk conducted a customised search in Google to check if the same photo was ever used in any report before the Pokhara plane crash on Jan 15. On the result page, the Desk found the same photo used in a report by International Business Times on a plane crash in February 2014 in Nepal. "Wreckage of Lost Nepal Plane Found, 18 Onboard Killed in Crash," read the article's headline on Feb 17, 2014. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that IBT had reported a plane crash that took place near Maine hill in the village of Dhikura in Nepal on Feb 16, 2014. The passenger plane carried 18 people; all were reported dead in the incident. The Desk also noticed that the report gave the photo credit to Reuters while captioning it as 'Representational Image.' Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another search for the photo, along with the keyword 'Reuters.' The search results led us to an article by Alamy, a website for stock photos. The article mentioned the photo contributors as 'Reuters/Alamy Photo Stock' and said it initially clicked on September 28, 2012. It also mentioned the name of the photographer - Navesh Chitrakar. The Desk next found the link to a Reuters report, which was posted on Sep 28, 2012. The report's headline, a slideshow with 15 photos, read: "Nepal air crash." The same photo, as carried by the news agency and other news websites, was captioned: "A Nepalese police officer stands in front of the wreckage of a Dornier aircraft, owned by private firm Sita Air, at the crash site in Kathmandu September 28, 2012. REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar". Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: A Google search for the keyword 'September 2012 plane crash in Nepal' led the Desk to a report by The Guardian. The headline of the article, published in 2012, read: "Plane carrying Britons crashes in Nepal, killing 19". Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo used by ANI and other news websites to report about the Pokhara plane crash in Nepal dated back to September 2012 and was of another plane crash in Nepal.

title: PTI Fact Check: Concept video of 'Artificial womb facility' taken out of context, shared as real by social media users
content: New Delhi, Jan 12 (Amisha Airen, Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of an artificial womb facility, claiming it allows infertile couples to conceive a baby and even choose its characteristics from a wide range of the available menu. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the 30-second clip shared on Twitter was a part of an extended version, a mere visual representation of a concept that doesn't exist. Hashem Al-Ghaili, the biotechnologist who shared the concept video, confirmed to the Desk that the technology depicted in the clip was just a concept. He also said that the video was taken out of context and was shared as real by some social media users. Claim While scanning the social media platforms, the Desk found a 30-second video shared in a tweet on Dec 24 last year. The tweet received 4449 likes and was viewed 688.3k times by other users. The tweet read: "I said years ago that science would soon produce humans; now we have artificial wombs. While there could be some medical, ethical, and governmental issues surrounding this innovation, I think it will help address complications before, during, n after childbirth; what do you think?" (Sic) The voiceover in the video said: "Introducing EctoLife, World's first artificial womb facility powered entirely by renewable energy. EctoLife allows the infertile couple to conceive a baby and become true biological parents of their own offspring. It's a perfect solution for women who had their uterus surgically removed due to cancer or other complications." Here is the link and archive link of the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet: While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found several Facebook users sharing the same video claiming that the 'artificial womb facility' allows couples to choose what characteristics their child will imbibe. Social media users from India, Australia, Bangladesh, and Nigeria, shared the same video and claim in their Facebook posts over the last few months. The links to the seven such posts can be found here , here , here , here , here , here and here . The archive links to the seven post can be viewed here , here , here , here , here , here and here . Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the links shared above: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search to find a few keyframes of the video. A separate Google Reverse Image Search on each of the six keyframes led the Desk to multiple such reports. On the search result page, the Desk noticed a YouTube video by Berlin-based science communicator and video producer Hashim Al-Ghaili on December 9, 2022. The video title read: "EctoLife: The World's First Artificial Womb Facility." The video's description read: "The world's first artificial womb facility, EctoLife, will be able to grow 30,000 babies a year. It's based on over 50 years of ground-breaking scientific research conducted by researchers worldwide." Below is the link and archive link of the video Below is the screenshot of the video: The Desk noticed that Hashim Al-Ghaili, who published the video on YouTube, has a verified channel with over 500K subscribers. The 8:39-minute video, posted on Dec 9 last year, has garnered over 18 lakh views. In the next step of its investigation, the Desk went through the video, which started with a voiceover as: "Introducing Ectolife, the world's first artificial womb facility powered entirely by renewable energy." It continued to explain that Ectolife allows "infertile parents to conceive a baby and become true biological parents of the baby." While watching the video, the Desk noticed that at 7:54 minutes, the voiceover stated that " biotechnologist and science communicator Hashem Al-Ghaili designed the concept of EctoLife facility." At 8:25 minutes, the video showed the text: "Concept By Hashim Al-Ghaili"." The Desk subsequently went through the 'About' page to learn more about the channel. The description read: "This channel is managed by Hashem Al-Ghaili and aims to share video content about science and technology, some of which are self-produced. I hope you enjoy what I share here." To check the veracity of the claims in the video, the Desk reached out to Hashim Al-Ghaili, sending a mail and asking about the details of the video he posted on its YouTube channel. Hashim Al-Ghaili replied to the mail and said: "I created the video myself. The technology depicted in the video doesn't exist yet. This is just a concept at the moment." "EctoLife is a concept designed to showcase how far reproductive technology has come. The main goal of creating the video was to ignite the discussion about emerging technology and to highlight scientific progress in the field of ectogenesis", he added. "I did my best to alert the audience that this is a concept and not a real-life company. The facility doesn't exist right now", Hashim added. The Desk reached out to Dr. Nisha Bhatnagar, medical director of Aveya Fertility, for her comment on the video shared on social media. She said: "It is just a concept. It is a theoretical thing." "As of now, we can grow the embryos in the lab till Day 5 only. Beyond Day 5, we don't have any capacity to grow the embryos in the lab. After Day 5, the outer shell ruptures, which we call hatching, and once it opens up, it needs a uterus to implant - a maternal uterus, not an artificial one," she added. The Desk subsequently concluded that the video shared in social media posts was a mere representation of a concept that doesn't exist yet.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scribbled banknotes not declared invalid by RBI; Social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a post claiming a new guideline by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has declared that all scribbled banknotes will become invalid. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the RBI never issued such guidelines, as mentioned in the Facebook post. The claim in the social media post was false. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp no. +918130503759 a Facebook post with a screenshot claiming that writing anything on banknotes will make them invalid under the new guidelines of the RBI. "As per new guidelines of the Reserve Bank of India, writing anything on new notes makes the note, and it will no more be legal tender. Just like US dollars. If you write anything in US dollars, it is not accepted by anyone. Just forward to the maximum people so that the Indian public understands the importance of this message:" the post read. Here is the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the page- Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the screenshot and found several Facebook posts dating back to 2016. A few Facebook posts with the same screenshot can be viewed here and here . The archive posts can be viewed here and here . In the next step of its investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search for the keyword 'Scribbled banknotes invalid RBI' but could not find any such reports on news portals. Had the RBI made any such announcement, it would have been reported by a news website. The Desk subsequently scanned RBI's website but couldn't find such guidelines or press releases. However, we found a press release on its website published on Dec 5, 2002, with the headline, 'Clean Note Policy: RBI.' According to the press release, the RBI, under its 'Clean Note Policy,' aims to give the citizens good quality currency notes and coins while the soiled notes are withdrawn from circulation. "The public members were urged not to write on the currency notes, and banks were instructed to provide unrestricted facility for exchange of soiled and mutilated notes," the press release said. Here is the link to the RBI press release , and below is the screenshot of the same: Under its ' Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) ' section on the website, the Desk found RBI's answer to a few banknote-related questions. Below are the questions and answers as highlighted on the RBI website- Q. What is the Clean Note Policy? Answer: Reserve Bank of India has been continuously making efforts to make good quality banknotes available to the members of the public. To help RBI and the banking system towards this objective, the members of the public are requested to ensure the following: * Not to staple the banknotes * Not to write/put rubber stamp or any other mark on the banknotes * Not to use banknotes for making garlands/toys, decorating pandals and places of worship, or showering on personalities in social events, etc. Q. Are coloured/stained notes or scribbled notes legal tender? Answer: All Bank notes, including Mahatma Gandhi (New) series notes with writing or colour stains on them, continue to be legal tender, provided they are decipherable. Such notes can be deposited or exchanged in any bank branch. However, a claim in respect of bank notes which carries any extrinsic words or visible representations intended to convey or capable of conveying any message of a political or religious character or furthering the interest of any person or entity will be rejected as per Reserve Bank of India (Note Refund) Rules, 2009 [As amended by Reserve Bank of India (Note Refund) Amendment Rules, 2018] . Here is the screenshot of the FAQs page on the RBI website: We also found a PTI report carried by the Economic Times on Aug 14, 2013, according to which the RBI had back then asked banks to issue suitable instructions to all officers and staff not to scribble or write on banknotes. Here is the link to the report and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the RBI never made any announcement on making scribbled banknotes invalid. The claim in the social media post was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, bodybuilder losing cool, kicking prize not from India; Social media user shared Bangladesh video with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A video of an angry bodybuilder, said to be an Indian, kicking his prize at an award ceremony was shared on social media, claiming he protested against alleged caste discrimination despite being the winner at the event. The PTI Fact Check team found in its investigation that the bodybuilder, identified as Jahid Hasan Shuvo from Bangladesh, was angry with the jury's decision not to declare him the winner and was given a blender machine as the runner-up prize. The claim in the video shared on social media was false. Claim The Desk received a Facebook post on its Fact Check on WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 requesting to verify the claim in the video. The Facebook post, published on Jan 5 this year, claimed that a bodybuilder allegedly belonging to a backward community was asked to stand at a corner on the stage despite being the winner at the event. The angry bodybuilder kicked his prize to protest against the discrimination he faced at the award ceremony. The post read: "शाबाश मेरे शेर यूं ही इन #जातिवादी मानसिकता पर लात मारते रहो 1 दिन हम जातिवादी परंपरा को तोड़कर रहेंगे| Sc #कास्ट से संबंधित (बॉडी बिल्डर) को विजेता होने पर भी स्टेज के कोने पर खड़ा करने की कोशिश पर उसके द्वारा दिया करारा जवाब. यह तुमने (मिक्सर जूसर) नहीं तोड़ा है, उनके घमंड को भी तोड़ दिया है" (Well done my lion, just keep kicking these #casteist mentality, one day we will break the caste tradition. Befitting reply given by him for trying to make a bodybuilder belonging to SC community stand in the corner of the stage despite being the winner. You have not broken this (mixer juicer), you have also broken their ego). the tweet read. Here is the link to and the archive link to the Facebook post. Below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video for the details and keyframes and conducted a Google Reverse Image search on one of them to find the extended video version on a Facebook account that belonged to a user named Jahid Hasan Shuvo. The Desk scanned the user's profile and found him to be a bodybuilder from Bangladesh, and he posted the original 1:39-minute video on his own Facebook page. Here is the link to the video he posted on his Facebook page on Dec 23 last year. Below is the screenshot of the video, which garnered 11 million views, 422k likes, and 31k comments till date. The Facebook profile page of the user, which has 275k followers, suggested it was him in the video shared with the 'caste discrimination' claim on social media. Below is the screenshot of his Facebook profile page: Below is the combined image of the screenshot of the video shared recently and the one shared by the bodybuilder from Bangladesh: To investigate why the bodybuilder was angry and kicked his prize in front of people on the stage, the Desk did a Google search with the keyword "Jahid Hasan Suvo kicked prize Bangladesh." The search results led us to a report by the Dhaka Tribune published on Dec 26 last year with the headline, "Bodybuilder Jahid gets lifetime ban for bizarre protest." The report read: "Bodybuilder Jahid Hasan Shuvo protested in an awkward way against alleged biasedness of the Bangladesh Bodybuilding Federation, kicking away from the stage one of his second-best prizes - a blender machine - in front of everyone at a national competition Friday. Within two days, the federation's executive committee slapped a lifetime suspension on the former champion for the unruly behavior. Defending his action, Jahid said it was a reaction against the corruption of the organizers, but he also apologized for how he did so, while the federation was in no position to tolerate it as they hoped that the exemplary ban would bring discipline in the game." Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page- To continue the investigation, the Desk contacted Shahed Siddique, Head of Input, Independent television in Bangladesh, to confirm the information in the Dhaka Tribune report. Siddique told PTI: "Yes, the Dhaka Tribune has correctly detailed the incident in its report. Jahid reacted because he was unhappy with the judges' decision to declare him the runner-up at the event. He was not happy with the prize also." The Desk subsequently concluded that the video was from Bangladesh and thas no caste discrimination angle.

title: PTI Fact Check: Taiwan's video of 3-yr-old girl swept into air by kite shared on social media as recent from Ahmedabad
content: New Delhi, Jan 18 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a kid carried away by a kite, claiming that the incident occurred recently in Ahmedabad. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that it was an August 2020 video from a kite festival in Taiwan. The claim in the video shared on social media was false. Claim While scanning social media platforms, the Desk found a Facebook post with a 51-second video of a 3-year-old swept away in the air by a kite claiming the incident happened in Ahmedabad recently. The post read: "Three-year-old girl flew away with the kite in Ahmedabad. Thank God she has come down safely. Very scary." Here is the link and the archive link to the video, which showed the little girl being lifted away with a kite and landing safely after remaining stuck in the flying kite for over 40 seconds. Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: While scanning Facebook for similar posts, the Desk found another post with the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link of the post Below is the screenshot of the post - Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool and found a few keyframes of the video. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to an article carrying the same video by Ladepeche.fr posted in French on Aug 30, 2020. The Desk translated the page into English. The headline read: " VIDEO. A 3-year-old girl soars, carried through the air by a kite in Taiwan."
