Here is the link to the article and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk then compared the different frames of the videos and found that both were the same. Here is the combination of the screenshots of both videos- In the next step of its investigation, the Desk did a keyword search on "Girl flies air with a kite in Taiwan," which led it to an article by AP news with the same video published in the same year. The headline read: " 3-year-old girl safe after being lifted by the kite in Taiwan" Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the article We also found another report by CNN about the same incident with the same video. Here are the links to the news report and the video included in it: The Desk subsequently concluded that the video of a girl lifted by a kite was not from Ahmedabad. The video dated back to August 2020 from Taiwan Kite Festival and was shared in recent Facebook posts with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old airplane accident videos from Afghanistan, Russia shared in name of Jan 15 Nepal plane crash on social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a couple of airplane accident videos claiming they showed how the Yeti Airlines flight crashed minutes before landing in Pokhara in Nepal on Jan 15. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that both videos were old and related to separate airplane accidents in Russia and Afghanistan in 2021 and 2013, respectively. The claims with the videos shared in social media posts were false. Claim 1 A Twitter user shared a video of a plane crashing before a moving car and going up in flames. The user claimed the footage was of the passenger plane crash in Pokhara on Jan 15. The tweet read: "Pokhara Nepal Plane Crash – "#नेपाल के #पोखरा में प्लेन क्रैश कुल 72 लोग सवार थे 16 से ज़्यादा शव बरामद (Pokhara Nepal Plane Crash Plane crash in Pokhara, Nepal A total of 72 people were on board, more than 16 bodies recovered)". Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet: Below is the screenshot of the tweet, posted on Jan 15, which so far garnered over 998K views, 2011 likes, and 730 retweets: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video clip to get a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to two more Twitter posts in which the same video was shared, claiming to be of the Pokhara incident. The tweets can be viewed here and here . Their respective archive posts can be viewed here and here . Shrikant Tyagi, a self-proclaimed politician, also shared the video while condoling the demise of those killed in the Pokhara plane crash. "पोखरा, नेपाल में हुई विमान दुर्घटना में कई यात्रियों के हताहत होने का अत्यंत दुःखद समाचार प्राप्त हुआ है।हादसे में मरने वाले चार भारतीय गाजीपुर के रहने वाले हैं। शोकाकुल परिजनों के प्रति गहरी संवेदना, ईश्वर पुण्यात्माओं को अपने श्री चरणों में स्थान दें।। ॐ शांति #NepalPlaneCrash," the tweet in Hindi read. The English translation of the tweet read: "Received this unfortunate news about the casualties in the plane crash in Pokhara, Nepal. The four Indians who died in the accident are residents of Ghazipur. Deepest condolences to the bereaved family members. May God give place to the pious souls in his holy feet. Om Shanti #NepalPlaneCrash." Here is the link to the tweet and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: The search results also led us to a report by The Guardian published on May 1, 2013, which carried a more extended version of the video clip shared on Twitter. The headline read: "747 cargo plane crashed at Bagram airbase – video," The dateline mentioned 'Afghanistan.' The caption of the video article read: "Footage purports to show the moment a Boeing 747 US cargo plane crashes on its ascent from Bagram airbase, Afghanistan on Monday. The crash resulted in the death of all seven American crew members. The exact cause of the crash is unknown, although there were thunderstorms in the area. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash". Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk compared the visuals of the two videos – one posted on Twitter and the other posted by The Guardian report – and found them to be exact. Here is a comparison of the two videos: The Desk also found a YouTube video posted by CNN on May 3, 2013, with the headline: "Viral video provides clues to 747 crash". The video included the same visuals of the plane crash as the clip shared in Twitter posts. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Dubai-bound Boeing 747-400 plane crashed just after take-off from Bagram airbase on 29 April 2013, killing six crew members. It was operated by National Air Cargo Group Inc and carried 207 tonnes of cargo, including five MRAPs, weighing between 12 and 18 tonnes each. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 10-year-old video of an airplane accident in Afghanistan was shared recently in Twitter posts claiming it was related to the Pokhara plane crash incident in Nepal. Claim 2 A Twitter user shared a 1:15-minute video of a plane accident and claimed it was related to the Pokhara airplane crash in Nepal on Jan 15. The tweet has garnered over 1.5 million views and over 3000 likes. The tweet read: "Nepal plane crash near #PokharaAirport caught on camera from ground, these visuals show the plane engine caught fire, which may have been a bird hit after which it just went down tilted." Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video to get some keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to several social media posts with the same video, claiming they were of the Pokhara plane crash incident. The posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here . Continuing its search, the Desk also found a YouTube video posted by India Today on Aug 17, 2021, the same as on social media. The headline of the YouTube video read: "Ilyushin Il-112V: Russian military transport aircraft crashes outside Moscow| NewsMo". Here is the link to the video , and below is the screenshot of the same: The video's description read: "A prototype military transport plane crashed while performing a test flight outside Moscow. Three people were aboard the plane and were feared dead. Watch the terrifying video." In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search for the keyword "Russian military aircraft crashed in Moscow, Aug 2021". The search results led us to a Twitter post by a user named 'Aeronews,' which reshared the same plane crash video posted by another Twitter handle named 'baza' on the same date. The tweet read: "An Il-112 military transport plane crashed in the Moscow region. There were three people on-board". Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the same. Below is a comparison of visuals from the two videos – one shared on social media and the other posted on Twitter in Aug 2021 – showing they are the same. A separate Google search for a specific set of keywords led the Desk to a report published by Reuters on Aug 17, 2021. The report's headline read: "Prototype military transport aircraft crashes in Russia." Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: A Google search for a combination of keywords "Ilyushin il-112v, Russia, plane crash" led us to a video uploaded on the official YouTube channel of CNN News18, posted on Aug 17, 2021. This was a shorter clip of the video shared on social media recently. The headline of the YouTube video read: "Military Plane Crashed In Moscow | Viral Video | Most Recent Plane Crash 2021 | CNN News18 Life". Here is the link to the video , and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claimed to be of the plane crash incident in Nepal's Pokhara was of an airplane accident in Moscow that took place in August 2021. The video was recently shared in social media posts with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Yorkshire cricketer Hedley Verity morphed to make it look like Swami Vivekananda and shared as WhatsApp forward
content: New Delhi, Jan 19 (PTI Fact Check): A user shared a photo of a bowler claiming to be Swami Vivekananda when playing cricket for Calcutta Town Club in 1884. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo was morphed and shared with a false claim. The original phot was of English cricketer Hedley Verity. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +81-8130503759 a black-and-white photo of a bowler requesting to verify the claim that it was a rare photograph of Swami Vivekananda playing cricket at Eden Gardens in 1884. The text with the black-and-white photo read: "A scarce photograph. In 1884, Eden Gardens, Calcutta, Narendra Nath Dutta (later became Swami Vivekananda) bowling for Calcutta town." Below is the photo shared with the fact-check request: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the photo. The search results led the Desk to a tweet posted in Nov 2021 with the same image and a similar claim: The tweet read: "This is one of the rarest pics in my possession... Year: 1884 Venue: Eden Gardens. While playing for Calcutta Town Club, the one seen bowling here in the pic is Narendra Nath Dutta, popularly known as Swami Vivekananda... #Collected Seen or unseen?" (Sic) Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet and below is its screenshot: Continuing its search with specific keywords, the Desk found a photo of the bowler with a different face on the Getty Images website stating he was cricketer Hedley Verity. The caption of the photo read: "Hedley Verity Yorkshire cricketer Hedley Verity (1905 - 1943) in action, circa 1940. (Photo by Hulton Archive/Getty Images)". Here is the link to the Getty Images' webpage , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk compared the two photos – one shared for verification and the other posted by Getty Images – and found that the former was photoshopped by adding Swami Vivekananda's face. Below is a comparison of the two photos: The Desk also found an article by ESPN Cricinfo entailing the journey of Hedley Verity. The report carried the same photo along with the caption: "Hedley Verity: one of England's greatest slow bowlers and a fine gentleman to boot," giving photo credit to Getty Images. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: A separate article by ESPN Cricinfo, published in March 2014, suggested that the photo was clicked in July 1932 when Verity delivered the best bowling figures in first-class cricket history, bagging all ten wickets in an inning against Nottinghamshire. Here is a link to the article , and below is its screenshot: On clicking the hyperlink provided in the article, the Desk found that the match between Yorkshire and Nottinghamshire was from the 1932 County Championship. The three-day game (played on July 9, 11, and 12 of 1932) was played at Headingley, Leeds, and was won by Yorkshire by ten wickets. The Desk then moved on to the next step of investigation to get details about Swami Vivekananda's interest in cricket and whether there was any available record. We conducted a Google search with the keyword "Swami Vivekananda, cricket, Eden Gardens." We found a report by The New Indian Express with the headline, 'When Swami Vivekananda claimed seven wickets and other Eden Gardens tales.' "While not much more is known about the multifaceted monk's dalliance with bat and ball, it is documented that he was a member of Town Club and an ardent participant in physical activities. He played football and encouraged friends to exercise," read a portion of the article. Here is the link to the TNIE article , and below is the screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the TNIE report, the Desk searched the book and found its limited online edition on Google Books website. Author Raju Mukherji wrote about the early days of Swami Vivekananda and his passion for cricket in the second and third paragraphs on page no. 75 in his book. The paragraphs can be seen in the screenshot of page no. Seventy-five of the book below- The contents of the book can be found here . Below is the front page of the book- When PTI's Supratik Sengupta reached out to the Rama Krishna Math and Mission in Kolkata to verify the claim as shared in the social media post about Swami Vivekananda, the Belur Headquarters spokesperson said they don't have any such proven record in their possession. "It is a wrong information. We don't have any such information in our records, in our archives. So far our knowledge goes it is inaccurate," he told PTI when contacted. The Desk subsequently concluded that the photo shared in the WhatsApp forward was morphed. The original image dating back to 1932 was of Hedley Verity, an English cricketer. And the claim about Swami Vivekananda's interests in cricket and him playing matches at the Eden Gardens and taking wickets in 1884 could not be established as verified by the Rama Krishna Math. It's mentioned in a book written by Raju Mukkherji, but the RK Mission and Math said it was not aware of any such details about him.

title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video of ice rods coming out from waterpipe not from Rajasthan; False claim shared on social media | Details Inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 20 (Pratyush Ranjan / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of ice coming out of a waterpipe, claiming it was from the Shekhawati region in Rajasthan. The PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the video was at least four years old. Multiple social media users and news websites shared the same video, linking it to different places in India, Pakistan, and Nigeria over the past four years. The claim in the video shared in social media posts that the video was from Rajasthan is false. Claim A Facebook user shared a video of ice cubes coming out of a water pipe, claiming the cold wave led to freezing water in an irrigation water pipe in the Shekhawati region in Rajasthan. The Facebook post read: "देख के रह जाओगे दंग राजस्थान के शेखावाटी क्षेत्र में हाड़ कंपा देने वाली सर्दी।सिंचाई के पाइप में जमी बर्फ...!! (You will be stunned to see the bone-chilling cold in the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan. Snow frozen in the irrigation pipe...!!),". Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post, which was posted on Jan 15 and garnered 4800 views. Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to another Facebook video claiming the footage was from the Marwar region in Rajasthan. The Desk found the same video published by multiple websites, and social media users on different dates between Dec 31, 2018, to Jan 18, 2023. Jan 18, 2023 A recent report using the same video was published by the Maharashtra Times regarding cold weather in Maharashtra. However, the information didn't say it was Maharashtra's video. Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot. Jan 17, 2023 The Twitter handle of Gaon Connection posted a video on the impact of cold waves in Rajasthan and used the same footage in its report at the beginning and in the middle of the report. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the page- The extended version of the same video report was also published on its YouTube channel on the same day. Jan 15, 2023 A Facebook user shared the same video claiming the video was from Rajasthan. Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post . Below is the screenshot of the Facebook post: Jan 3, 2020 A Twitter user shared the same video claiming it was from Plateau state in Nigeria. Here is the link to the post , and below is the screenshot- Jan 7, 2019 Continuing its search on another keyframe, the Desk came across a report by The Scroll website posted on Jan 7, 2019, with the same video claiming it was from Haryana. Here is the link to the Scroll. in report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that the 38-second YouTube Video clip in the report was a part of the 1:16-minute video shared in the recent Facebook post that 'linked' it to Rajasthan. Jan 6, 2019 We found the same video on the ABP News video page claiming the incident of water freezing in the waterpipe captured in the video happened in Haryana in Jan 2019. The report was published on Jan 6, 2019. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page- Jan 4, 2019 The same video was published on the video page of the Indian Express website giving credit to AP on the video, which also claimed it happened in Haryana. Here is the link to the video and below is the screenshot of the page- The Desk searched Google with specific keywords, including 'AP video,' but couldn't find anything from AP on it. Jan 4, 2019 A subsequent search led the Desk to another report by Daily Mail published in Jan 2019, which claimed the video was from Haryana. The headline read: "Hypnotic footage shows perfectly formed 'ice pops' shooting out of an irrigation hose when farmer tries to water his fields as cold spell grips northern India." Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page: The Daily Mail report claimed the 43-second video was first shared on social media by a farmer. The social media posts that shared the video this year claimed it was from Rajasthan. The reports published using the same video in Jan 2019 claimed the footage was from Haryana. One user claimed it was from Nigeria. Subsequently, the Desk came across the same video on a social media post published on Jan 1, 2019, claiming it was from Pakistan. However, a report on the Nai Dunia news website published on Dec 31, 2018, claimed the video was from Mainpat in Chhattisgarh. Jan 1, 2019: Samaa TV The Desk continued with the investigation and came across a tweet by Samaa TV, posted on Jan 1, 2019, claiming that the phenomenon was noticed and captured on camera in the Khuzdar area of Balochistan in Pakistan. "بلوچستان کے علاقے خضدار میں سردی کی شدت سے پانی کے پائپ سے برف گرنے کی یہ ویڈیو سوشل میڈیا میں تیزی سے وائرل ہو رہی ہے," the tweet in Urdu read. This was roughly translated to English: "This video of snow falling from a water pipe due to extreme cold in the Khuzdar area of Balochistan is becoming viral on social media." Here is the link to the tweet , and below is the screenshot of the same: Dec 31, 2018: Nai Dunia A report by Nai Dunia, published on Dec 31, 2018, claimed that the video was from Mainpat in Chhattisgarh. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: We noticed the Nai Dunia report showed the same video uploaded on its YouTube channel on Dec 31. Here is the link to the video . Below is the screenshot of the page- Since the video was published on Dec 31, 2018, the Desk searched Google to find the details of the weather condition of Mainpat in Dec 2018. The historical report of Chhattisgarh's Mainpat was found on a website that captures and predicts weather conditions. As per the details on the site (wunderground.com), the lowest temperature recorded in Mainpat was 46 Deg F (7.7 Deg Celsius) at 12.30 AM on Dec 31. Here is the link to Mainpat's Dec 31 weather report , and below are the screenshots - 32°F (0°C) is the temperature at which freshwater generally freezes. Mainpat's temperature was 14°F above that level on Dec 32, 2018. The Desk couldn't establish the origin of the video but subsequently concluded that it was not from Rajasthan, as claimed in the recent social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this Pongal feast is not from UK PM Rishi Sunak's office; Video shared by social media users, news portals with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video claiming to be of UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak's staff and country's defense officials celebrating Pongal festival. The video was also shared by some media outlets carrying the same claim. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was from Waterloo in Canada. The claim in the video shared on social media and news portals was false. Claim An Instagram user shared a video, claiming to be of UK PM Rishi Sunak's staff and country's defense officials enjoying a Pongal feast. "Viral Video of UK defense & PM's office staff celebrating Pongal/Makar Sankranti festival. A welcome change," read the post shared on Jan 17, which has so far garnered over 8600 likes. Here are the links to the Instagram post and its archive post : Below is the screenshot of the Instagram post: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a report by The Indian Express. On opening the link from the Google search results, it led to an error page. The Desk, however, found the archive post through Wayback Machine. The archive post can be viewed here. Here is a combination image of the archive page and the recent search result on the Indian Express report: The Desk also found that the video with the same claim was carried by India TV . The news outlet, however, corrected the report afterwards. Here is a combination of the archive page and the recent page of the report by India TV: Another media outlet, The New Indian, shared the video with the same claim on Twitter. Here are the links to the Twitter post and its archive post and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk also found that India Today , in its report originally published on Jan 17, reported that the video was of Rishi Sunak hosting Pongal feast for his office staff in London. They later updated the report. We found the archive page of India Today report via Wayback Machine. Here is a combined image of archive page and updated page of India Today's report: The Desk then conducted a Google search with a relevant set of keywords and found a Facebook post by Tamil Culture Waterloo Region. The post confirmed that the event took place in Waterloo, Canada, and not the UK. The post also mentioned that the Pongal feast was attended by the Regional Chair City Mayors, councillors, Police Chief and staff. The Facebook page also shared an event of the celebrations which was held at the address mentioned as: "1058 Spitzig Rd, Breslau, ON N0B 1M0". The details of the event were mentioned as: "Tamil Cultural Association of Waterloo Region's annual Thai pongal celebration. Tamil Thai pongal is also known as Tamil thanks giving. South indian classical dance programs, Sri lankan Tamil music, Speech. Traditional tamil pongal food be served on Banana leaf. It will be held at Woodland Christian High School, 1058 Spitzig Road, Breslau, Ontario. E-tickets are now open. Visit our website www.tamilculturewaterloo.org". Here is the link to the event page on Facebook and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next step of investigation, the Desk conducted another Google search for the keywords "Tamil Thai Pongal Celebrations 2023, Photos" which led to a tweet by the Mayor of Kitchener, Berry Vrbanovic, who had shared several pics from the event. "A wonderful evening last night with @waterlootamils & community leaders celebrating #ThaiPongal with foods & cultural traditions together with our local Tamil-Canadian community. Canada & our community are blessed with the diversity that makes us such a great place to live," the tweet read. Here is the link to his tweet and below are the screenshots of the same: The Desk noticed that one of the pics shared by Vrbanovic was from the feast, whose video was shared in the Instagram post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Pongal feast was not from UK PM Rishi Sunak's lunch party for his staff, but of an event organised by the Tamil Cultural Association in Waterloo, Canada.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of PM Modi watching Pathaan trailer digitally edited; Social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video claiming Prime Minister Narendra Modi allegedly watched trailer of Shahrukh Khan's upcoming movie Pathaan. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was digitally morphed and dated back to 2019. The video shared in aocial media posts was digitally morphed. Claim A Twitter user shared a video which showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi 'watching and applauding the trailer of upcoming Bollywood film Pathaan'. The tweet read: "Modi ji watch Pathaan trailer. #Pathaantrailer #Pathaan" (Sic) Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet, which was posted on Jan 19 and garnered 1231 views. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a tweet by Times of India posted on July 22, 2019, which carried similar visuals. The tweet read: "Efforts such as #Chandrayaan2 will further encourage our bright youngsters towards science, top quality research and innovation: PM @narendramodi" Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet Below is the comparison of the video posted on Twitter as recent and the one posted by Times of India in 2019: Taking a cue from the information available on the Twitter thread posted by TOI, the Desk conducted a Google search for a specific set of keywords which led us to a 8:18-minute video posted by India Today's official YouTube channel on July 22, 2019. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi watched the live telecast of Chandrayaan-2 launch by ISRO. ISRO Moon Mission, Chandrayaan 2, has been successfully launched from the Sriharikota space station. After a tense countdown at the Isro space centre, Chandrayaan 2 launch took place at exactly 2:43 on Monday. The much-anticipated launch on Monday afternoon after the initial attempt on July 15 was watched by a billion population after it was abandoned due to a technical snag. Chandrayaan 2 took off aboard the most powerful GSLV-Mk-III rocket dubbed 'Baahubali'. #NarendraModi #Chandrayaan2Launch #ISRO," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next step of investigation, the Desk searched for any media report carrying the news as made in the viral claim. However, we could not find any report on the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2019 video of PM Modi watching the launch of Chandrayaan-2 was digitally altered to make it look like he was watching the trailer of Shah Rukh Khan's upcoming Bollywood film Pathaan. The edited video was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Two-year-old photo of all-party meeting shared on social media as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, along with Home Minister Amit Shah and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. The user claimed that the photo was of a "secret meeting" between BJP and Congress leaders. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo dated back to August 2021 and was of the customary Speaker's meet with parties following the adjournment of the Lok Sabha. The photo was shared in social media posts with a false claim. Claim Tweeting a photo of PM Modi seated with Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, along with Home Minister Amit Shah and Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, a user claimed it was of a "secret meeting" between the BJP and Congress leaders. The tweet read: "Secret meeting of BJP Congress. Congress will give BJP a chance to become the Prime Minister in 2024. Muslims should boycott Congress. The vote of Muslims will be spoiled if voted for Congress. because here's the deal" Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the tweet- Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the photo. The search results led us to another couple of tweets carrying the similar claim. The Twitter posts can be viewed here and here and their archive posts can be seen here and here . The Desk also found a report by Hindustan Times, published on Aug 12, 2021, which carried the same photo. The headline of the article read: 'PM Modi, Sonia Gandhi at Speaker's meet with parties post Lok Sabha adjournment.' Here is the link to the report and below is the screenshot of the same: It carried a photo showing PM Modi, Sonia Gandhi and other leaders in the same attire, sitting arrangement and identical background as seen in the viral image. In customised Google search, we found another report by The Tribune with same picture published on Aug 11,2021. The headline read: "PM Modi, Sonia Gandhi share smiles at Speaker's meet". Here is the link and screenshot of the report: We also found multiple news articles by various news outlets carrying the similar photo while reporting about the Speaker's meet in August 2021 after the adjournment of Lok Sabha. The news reports by NDTV and Republic World can be seen here and here respectively: The Desk also found a tweet by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, posted on Aug 11, 2021, which carried a 1:00-minute of the Speaker's meeting. Here is the link to the tweet and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo claimed to be of a "secret meeting" between the BJP and the Congress was of the Speaker's meet with parties in August 2021 following the adjournment of the Lok Sabha.

title: PTI Fact Check: Male dancer performing to 'Besharam Rang' not Bilawal Bhutto, video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of two people dancing to the 'Besharam Rang' song at an event was recently shared on Twitter with the claim that the male dancer featured is Pakistan Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto. However, a PTI fact check found the man in the clip is actually a media student in Karachi. The song from Shah Rukh Khan's upcoming movie 'Pathan' has gone viral on social media since its trailer launch and created controversy because of its lyrics and costumes. The song has been a massive hit among Instagram users copying the dance steps in their reels. Claim A Twitter user shared a dance video in which a male and a female dancer were seen performing the 'Besharam Rang' Song, claiming that the man in the video was Pakistan's foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto. The tweet, which garnered over 863K views with nearly 7000 likes and over 1800 retweets, read: "Pakistan is in safe hands of leaders like Bilawal Bhutto...they want Kashmir...". (Sic) Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the them led to another similar claim on Twitter. Here are the links to the tweet posted on Jan 22 and its archive post . The Desk also found a tweet by journalist Rohan Dua who quoted the same tweet which shared the video earlier. His tweet post on Jan 22 read: "आइए मिलिए एक बार पूर्व पाकिस्तान प्रधान मंत्री बेनज़ीर भुट्टो — जिन्हें आत्मघाती बम और गोलीबारी से मार कर हत्या कर दी थी — के इस लायक़ बेटे से । गौर तलब है की इस मुल्क के कुछ मियाँ बंदूको से बात करते है तो कुछ इन लचकीले नाच की कलाओं से — दोनो ही ख़तरनाक. (Come meet this worthy son of former Pakistan Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto - who was assassinated by a suicide bomb and a gunfight. It is worth noting that some people of this country talk with guns and some with these flexible dance skills - both are dangerous.) Here is the tweet by Dua and its archive post : A further search on the keyframes led the Desk to an Instagram post by a Pakistani social media influencer Inaya Khan on Jan 12. The video in the post looked almost the same as the one posted on Twitter, except that it was shot from a different angle. The Desk compared the visuals of the two video and concluded that they were same. Below is a combination of screengrabs from the two videos: Inaya's Instagram post, which read, "Besharam Rang dance Partner @mehrozbaigofficial", tagged the male dancer with her as Mehroz Baig, an Instagram user with 21.3K followers. The Desk scanned his Instagram profile and found that he was tagged by Inaya in another dance video from the same event. The caption of the video, posted on Jan 19, suggested the occasion was the wedding ceremony of Inaya's sister. "Kusu Kusu Dance Performance with the one @mehrozbaigofficial Videographer @rafayiqbalfilms #inayakhan #innakhan100 #mehrozbaig #behenkishaadi," the caption read. Here is the link to the Instagram post and below is the screenshot of the same: To further cross-check the claim made in the Twitter post, the Desk reached out to Mehroz Baig over e-mail, who confirmed that it was him dancing in the video. "I'm basically a student doing bachelors in media studies from Iqra University, Karachi. I'm currently 25 years old. This event took place on Jan 8 at Sunset Club Karachi, where I performed with Inaya khan on her sister's wedding," he told PTI. Pakistani journalist Lubna Jerar Naqvi also confirmed to the Desk that the man in the viral video was not Pakistan's foreign minister, but Mehroz Baig. "A video of a couple dancing at some party/wedding is being shared as that of Pakistan's Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. This video is not of Minister Bhutto. It is a video of @InayakhanOfficial – who has 895 posts 143K followers 283 following on insta - and @mehrozbaigofficial – who has 3,701 posts 21.3K followers 2,981 following on insta. Both of them have shared it, and other videos from the same event, on their Insta and YouTube Channels. Many people, including several prominent, who have verified accounts on Twitter, Facebook and YouTube have been sharing and claiming it is a video of Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari," Lubna told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man dancing on Bollywood song 'Besharam Rang' in the video posted on Twitter was not Pakistan's Bilawal Bhutto, but Mehroz Baig, a media student from Karachi.

title: PTI Fact Check: Tweet on XBB.1.5 subvariant and vaccination taken out of context, led to misleading posts on social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): The NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene's Twitter handle posted a tweet that the Omicron XBB.1.5 subvariant of Coronavirus was "more likely to infect people vaccinated or had already been infected with COVID-19". The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the tweet was taken out of context and shared by multiple social media users with misleading claims. Two medical experts told PTI that there was no conclusive evidence that people vaccinated against COVID-19 were more vulnerable to the XBB.1.5 subvariant of Omicron, as claimed in the tweet. Claim A tweet by the Twitter handle of the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene claimed that those vaccinated against COVID-19 were more prone to get infected by the XBB.1.5 subvariant of the Omicron variant of COVID-19. "Omicron subvariant XBB.1.5 now accounts for 73% of all sequenced COVID-19 cases in NYC," the department's tweet began. "XBB.1.5 is the most transmissible form of COVID-19 that we know of to date and may be more likely to infect people who have been vaccinated or already had COVID-19," read the tweet, which has 1.2 million views and over 500 retweets. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet, which was shared on Jan 13 this year. Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation Before starting the claim investigation, the Desk took an overview of all the available information regarding the XBB.1.5 subvariant of the Omicron variant of COVID-19. On Jan 18, the World Health Organisation released an information note on the new subvariant. According to the WHO, "The recently detected XBB.1.5 variant is a sub-lineage of the Omicron XBB sub-lineage . Although data on XBB.1.5 are still minimal, currently available information indicates that XBB.1.5 has a growth advantage compared to other circulating Omicron sublineages and may contribute to an increase in cases globally". Below is the screenshot of a portion of the article: Also, the screenshot of the NYT data shows how the cases of XBB.1.5 subvariant went up and down in NYC- Meanwhile, a Jan 20 report by Reuters quoted data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to state that the Omicron XBB.1.5 subvariant was estimated to account for nearly half of the COVID-19 cases reported in the United States to date. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next step of the investigation, the Desk researched the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines and also checked what global health agencies had to say about the possibility of vaccination increasing the risk of infection or reinfection. In its Questions and Answers page on COVID-19 vaccines, the World Health Organisation (WHO) clearly stated that COVID-19 vaccines are "very effective at preventing serious illness, hospitalization, and death from all current virus variants." It also stated that while the vaccines reduce the risk of developing severe illness and death, "no vaccine is 100% effective". "A small percentage of people will still get ill from COVID-19 even though they have been vaccinated," it added. Here is a screenshot of a portion of the WHO's response to a query on the effectiveness of vaccines against different variants. On a separate question of whether someone can still get infected with COVID-19 after getting vaccinated, the WHO said: "Yes. The maximum protection from COVID-19 vaccines is not reached until several weeks after full vaccination. If you have a two-dose vaccine, you don't get full immunity until 2 – 4 weeks after the second dose. You can still become infected and ill during this time." "While COVID-19 vaccines are highly effective against serious illness, hospitalization, and death, no vaccine is 100% effective. As a result, many vaccinated people will get infected and may fall ill with COVID-19 despite being fully vaccinated. This is known as a 'breakthrough infection' or 'breakthrough case,'" it added. Here is a screenshot of the WHO's response to the query: On the longevity of the protection from the COVID-19 vaccines, the WHO stated that while the exact duration is unknown, the data suggests that most people have strong protection against severe illness and death for at least six months. "There is increasing evidence that the effectiveness of the COVID-19 vaccine against infection and mild symptoms can wane over time. In light of this, the WHO Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE) has advised that booster doses are offered to people 4-6 months after the primary vaccination series is completed. A booster dose should be taken when offered to strengthen protection against serious illness and death from COVID-19," it added. Below is a screenshot of the WHO's response: XBB.1.5 accounts for 49% Covid cases in US We already discussed the XBB.1.5 subvariant of Omicron being the dominant strain of COVID-19 in the United States, accounting for over 49 per cent of the overall cases reported there. The Desk searched for the COVID-19 vaccination figures of the United States to understand what percentage of the population has received single or both doses to date. Finding this data was necessary because the viral claim had raised the vaccination question. According to Our World in Data , 69 per cent of the overall population of the US has been fully vaccinated till Jan 17, while 12 per cent has been partially vaccinated. This means that 81 per cent of the total population has been wholly or partially vaccinated. Going by the number of people, 229.51 million were vaccinated entirely, while another 39.26 million were partially vaccinated till Jan 17. Below is a chart showing the population division of the United States in terms of vaccinations: According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, a US government agency, 50.6 million people have also received the booster vaccine. Below is CDC's age-wise data on vaccination in the US : With the data suggesting that over 80 per cent of the US population is vaccinated (69 per cent fully vaccinated) and the WHO affirming chances of reinfection in vaccinated people, it would be imperative to say that the claim made in the NYC Health Department's tweet is nothing like an alarming revelation. Since a significant part of the population stands vaccinated against the virus, several cases of reinfection will also be from those who have received the jab. To better understand the claim made by the NYC Health Department, the PTI Fact Check Desk reached out to Dr. Rajib Dasgupta, Professor, Centre of Social Medicine & Community Health at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi. Dr. Dasgupta said the XBB.1.5 is the "most transmissible subvariant" and has extensive "immune-escape properties." "The statement (claim in the tweet) made is what, in epidemiological terms, is referred to as spurious association. This is assuming no other motivation for a statement such as this. As most of the population gets vaccinated, most cases will be among the vaccinated group. XBB.1.5 is the "most transmissible subvariant detected yet" and has emerged as the dominant variant in the northeastern states/parts of the USA. It has immense immune-escape properties and is therefore infecting large numbers, including those previously vaccinated and those who had COVID earlier," Dr. Dasgupta told PTI. The Desk also reached out to Dr. N K Arora, Chairman of India's COVID-19 Working Group of the National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI), for his comment on the claim in the tweet. Dr. Arora said, "the infection rate in the case of XBB.1.5 in a country depends on the "vaccination status and the hybrid immunity of the community." "In India, the XBB.1.5 has been detected but has not expanded. Similarly, the Omicron BA.5 variant occurred, which was dominant at some time in North America and Europe, but it did not expand. In other words, we are saying that local epidemiology is more important. Today, the important point is whether any virus is associated with severe disease, hospitalization, or death in a particular context. Fortunately for India, the number of cases is hovering around 150 per day, with practically no hospitalisation and death. Many of these subvariants, which are circulating in higher proportion in other countries, have not been able to expand similarly within the Indian context," Dr Arora told PTI. As of Jan 24, 67.6 per cent of India's total population has been fully vaccinated while over 73 per cent of the total population has received at least one dose. The overall jabs administered in the country stood at 2,20,30,63,139 at the time of publishing this article. India has recently been reporting less than 100 days daily, which has brought down the active cases to less than 2,000. Subsequently, the study by the global health agencies on the new subvariant and COVID-19 vaccines and experts have opined there is no conclusive evidence backing the claim that those vaccinated are at a higher risk of getting infected with the XBB.1.5 sublineage of the Omicron variant. The Desk also noticed that the NYC Health Department's twitter handle intended to clarify the claim in its previous tweet. This was indicated in the same thread's second tweet: "Getting vaccinated and getting the updated booster is still the best way to protect yourself from hospitalization and death from COVID-19, including from these new variants." Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: As the imprecisely worded tweet led to misinformation on the virus subvariant and COVID-19 vaccination, the NYC Health Department made it clear on their website that the elevated risk of infection was relative to other variants, not to unvaccinated people. "It may be more likely to infect people who have been vaccinated or previously had COVID-19 compared to prior variants," read an article on 'New Variants' on the official website of the NYC government. Here is the link to the webpage , and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a poorly worded tweet by the NYC Health Department was taken out of context or misconstrued to mean that vaccinated people were at higher risk of infection than unvaccinated people. What the tweet intended to convey was that vaccinated people were at a higher risk of disease with the new variant compared with previous ones.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this foreign dance group didn't perform on Indian patriotic song at 'America's Got Talent'; Digitally altered video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a dance troupe performing at the famous 'America's Got Talent' purportedly on an Indian patriotic song. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video dated back to 2018, and was digitally altered and shared on social media with false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a video of a dance troupe performing at the 'America's Got Talent' reality show on what can be heard as an Indian patriotic song 'Jai Ho India'. The post, which garnered over 27K likes with nearly over 8.7K reshares, read: "अमेरिका के एक टेलेन्ट शो में भारत के देशभक्ति गीत पर दिल को धड़का देने वाला अति सुंदर नृत्य, रोंगटे खड़े हो जायेंगे." (Heart-throbbing exquisite dance on India's patriotic song in a US talent show, will give you goosebumps) Here are the links to the post and its archive post . Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Facebook post by BJP leader and Madhya Pradesh's Cabinet Minister Dr Mohan Yadav who shared the video with the same claim. Here are the links to the post and its archive post and below is the screenshot of the same: The search further led the Desk to a YouTube video – an extended version of the viral video – posted on June 28, 2018. The title of the YouTube video read: "ZURCORAH Aerial Dance Group GOLDEN BUZZER America's Got Talent 2018." Here is the link to the video and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the entire 4:47-minute video and noticed that the audio was different from the viral video. Also, the description of the video suggested that the dance troupe performed in the 13th season of the reality show and even won the Golden Buzzer for its performance. Continuing its search, the Desk found another video by posted verified YouTube channel Talent Recap posted on Aug 5, 2020. The title of the video read: "#2 Most Viral Audition: Zurcaruh The Austrian High FLYING Dance Act". In this video, the judges recalled the performance made in the 13th season and how it left them stunned. Here is the link and screenshot of the video: In a customised search, we found an official Instagram account of the dance group "Zurcaruh". A video of the dance performance on the page was posted on Aug 5, 2020 with the caption: "Today Zurcaroh's perfomance was aired on the @agt 15th anniversary episode which takes a look back at the most notable acts in the America's Got talent history. Once again we got #2 most viral with 423 millions views. We thank you all!!" Here is the link to the Instagram post and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next step of investigation, the Desk then performed a keyword search on the internet about the song in the video shared on social media, and found that it was 'Jai Ho India', sung by Vicky Parekh. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video was digitally altered to add the Indian patriotic song in the background. The original video showed that a different music was played during the group's performance in 2018.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2-year-old video of WFI president Brij Bhushan Sharan slapping a wrestler shared as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of BJP MP and Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan Sharan allegedly slapping a wrestler for asking questions at an event. Sharan has been accused of sexually harassing women wrestlers by top wrestlers, including Vinesh Phogat, Bajrang Punia, Sakshi Malik and Ravi Dahiya. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video shared in the Facebook post was two years old and shared as recent with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user posted a video of WFI president Brij Bhushan Sharan slapping a wrestler on stage for asking questions over the sexual harassment charges that the former was facing. "BJP MP and President of Wrestling Federation of India, Brij Bhushan Sharan, who has been accused of sexual harassment, slapping a wrestler on stage for asking questions," read the Facebook post, dated Jan 20. Here are the links to the post and its archive post . Below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a report by The Outlook, published on Dec 19, 2021, which carried the same video. The report's headline read: "Wrestling Federation Of India President Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh Slaps Wrestler In Public - Watch Video" Here is the link to the report and below is the screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident took place during the Under-15 National Wrestling Championships at Shaheed Ganpat Rai Indoor Stadium, Ranchi. According to the report, during the age verification, the wrestler was found to be above 15 years of age and was stopped from participating in the competition. However, the wrestler lodged a complaint and then stepped onto the stage and started arguing with the WFI president. Singh, who was reportedly trying to pacify the wrestler, lost his cool and slapped the wrestler in front of everyone, the report added. Continuing its search, the Desk found another video report by One India News posted on Dec 18, 2021. The title of the video report read: "BJP MP slaps wrestler: Brijbhushan Sharan Singh sparks anger | Oneindia News" The description of the YouTube video read "BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has sparked anger after slapping a wrestler from UP at an event. The internet called out his arrogance while he defended his actions." Here is the link and screenshot of the video: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2021 video of Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh slapping a wrestler was shared as recent amid the WFI President facing sexual harassment charges.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Gaurav Bhatia didn't make remarks against PM Modi; 5-second video clip shared by Congress leader with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Congress leader shared a video of BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia claiming he criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a TV debate show. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the 5-second footage was trimmed from the video of Bhatia's remarks during a debate show on a TV channel. In the more extended version of the video, he responded to a claim from the Congress leader, and one line from his remarks was trimmed to share in the social media posts with the misleading claim. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759, a tweet posted by a verified handle, belongs to Congress leader Mohammad Waseem. The bio on the profile page says he is the in-charge of Rajasthan and Bihar Pradesh Congress Committee's Minority Department. The tweet, posted on Jan 23, read: "लोकतंत्र का अपमान तो तब होता है जब नरेंद्र मोदी प्रधानमंत्री बनते हैं | कभी गोडसे मुर्दाबाद कभी प्रधानमंत्री मोदी जी का अपमान, जब हिम्मत नहीं होती सुप्रिया जी से डिबेट करने की तो काहे आकर अपनी पार्टी की फजीहत कराते हो." (Democracy is insulted when Shri Narendra Modi becomes the Prime Minister of the country. Sometimes Godse Murdabad, sometimes insulting the prime minister. When you don't have the courage, why do you come to debate with Supriya ji to insult your party) (Sic) Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet, which garnered over 33k views, more than 580 retweets, and above 1700 likes. Below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Facebook, which shared the same video and the claim. Here are the link and the archive link to the post shared on Jan 23 and reshared by eight other users. Below is the screenshot of the post: The search further led the Desk to a YouTube video – an extended version of Bhatia's statement on the AajTak channel – posted on Jan 21, 2023. The title of the YouTube video read: "Halla Bol: Congress की प्रवक्ता Supriya Shrinate ने कहा- मुझे गर्व है भारत जोड़ो यात्रा पर" (Halla Bol: Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate said – I am proud of the Bharat Jodo Yatra.) The Desk watched the entire 7:34 minute video and noticed that Bhatia made the statement shared by the Congress leader and a Facebook user at 7:10 minutes when he responded to Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate's comment on insulting Congress chief. Bhatia was heard saying after 7:00 in the video: "इन्होने कहा आप अपमान करते हैं हमारी पार्टी के अध्यक्ष का । लोकतंत्र का अपमान हो रहा है इनके हिसाब से । लोकतंत्र का अपमान तब होता है जब श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी प्रधानमंत्री हैं बनते देश के और उनको कहा जाता है चौकीदार चोर है, और उसके बाद माफ़ी मांगी जाती है कान पकड़ के, राहुल गाँधी कहते हैं Sorry I lied before the honourable Supreme Court" ("They said we insult their party president. According to them it's an insult to democracy. Democracy gets insulted when Shri Narendra Modi becomes the prime minister of the country and he was called the 'watchman is the thief'. And after that they say sorry holding the ears, Rahul Gandhi said 'Sorry, I Lied' before the honourable Supreme Court…"). The 5-second video clip, shared on Twitter and Facebook, can be seen between 7:12 and 7:17 minutes in the YouTube video. The rest of the part was removed to make it look like Bhatia spoke against PM Modi. Here is the link to the video , and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Gaurav Bhatia's comment made during a TV debate show was shared on social media platforms with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi is not with producer of BBC documentary on Modi in this photo; Social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Jan 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Rahul Gandhi, claiming one of two persons with the former Congress president was the producer of the controversial BBC documentary. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that it was an old photo in which Rahul was seen with British politician Jeremy Corbyn and Sam Pitroda during his meeting in 2022. The old photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of Rahul Gandhi, claiming that one of the two persons with him was the producer of a controversial BBC documentary on Prime Minister Narendra Modi. "Exactly six months ago, Rahul Gandhi was in the UK, n he said "Kerosene has been poured all over India, now it just needs a spark of fire" Congress conspiracy behind BBC documentary to instigate riots in India? Pappu with BBC documentary producer!" read the tweet posted on Jan 25 which garnered more than 1250 views and 25 retweets. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive link . Below is the screenshot of the tweet: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the photo. The search results led us to another couple of tweets carrying similar claims. The Twitter posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be seen here and here . Below is the screenshot of both tweets: The Desk subsequently found a report by The Indian Express, published on May 24, 2022 carrying the same photo. The headline of the article read: 'BJP targets Rahul over meet with Labour MP Corbyn, Congress hits back' Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: The report stated that "Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday came under fire of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for meeting Britain's Labour Party leader Jeremy Corbyn in London. The BJP hit out at the Congress MP for allegedly endorsing the UK MP's "anti-India" views on foreign soil." "The remarks took social media by storm when BJP leader and Union law minister Kiren Rijiju shared a picture of Gandhi's meeting with Corbyn and attacked the former Congress president for going against his own country," the report added. Continuing its search, the Desk found another tweet by the Indian Overseas Congress on May 23, 2022. The tweet read: "Our chairman @sampitroda with @RahulGandhi in London." Here is the link to the tweet and screenshot of the tweet: The Desk searched for the details of the BBC documentary producer and came to know that the first episode of the controversial documentary "India: The Modi Question," produced by Richard Cookson and Mike Radford, was released on January 17, 2023. We took this as a cue and searched Google for "Rahul Gandhi Richard Cookson Mike Radford" but could not find any relevant results or photos. In the next step of investigation, the Desk conducted a search on Jeremy Corbyn to establish whether the British politician had any association with the BBC. According to Corbyn's biography on Britannica , he served as the leader of the Labour Party from 2015 to 2020. "He was elected to a local London council at the age of 25 and soon after began working for the National Union of Public Employees. He was elected to Parliament in the 1983 general election for the safe Labour seat of Islington North, a working-class area close to central London," the article stated. "He also was close to Tony Benn, Labour's leading left-wing figure in the 1980s and '90s, and wrote regularly for the small daily communist newspaper Morning Star," it added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2022 photo of Rahul Gandhi with British politician Jeremy Corbyn was shared on social media with a false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video, photo unrelated to Shah Rukh Khan's film Pathaan shared on social media with false claims; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Shah Rukh Khan-starrer Pathaan, which created controversy due to one of its songs and the colour of the costumes of lead actress Deepika Padukone, released on Jan 25 and received good reviews from most of the audiences. Social media platforms have been flooded with photos and videos shared by users who claimed the movie earned positive responses. However, a photo and a video shared by social media users are old and unrelated to SRK's Pathaan. The PTI Fact Check Desk noticed that the photo was edited, and the video was old and shared in the context of SRK's movie Pathaan. While scanning social media platforms, the desk found a photo in which a police unit was seen guarding a building with a poster of Pathaan on top of it. Similarly, the desk came across a video in which a man was seen crying inconsolably, purportedly heaping praises on the film, which the user described as a "Pathaan review in a single video." In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that both claims were false. The photo in the first claim dates back to 2018, when Hindu right-wing groups protested against Sanjay Leela Bhansali's film Padmaavat. The image was digitally altered to replace Padmaavat's poster with that of Pathaan. Similarly, the video in the second claim dated back to April last year and was of a man crying after watching the Kannada film KGF: Chapter 2. Claim 1 A Facebook user shared a photo of a police unit guarding a building, purportedly a cinema hall screening Shah Rukh Khan and Deepika Padukone-starrer Pathaan. The post, dated Jan 23 read: "अंधभक्तों के लिए खास सरकारी प्रबंध... फैलते हुए आयेंगे, सूजते हुए जाएंगे। (Special government arrangement for blind bhakts. Will come spreading, will go swollen.)" Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse search on the photo. The results led us to a report by Laffaz published on Jan 28, 2018, which carried a similar image of a unit of security personnel guarding a cinema hall screening the Bollywood film Padmaavat. The Desk compared the two photos – one shared in the Facebook post and the other carried in the Business Standard report – and found striking similarities. Below is a comparison between the two photos: The report carried several other images of the film, marred by protests from Hindu right-wing groups, being screened at several cinema halls under heavy security. The Indian Express also carried a similar photo in its report dated Jan 25, 2018. The report's headline read: "Padmaavat: Curtains go up under security net." Here is the link to the report and below is its screenshot: The photo carried by The Indian Express suggested that the photo was taken outside Delhi's Delite Cinema. The protests against Padmaavat were led by Karni Sena, who alleged that the history related to Rani Padmavati was distorted in the film. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2018 photo of security personnel guarding a cinema hall screening 'Padmaavat' was digitally altered to make it look like the unit was protecting a cinema hall screening Pathaan. Claim 2 A Twitter user shared a video of a man crying inconsolably. The user claimed that the fan was emotional after watching Pathaan. "#Pathaan review in a single video," read the tweet posted on Jan 25, which has garnered 2.8 million views and nearly 28,000 likes. Here are the links to the post and its archive post and below is its screenshot: Investigation The Desk started its investigation by scanning the comment section of the tweet and found several comments claiming that the video was an old one from the time of the release of the Kannada film KGF: Chapter 2. "This one was for KGF.. old vid," read a comment by a verified Twitter handle named exsecular. To this, the user replied: "Lol, I talk about the same energy. Meme hai." While the user himself indicated that the video was old and not related to Pathaan, we continued our investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of them led the Desk to several YouTube videos, posted on April 14 and April 27 last year. The first video was the same as the one posted on Twitter. The headline of the video, posted by Public TV – a verified YouTube channel – read: "KGF Chapter 2: Fan Cries After Watching The Movie | Rocking Star Yash | Prashanth Neel". In the 34-second video, the man can be heard speaking Telugu, which roughly translates to English as: ""Guys want to see kissing scenes but the mother scene was awesome. The scene moved me to tears. The movie reminded us of our mothers. Yash (Kannada actor) has done a great job. Agarbatti (Incense stick) connects the devotees with the deity and this (Suththi) hammer connects the fans with Yash."." Here is the link to the video , and below is its screenshot: In the second video, which is 31 seconds long, the same man said he watched the movie for the fourth time as he continued to praise the film and the lead actor. He also praises the mother scene in the movie and then starts humming one of the songs from KGF: Chapter 2. Here is the link to the video , and below is its screenshot: Below is a comparison of screengrabs from the two videos – one shared as recent on social media and other on YouTube: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was old and unrelated to the newly released film Pathaan.

title: PTI Fact Check: Tweet calling 'Global Warming' a hoax is misleading; Selected years' data shared to highlight 'global cooling' trend falsely
content: New Delhi, Jan 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user cited data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and claimed the Earth has been cooling, not warming, over the years, allegedly proving that global warming from carbon emissions was a hoax. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a selected part of the NOAA graphics on land and ocean temperatures over the years was taken out of context to highlight the 'global cooling' trend falsely. The NOAA and two environmental science experts, whom the Desk reached out to for comment, vehemently refuted the claim made in the post on Twitter. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 a tweet by a verified handle showing an NOAA graph displaying land and ocean temperatures over the last eight years, from 2015 to 2022. Based on the graph, the post claimed that Earth's temperature reduced, not increased, at a rate of 0.11 degree Celsius per decade. The tweet, posted on Jan 13 this year, further said that the topic of global warming due to CO2 emissions was a "hoax." " NOAA makes it official. Last eight years... global cooling... at a rate of 0.11°C/decade.... despite 450+ billion tons of emissions worth 14% of total manmade CO2 in the atmosphere. CO2 warming is a hoax," read the tweet, which garnered over 13 million views, 18,000 likes, and 8,500 retweets. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the graph. A separate search on the results combined with the keywords "global cooling, NOAA" led us to the official website of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The Desk found a graph that displayed temperature trends over ears from 1880 to 2022, which showed a consistent rise in global average temperatures. Here is the link to the NOAA webpage , and below is the screenshot of the graph: On carefully studying the graph and then zooming in on the period displayed on the chart shared in the tweet, the Desk found that the Twitter user had used the same data but only for a selected period and presented it out of context. Below is a screenshot of the data on the NOAA graph for the period 2015-2022. The graph on land and ocean temperatures suggests that Earth's average temperature had risen consistently since 1976, except in 1984 when it reduced by 0.08 degree Celsius. There have been several instances when the Earth's average temperature witnessed a dip. However, the last 38 years (from 1985 to 2023) have seen temperatures rising. The Desk then closely monitored NOAA's Climate at a Glance time series tool and found that it allows users to generate global temperature charts based on parameters like date and location. For instance, the user who claimed on Twitter selected a time frame of January 2015 to January 2022, which showed a cooling trend of 0.09 degree Celsius per decade; however, if we choose the period between January 2010 and January 2016, the tool shows warming trend of nearly 0.5 degrees Celsius per decade. Below is a screenshot of the same: Another report by NOAA contradicted the claim made by the Twitter user. The report, published on Jan 13, 2022, stated, "2021 ranked sixth on the list of warmest years on record, dating back to 1880." "Earth's average land and ocean surface temperature in 2021 was 1.51 degrees F (0.84 of a degree C) above the 20th-century average. It also marked the 45th consecutive year (since 1977) with global temperatures rising above the 20th-century average. The years 2013-2021 all rank among the ten-warmest years on record," the report added. The Desk then went through a report by the United Nations, which explained its 'Climate Action' goal as part of its Sustainable Development Goals. It stated that the global temperature has already risen 1.1 degree Celsius above the pre-industrial level. "The global temperature has risen 1.1ºC above the pre-industrial level, melting glaciers and rising sea levels. The impacts of climate change also include flooding and drought, displacing millions of people, sinking them into poverty and hunger, denying them access to basic services, such as health and education, expanding inequalities, stifling economic growth, and even causing conflict. By 2030, an estimated 700 million people will be at risk of displacement by drought alone," the report stated. Here is a link to the UN report , and below is a screenshot of the same: In December last year, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres announced that he would convene a Climate Ambition Summit next September and called on every leader to "step up – from governments, business, cities, and regions, civil society and finance." NASA also confirmed the global warming trend over decades, which has continued steadily. Here is a screenshot of the key takeaway of the report: The report also presented a graph showing the land-ocean temperature index, clearly indicating a continuous rise in the average global temperatures. Below is a screenshot of the graph: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Twitter user cherry-picked the NOAA data for a short time and presented it out of context to claim that the Earth was witnessing global cooling. NOAA refutes 'global cooling' claim The Desk contacted NOAA by e-mail for its comment on the claim's veracity. In its response, the organisation's climate scientist Ahira Sanchez-Lugo said: "Although the climate is changing to a warmer climate, it is also subject to natural variabilities such as El Niños (hot temperatures across the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean) and La Niñas (unusually cool temperatures across the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean). El Niños and La Niñas not only affect global weather patterns, but they can also affect global temperatures. During El Niños, global temperatures tend to be warmer than in years when ENSO neutral or La Niñas were present. In contrast, global temperatures are slightly cooler (but above average) during La Niñas." "2016 started with a strong El Niño, which helped boost global temperatures to record highs. And since then, we have had Rs 3 La Niñas, which help slightly cool global temperatures. The selected timeframe from 2016-2022 can create the appearance of a cooling trend," Ahira added. "Similarly, if you select 2012-2016, you get a warming trend of 0.97 deg C per decade! This is why we use timescales of at least ten years when computing trends," the NOAA scientist concluded. Below are the graphical representations shared by the NOAA scientist. The first shows El Niños and La Niñas which occurred between Jan 1950 and Jul 2022. The second and third show a steady rise in the global temperature over the years. What do experts have to say? The Desk also reached out to two experts to understand the phenomenon and whether the selective data in the claim suggested an overall global cooling trend. Dr. Aniket Kumar, Assistant Professor, Department of Environmental Sciences, Dyal Singh College, University of Delhi, told PTI that the user who made a claim cherry-picked the 2016-2022 data to make his point, which was not the case otherwise. "When we talk about climate change, we talk about long-term data, i.e., at least 30 years. Due to global warming, we are seeing erratic changes in temperature in various parts of the world. So, some years are sweltering, and some years are less hot," added Kumar. "This gentleman (The Twitter user) has taken selective data from 2015-16 till 2022, claiming cooling is happening. Now 2015 -16 were known to be sweltering years, so compared to that particular year, other years were not that hot, so the graph showing us the cooling in the decade," he said. On the user's claim that global warming due to CO2 emissions was a hoax, Kumar said: "Global warming is real, and it is true we are going to see a more erratic pattern in average temperature in coming years." The graph below shows the land-ocean temperature trend over the period 1990-2022 that witnessed a rise of 0.31 degree Celsius per decade: The Desk also contacted Dr. Rajeev Singh, an Associate Professor in the Department of Environmental Science at Jamia Millia Islamia University in Delhi, for his comment. Dr. Singh echoed similar sentiments on the claim made by the Twitter user in his post. "I could not relate to this 8-year temperature data as there is no evidence of decreasing CO2 emission in these years. Also, there have been reports of increasing CO2 emissions, heat, and temperature in recent years. So, saying that CO2 warming is a hoax is not relevant. The tweet graph shows a single parameter without much details and correlation," Dr. Singh told PTI.

title: PTI Fact Check: Bageshwar Dham's Dhirendra Shastri not given Z+ security; Fake tweet in name of BBC Hindi Twitter handle shared on social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook page shared a screenshot of an alleged tweet in the name of the BBC News Hindi Twitter handle claiming the central government gave Bageshwar Dham's Dhirendra Krishna Shastri Z+ security. Dhirendra Shastri was recently into controversy after social activist Shyam Manav accused him of promoting superstitions. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo containing the alleged tweet by the BBC News Hindi Twitter handle was fake. The screenshot was shared by a satire page and went viral on social media with the false claim. Claim A Facebook page shared a photo – an alleged screenshot of a tweet by BBC News Hindi's Twitter handle – which claimed that the central government gave Dhirendra Krishna Shastri Z+ security. It also claimed that the United Nations (UN) backed the government's action (of providing security to the godman), and Interpol had registered a case against social reformer Shyam Manav for challenging Shastri. "विवादों में फंसे धीरेंद्र शास्त्री के लिए मोदी सरकार ने Z+ सिक्योरिटी । 25 कमांडोज के साथ रहेंगे धीरेंद्र शास्त्री, UN ने भी कहा-मोदी सरकार ने किया सही काम , विरोध कने वाले @ShyamManav पर इंटरपोल ने दर्ज किया मुकदमा," read the screenshot of the alleged tweet in the screenshot shared in the Facebook page on Jan 21. The English translation of the text in the screenshot read: "Modi government has given Z+ security to controversial Dhirendra Shastri. Dhirendra Shastri will be with 25 commandos; UN also said – the Modi government did the right thing, Interpol filed a case against protester @ShyamManav" (sic). Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the screenshot. The search results led us to another Facebook post carrying the same screenshot. Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post , and below is its screenshot: The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Dhirendra Shastri, Z+ Security" but could not find any relevant news report. Had the central government made any such announcement, it would have grabbed the headlines across news channels and outlets. In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk scanned the Twitter handle of BBC News Hindi to search if it made any such tweet on Jan 23, as mentioned in the screenshot. The Desk went through all 42 tweets made by the official Twitter handle of BBC News Hindi on Jan 23 but could not find the one shared as the screenshot in the Facebook post. The Desk then searched Google with the keyword "Dhirendra Shatri security." The search results led the Desk to a report by The Week, posted on Jan 24. The report's headline read: "Bageshwar Dham chief gets life threat; Chhatarpur police form 25-member probe team". Here is the link to the news report , and below is its screenshot: The report quoted the police saying that the security at Bageshwar Dham in Gadha town of Chhatarpur had been increased following the death threat. However, nowhere could we find the mention of the central government providing security to Shastri. Instead, the Desk found a video report by AajTak, according to which the security of Shyam Manav was increased after he allegedly received death threats. According to the news report, nine personnel, including a senior official, were deployed by Nagpur Police in Manav's security. The headline of the YouTube video posted by AajTak's official channel on Jan 23 read: "Bageshwar Dispute: बढ़ाई गई धीरेंद्र शास्त्री को चुनौती देने वाले श्याम मानव की सुरक्षा (Bageshwar Dispute: Security of Shyam Manav, who challenged Dhirendra Shastri, increased)." Here is the link to the video , and below is its screenshot: In his interview with AajTak, Shyam Manav himself confirmed that he was already provided with Y+ security, which had been enhanced following the death threats. The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Shyam Manav Interpol case" but could not find any relevant report around the claim. A report by ABP Live, published on Jan 24, stated that a defamation case had been filed against Manav in Jabalpur of Madhya Pradesh. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: Continuing the investigation, the Desk scanned the Facebook profile of the user who posted the alleged tweet and found it to be a parody page. The page's 'About' section read: "Parody Tweets That seems Real." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot of a fake tweet in the name of BBC News Hindi tweet was shared with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Factually incorrect article claiming 'huge asteroid to hit Earth' shared on Twitter; 'Box truck' sized '2023 BU' asteroid passed 2,200 miles from Earth
content: New Delhi, Jan 30 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared an article that claimed a 'huge asteroid' was set to hit the Earth on Jan 27 this year, as written in its headline. The PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the asteroid named 2023 BU was the size of a 'box truck,' It made one of the closest approaches to Earth when it passed 'just 2,200 miles from Earth' on Jan 27. The asteroid had no chance of hitting Earth and was too small to be dangerous. The claim in the screenshot shared in the social media post was false. Claim A Twitter user shared an article claiming a "huge asteroid" was set to hit the Earth on Jan 27. The article's headline, shared in a Twitter post on Jan 24, read: "Huge asteroid is set to hit the Earth this week." Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet posted on Jan 24.
