content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of fighter jets shooting down a balloon in the air, claiming it was the footage of F-22 fighter jets firing a heat-seeking missile at the suspected Chinese spy balloon earlier in February this year. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video shared in the social media post was not real but a product of digital simulation, and it went viral soon after the US Air Force announced that it shot down a Chinese 'spy' balloon. Claim The 2:20-minute video was shared in a tweet published on Feb 8 and garnered over 290K views, nearly 2000 likes and over 400 retweets. The text in the tweet read: "Shooting down the Chinese Balloon... The real action was caught on camera. Can be easily done by our IAF too (Sic)." Here are the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the page: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video for keyframes, and a subsequent Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to another tweet sharing the same video and claim. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is its screenshot: While going through the comments on the tweet, the Desk noticed several users claimed the video was not real but a simulation. Here is the link to one such comment , and below is its screenshot: Taking a cue from this, the Desk, frame by frame, analysed the video and noticed that the audio was apparently of the two aircraft communicating. We also noticed that the aircraft appearing in the video at 1:04 minutes looked animated. Continuing the investigation, we conducted a customised keyword search. We found several reports and a video on a US fighter jet shooting down the suspected Chinese balloon on different news portals. Multiple fighter and refueling aircraft were involved in the mission, but only one -- an F-22 fighter jet from Langley Air Force Base in Virginia -- took the shot at 2:39 p.m. (1939 GMT), using a single AIM-9X supersonic, heat-seeking, air-to-air missile, a Reuters report quoted a senior U.S. military official as saying published. The DW News website posted a video on Feb 5 with the headline: "US shoots down Chinese spy balloon". Here is the link to the video , and below is its screenshot: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk compared the two videos –- the one shared on Twitter and the other posted by the DW News website -- and noticed the fire and black smoke after the missile hit the balloon in the visuals shared on Twitter. On the other hand, the video shared by DW News showed white smoke coming out of the balloon. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos: The Desk continued its search and found another report by the Times of India, dated Feb 5, which carried a 1:19-minute by the Associated Press. Here is the link to the report titled " Watch: US military shoots downs Chinese spy balloon amid heightened tensions ", and below is the screenshot of the same: In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk conducted another Google search with the keyword "Chinese balloon, simulation" and found a YouTube video by Growling Sidewinder, a verified channel, published on Feb 5. While watching the entire video, we noticed that this was an extended version of the video shared in a Twitter post. Here is the link to the video , titled "Real Audio | F-22 Raptor Vs Chinese Spy Balloon | Digital Combat Simulator | DCS |". Below is the screenshot of the page: Below is the combined image of the screenshots of a similar keyframe of both videos – the one shared in the Twitter post and the other posted by Growling Sidewinder on YouTube. The Desk also scanned the video description, highlighting a list of products and technologies used to produce such simulation videos. "On this channel, we like to do dogfighting. Most videos are some dogfight between 2 different aircraft as we explore their different capabilities. From time to time, I like to dabble in Virtual Reality, I think VR is a great new technology, and I love to show that stuff off for the channel from time to time," the description read. Below is a screenshot of the video description: The Desk subsequently concluded that the video shared in the tweet was a simulation product. It was not the original video of the US showdown, as described in the viral claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this Bob Geldof's interview with BBC Newsnight not original; Spoof video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man, claimed to be Bob Geldof, was shared on WhatsApp saying the legendary singer-writer predicted the rise of social media and smartphone use in one of his interviews at BBC in 1999. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the person who appeared as the guest in the video was not Bob Geldof. It was a satire video produced by comedian Michael Spicer impersonating singer David Bowie. The claim in the WhatsApp forward video was false. Claim The Desk received a video on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 with a request to verify if it was genuine. The 2:15 minute showed a man in sunglasses and sporting shoulder-length hair, predicting the rise of social media and smartphone usage and how it will dominate society. It was claimed that the man was singer-songwriter Bob Geldof and the video was part of his interview with BBC's Newsnight, aired in 1999. "23 years ago, Bob Geldof (Pop singer) was interviewed by BBC Newsnight in 1999. At that time, it was assumed he was high while giving this interview, but listen to his predictions then," read the caption received along with the video. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one of them and the keyword "Bob Geldof BBC interview 1999" led us to a Twitter post dated Apr 21, 2022. "This is Bob Geldof (the pop singer) interview on BBC Newsnight in 1999. Don't know if he was high while giving this interview, but he predicted 100% correctly," read the Twitter post carrying the same video. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk scanned the search results, but it could not find any articles or videos from verified sources, except a few social media posts recently sharing the claim. The Desk, continuing the investigation, watched the 2:15-minute video and noticed that the man claimed as Bob Geldof didn't look like the singer-songwriter. Below is a combined image of the photos of the man in the video and Bob Geldof: Subsequently, the Desk noticed the video also had old and pixelated inserts of the host Jeremy Paxman. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of two different keyframes of the video – one showing the person claimed as Geldof and the other of the host – that gave a sense that the video was edited to use a different set of visuals. In the next step of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on one of the keyframes of the video and found the same video shared by the official Twitter account of the British Writer and Comedian, Michael Spicer. Spicer uploaded the same video on January 3, 2022 wit,h the text: "David Bowie Predicts the Impact of the Internet on Newsnight (1999)." Here is the link to the Twitter post , which has so far garnered 1.6 million views and over 19000 likes, and below is its screenshot- We also found a Twitter post by London-based journalist Stefan Simanowitz, dated Jan 3 last year. "Tomorrow belongs to those who hear it coming" David Bowie predicts the Impact of the Internet & Social Media on Newsnight (1999) (by @MrMichaelSpicer)," read the caption of the tweet. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is its screenshot: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another keyword search on Google and found the original YouTube video of the interview, shared by BBC Newsnight on Jan 11, 2016. Here is the link to the video titled 'David Bowie speaks to Jeremy Paxman on BBC Newsnight (1999)' and below is the screenshot of the same: "In this BBC Newsnight interview from 1999, David Bowie talks to Jeremy Paxman about going to meet Tony Blair in stilettos, his alter egos - and makes some incredibly accurate predictions about the potential of the internet," read the description of the YouTube video. The Desk noticed that the comments made in the two videos – one shared in the Twitter post and the other shared by Simanowitz – were the same, with Paxman asking the same questions. In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk went through the comment sections of all three videos – one received for fact check – and noticed several users commented about it being a spoof video. Below is the link to one such comment and a screenshot of the same: We also scanned BBC's website and social media handles but could not find anything related to "Bob Geldof's interview at BBC Newsnight. When the Desk carefully scanned the BBC Newsnight YouTube Video and the video shared in the tweet, it found that both the videos had Jeremy Paxman as the host, wearing the same attire and asking the same questions. At 10.54 minutes in the YouTube video , Paxman asked: "It's just a tool, though, isn't it?" In the Twitter video , he was seen asking the same question 12-second onwards. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the host from both videos- Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was a satire, in which British comedian Michael Spicer tried to impersonate David Bowie using a few clips of the host from David Bowie's interview at BBC Newsnight in 1999.

title: PTI Fact Check: Man singing Hindi ghazal not Kenyan; Video of Indian singer shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a man singing a Hindi ghazal claiming the singer was from Kenya. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the singer was an Indian named Sanjay Sawant. The claim shared in the social media post was misleading. Claim A Facebook user shared a video of a man singing an old Bollywood ghazal - 'Na kisi ki aankh ka noor hoon' from the Hindi film Laal Quila (1960) – which legendary singer Late Mohd Rafi originally sang. The user claimed in the Facebook post that the singer was from Kenya, highlighting how fluently he spoke Hindi despite not being an Indian. "Unbelievable that he is not Indian. This African singer is from Kenya in Kisumu Tribe Lou. He is Black Kenyan. Just close your eyes and listen to his voice," the user wrote in his post dated Feb 9. Here is the link and the archive link to the Facebook post. Below is a screenshot of the page. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led us to a YouTube video posted nearly five years ago, the same as a Facebook video with the same claim. "This African Singer is from Kenya. Just close yr eyes n listen to his voice ?" read the caption of the video shared on Mar 22, 2018, which has garnered over 24,000 views and close to 400 likes to date. Here are the links to the YouTube post and its archive post . The screenshot of the same can be seen below: Scanning the comments section of the YouTube post, the Desk came across a comment stating that the singer was Sanjay Sawant, an Indian. Here is a screenshot of the comment made on the YouTube post: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a keyword search for "Sanjay Sawant, Na kisi ki aankh ka noor hoon". The Google search results led us to the original version of the video uploaded on YouTube by the channel 'Jagruti Films' on Jan 9, 2021. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the YouTube post: Several comments on the page, including one by the channel itself, mentioned the singer as Sanjay Sawant. The Desk then scanned the About page of the channel and found the contact details of Sittu Kumar from Jagruti Films, which is based in Bhuj, Gujarat. Kumar confirmed to PTI that the person singing in the video was Sanjay Sawant, a famous singer from Maharashtra. We also found the official Facebook page of Sanjay Sawant. The videos on the page confirmed that the person singing the ghazal in the Facebook video was him. Here is the link to Sawant's Facebook page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the person singing Bollywood ghazal 'Na kisi ki aankh ka noor hoon' was not Kenyan. He is Sanjay Sawant, a singer from Maharashtra.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, saucer-shaped cloud, HAARP technology not linked to Feb 6 Turkiye earthquakes; Social media posts shared with misleading claims
content: New Delhi, Feb 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a rare cloud formation, linking it to America's HAARP technology and the Feb 6 earthquakes in Turkiye, which killed more than 31000 people and injured thousands of others. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the sizeable circular cloud formation was a natural weather phenomenon known as a lenticular cloud. Also, the HAARP Program Office at the University of Alaska, Fairbanks, rejected the claim that its weather technology was the reason behind the rare cloud formation or the earthquakes in Turkiye. The claim shared in the social media posts were misleading. Claim A Twitter user shared a 1:39-minute video which showed a sizeable saucer-shaped cloud formation, deep orange coloured at sunset, appearing in the sky and claimed it was observed in Turkiye before the devastating earthquakes hit the country on Feb 6. The user also mentioned America's HAARP technology, indicating a connection between the technology and the earthquakes. "WATCH: This creepy cloud allegedly appeared over Turkiye before the historic earthquake that has now claimed thousands of lives. Many Turks are linking the mysterious cloud with the Apocalyptic loss of lives through the 7.8 magnitude quake. Others say America's HAARP technology," read the Twitter post dated Feb 10. Over 220K people viewed the tweet, more than 1500 liked it, and 800 others shared the post. Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the Twitter post: The user posted a thread of eight tweets quoting different other users to bring HAARP technology and the rare cloud formation into the centre of discussion as reasons behind the deadly Turkiye tremors. The thread of the tweets can be seen here . Investigation To investigate the claims, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Twitter and found another tweet with the same claim and a video that captured the same occurrence from a different angle. The tweet that shared a 48-second video of the cloud read: "Last week, Turkiye cloud! Turkiye was attacked with HAARP." The tweet, which was published on Feb 7, garnered over 2.2 million views, 5500 likes and 2500 retweets. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post: The tweets had two different claims - the first one pertained to the rare cloud formation, and the second claim was about the HAARP technology as the reason behind the cloud formation and earthquakes that hit Turkiye and Syria on Feb 6. The Desk started investigating the claims, with the first claim on the rare cloud formation in Turkey before the earthquakes- Investigation – Claim 1 While scanning the comment section, the Desk noticed a user's reply with a screenshot of a report which suggested the rare cloud formation was observed in Turkiye's Bursa on Jan 19 this year. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "rare cloud formation, Bursa Turkiye". The search results led us to a YouTube video dated Jan 20, which showed several other visuals of the occurrence. The title of the YouTube video read: "lenticular clouds spotted over the sky of Bursa, Turkiye". According to the video's description, the occurrence was of "lenticular clouds" formed when "the air is stable and moist and winds originating from a similar direction blow across mountains at different altitudes through the troposphere". Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently found that several news portals reported on the formation of lenticular clouds as 'UFO-like clouds'. The reports can be seen here and here . What are Lenticular Clouds? Before proceeding to the next part of the claim, the Desk conducted another search with the keyword "lenticular cloud, Turkiye" to know more about the occurrence. The search results led us to a report by Daily Mail dated Jan 19, the day the phenomenon was observed in Bursa, which explained the phenomenon, quoting the Met Office. "They look a lot like the traditional shape of flying saucers in science fiction, and real lenticular clouds are believed to be one of the most common explanations for UFO sightings across the world," the report read. "When air blows across a mountain range, in certain circumstances, it can set up a train of large standing waves in the air downstream, rather like ripples forming in a river when water flows over an obstruction," it added. A report in The Washington Post read: "It was just a lenticular cloud — not uncommon in the vicinity of tall mountains." "Photographs and videos of the cloud have gone viral, captivating viewers around the world. Some have questioned the legitimacy of the images. But they're genuine, and they offer an opportunity to dive into some fascinating meteorology," added the WaPo report. An Insider report carried a photograph of the occurrence in Turkey on Jan 19 and quoted meteorologist Marshall Shepherd, a Forbes contributor, saying, "The brilliant colours of the cloud can be attributed to irisation, which is when droplets or ice particles cause light to spread or bend in clouds." Below is the screenshot of the report carrying the photo of the cloud- On the question of the formation of such clouds, a NASA report said: "Lenticulars are formed when strong winds blow across complex terrain, causing the water vapour in the air mass to alternately compress, then decompress, and thus condense into shapes which roughly mirror the terrain beneath. They are also near-certain indicators of turbulence." Continuing the search, the Desk also found a United Kingdom's Met Office report on the phenomenon of lenticular clouds, but no information linked it with earthquakes. Here is the link to the UK Met Office's report . Below is a screenshot of the page: We also came across the USA Government's National Weather Service (NWS) report on lenticular clouds. There was no mention of these clouds causing earthquakes in it. Another customised search in Google led us to a Reuters report dated Feb 7 titled, "Why was the Turkiye-Syria earthquake so bad?" "The East Anatolian Fault is a strike-slip fault. In those, solid rock plates are pushing against each other across a vertical fault line, building stress until one finally slips in a horizontal motion, releasing a tremendous amount of strain that can trigger an earthquake," it said. Also, the distance between Kahramanmaras in Turkiye's extreme southeast (The epicentre of the Feb 6 tremor) and Bursa in the northwest (Where the lenticular cloud was observed on Jan 19) is about 1,000 km. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the rare saucer-shaped clouds seen in Turkiye's Bursa on Jan 19 were due to a rare weather phenomenon called lenticular clouds. It had connections with the earthquakes that hit the country on Feb 6. Investigation – Claim 2 The other claim made in social media posts pertained to America's HAARP technology, which links to the Feb 6 earthquakes. The Desk started the investigation by gathering information about the technology. HAARP, which stands for High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program, was initially built as a joint project by the US Air Force and US Navy in 1993, with control transferred to the University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF) in 2015. The official website of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks , mentioned HAARP as "the world's most capable high-power, high-frequency transmitter for study of the ionosphere." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to the HAARP Program section of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks, via e-mail. In its reply to PTI, the institution categorically denied any link between the weather technology and the Feb 6 earthquakes, claiming that HAARP "cannot create or amplify natural disasters". "The recent earthquake and tragic loss of life in Turkiye highlight the destruction that natural disasters can cause. The research equipment at the HAARP site cannot create or amplify natural disasters," Jessica Matthews, HAARP program manager, told PTI. Below is the screenshot of the FAQ page shared by the Public Information Office of the UAF Geophysical Institute shared, which read: "Radio waves in the frequency ranges that HAARP transmits are not absorbed in either the troposphere or the stratosphere—the two levels of the atmosphere that produce Earth's weather. Since there is no interaction, there is no way to control the weather. The HAARP array (called the Ionospheric Research Instrument) is a large radio transmitter. Radio waves interact with electrical charges and currents and do not significantly interact with the troposphere. Further, if the ionospheric storms caused by the sun itself don't affect the surface weather, there is no chance that HAARP can either. Electromagnetic interactions only occur in the near vacuum of the atmosphere's rarefied but electrically charged region above about 60-80 km (a little over 45 miles), known as the ionosphere. The ionosphere is created and continuously replenished as the sun's radiation interacts with the highest levels of the Earth's atmosphere." Here is the link to the page . The University also rejected any relation between the HAARP technology and natural disasters, stating that its research campaigns are held at only one site in Gakona, Alaska, which operates approximately 2-4 times a year. Continuing the keyword-based customised search on Twitter, we found a post shared on Feb 3 about a possible "sooner or later 7.5 Magnitude+ earthquakes in the Turkey region". The tweet, which shared a region map, garnered more than 54 million views, 52k retweets, and 196k likes. Here is the link to the tweet . Below is the screenshot of the post- The Desk scanned the user's profile (Frank Hoogerbeets, @hogrbe) which suggested he was a researcher with Solar System Geometry Survey based in the Netherlands. In one of his tweets , he said: "I am not an 'oracle', 'mystic' or 'prophet', and I never give exact dates for larger earthquakes, as some (Turkish) media suggest. I am a researcher studying the relationship between earthquakes and planetary positions, and I developed specific software (#SSGI) for that purpose." However, there has to be an established scientific basis for earthquake predictions, and such claims should constantly be scrutinised for scientific evidence before sharing as real. The Desk subsequently concluded that the tectonic nature of the Earth was the possible reason behind the Feb 6 earthquakes in Turkiye, and it had nothing to do with the lenticular clouds observed in the country on Jan 19. Also, linking the Turkiye earthquake to the HAARP operations could not be established by any authentic source of information.

title: PTI Fact Check: 1962 photo of Jawaharlal Nehru shared in social media posts with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of former prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru claiming he was allegedly 'slapped by a Hindu saint' and 'forced to leave' from a meeting after the incident. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo, dating back to 1962, was from a Congress meeting in Patna where the crowd turned chaotic to catch a glimpse of the then-prime minister. The claim in the photo shared in the social media posts was false. Claim A Twitter user shared a black and white photo of India's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, claiming he was 'driven away' from a meeting, purportedly after being 'slapped' by a Hindu saint. The tweet has received over 1,000 views and 51 likes so far. The post, published on Feb 10, read in Hindi: "चौकिये मत। नेहरूजी के साथ कुछ गलत नहीं हो रहा है। अजमेर की एक सभा में नेहरूजी ने कहा कि हमने मुस्लिमों सहित शरणार्थियों का स्वागत किया है। इससे नाराज होकर एक संत विद्यानंद बिदेह ने नेहरू जी के गाल पर थप्पड़ मार दिया था। लोग घटनास्थल से नेहरूजी को भगाने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं." (Don't get surprised. Nothing wrong is happening with Nehruji. In a meeting at Ajmer, Nehruji said that we have welcomed Muslim refugees. Annoyed by this, saint Vidyananda Bideh slapped Nehru ji. People are trying help Nehruji leave from the incident place." Sic) Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is the screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo. The search results led us to another Twitter post from Sep 14, 2019, claiming that Nehru was allegedly slapped at a meeting for saying that "Aryans are refugees in India". Here are the links to the post and archive post , and below is its screenshot: Meanwhile, another tweet dating back to Jan 25, 2016, carried the same photo, claiming Nehru was "thrashed" by the people of Jammu and Kashmir following the "failure of the China war". Here are the links to the tweet shared by over 130 people and its archive post . Below is a screenshot of the Twitter post: Other similar Twitter posts carrying the photo with similar claims can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. Taking a cue on the possible time frame of the photo from the viral social media claims, the Desk conducted a Google search for the keyword "Jawaharlal Nehru, Congress meeting chaos, 1962". The search results led us to an AP Archives page, where the same photo was posted on Jan 1, 1962, and was titled "Nehru almost falls". "A security man grabbed Indian Prime Minister Nehru to keep him from plunging into a riotous crowd at a meeting of the Congress Party in Patna, India, January 1962. Later in the year, Communist China's attack on India plunged Nehru into new troubles," read the description of the photo. Here is the link to AP's gallery image , and below is a screenshot for the same. Since the caption stated that the photo had been taken at a Congress meeting in Patna in 1962, we searched through newspapers from the same period. We found an article about the incident from the Indian Express archives. The archive link to the Indian Express newspaper of Jan 5, 1962 edition and its screenshot below. The article states, "At one stage, an angry Nehru, obviously for his safety, used his fists and hit out at security men and Congress leaders who prevented him from jumping into the crowd." Below is a screenshot of the snippet. To find out what the incident was about, the Desk read the entire article. It stated that on Jan 5, 1962, a stampede broke up the Congress plenary session as a "seething mass of humanity" continually pressed forward to get a glimpse of Nehru. Page 7 of the newspaper, containing the details of the incident, mentioned: "The crowds who were pushing each other to have a glimpse of Mr Nehru were partially satisfied as they saw him address them for a few minutes. Mr Nehru made a special appeal to the crowd to see that no child or woman was pushed around. He asked all children and women caught up in the stampede to be allowed to come to the dais." Below is a screenshot of the snippet from the newspaper: The Desk also found an archive edition of The Florence Times, dated Jan 8, 1962, which carried the same AP photo. The caption read: "Security men hold back Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to prevent him from plunging into a raucous crowd in Patna, India, Friday, in a personal effort to restore order. A wild demonstration by Indian peasants broke up this meeting of Nehru's Congress Party and set 24 persons to the hospital." Here is the link to the archive edition of the newspaper, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a photo of Jawaharlal Nehru dating back to 1962 had been shared in social media posts with misleading claims over the years.

title: PTI Fact Check: Accused in Delhi's Nikki Yadav murder case not from minority community; Social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A 23-year-old Delhi girl named Nikki Yadav was allegedly killed by her live-in partner on the intervening night of Feb 9-10 for objecting to her partner's marriage with another girl. Soon after the media reported the crime, several posts floated on social media claiming a communal angle in the incident. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the accused, identified as 24-year-old Sahil Gahlot, was not from the Muslim community. The social media posts were shared with a false claim, giving it a communal spin. Claim A verified Twitter handle shared four photos of the deceased girl Nikki Yadav and her live-in partner Sahil Gehlot claiming that the 23-year-old's murder was yet another case of 'love jihad'. "भले ही कितने ही श्रद्धा मर्डर हो जाएं,भले ही कितनी निक्की यादव काट दी जाएं, लेकिन हम हिन्दू लड़कियां है जो कभी नहीं सुधरेंगी।कभी किसी हिन्दू का घर नहीं बसायेंगी,बस "लव जेहादियों" से गले कटवायेगी। #निक्की_यादव," read the tweet dated Feb 15, which has garnered nearly 2000 views and over 50 likes to date. The tweet roughly translated to English: "No matter how many Shraddhas are killed, no matter how many Nikki Yadavs are cut, we Hindu girls will never change. We will never settle a Hindu's house, jet our throats cut by 'Love Jihadis'." Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post . Below is a screenshot of the Twitter post. Investigation The Desk started the investigation by scanning social media platforms, looking for similar claims. We found two Facebook posts. Claiming that Nikki Yadav's murder was a 'love jihad' case. The posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. Below are the screenshots of the two Facebook posts: We also found two tweets hinting that the accused was a Muslim. The Twitter posts can be seen here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. Below are the screenshots of the two Twitter posts: To verify the veracity of the claims in social media posts, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found a PTI report carried by The Print, which stated the accused, Sahil Gahlot was a resident of Mitraon village in southwest Delhi. He was arrested on Feb 14 by the police. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk contacted the Delhi Police Crime Branch for more details and to ascertain whether the accused was a Muslim, as claimed in social media posts. We accessed the FIR copy of the case, which mentioned Sahil Gahlot as a resident of Mitraon village in the Najafgarh area and his father's name as Virendar Singh. Below is a screenshot of the relevant section of the FIR copy: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the accused was not a Muslim, as claimed in social media posts. About the case After going through the FIR and scanning news reports, the Desk found that Nikki and Sahil had been in a relationship since 2018 and were living together in Dwarka. The 24-year-old accused – a pharma student – killed his live-in partner on the night of Feb 9-10 after she objected to his marriage with another woman fixed by Sahil's family. When Nikki confronted Sahil about his marriage, he reportedly killed her using the data cable of his mobile phone in his car and then kept her body in a refrigerator at his dhaba in Mitraon village, a senior police officer told PTI. The accused then got married to another woman the same day. Both families claimed they were unaware of the relationship between Nikki and Sahil. When the latter's family learned about Nikki, they fixed his marriage with another woman. Sahil, however, did not tell Nikki about this. She confronted him when she learned that her partner's marriage had been fixed somewhere else. The two went out of the house on the night of Feb 9. After fighting in the car for around 2 hours, Sahil allegedly strangled her with a charging cable near the Kashmere Gate area. Unable to decide what to do next, Sahil took the body to this dhaba and hit it in the refrigerator. Later in the day, on Feb 10, he got married. The police said they acted on a secret tip-off to capture the accused, who later admitted to killing Nikki. The body was recovered on Feb 14, four days after the murder.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photos of PM Modi wearing Islamic skullcap digitally altered; Social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared two photos of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in which he was shown 'wearing the Islamic skullcap'. The PTI Fact Check found that the images were digitally altered and shared in the social media post with a false claim. Claim "Shinde was shocked.. thought for a moment "did I shake hands with AIMIM?" read the tweet dated Feb 11, which garnered over 4500 views and 100 likes. The caption referred to Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde standing beside PM Modi in the first photo. Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the Twitter post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the first photo shared in the Twitter post. We found a report by Mid-Day dated Feb 10, which carried a similar picture, but showed PM Modi without a skullcap. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the photo caption mentioned the credits to Eknath Shinde's Twitter account. Taking a cue from this, we searched Shinde's official Twitter handle and found a post dated Feb 10, which carried several photos from the event attended by PM Modi, including the one shared in the Twitter post. We could not see PM Modi wearing a Muslim skullcap in the photos. Here is the link to the Twitter post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The tweet in Marathi was roughly translated to English as: "'Aljamiya-Tus-Safiya' Arabic Educational Institute at Andheri Marol, Mumbai was inaugurated today under the auspices of Prime Minister Hon'ble @narendramodi ji. Deputy Chief Minister @Dev_Fadnavis was also present on this occasion." In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image search on the second photo shared in the Twitter post. The search results led us to a Twitter post shared from PM Modi's official Twitter handle on Feb 10. The post included several photos from the event, including the one shared in a Twitter post. In none of the images the prime minister was seen wearing a Muslim skullcap. Here is the link to the Twitter post , and below is the screenshot of the same: The event was the inauguration of the new Mumbai campus of the Aljamea-tus-Saifiyah, an Arabic academy. The person seen with PM Modi in the photos is Syedna Mufaddal Saifuddin, leader of the Dawoodi Bohra community, which has been the focus of the BJP's outreach to the minority communities. Subsequentially, the Desk concluded that digitally altered PM Modi to make it look like he wore a Muslim cap was shared in social media posts with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, WHO never issued advisory on milk contamination in India; Claim shared in social media post was false
content: New Delhi, Feb 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a newspaper clipping claiming that the WHO issued an advisory on milk contamination in India was shared on WhatsApp recently. The screenshot of the report claimed that if milk adulteration were not checked, 87% of people in the country would have cancer by 2025. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the World Health Organisation never issued any such warning as claimed in the report. The claim shared in social media posts was baseless. Claim The Desk received a photo on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 with a request to verify the claim. The screenshot – an image of a Hindi newspaper clipping – was of an article with the headline, "दूध नहीं जहर पीता है इंडिया, उत्पादन 14 करोड़ लीटर लेकिन खपत 64 करोड़ लीटर" The English translation of the title read: "Not milk, India is consuming poison, production 14 crore litre but consumption 64 crore litre". The report's subhead read: "WHO warns - "87% Indians will have cancer by 2025 if adulteration is not stopped". In the report, it was claimed that the Animal Welfare Board members had intimated government that 68.7 per cent of milk or milk products sold in the country were not as per the standards laid down by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). Below is a screenshot of the photo: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by conducting a Google Reverse Image search on the photo. The search results led us to several Facebook posts which shared the same photo with the same claim. Three such Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here . Their archive posts can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. The Desk also came across a news article by Dainik Bhaskar, dated Sep 20, 2018. The headline of the article read: "चौंकाने वाला खुलासा : रोज सुबह दूध नहीं, जहर पी रहे हैं आप... क्योंकि देश में बिकने वाला 68.7 फीसदी दूध निकला नकली; WHO ने भी जारी की चेतावनी". The Desk noticed that the Dainik Bhaskar was published a day after the date mentioned in the photo of the purported newspaper clipping, i.e. Sep 19. The viral photo mentioned the article was by Money Bhaskar. Here are the links to the article and its archive post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a Google search for the keyword "WHO warning on milk adulteration in India" and found a press note issued by the organisation regarding the viral news reported by a section of the media in September 2018. "Contrary to reports in a section of media, which would like to state that it has not issued any advisory to the Government of India on the issue of adulteration of milk/milk products," read the press note. Here is the link to the WHO press note , and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results also led us to a PDF file of Lok Sabha proceedings dating back to November 2019 when the claim had resonated in the Parliament. The then Union Health Minister Dr Harsh Vardhan, replying to a Parliament member's question on reports of WHO warning on adulterated milk, said that the global agency issued no such advisory to the Government of India. Here is the link to the then-health minister's response to the question in Lok on Nov 22, 2019, and below is a screenshot of the same: Harsh Vardhan also refuted the claim made in the viral photo that 68.7 per cent of milk and milk products sold in India were not as per standards laid down by the FSSAI. "The Nationwide Milk Safety and Quality Survey conducted by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) in 2018 revealed that only 7% (456 out of a total of 6,432 samples) had contaminants (antibiotics, pesticides and aflatoxin M1) that make milk unsafe for consumption. Further, only 12 out of 6,432 samples had adulterants that affected milk safety. These 12 samples include six samples adulterated with hydrogen peroxide, three samples adulterated with detergents, two samples adulterated with urea, and one sample was found to have neutraliser," he stated in the Parliament. Here is a screenshot of Harsh Vardhan's reply in Parliament: In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk searched the annual milk production and consumption in India and found the latest details in the Economic Survey 2021-22. According to the survey, the annual milk production in the country in 2020-21 stood at 209.96 million tonnes, which converts to 18,460.67 crores in litres. This means that an average of 50.58 crore litres of milk was produced daily in the fiscal year 2020-21. Here is the link to the Economy Survey report , and below is the screenshot of the same: The data disapproved the claim made in the viral newspaper clipping that annual milk production in India was 14 crore litres against the yearly consumption of 64 crore litres. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the WHO never issued any advisory to the Government of India on adulterating milk and dairy products. Since the newspaper clipping had quoted Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) member Mohan Singh Ahluwalia, the Desk reached out to him and the AWBI for their comment. We will update the article as soon as they reply to our queries shared on e-mail with them.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, military personnel at Indonesian airport were not Chinese troops; Video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of military personnel lined up at an Indonesian airport, claiming the Chinese troops entered the country to protect its workers there. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the military personnel at the Indonesian airport was part of a specialised unit of the Indonesian National Police. The claim in the video shared on social media was false. Claim A Facebook user shared a video showing scores of military personnel at an airport in Indonesia, claiming the Chinese troops entered the country to protect China. The post published on Feb 2 was in Indonesian, had a 25-second video clip, and garnered around 600 views. The English translation of the post read: "Chinese communists threaten Indonesia. The Chinese Army has entered Indonesia to protect Chinese TKA." (TKA is an abbreviation for 'foreign workforce' in Malay, Indonesia's official language.) Here are the links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid tool search on the video and found a few keyframes of the footage. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Twitter post dated Feb 3, carrying the same video with a similar claim. The post's English translation, originally in Indonesian and received over 1,200 views, read: "If this news is true, extraordinary. Yesterday, Chinese foreign workers came to Indonesia wearing work uniforms. Now the Red Army soldiers from mainland China are coming to our country wearing military uniforms. News about this, until now, there has been no response from the authorities!" Here are the links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot- The Desk subsequently conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Chinese military personnel arrive in Indonesia". Still, they could not find any report to support the claim in the social media posts. However, we found an Instagram post by the verified account of Divisi Humas Polri, which is the public relations division of the Indonesian Police, clarifying that the military personnel visible in the video were Brimob troops arriving in the country after serving at the Cartenz Peace Task Force in Papua. Here is the link to the post , and below is its screenshot- The English translation of the Instagram post, which was in Indonesian, read: "A video has been circulating on the TikTok @ 99bima_satria" account with the narration "What's wrong with our police and the Chinese army. The video sourced from that account was deliberately made to spread societal anxiety. The Public Relations Division of the National Police confirmed that the video was NOT TRUE or a HOAX. The video shows Brimob troops arriving after serving at the Cartenz Peace Task Force, Papua." The Mobile Brigade Corps abbreviated 'Brimob', is the special operations, paramilitary, and tactical unit of the Indonesian National Police. Operation Cartenz' Peace, formerly Operation Nemangkawi, was a joint operation conducted by the Indonesian National Armed Forces and National Police to curb armed separatist rebels in Papua. The Desk searched for more about the peace operation and found a report on the Tempo—Co website. The report's headline read: "Indonesian Police Extend Cartenz Peace Operation in Papua until June 2023". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: While searching for more information, the Desk also found a 1:31-minute video of the Cartenz Peace operation on YouTube, with the channel mentioning it as the official one of Brimob's PR division. The video's title, dated Dec 29, 2022, read: "PEMBERANGKATAN OPS DAMAI CARTENZ 2022". When translated to English, it read: "CARTENZ PEACE OPS DEPARTURE 2022". Here is the link to the video , and below is a screengrab of the same: We noticed that the official dress of the Indonesian security personnel in the video had striking similarities with the troops' clothing in the video clip shared on social media posts. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos- After watching the two videos, we also noticed that the security personnel in both videos had a small-sized national flag of Indonesia on their arms in the dress. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos- Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the troops in the video clip shared in social media posts were a particular unit of the Indonesian Police.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of Delhi woman assaulting cab driver shared in social media posts as recent
content: New Delhi, Feb 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video of a woman manhandling a cab driver following a heated argument claiming it happened recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a video of a two-year-old incident. The old video was shared on social media without any context. Claim An Instagram user shared a video of a woman arguing with a cab driver, grabbing him by the collar and manhandling him. The post, published on Feb 15 and garnered over 5,700 views, read: "Delhi cab driver successfully rescued". Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is a screenshot of the page- Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid tool search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to another Instagram post where the same video had been shared on Feb 15. Here are the links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. The video received over 3,000 likes and was captioned, "Delhi cab driver successfully rescued." Since the caption mentioned that the incident had been reported from Delhi, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Delhi woman argument cab driver" and found a report by the India Today website published on Nov 18, 2021. The report's headline read: "Delhi woman slaps and punches cab driver in a viral video. Punish her, says Internet". Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot. The Desk noticed that the report carried an extended version of the video in which the woman was seen slapping and punching the cab driver. The video was posted by a Twitter user on Nov 21, 2021. Here is the link to the tweet . "The video is from Delhi's Patel Nagar. It was shared by Twitter user Aditya Singh on November 17," the report stated. "…a woman was seen in the middle of the road, slapping and punching a cab driver. The man did nothing to resist the woman from hitting her. The bystanders came to the man's rescue and questioned the anonymous woman's unruly behaviour," it added. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the two videos– one shared in the recent Instagram post and the other shared in the tweet from the news report in 2021. The Desk subsequently conducted another Google search with the keywords "Delhi woman assaults cab driver" and found another report by the Times Now website published on Nov 17, 2021. The report's headline read: "In a rerun of Lucknow's 'thappad kaand', woman slaps cab driver in public view in Delhi – WATCH" Here is the link to the article . The Times Now article too carried the same video shared in the recent Instagram post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video clip of a two-year-old incident of a woman assaulting a cab driver in Delhi was shared as recent in social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: Job for 'weed smokers' announced by a German company falsely linked to UP Govt in social media posts
content: New Delhi, Feb 18 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A photo with a logo of a Hindi news channel was shared on social media claiming the Uttar Pradesh government offered a job opportunity for 'weed smokers' with a salary of over Rs 80 lakh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a social media post by a news channel's website shared out of context. The claim in the tweet shared with the photo was false. Claim A verified Twitter handle representing the media cell of the Samajwadi Party shared a photo with a Hindi news channel 'ABP Live' logo, claiming that 'weed smokers' will get jobs with a salary of over Rs 80 lakh in Uttar Pradesh. The text in the post read: "योगीराज में कुछ भी संभव है (Anything is possible in Yogi-raj)" "गांजा पीने वालों के लिए नौकरी आई, सैलरी 80 लाख से ज्यादा (Job for week smokers, salary over Rs 80 lakh)," read the text on the photo in the tweet posted on Feb 16 and garnered over 78K views and nearly 1400 likes. Here are the links to the tweet and the archive post . Below is a screenshot of the page: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in a Twitter post. The search results led us to another carrying the same picture with the same claim. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post . Below is a screenshot of the Twitter post - The Desk went through the comment sections of the Twitter posts and found several users mentioning that a company in Germany announced the job for 'weed smokers'. Here is the link to one such comment , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "job for weed smokers". The search results led us to a report by The Tribune website, dated Feb 16. The report headline read: "German pharma company lays out job offer for 'weed smokers', offers a whopping salary of Rs 88 lakh." Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted another report by The Sun, according to which Cologne-based Cannamedical company sought a worker who could "smell, feel, and smoke" its product. The Desk also found an Instagram post by ABP News with the same photo as shared in social media posts. "जर्मनी की एक कंपनी ने गांजा पीने वालों के लिए नौकरी निकाली है. इसके लिए जो सैलरी रखी गई है वो आपके होश उड़ा सकती है. कंपनी इस काम के लिए लगभग 88 लाख रुपये तक देने को तैयार है. Cannamedical को ऐसे व्यक्ति की जरूरत है जो कैनाबिस से बने उनके प्रोडक्ट को चख सके. आपका इस नौकरी पर क्या ख्याल है, कमेंट कर बताइए," read the Instagram post dated Feb 16, which has garnered over 60K likes to date. When translated to English, the post read: "A German company has announced a job for those who smoke marijuana. The salary for this job will blow your mind. The company is ready to pay up to Rs 88 lakh for this work. Cannamedical needs someone who can taste their cannabis products. Comment what you think about this job." Here is the link to the Instagram post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The ABP Live website also published a news report on Feb 16. The headline of the article read: "गांजा पीने वालों को नौकरी दे रही है ये कंपनी, सेलेक्ट हुए तो सैलरी मिलेगी 88 लाख रुपये (This company is offering job to week smokers, will get salary of Rs 88 lakh if selected)". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report stated that the job was announced by a German pharmaceutical company named Cannamedical for someone who could "smell, feel, and smoke" its product. When the Desk searched for the company's details, it found a report on the EU Start-ups website . Founded in 2016, Cannamedical began operating following the legalisation of medical cannabis in Germany in March 2017. The company now employs around 40 employees in Cologne, generating a €1 million turnover, according to a report published on the EU start-up website in Jan 2019. The report said: "Cologne-based medical marijuana startup Cannamedical Pharma GmbH is one of Germany and the EU's leading cannabis wholesalers. Its products include high-quality cannabis varieties, cannabinoid oil, medical marijuana grinders, and patient ID cards to treat medical conditions including cancer and chronic pain." The detail can be read here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a photo reporting about a job for 'weed smokers' in Germany was shared in social media posts, falsely linking it with the UP government.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally morphed video of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan with Dhirendra Shastri of Bageshwar shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and her daughter Aaradhya with Dhirendra Krishna Shastri of Bageshwar Dham Temple was shared on social media, claiming the Bollywood actor met the self-styled godman recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that two separate and unrelated videos were edited and combined to make it look like Aishwarya met Shastri at a recent event. The fake video was uploaded on YouTube and later shared with a false claim on social media. Claim A YouTube video showed Bollywood actor Aishwarya Rai Bachchan with her daughter Aaradhya visiting Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, also known as Bageshwar Dham Sarkar of Bageshwar Dham Temple. The footage showed Shastri addressing a few health problems, after which the narrator stated that the former also gave suggestions for Aishwarya's husband and actor Abhishek Bachchan and predicted the future of Aaradhya. The video headline posted on Feb 11 read: "Bageshwar Dham baba ke pas pahuchi Aishwarya Rai Bachan ll (what do people make) #viral #motivation". Here is the link and the archive link to the YouTube video. Below is a screenshot of the page: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided 30 keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes along with the keyword "Bageshwar Dham" led us to the Instagram account of Shastri. On scanning the account, the Desk found a Jan 8 post which showed Shastri wearing the same pink-coloured outfit as seen in the YouTube video. The caption of the post read: "हमारे सरकार का दीदार….नागपुर". Here is the link to the Instagram post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the post and its caption, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Bageshwar Dham Sarkar, Jan 8 satsang, Nagpur". The investigation led us to a live video of one of his satsangs – Divya Darbar –held in Nagpur, Maharashtra, on Jan 8. The title of the video, which was live-streamed by Bageshwar Dham Sarkar's official YouTube channel, read: "LIVE: Divya Darbar "दिव्य दरबार" | 08 Jan | Bageshwar dham Sarkar | Nagpur, Maharashtra". Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of its page: The Desk went through the 2:58:38-hour video. At 1:27:15 timestamp, Shastri can be heard making statements about stomach problems and intestinal and liver infections. The Desk closely watched the two videos – the viral one and the other posted by Shastr''s YouTube channel – and found them to be the same. Below is a comparison of screenshots of the two videos: In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk performed a separate Google Reverse Image Search on a keyframe showing Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and her daughter Aaradhya. We came across a YouTube video uploaded on October 10, 2019, by a secret media hacker'. The title of the video read, "Aishwarya Rai With Daughter Aaradhya Bachchan Maa Durga Puja 2019". Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of its page: The Desk compared the visuals of the two videos – the one shared on YouTube recently and the other uploaded in 2019 – and found them to be the same. We compared another visual seen in both videos, proving that visuals from the 2019 video were clipped and used in the viral video. The Desk also found reports by the Filmfare and the Vogue India websites on Bachchan's visit to the Durga Puja pandals in Mumbai on Oct 8, 2019. The reports can be viewed here and here . In the next investigation step, we conducted a Google search with the keyword "Aishwarya Rai visits Bageshwar Dham" but found no authentic report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was made using clips from two old and unrelated videos.

title: PTI Fact Check: 5-year-old video of Varanasi flyover collapse shared as recent in social media posts with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of several vehicles trapped under a collapsed flyover claiming the incident happened recently in the Thane district in Maharashtra. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was related to the flyover collapse incident in Varanasi in May 2018. The video was recently shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a 45-second video clip of several cars being crushed and trapped under what looked like a huge cement slab. The user claimed in the post, dated Feb 15, that the incident occurred in Thane "just now". "It's in Thane just now," read the Twitter post, which garnered over 1,200 views to date. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the page: (Warning: The video includes abusive language. Viewer discretion is advised.) Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found six keyframes. We then conducted a separate Google Reverse Image search on each keyframe. We came across another Twitter post dated Feb 18, which carried an extended version of the same video and claimed that 19 people died in a bridge collapse in Thane. With over 2000 views, the tweet read: "Bridge collapsed in thane which became the reason for the death of 19 people DEATH' IS UNPREDICTABLE #DEATH #ACCIDENT #CARACCIDENT #viral #Incident." Here are the links to the tweet containing the 58-second video and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: We searched Google with the keywords "Thane bridge collapse" and "Thane flyover collapse" but could not find any authentic report carrying such news. Had such a mishap happened, it would have grabbed the headlines across news channels and outlets. The Desk, however, found a YouTube video by ABP News, dated May 16, 2018, reporting a flyover collapse in Varanasi. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The video, titled "Varanasi Flyover Collapse: Most Of The UP Roadways Bus Passengers Lost Their Lives | ABP News", included similar visuals as shown in the video clip shared in Twitter posts. The Desk found another YouTube report by The Outlook published on May 15, 2018, on Varanasi's flyover collapse, which carried similar visuals. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for specific keywords. This led us to an article by The Indian Express dated May 16, 2018, which carried details of the incident. The headline read: "Varanasi flyover collapse: 18 dead, FIR against the govt-run corporation; top 10 developments". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video clip of a five-year-old mishap in Varanasi was shared in social media posts, claiming a recent flyover collapse in Maharashtra's Thane.

title: PTI Fact Check: Man in viral photo was not Vicks VapoRub inventor; Social media posts shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of an African-American man claiming he was Lunsford Richardson, the inventor of Vicks VapoRub -- a widely used cold-relieving ointment -- who invented the lotion when his three kids were sick. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man in the photo was not Lunsford Richardson but an entrepreneur tobacconist named Lunsford Lane. Lunsford Richardson created Vicks VapoRub out of love and concern for his sick son Smith Richardson. The social media post was shared with misleading claims. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of an African-American man claiming he was Lunsford Richardson, the inventor of Vicks VapoRub, a globally famous cold relief ointment. The post, published on Dec 19 last year, and garnered over 31,000 views and 900 likes, read: "BLACK HISTORY FACT: In 1880, African American Lunsford Richardson from Selma, NC, invented Vicks Vapor Rub! He invented this remedy when all 3 of his kids were sick while living in Greensboro, NC. Richardson thought that his brother-in-law, last name Joshua "Vick", had a catchier sound to it than his own. Richardson has also been accredited for the invention of headache powders. THANK YOU, MR. RICHARDSON! (sic)." Here are the links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Twitter post and found that the same photo was shared in social media posts last year. Two such Twitter posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be seen here and here . When the Desk scanned the comments on the tweets, and noticed a few other users claimed that the man in the photo was not Lunsford Richardson, the inventor of Vicks VaporRub. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "who invented Vicks VapoRub" and found a report on the official website of Vicks . The report mentioned Lunsford Richardson as the founder of Vicks and the inventor of Vicks VapoRub and carried his photo in it. Here is a link to the page and a screenshot of the same: It was visible that both the photos were different; the Desk subsequently conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the picture in the social media post and found a report by the North Carolina History Project. It stated that the person in the photo was Lunsford Lane, an entrepreneur tobacconist and abolitionist born in North Carolina. "He (Lane) is most famous for writing a slave narrative that included descriptions of his business activities while in bondage and his troubles securing his and his family's freedom," the article stated. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot. The Desk also found the life account of Lane on the website Documenting the American South (DocSouth). Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched for why the Vicks VapoRub was invented, and found a detailed story on its official website about how Lunsford Richardson invented Vicks VapoRub and how the ointment was named Vicks VepoRub. According to the website, Lunsford invented Conia Salve, later named Vicks VapoRub, "out of love and concern for his sick son" in 1894. Here is the link to the article , and below is the screenshot of the page: While scanning the website, the Desk found the article highlighted that "Lunsford chose Vicks over his name as an avid gardener and saw an advertisement for Vick's Seeds. He felt it was short, easy to remember, and looked good on a label. Dr Joshua Vick was also the name of Lunsford's brother-in-law, and as the long-serving town doctor, he was equally trusted in the community and was happy to allow Lunsford to use his last name for his line of products." The Desk subsequently concluded that the man in the photo shared in social media posts was not Lunsford Richardson, the inventor of Vicks VapoRub. Also, Vicks' official website mentions that Richardson invented the ointment in 1894, not 1880, 'out of love and concern for his sick son'.

title: PTI Fact Check: Selected part of PM Modi's Rajya Sabha speech shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared two video clips of PM Modi's 'vote of thanks' speech delivered in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha recently, claiming the prime minister gave two different numbers of the beneficiaries of the Jal Jeevan Mission in his speeches in both Houses of Parliament. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claim in the social media post was misleading as PM Modi did not change the number of the tap water project beneficiaries in his speeches. In his first vote of thanks speech in Lok Sabha on Feb 8, PM Modi said that the Jal Jeevan Mission included eight crore beneficiaries of the drinking water project since its launch three years before. However, in his Rajya Sabha speech the next day, he said the total number of beneficiaries crossed 11 crores this year, including three crores existing till 2014. Jal Jeevan Mission is a flagship programme the Narendra Modi-led central government started in 2019 to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections by 2024 to all households in rural India. Claim A Facebook user shared a video that included two clips of PM Modi's 'vote of thanks' speeches in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha earlier in February. The user claimed that PM Modi overstated the number of tap water beneficiaries under the Jal Jeevan Mission by three crores in his Rajya Sabha speech than the figure he mentioned in the Lok Sabha speech a day earlier. The Facebook post, which garnered over 6300 likes and 1700 shares, read: "सरेआम मोदी का झूठ पकडाया !!! लोकसभा में मोदी ने बताया कि नल जल योजना के लाभार्थी '𝟴 करोड़' हैं। दूसरे ही दिन राज्यसभा में मोदी नल जल योजना के लाभार्थी की संख्या'𝟭𝟭 करोड़' बताते हैं। महज 21 घंटे में '𝟯 करोड़' लाभार्थी बढ़ गए। आरएसएस की पहली ट्रेनिंग ही झूठ से शुरू होती है।" ("Modi's lie caught publicly!!! Modi told in Lok Sabha that the number of beneficiaries of the Nal Jal Yojana is 8 crore. The very next day, he stated in the Rajya Sabha the number of beneficiaries of Nal Jal Yojana as 11 crore. 'Three crore' beneficiaries increased in just 21 hours. The very first training of RSS starts with a lie." (Sic)). Here are the link and the archive link to the post. Below is the screenshot of the page– Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a keyword search on Twitter and found a similar post shared by the official handle of the Congress party on Feb 9. The tweet read: "PM मोदी के फेंकने का नमूना देखिए। कल लोकसभा में बताया कि नल जल योजना के लाभार्थी '𝟴 करोड़' हैं। आज राज्यसभा में बताया कि नल जल योजना के लाभार्थी '𝟭𝟭 करोड़' हैं। महज 21 घंटे में '𝟯 करोड़' लाभार्थी बढ़ गए। ये कौन सा जादू है?" (Here's an example of PM Modi bluffs. He told Lok Sabha yesterday that the beneficiaries of the Nal Jal Yojana are '8 crore'. He said in Rajya Sabha today that the beneficiaries of Nal Jal Yojana are '11 crore'. 'Three crore' beneficiaries increased in just 21 hours. What magic is this?" The post received 743K views, over 11,000 likes and more than 4,200 retweets. Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet, and below is the screenshot of the page- Taking a cue from the date mentioned in the videos shared in social media posts, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "PM Modi's Lok Sabha speech, Feb 8". We found a YouTube video of Narendra Modi's reply to the motion of thanks to the President's address in the Lok Sabha, posted by Sansad TV on Feb 8. The video headline read: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Reply | Motion of Thanks on President's Address in Lok Sabha". The Desk watched the entire speech of PM Modi's Lok Sabha speech and noticed he talked about the Nal Jal Yojana at 57:30 minutes in the YouTube video. "आज़ादी के ७५ साल बीत गए। आठ करोड़ परिवारों को आज नल से जल मिला है। वो माताएं तुम्हारे झूठ को कैसे स्वीकार करेंगी? तुम्हारी गलतियों को, गालियों को, कैसे स्वीकार करेंगी? (75 years of Independence have passed. 8 crore families have got 'Nal se Jal' today. How will those mothers accept your lies? How will they accept your mistakes and abuses?)", said PM Modi in the relevant portion of the speech. Here is the link to the YouTube video . Below is a screenshot of the page: Continuing the investigation, the Desk conducted another Google search with the keyword "PM Modi Rajya Sabha speech Feb 9" and found a YouTube video by Sansad TV posted on the same date. The video headline read: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Reply | Motion of Thanks on President's Address in Rajya Sabha". While watching the video, the Desk found that the PM mentioned the Nal Jal scheme at 13:13 minutes in his speech video. When talked about the drinking water scheme, the PM said: "आज़ादी के पहले से अब तक, हम सरकार में आये तब तक, सिर्फ तीन करोड़ घरों तक नल से जल मिलता था। आदरणीय सभापति जी, पिछले तीन-चार साल में, आज, 11 करोड़ लोगों को नल से जल मिल रहा है|" (From the time before Independence till the formation of our government (in 2014), only 3 crore people used to get tap water. Respected Chairman, since the past three-four years, 11 crore families have been now receiving water from tap connections). In the video, PM Modi stated that since Independence until the Narendra Modi-led govt was formed at the Centre, only three crore families could get drinking water from tap-water connections. As a result of the Nal Jal Jeevan scheme launched in 2019, eight crore additional households got tap water connections in the last three years. The PM further said 11 crore families are receiving water from tap connections. It was evident that a smaller clip of his Rajya Sabha speech video was shared in social media posts with a misleading claim. Here is the link to the video. Below is a screenshot of the page: In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk scanned the official website of the Jal Jeevan Mission for the latest data on the number of project beneficiaries. The website shows that 7,98,87,738 households have been provided water connections since the scheme's launch in 2019. Below is the screenshot of the website, which has the data of the households that had the tap water connections on Aug 15, 2019, and now on Feb 21, 2023. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the webpage: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to Prahlad Singh Patel, the Union Minister of State for Food Processing Industries and Jal Shakti in the Narendra Modi government at the Centre. "The Congress is misleading on this. The number of tap water beneficiaries stood at 3.23 crore till the launch of the Jal Jeevan Mission in 2019. The figure now stands at 11 crores. This means that eight crore families have been provided tap water connections since the programme's launch, as stated by our prime minister. There should not be any confusion about this": Patel told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that PM Modi did not inflate the number of beneficiaries receiving water from tap connections in one of his speech videos shared on social media posts. A smaller version of his speech in Rajya Sabha recently was shared in social media posts with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Mixture of tomato pulp, lemon juice, toothpaste doesn't whiten teeth in minutes; Social media post shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook video shared as WhatsApp forward claimed that a mixture of tomato pulp, lemon juice and toothpaste whitens teeth within 2-3 minutes. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claim made in social media posts was misleading. A dental expert told PTI that using such products in the name of home remedies could damage the enamel, the protective layer of teeth. Claim The Desk received a Facebook post on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 with a request to verify if the claim in it was genuine. A 3:41-minute video was shared in the Facebook post by a page named 'Our Pure Tips' on June 10, 2021, showing the process of mixing tomato pulp, lemon juice and toothpaste. "Teeth whitening at home in 2 minutes how to naturally whiten your yellow teeth," read the video's caption, which garnered 11,000 likes and 1800 shares. Here are the links to the Facebook post and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation and found the same video published on YouTube claiming teeth whitening in "just 2 minutes" by applying a mixture of tomato pulp, toothpaste and lemon juice. "In just 2 minutes | How to Whiten Teeth with Tomato at Home," read the caption of the video posted in May 2020, which over 5,300 people have viewed to date. Here are the links to the video and its archive post , and below is the screenshot of the same: Continuing the investigation, the Desk searched Google with the keyword "impact of tomato pulp and lemon juice on teeth". The search results led us to a report by the ScienceDirect website explaining how citric acid (found in lemon) could damage the enamel, the protective layer of the teeth. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Further customised search in Google led us to another report by the Express.co.uk website quoting Dr Richard Marques, a dentist, who highlighted the impact of lemon and tomato consumption on teeth. Here is the link to the article titled "Diet warning: Eating THESE seven unlikely foods could DAMAGE your teeth for good". Below is the screenshot of the paragraphs of the report which described the high use of lemon and tomato as not good for the teeth- Tomatoes In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Dr Vaibhav Gupta, Dental Surgeon and Implantologist, to check the claim's authenticity. Dr Gupta categorically refuted the claim made in the social media post. "This is misleading information. These tricks in the name of home remedies don't work. The acids in tomato (oxalic acid) and lemon (citric acid) will permanently damage teeth's safety layer, i.e. Enamel, leading to teeth hypersensitivity. The only safest way to get your teeth whitening is to visit your professional dentist and get it done correctly," Dr Gupta told PTI. The Desk also scanned the Facebook page 'Our Pure Tips', which shared a video on tomato pulp and lemon juice for teeth whitening, and found that it had mentioned its website in the About section. The website's About us page mentioned a disclaimer that the content and videos were "only intended for informational purposes". "This channel doesn't take any responsibility for any harm, side effects, illness, or any health or skin care problems caused due to the use of our content or anything related to this," it stated. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim of teeth whitening through tomato pulp and lemon juice in the Facebook video was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Pakistan peddled as recent from Jaipur on social media with the false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyish Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a crowd under a flyover, claiming the people recited the Hanuman Chalisa in response to the namaz in Rajasthan's Jaipur. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video shared on social media dates back to January 2021 from Pakistan's Lahore. The claim video was shared in social media posts with misleading claims. Claim A Twitter user shared a 30-second video clip which showed a huge crowd gathered under a flyover. The user claimed that the video was from Jaipur, where Hindus gathered in unprecedented numbers and recited Hanuman Chalisa, responding to the namaz by Muslims. "जयपुर में नमाज का जवाब देते हुए रामभक्तों ने बीच सड़क पर हनुमान चालीसा अप्रत्याशित तादात में एकत्रित हो कर पढ़कर देश के हिन्दुत्व को गौरवान्वित किए। इसके लिए बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद जय सिया राम," read the post dated Feb 15. "Responding to Namaz in Jaipur, the devotees of Ram made the country's Hindutva proud by reciting Hanuman Chalisa in an unprecedented number in the middle of the road. Thank you so much, Jai Siya Ram," read the English translation of the tweet. The Twitter post has garnered over 7,600 views, more than 740 likes, and 250 retweets to date. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video and found a few keyframes of the same. A Google Reverse Image search on one of them led the Desk to another Twitter post shared on Jun 19 last, which carried the same video with a similar claim. "Jaipur me namaz ka jawab dete huye ram bhakt sadak par Hanuman chalisa padh rahe hain inki tadaad dekh kar dil khush ho gaya hum proud fill karte hain ki hum hindu hain," read the tweet. An English tweet translation read: "Responding to Namaz, Ram Bhakts are reciting Hanuman Chalisa on the road. The heart is full of joy seeing their numbers. We are proud to be Hindus." Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a YouTube video posted on Jan 4, 2021. The 30-second video clip shared by Labbaik News was the same as the one shared in social media posts. The 'About' page of the channel showed that Labbaik News was a Pakistani channel. The headline of the video read: "Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi Chehlum | TLP Chehlum 2021". Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Allama Khadim Hussain Rizvi Chehlum" and found an article by The Print, reporting about the death of Khadim Hussain Rizvi, chief of the Tehreek-e-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP) on Nov 19, 2020. "Khadim Hussain Rizvi, Pakistan's 'blasphemy activist', dies in Lahore at 54," read the report's headline dated Nov 20, 2020. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: We conducted a separate Google search for the term 'Chehlum' and found that it meant remembrance and prayer service on or about the fortieth day after the death of a person. Khadim Rizvi's Chehlum was observed in Lahore on Jan 3, 2021. A Google search with relevant keywords led us to a YouTube video of the observance near Mosque Rehmatul Lil Alameen at Multan Road's Battery Stop in Lahore. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The video showed thousands of people gathered under a flyover. This video was shot from a different angle than the one shared in social media posts.
