We also found an article by Baaghi TV reporting thousands of people attending Khadim Rizvi's Chehlum in Lahore on Jan 3, 2021. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk carefully watched the 30-second video clip and heard people chanting "Rasulallah" along with other words. Nowhere could we hear anything related to Hanuman Chalisa in the video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Pakistan was shared recently, claiming it was from Jaipur.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from China showing massive fissure in land falsely linked to Turkiye earthquake
content: New Delhi, Feb 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared an 8-second video clip of a massive crack in the land, claiming a 300-kilometre-long fissure in the Earth's crust caused by the Turkiye-Syria earthquakes occurred on Feb 6. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video was old and purportedly from China. We could trace its origin on the Internet back to November 2022, which predates the earthquakes. The claim shared in the social media post was misleading. Claim A Twitter user shared an 8-second clip of what looked like a massive crack in land and claimed that it showed a 300-km-long fissure in the Earth's crust caused by the Feb 6 earthquakes in Turkiye and Syria that had claimed over 41,000 lives. "Turkiye Syria Earthquake Caused 300 km Long Crack in Earth's Crust #Turkiyeearthquake2023 #earthquake #TurkiyeSyriaEarthquake2023 Turkiye-Syria," read the tweet dated Feb 20. The Twitter post has garnered over 286K views, 1100 like and 500 retweets to date. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video clip and found three keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one led us to another tweet posted on Feb 20, which carried the same video and claim. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then went through the comment sections of the two Twitter posts and found several users claiming that the video was old and from China. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a separate Google search with the keyword "land crack video China" and found a YouTube video posted on Nov 4, 2022. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that it was an extended version of the video clip shared in Twitter posts. The 33-second video clip included the visuals in the 8-second video clip shared in Twitter posts. Below is a comparison of screengrabs from the two videos – one shared in Twitter posts and the other found on YouTube – which shows that both were identical. When translated from Chinese to English, the video title read: "The Great Ravine in Pinglu County. A chasm about 10 kilometres long is drawn on the entire plain. What kind of force divides it into two parts?" We also found that the same video was carried by a Chinese website named Zhihu. The article's title read: "How did the ditch in Pinglu County form?" Here is the link to the website , and below is a screenshot of the same: While we could not ascertain the date this article was published, the comments discussing the crack were as old as February 2022. Here is a screenshot of a comment after the Desk translated the webpage to English using the Google Translate tool: In the next stage of its investigation, the Desk searched Pinglu County's location in the southern Shanxi province of China on Google Earth. After closely scanning the area, we found a site similar to the one shown in the video clip shared on Twitter and the one published on YouTube. Below is a comparison of the visuals in the video with the Google Earth view of the location: We also noticed that the Twitter user, who shared the video clip, made another couple of tweets two days later, on Feb 22, after several users commented about the video not being from Turkiye. "It's a viral video based on trending videos. Suppose it's fake or unreal. Sorry for the inconvenience," the tweet dated Feb 22 read. "I didn't mean to share any fake news. As you visit my profile, I always share helpful posts. I never try to share any false news. This video was in trending, so I shared this on my timeline. As I share some other earthquake videos," read another tweet. Below is a screenshot of the two tweets made by the user: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claimed a massive crack in land in Turkiye due to the recent earthquakes from China. While we could not ascertain the exact timeline of the video, it predates the earthquakes which occurred on Feb 6.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Raipur girl who was dragged by hair on road shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a man dragging a girl by her hair on the street, claiming it was an 'attack on the Hindu community'. The PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that there was no religious angle in the incident, as both the accused and the victim belonged to the same community. The claim shared in the social media post was false. Claim A Twitter user shared a 10-second video clip showing a man dragging a girl by her hair on the road while holding a sharp-edged weapon in the other hand. "This brute who is walking on the road after attacking the girl. I am more angry than seeing the dead people standing there. #Raipur, This spectacle continued for one & a half hours & the #Chhattisgarh police were sleeping? #हिन्दू_राष्ट्र_घोषित_करो #Boycott_UCC #HindusUnderAttack (Sic)," read the caption of the Twitter post published on Feb 20. Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet, which garnered over 9000 views to date. Below is a screenshot of the post- Investigation Taking a cue from the caption of the Twitter post, the Desk conducted a Google search for the keyword "Raipur man drags woman by her hair" and found a Feb 20 article by The Indian Express website, carrying a PTI report on the incident. The report's headline read: "Chhattisgarh: Man stabs teenage girl, pulls her by the hair on a busy road for refusing to work at his shop; arrested". Here is the link to the report . The report said that the 47-year-old accused, identified as Omkar Tiwari, was arrested on Saturday night (Feb 18) for allegedly attacking a 16-year-old girl with a sharp weapon and pulling her by her hair on a busy road in Raipur. The report quoted the police stating that the accused was angry because the girl stopped working at his shop in Raipur. In the investigation stage, the Desk reached out to Raipur SSP Prashant Agrawal for his comment on the claim in the social media post and for the details of the reported incident. Agrawal rejected the claims of any communal angle in the incident and confirmed that the accused and victim were from the same community. He shared with the Desk a press release by the Raipur Police on the incident. The release stated that Omkar Tiwari – the owner of Tiwari Masala Centre – was forcing the girl to return to work after she left the job at his place. On Feb 18, Tiwari allegedly barged into the girl's home and asked her mother to give him her daughter, whom he also wanted to marry. Angry at the girl and her mother's rejection, he attacked the girl with a sharp-edged weapon causing severe injuries on her hand and neck. Here is a screenshot of the press release- Below is the photo of the accused whom Raipur Police arrested after the incident. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post carrying the video of the incident used hashtags to give it a communal swing.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post on Air India offering discount to senior citizens shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a link to the 'Senior Citizen Concession' section on Air India's website and claimed that the Ministry of Civil Aviation had announced a 50 per cent concession on the airline tickets for senior citizens aged 60 years and above. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the airline offered only a "25 per cent discount" on basic flight fares on "select classes in the Economy cabin". The social media post was shared with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared the link to the 'Senior Citizen Concession' section on Air India's official website and claimed that the Ministry of Civil Aviation had announced a 50 per cent discount on Air India flight tickets for senior citizens aged 60 and above. The user also claimed that the offer was available for all senior citizens of Indian nationality, including NRIs and OCI holders, on tickets for domestic destinations. "Congratulations, all Senior Citizens. Great News, The Aviation Ministry passed the airfare brought forward to Modi. All senior citizens of Indian nationality, Including NRIs & OCI holders, over 60 years of age, get Air India Flight tickets at half the price for travel within INDIA. Please inform Senior Citizens belonging to your families and friends," read the Facebook post dated Feb 20. Here are the links to the post and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by clicking on the link in the post, directing us to the 'Senior Citizen Concession' section on the Air India website. Here is the link to the webpage , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the information on the page, a senior citizen of Indian nationality who is permanently residing in India and has attained the age of 60 years on the date of commencement of the journey is eligible to avail "25% discount of basic fare on select booking classes in the Economy cabin". The webpage mentioned that the offer was for senior citizens of Indian nationality who were permanently residing in the country and did not mention the NRIs OCI holders, as stated in the Facebook post. The Tata Group took over the management and control of Air India on Jan 27, 2022. The conglomerate had made a successful bid of Rs 18,000 crore to buy Air India in October 2021. Till Sep 29, 2022, the airline continued to provide a discount of "50 per cent of basic fare on select booking classes in Economy cabin". The archived webpage from that date showed the airline stated that only a 25 per cent discount could be availed on tickets booked on and after Sep 29, 2022. Here is the link to the archive webpage , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Air India via e-mail. "We would like to inform you that to get the information regarding the "Senior Citizen Concessionary Fares", kindly visit the given link https://www.airindia.in/senior-citizen-concession.htm and check for the same or you can also contact our customer support executives. So that they will further assist you as promised," it stated in its response. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Air India offers less than 50 per cent of base ticket fares to senior citizens aged 60 and above.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of people queueing up at Bank of Baroda's Al Ain branch in Abu Dhabi shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a crowd outside the Al Ain Branch of Bank of Baroda (BoB) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), claiming people gathered at the bank to close their accounts after its CEO's interview to a news agency on the Adani Group. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found that people had gathered outside the bank to close their accounts because the BoB was shutting down its operations at the Al Ain Branch. The Bank's decision was taken a year back, and it was informed to the central bank of UAE as well. The photo was shared in the social media post with a misleading claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo showing people queued up outside the Al Ain Branch of Bank of Baroda in the UAE and claimed that they had gathered to close their accounts following a statement by the bank's CEO in reply to a question on the Adani Group. "Crowds queueing up at Bank of Baroda Al Ain Branch, UAE to close their accounts, after the statement by its CEO, that BoB will still fund Adani companies, after the exposé of Adani's fraud. There are real consequences to electing criminals to Parliament. (Sic)," read the tweet dated Feb 26. The Tweet has garnered 2600 likes and nearly 800 retweets so far. Here are the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo. The search results led us to another tweet which carried the same picture with the same claim. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then moved forward to confirm the location and the details of the bank and its branch in the social media posts. We searched for "Bank of Baroda Al Ain Branch, UAE" on Google Earth. While the 'Street View' of the location was unavailable, we found the location of the building where the bank was situated. Here is a link to the Google Earth location of the bank, and below is a screenshot of the page: We then closely watched the viral photo and noticed a business named' VIP' beside the bank. Looking for the location on Google Maps, we found it along with its photo, which was the same as seen in the viral image. Below is a screenshot of the Google Maps location: Al Ain is the fourth largest city in the UAE and is part of the emirate of Abu Dhabi. The addresses of the two locations – BoB's Al Ain branch and VIP Xeroxing – proved that the location was genuine, as claimed in the social media posts. In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk verified the claim that people were closing their accounts in the Al Ain branch over the CEO's alleged statement on funding Adani companies. A Google search with the keyword "Bank of Baroda, Adani Group" led us to a report by Bloomberg titled "BoB to Weigh All Loan Asks, Including Adani, on Merit". According to the report, when BoB CEO and MD Sanjiv Chadha was asked if it will consider lending to the Adani Group, he said: "Irrespective of borrower, you have underwriting standards and you stick to them in good times as well as bad times." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The same Bloomberg report was also carried by Business World. The headline of the article read: "Bank Of Baroda To Continue Lending To Adani Group: Report". The Feb 20 report quoted BoB CEO and MD Sanjiv Chadha saying that 'the bank was prepared to provide loans to the Adani Group, provided that it satisfies the lender's underwriting criteria'. "Chadha also expressed that he is not worried about the market instability associated with Adani stocks," the report added. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "BoB Al Ain Branch, people closing bank accounts". The search results led us to a press release by the Bank of Baroda dated Feb 26. The release stated that the bank was closing its operations at the Al Ain Branch in Abu Dhabi Emirate, AUE, from March 22, 2023. However, the press release should have mentioned Adani Group in its press release. "Effective 22.03.2023, our Al Ain Branch in Abu Dhabi Emirate, UAE, will close its operations. As an alternative arrangement, for continuity of services, w.e.f 22.03.2023, all accounts currently maintained at Al Ain Branch will be transferred to our Abu Dhabi branch, which is adequately equipped to extend services effectively," read a part of the press release. Here is the link to the bank's press release , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a tweet by the bank dated Feb 26, which stated that the decision to shut operations at the Al Ain Branch had been taken a year ago. This predated the controversy around the Hindenburg report on the Adani Group, which was released in January this year. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk contacted the bank via e-mail to verify the claim in the social media post and will update the report accordingly. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that people queued up outside the Bank of Baroda's Al Ain Branch in Abu Dhabi as the bank was shutting its operations at the said branch.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered photo of Joe Biden eating ice cream shared in social media posts with false claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of US President Joe Biden eating ice cream, claiming it was from his recent visit to Kyiv, the capital city of war-torn Ukraine. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a two-year-old image digitally altered and shared in a social media post with a false claim. The photo went viral after Biden made a surprise trip to Kyiv on Feb 20, ahead of the first anniversary of the start of the Russia-Ukraine war. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo showing American President Joe Biden eating an ice cream. The user claimed the photo was taken during Biden's recent visit to Kyiv, Ukraine. "Dark Brandon: 'If I want to eat an ice cream cone in Kyiv, I'll eat an ice cream cone in Kyiv,'" read the post, dated Feb 21, which has garnered 323 reactions. Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image on the photo. The search results led us to a Twitter post from Feb 21, where the same photo had been shared with a similar claim. " 'If I want to eat an ice cream cone in Kyiv, I'll eat an ice cream cone in Kyiv.' Rs Joe Biden," read the post, which has garnered over 10,600 views and 1,200 likes so far. Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. The Desk also found an article by the National Review website published on July 1, 2021, which carried a similar photo of Biden eating ice cream. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the page- The caption of the photo gave credit to Reuters. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised Google Search with the keyword "Joe Biden ice-cream Reuters". This led us to a Twitter post by Reuters dated May 29, 2021, which carried the same photo. "President Joe Biden eats ice cream during a visit to Cleveland, Ohio," read the post. Here are the links to the tweet and its archive post . Below is a screenshot of the page: We found a striking similarity between Reuters' photo and the one shared in social media post. Below is a comparison of both photos- While the photo was supposedly the same, the viral background showed an eatery. To identify the location, the Desk cropped the eatery's name from the picture and conducted a Google Reverse Image Search. The search results led us to the webpage of Four Square, an online city guide. The page included reviews and photos from 'Kyivska Perepichka' – a fast-food restaurant in Kyiv. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: The photos of the restaurant indicated that it was the same as seen in the photo shared on social media posts. We also found an image which showed two men standing at the counter. The picture had striking similarities with the viral replication. Below is a comparison of the two photos: The Desk subsequently concluded that a two-year-old image of Biden eating ice cream had been digitally altered and shared in social media posts with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of Kamal Nath shared recently on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Feb 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An eight-second video of former Madhya Pradesh chief minister Kamal Nath, claimed to be recent, purportedly saying 'the Congress would suffer a massive loss if 90 per cent of the Muslims didn't vote for the party. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was over four years old. The Nov 2018 video was shared on social media with a misleading claim. The video was shared on Twitter just days after Kamal Nath visited the revered Bageshwar Dham in Gadha town of Chhatarpur and met the controversial self-styled godman Pandit Dhirendra Shastri known as Bageshwar Baba. Madhya Pradesh will go to polls later this year. Claim UP BJP spokesperson Prashant Umrao shared an 8-second video clip which purportedly showed former Madhya Pradesh CM Kamal Nath telling Congress workers that the party will suffer a massive loss if 90 per cent of Muslims don't vote in their favour. "बार बार अपनी गिरगिट वाली फितरत को उजागर कर रहे हैं कमलनाथ। श्री बागेश्वर धाम में माथा टेकने का ड्रामा रचने के बाद पूरा ध्यान मुस्लिम वोटों पर," read the tweet dated Feb 24. The Twitter post has garnered over 40K views, 2800 like and 1200 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video and found a few keyframes of the same. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to a Twitter post by Maharashtra BJP leader Wasim Khan, which carried the same video with a similar claim. "कमलनाथ जी ९०% छोड़िए अब @INCIndia को मुस्लिमों का ९% वोट भी नहीं मिलेगा क्योंकि मुसलमान आज समझ चुका है देश का विकास @narendramodi जी के नेतृत्व में @BJP4India ही कर सकती है," read the post dated Feb 24. An English translation of the post read: "Kamalnath ji leave 90%, now @INCIndia will not get even 9% votes of Muslims because today Muslims have understood the development of the country @narendramodi under the leadership of @BJP4India." Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Kamal Nath, 90 per cent Muslim votes". The search results led us to a more extended version of the video shared by NDTV on YouTube on Nov 21, 2018. The clip was reportedly released by the BJP just a few days before Madhya Pradesh went to polls on Nov 28, 2018. "…You are talking about 80 (per cent); I'm talking about 90 (per cent)! And we have figures in front of us. You all know about your area… for example, in your municipality, you know where the Muslim votes are. How much was voter turnout recorded in that booth? If a 60 per cent turnout was recorded, there must be some reason… We need not 80 per cent but 90 per cent of Muslims to come out and vote... If 90of % of Muslims don't vote for us, we could suffer a huge loss," Nath can be heard speaking in the video. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The news of Nath's controversial remark on the Muslim vote bank was also carried out by the Times of India website in its report dated Nov 21, 2018. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the page: According to the report, the BJP approached the Election Commission seeking action against Nath and the party. On the other hand, the Congress asked what was wrong with the video and called the BJP's allegations a conspiracy to divide voters into communal lines. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of Kamal Nath asking his party men to ensure 90 per cent Muslim votes dated back to 2018, which was shared as recent with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video claiming two men didn't steal flower pots in Gurugram shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 1 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of two men, in their luxury SUV, allegedly stealing flower pots set up for a G-20 event in Haryana's Gurugram vehicle went viral on Feb 28. A day later, a Twitter user shared a video claiming the two men were not stealing the flower pots but putting them down from their car. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was edited and played backwards to share it with the false claim. While the Twitter caption included an emoticon indicating it to be sarcastic, the user didn't make it clear in the caption, and some of the users believed the video was authentic. Claim A Twitter user with a verified handle shared a 1:03-minute video which showed two men unloading flower pots from the boot of a car and claimed that it was the original video against the one which went viral in which the two men were seen allegedly stealing the flower pots set up for a G-20 event in Gurugram. "ये है असली वीडियो, गाड़ी से गमले उतारे जा रहे थे," read the tweet dated Mar 1, which has garnered over 207K views, along with more than 6000 likes and 800 retweets. "This is the original video; pots were being brought down from the car," read the post in English. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video shared in the Twitter post and found 16 keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Feb 28 Twitter post, which carried a video in which the two men could be seen loading flower pots in the boot of Kia Carnival with the number plate ending '0006' – a VIP number. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet with over 477K views and 7500 likes. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk then closely watched the two videos – the one shared by a Twitter user claiming the two men were removing the flower pots from the car and the other claiming vice-versa. On carefully watching the video in question, the Desk noticed that other vehicles passing by Kia Carnival – the SUV used by the two men – were moving in the reverse direction. The movement of cars in the second video seemed normal. Below is a frame-by-frame comparison of the two videos: The bike rider crosses the SUV at the 00:01-minute timeframe in the first video (claiming that the two men were stealing but putting down the flower pots) and at 1:02-minute in the second video (posted a day earlier claiming they stole the pots). In this frame, the cyclist can also be seen moving in the reverse direction in the first video and generally in the second video. The comparative frame above showed a similar movement pattern of the car with the yellow number plate. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Flower Pots Theft Gurugram". The search results led the Desk to a PTI report from The Week on Feb 28. The report headline read, "Video of man stealing flower pots in Gurugram goes viral FIR lodged". According to the report, Gurugram Police lodged an FIR into the theft of flower pots set up for a G20 event in Gurugram after a video of two men allegedly stealing them went viral on the internet. Here is the link to the report . According to the report, "The incident took place Monday in front of the Ambience mall on the Delhi-Gurugram expressway. The man in the video can also be seen putting those pots in an SUV". "It has been observed that some passers-by/thieves are stealing flower pots placed on the roadside. A video of the theft of flower pots is also going viral on Twitter, in which the registration number of the car used in the theft is HR 20 AV 0006," read a part of the complaint filed by Metropolitan Green Planner, Urban Environment Division of GMDA. We also found a Feb 28 report by the Times of India, which included a Twitter post carrying the video where two men were seen stealing the flower pots and putting them in the car boot. Here is the link to the report titled "Men driving Kia Carnival to steal flower pots set up for G-20 event in Gurgaon, video viral". Here is the link to the Twitter post by TOI , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a Mar 1 Twitter post by Gurugram Police informing about the arrest of the accused named Manmohan. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the post: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video claiming that the two men were removing flower pots from their car boots in Gurugram and not stealing them was edited in reverse mode to make the false claim. The Desk also noticed that the Twitter post was marked under 'Funny Tweets' category by Twitter.

title: PTI Fact Check: Chhattisgarh CM Bhupesh Baghel didn't welcome Congress leaders with gold chains; Video shared in social media posts with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 1 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel welcoming Congress leaders by garlanding them at the Congress plenary session, claiming the CM gifted the delegates gold chains. The Congress' 85th plenary session was held in Raipur from Feb 24 to Feb 26. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the garlands were made out of grass and parts of a tree by an indigenous tribe of the state. The claim shared in the video that it was gold chains was false. Claim A Twitter user shared a 1:30-minute of Chhattisgarh CM Bhupesh Baghel welcoming Congress leaders at the 85th plenary session of the Congress in Raipur. The user claimed that Baghel garlanded them with gold chains. "लगता है छत्तीसगढ़ में आलू से सोना बहुत ज़्यादा बन गया है इसलिए हमारे मुख्यमंत्री महोदय ने सभी अतिथियों का स्वागत सोने की चैन पहना कर किया। परम्परागत तो टीका लगा कर हाथ जोड़ कर फुल से स्वागत होता है। #लुटेरों_का_अधिवेशन #राहुल_गांधी_जवाब_दो," read the tweet dated Feb 25. An English translation of the tweet read: "It seems that in Chhattisgarh, potatoes have yielded too much gold; that's why our Chief Minister welcomed all the guests with gold chains. Traditionally, people are welcomed with folded hands by applying tika." Here is the link and the archive link to the Twitter post, which has garnered over 5800 views. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to another Twitter post, which carried a shorter version of the same video with the same claim. Here is the link and the archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the event and location mentioned in social media posts, the Desk scanned the Twitter account of Bhupesh Baghel and found a Feb 24 tweet carrying the same video. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the post: We found another tweet by Baghel posted on Feb 27 clarifying about the garland and hitting out at the BJP for claiming it to be a gold chain. "झूठ बोलो, बार-बार झूठ बोलो, जितना ज़ोर से बोल सकते हो, उतना बोलो".. इस सूत्र पर चलने वाले इस अनमोल तोहफे का भी अपमान कर रहे हैं, साथ ही प्रकृति पुत्रों/पुत्रियों की कला और #छत्तीसगढ़ की संस्कृति का भी। आख़िर छत्तीसगढ़ के लोगों, यहाँ की संस्कृति से भाजपा को इतनी नफ़रत क्यों है?" read the Twitter post, which included a 2:34-minute video. The tweet roughly translated to English: "Lie, lie again and again, lie as loud as you can. Those who follow this formula are insulting this precious gift, the art of the sons/daughters of nature, and the culture of #Chhattisgarh. After all, why does the BJP hate the people of Chhattisgarh and its culture so much?" Here is the link to the Twitter post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The combination video showed a man – Itwari Ram Machiya, a member of the 'Baiga' community – describing how the garland, known as 'Biranmala', is made while a woman was shown preparing the bouquets. Machiya explained that the garland is made from parts of a tree called 'Khirsali' and 'Sutakhar' grass. He stated that these garlands were used to welcome Congress leaders at the party's plenary in Raipur held from Feb 24 to Feb 26. Machiya also praised Baghel for taking forward and promoting their tradition. The Desk conducted a customised Google search in the subsequent investigation stage with the keyword "Baiga Community". The search results led us to a topic page about the community on Madhya Pradesh Tourism's official website, titled 'The Mysterious Baiga Tribe Of Madhya Pradesh, India'. Here is the link to the website , and below is a screenshot of the page: The Desk noticed that the woman in the photo wore a similar garland, claimed as a gold chain in the video shared in social media posts. Below is a comparison of a visual from the video and the photo on the MP Tourism website: According to the website, the Baiga tribe found its "first documented reference in a British army report of 1867. The report that Captain W.B. Thomson refers to the Baiga tribe as "the wildest of the tribes, inhabiting the most inaccessible hills and the remotest forests; living on what they can secure with their bows and arrows, in the use of which they are very skillful, and on forest produce, and the small crops which they grow on the hillside." "Today, the Baiga tribe is concentrated in the state of Madhya Pradesh but can also be found inhabiting parts of Uttar Pradesh, Chhatisgarh, and Jharkhand," it added. The Desk then contacted AICC Secretary Pranav Jha, who was present at the occasion, to cross-check the claim made in social media posts. Jha outrightly rejected the claim that the garlands were gold chains. "These garlands are known as Biranmala, made by the indigenous Baiga tribe. It is made out of Sutakhar grass. The Baiga tribals use this in their traditional dance. Baghel Ji ordered 60 such garlands for senior party leaders. People have distorted and misrepresented it," he told PTI. Jha also shared with the Desk photo of the 'Biranmala' garland, ordered by the chief minister for senior party leaders. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Baghel welcomed Congress leaders with 'Biranmala', a traditional garland made by the indigenous Baiga community.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake photo of Shane Warne's image on $5 note shared in social media posts; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A photo of an AU$5 currency note with a picture of Shane Warne was shared on Twitter, claiming the Australian government decided to print the image of the late Australian cricketing legend on currency notes as a tribute. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image was digitally altered to share a false claim in a social media post. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of an AU$5 currency note with a picture of late cricketer Shane Warne. The user claimed the Australian government released the currency note as a tribute to the cricketing legend who passed away in March last year. "Australia posted Shane Warne picture on their currency note, a great tribute to cricket legend @aaliaaaliya @IdreesSatti6 @SameerVolunteer @Qasam511 @M_K_Z_D @azhara934 @ShamaKhan117 @surgeonshamim @syedhala @alismc2051 @ImtiazM01897291 @twqureshi @itx_leoRajput @iTahirkhanzada," read the Twitter post dated Feb 3. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, which has garnered over 500 views. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo. The search results led the Desk to a Twitter post by former English cricketer Michael Vaughan with the same picture and similar claim. "Couldn't think of a better way to celebrate the King Australia .. #Australia," Vaughan wrote in his tweet dated Feb 3, which has garnered over 670K views, more than 6200 likes and 240 retweets to date. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the post: Indian cricketer Pragyan Ojha also shared the same photo with a similar claim. "Indeed an extraordinary way of showering love & respect on an absolute legend @ShaneWarne," read his tweet on the same date. Here is the link to the tweet . The Desk then searched for information on whether the Australian government released a new 5-dollar currency note. The research led us to the official website of the Reserve Bank of Australia. A press release on Feb 2, titled "New $5 Banknote Design", stated, "The Reserve Bank has decided to update the $5 banknote to feature a new design that honours the culture and history of the First Australians. This new design will replace the portrait of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II. The other side of the $5 banknote will continue to feature the Australian Parliament." Here is the link to the press release , and below is a screenshot of the webpage: Further scanning the website, we found the photo of the new $5 currency note in circulation, which carried the image of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Australian 5 dollar currency note new design". The search results led the Desk to a Reuters report carried by CNBC. The report headline read: "Australia will replace Queen Elizabeth's image on 5-dollar banknote". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then compared the two photos – the currency note shown in the viral image and the other carried by CNBC in its report. We found striking similarities, except for the pictures of Shane Warne and Queen Elizabeth II. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Shane Warne picture of 5-dollar currency note". We found an article by The Sports Rush dated Feb 2, titled "Couldn't think of a better way to celebrate the King Australia": Michael Vaughan advocates for Shane Warne to replace Queen Elizabeth on the new $5 note". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the page: The report stated that Vaughan "vouched for Warne to replace the Queen on the note". However, we could not find any further information on the matter. Neither could we find any other report carrying any such news as claimed in the social media posts. We also noticed that these social media posts with the image of Warne of a $5 currency note were shared on Feb 3, a couple of days after the Reserve Bank of Australia issued the press release stating that Queen Elizabeth will feature in the new design of the note. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake photo of a 5 Australian dollar currency note with a picture of late cricketer Shane Warne was shared in social media posts with a claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2013 photo of Bhojpuri actor's arrest peddled as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo showing two men in police custody, claiming they were barbers who confessed to receiving funds from a mosque to infect Hindu customers who visited their shop with AIDS virus. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo was of Bhojpuri actor Irfan Khan and his accomplice Sanjay Yadav, who were arrested in 2013 in a theft case. The 10-year-old photo was shared with a false claim in a social media post. Claim A Facebook user shared on Feb 26 a photo of two men in police custody and claimed they were Muslim barbers who confessed to receiving funds from a mosque to infect Hindu customers with HIV/AIDS as part of their Jihad. Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot- Investigation The desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Facebook post. It came across an article published by India TV on July 18, 2013, which carried the same picture as shared in the social media post. The article's headline read: "Mumbai police arrests Bhojpuri actor Irfan Khan for credit cards theft, fraud". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of its page- "Mumbai Police have arrested from Bihar's Chhapra district, a renowned Bhojpuri actor Irfan Khan and his friend Sanjay Yadav on charges of stealing credit cards, cheques books and bill books and then purchasing valuables," read a portion of the report. Below is a comparison of both photos- Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Bhojpuri actor Irfan Khan arrested 2013". The search results led us to a 10-year-old video on Dailymotion posted by the verified account of Tv9 Gujarat. "Mumbai: Bhojpuri actor arrested in a theft case," read the video title. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the page: Below is a comparison of a screenshot of the Dailymotion video and the photo in the viral Facebook post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 10-year-old photo of the arrest of a Bhojpuri actor and his accomplice was shared in social media post with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Uddhav Thackeray didn't call Mughal emperor Aurangzeb his brother during his speech; Claim shared in social media misleading
content: New Delhi, Mar 3 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of Shiv Sena chief Uddhav Thackeray and called him the 'biggest traitor' because the former Maharashtra CM called 'Aurangzeb' his brother and a martyr in his speech. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped part of Thackeray's speech from June 2022 was taken out of context and used in the social media post with a false claim. The video was shared just days after the long-prevailing power tussle between the two warring factions of Shiv Sena – one led by Thackeray and the other shown by CM Eknath Shinde – culminated with the Election Commission's decision to recognise the Shinde-led faction as the real Shiv Sena and also allotting the 'bow and arrow symbol to it. Claim On Feb 28, Maharashtra BJP leader Nitesh Rane tweeted a 30-second video clip showing the former chief minister talking about 'Aurangzeb' and calling him his brother and a martyr. Rane called Thackeray the "biggest traitor" in his Twitter post, which garnered 650K views and over 3800 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk looked for similar claims on social media and found a Facebook post published on June 18, 2022. The post carried a different video of Thackeray delivering a speech on the dais with a similar claim. "अगर किसी को मराठी भाषा समझ मे नही आती हैं तो मैं बता देता हूँ कि महाराष्ट्र के मुख्यमंत्री बोल रहे हैं कि भगवा टोपी गमछा लगा लेने से कोई हिन्दू नही हो जाता,और दूसरा बिंदु बोल रहे है कि औरंगजेब हमारे देश के लिए शहीद हुआ था...*धन्य हो शिवसेना प्रमुख जी*," read the Facebook post. An English translation of the post read: "If someone does not understand the Marathi language, then I can tell that the Chief Minister of Maharashtra is saying that wearing a saffron cap does not make one a Hindu, and the second point is saying that Aurangzeb was a martyr for our country. Thank you, Shiv Sena chief." Below is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk noticed the text on the video shared in Rane's Twitter post mentioned 'Aurangabad Updates'. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a Google search with the keyword "Uddhav Thackeray Aurangzeb speech Aurangabad". The search results led the Desk to a live stream link on Uddhav Thackeray's official Facebook page, dated Feb 19. The event was organised in Andheri in Mumbai, where Thackeray interacted with the north Indian community and mentioned how he considered everyone who calls India his motherland his brother. Here is the link to the Facebook live stream , and below is a screenshot of the page: On watching Thackeray's speech, the Desk noticed that he started speaking about Aurangzeb at the 32:12 timestamp. "This happened 3-4 years back; maybe you would have forgotten or not read about it. One of our soldiers in Kashmir was on holiday and would meet his family. When terrorists learned he was left alone, they kidnapped and killed him. After a few days, his mutilated body was found somewhere. Was he ours or not, who sacrificed his life for the country? Now if I say he was my brother, you will ask if I know his name. His name was Aurangzeb. He might be from the Muslim community, but he sacrificed his life for our country, so doesn't that make him our brother? He was indeed our brother," Thackeray said in his speech. Below is a combined image of the screenshots of both videos – one shared by Rane on Twitter and the other found on Thackeray's official Facebook page. A portion of this speech was used in the video to make it look like Thackeray called Aurangzeb – the Mughal emperor – his brother and a martyr. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ascertained the veracity of the claim made in the June 2022 Facebook post mentioned above. Taking a cue from the video and the time and date when it was shared, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google and came across an extended version of the 30-second video on YouTube. TV9 Marathi posted the 2:19-minute YouTube video on June 8, 2022. The title of the video read: "Uddhav Thackeray | औरंगजेब देशासाठी शहिद झाला! : उद्धव ठाकरे-TV9". The English translation of the title read: "Uddhav Thackeray | Aurangzeb became a martyr for the country!: Uddhav Thackeray-TV9". Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the 2:19-minute video, Thackeray started talking about Aurangzeb at 1:06 timestamp. "A soldier who killed many terrorists was kidnapped on his vacation when he was going home. A few days later, his dismembered body was found. His name was Aurangzeb, and he was a martyr for the country. Just because he is a Muslim, won't you accept him as your own?" reads a rough translation of Thackeray's speech in Marathi. Below is the combined image of the screenshots of both videos – the one shared in a Facebook post last year and the other shared by a news channel on YouTube simultaneously. We again found that a selected portion of Thackeray's speech was shared in the social media post to make it look like he called Aurangzeb – the Mughal emperor – his brother and a martyr. The Desk came across a report by Lokmat (News 18), which explained what Thackeray said and the context. The Desk translated the Marathi webpage to English using the Google Translate tool. The headline read: "'Aurangzeb was martyred for the country, that is our Hindutva' what exactly did the Chief Minister say?" "Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was brutally murdered by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Shiv Sena has been demanding for the last several years that the name of Aurangabad should be changed to Sambhajinagar. But the chief minister clarified in his statement that not all persons named Aurangzeb are the same. For this, he cited a jawan named Aurangzeb who was martyred in Kashmir on the country's border," read a portion of the article. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Priyanka Chaturvedi, the leader of the Uddhav Thackeray-led faction of the party, who vehemently refuted the claim. "These people have used money and power unethically to pull down a government unconstitutionally. Now, they are falling to a level where appreciating a martyr killed in Kupwara named Aurangzeb is being used to spread lies about their opponents. Even giving credit to someone like Rane is a huge disrespect to me. Nirmala Sitharaman called his (Aurangzeb) story an inspirational story which will inspire families in times to come to send their children to the Army. If he has a problem with Uddhav Thackeray appreciating Aurangzeb's martyrdom, he should have a bigger problem with Nirmala Sitharaman," Chaturvedi told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Thackeray's two different speeches on the martyrdom of Aurangzeb – a soldier of the Indian Army – were clipped and selected portions of the speeches were used in social media posts to claim that he appreciated Aurangzeb – the Mughal emperor – and called him his brother and a martyr of the country. Rifleman Aurangzeb belonged to the 4 Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry and was posted at the camp at Shadimarg in Shopian. He was abducted while on his way to meet his family and was killed by militants in Pulwama on June 14, 2018.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2-year-old video of snowfall in Saudi Arabia peddled on social media as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 6 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a 31-second video clip of camels sitting amid heavy snow and blizzard, claiming it was the first snowfall snowed in 100 years in Saudi Arabia. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video shared on social media was two-year-old footage from Saudi Arabia. The claim in the social media post was misleading. Claim A verified Twitter user posted a video on Feb 26 which showed camels sitting amid heavy snowfall and blizzard and claimed that this was the first time it had snowed in Saudi Arabia in 100 years. The post, which garnered over 51,000 likes and 40 lakh views, read, "Global Warming strikes again, first snow in Saudi Arabia in 100 years (sic)." Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid tool search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to a Twitter post dated Feb 25, where the same clip had been posted with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The post, which has over 8,500 likes and 10 lakh views, read, "Saudi Arabia: snow falls for the first time in almost 100 years! Haarp help for New World order". The search results also led to a video posted by Khou TV on Feb 19, 2021, with the headline "Camels watch a snowfall — in Saudi Arabia? (It's not that rare.)". Here is a link to the video , and below is the screenshot. The same video had been posted with the description, "These camels watched as the snow fell in the mountains near Tabuk, Saudi Arabia on Thursday (2/18). It's rare to see snow in certain parts of the country." The Desk compared the visuals of the two videos – one shared in a viral social media post and the other posted by Khou TV – and found them to be the same. We also found that the same video had been posted on Reuters' verified YouTube channel on Feb 20, 2021. Here is a link to the video , and below is the screenshot. The video's description read, "A group of camels were treated to a display of snowy weather in the mountains north of Tabouk, Saudi Arabia." The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword 'Snowfall in Saudi Arabia' and found many reports on snowfall from previous years, suggesting it was not rare in Saudi Arabia. The Desk found reports on snowfall in parts of Saudi Arabia in 2018, 2019 and 2020 and 2022. The articles can be read here , here , here and here . The desk subsequently concluded that a two-year-old video of snowfall in Saudi Arabia had been posted online as recent with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake newspaper screenshot shared on social media with unverified claims
content: New Delhi, Mar 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a purported clipping of a Hindi newspaper, claiming it reported the alleged killing of the Hindi-speaking migrant labourers in Tamil Nadu. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the newspaper clipping photo was fake and was shared in a social media post with unverified claims. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo of a purported newspaper clipping which claimed that Hindi-speaking migrant workers were killed in Tamil Nadu. It also claimed that Tamil Nadu CM M K Stalin had asked Hindi-speaking migrant workers to leave the state before Mar 20. The text in the photo also quoted UP CM Yogi Adityanath requesting the workers to return to their condition as soon as possible as several deaths were occurring there. "Aa gya अंत (the end is here)," read the post published on March 4. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Facebook post. The search results led the Desk to a YouTube video published with the same picture. "Tamilnadu mean hindi majduro ko Jaan se maar Diya ja raha hai (Hindi-speaking labourers are being killed in Tamil Nadu)," read the title of the video. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also noticed that the purported article in the newspaper clipping with the logo of Dainik Jagran had several things that needed to be corrected and used several English words. In fact, "CM MK Stalin" was written as it is in the clipping. The Desk also noticed that the photo contained a "News-Banner News-Banner mark. The app, available on Google Play Store, includes several themes, including one similar to the image shared in the social media post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the e-paper of Dainik Jagran's Lucknow edition for Mar 2. We could not find any such news as claimed in the viral post. The Desk spoke to Ashutosh Shukla, editor of Dainik Jagran's Lucknow branch, who vehemently denied the claim. "No such news was ever published in our newspaper on that date. The screenshot of the newspaper report is fake," Shukla told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake photo was shared as a newspaper clipping in social media post. We also found two reports on the websites of two Hindi newspapers, Dainik Bhaskar and Jansatta , on the alleged targeting of Hind-Speaking labourers in Tamil Nadu. The Desk found a tweet by Bihar CM Nitish Kumar's Twitter handle about the news reports on the alleged attack. The tweet can be seen here . Below is the screenshot of the post published on March 2. However, the Desk came across a report by The Indian Express website quoting Tamil Nadu DGP, who claimed: "the videos on attacks on the migrants in the state are fake". Here is the link to the report published on March 4. Below is the screenshot of the page- We found another report by The Indian Express website quoting Tamil Nadu CM Stalin saying, "he will protect his brothers". The report said he made this statement after speaking with Bihar CM Nitish Kumar. Here is the link to the report published on March 5. Below is the screenshot of the page-

title: PTI Fact Check: Year-old photo of cheetahs from Kenya's Masai Mara National Park shared on social media in name of MP's Kuno National Park
content: New Delhi, Mar 07 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A photo of three cheetahs sitting like the lions of the 'Ashok Stambh' was shared in a Facebook post, claiming the picture was recently taken at Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park, where twelve South African cheetahs arrived in Feb this year as part of an intergovernmental agreement to reintroduce the big cats to India. These 12 cheetahs joined eight others from Namibia in the same national park last year. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo shared in the Facebook post was clicked at Kenya's Masai Mara National Park a year ago. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user posted a photo on Feb 26 of three cheetahs in the same pose as the lions on the 'Ashok Pillar' and claimed that it was clicked recently at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh. The Hindi text in the viral photo roughly translated to English: "Sycophants, get Burnol! According to some big scholars, cheetahs give pose after seeing the camera. This fresh picture has arrived from Kuno park in Madhya Pradesh. These are the same cheetahs brought to India by Modi ji from Namibia. These Cheetahs are sitting like the lions in the Ashoka Stambh, the symbol of India (Sic)." Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image search on the photo, which led to a report by The Epoch Times website in April last year with the same photo used as the lead image. The report's headline read: "Rare Photo: Cheetah Seems to Have '3 Heads' in This Perfect Safari-Time Illusion". Here is a link to the article , and below is the screenshot. Below is the combined photo of the screenshots of the image in the Facebook post and the picture in the Daily Mail article published in 2022- When the Desk scanned the report, it came to know that Wimbledon-based wildlife photographer Paul Goldstein clicked the photo in January 2022. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Paul Goldstein photography cheetah" and found the same picture was posted by Goldstein in his Instagram post on January 19, 2022. Here are the links to the Instagram post , which has garnered over 47,000 likes, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a year-old photo of cheetahs clicked at Masai Mara National Reserve in Kenya was recently shared in the name of the Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 report of Cambridge University's ranking falsely linked to Rahul Gandhi's recent visit
content: New Delhi, Mar 9 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a screenshot of a report on Cambridge University's ranking at its lowest-ever place in the world university table, claiming this happened after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's lecture at the varsity recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Cambridge University's ranking drop report was published in June 2019. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a screenshot of a news article by The Guardian, with the headline "Cambridge slips to lowest-ever place in world university table", and linked it to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's visit to the University in the United Kingdom, where he delivered a lecture recently. "When you invite a duffer to talk on geopolitics, an agenda-driven man who insults his nation in a foreign country and mocks the democratic election process in front of the global mafia, this happens. You lose credibility for giving such a duffer with zero credibility to a public platform—just a thought. Perfect timing or perfect reflection.....but looks interesting (Sic)," read the post published on Mar 4. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo of the news article shared in the Facebook post. The search results led the Desk to a Twitter post by Rishi Bagree, a user with a verified handle. Bagree shared the same photo on Mar 4 and wrote: "Is this a coincidence". The post has garnered over 360K views, more than 8700 likes and 1800 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently conducted a Google search with the keyword "Cambridge slips to lowest-ever place in world university table" and found The Guardian report published in June 2019. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the drop in Cambridge University's ranking from sixth to seventh came from a "Brexit vote and with many institutions making cuts due to financial uncertainty." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised search to know Cambridge University's latest ranking in the global list. The search results led us to a report by Forbes, dated Feb 16. The article's title read: "Want To Study Abroad? The 2023 Best Universities In Europe According To Worldwide Rankings". "For the last seven years, the overall THE rankings have set Britain's Oxford University as #1 globally. The 2023 results place Harvard at #2 while another Brit, the University of Cambridge, jumps from fifth in 2022 to third this year, above both Stanford University and MIT," read the report. Here is the link to the article by Forbes, and below is a screenshot of the page: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a three-year-old report was recently shared after Rahul Gandhi visited the University.

title: PTI Fact Check: Italian PM didn't refuse to shake hands with PM Modi; False claim shared in social media posts
content: New Delhi, Mar 9 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni, claiming she refused to shake hands with PM Modi and greeted him with a 'namaste'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claim in the social media post was false as the photo shared in the social media post was taken at a specific time to make it look like the Italian PM refused to shake hands with PM Modi. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi offering a handshake to his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni and the latter greeting him with folded hands. The user claimed in the social media post that Meloni refused to shake hands with PM Modi. "Italy's Prime Minister refuses to shake hands with Narendra Modi because she's sanskaari. Gazab ki Bezzati! (Sic)" read the post published on Mar 5. The Twitter post has garnered over 2400 views and 175 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched for similar claims on social media and found that Congress spokesperson Alka Lamba shared the same photo on Mar 4. "भारत का परिधान मंत्री - इटली की प्रधानमंत्री. अति संस्कारी (Apparel Minister of India - Prime Minister of Italy. Very cultured) (Sic)," she wrote in the post, which garnered 1 million views, along with more than 22K likes and 2600 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Further scanning the results from the Google Reverse Image Search, the Desk found a video posted by the official YouTube channel of Sansad TV. The video's title, dated Mar 2, read: "Italian PM Giorgia Meloni receives ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhawan". The Desk watched the video using the tool 'Watch Frame By Frame' and noticed that at the 5:16-minute timestamp, PM Modi offered a handshake to Meloni when she had folded her hands in 'namaste' style. When she noticed PM Modi's offering a handshake, she responded with the same the next minute, which can be seen at 5:17 minutes in the video. The video can be seen here . Below are the screengrabs of the two timestamps showing the Italian PM doing 'namaste' with her folded hands and then shaking hands with PM Modi before sitting in her vehicle. The YouTube channel of PMO India also uploaded the same video . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo shared in social media posts was false as both prime ministers were seen shaking hands in the video.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake video of Bill Gates' interview peddled as real on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates' interview was shared as a WhatsApp forward in which the interviewer asked questions about him stealing the Microsoft software and promoting the COVID-19 vaccine to make money. The purported interview ended abruptly, with Gates 'looking upset' at the end. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was an edited video, and no such questions were asked or discussed in the original version of the video, which is available on the YouTube channel of ABC News. The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation also refuted the claim in a reply mail to PTI. The claim shared with the edited video was false. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759, a video of a journalist's purported interview of Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates. The user requested to verify the authenticity of the video. In the video, the journalist confronted Gates with tough questions and accused him of stealing the Microsoft software and promoting an unapproved COVID-19 vaccine, which helped him make billions. The 1:40 minute ends abruptly, with Gates telling the journalist to end it in frustration. Here is a screenshot of the video received on WhatsApp: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Twitter post by senior lawyer Prashant Bhushan, who shared the same video. "Watch: Bill Gates talking about how he was uniquely qualified to promote the untested & dangerous Covid Vaccines! It would be funny if the man did not do so much damage to the world. But he is still feted in India. Indian Express recently invited him to deliver the Goenka lecture," read the post dated Mar 9. The post has garnered 142K views, more than 1600 likes and 600 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the Twitter post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a Google search with relevant, which took us to a video posted by ABC News (Australia) YouTube channel on Jan 31. The outfit worn by Gates and the anchor and the background made it clear that it was the same interview as in the viral WhatsApp video. The video title read: "Bill Gates complained to tech companies about 'laughable' COVID-19 conspiracy theories | 7.30". Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The video's description read: "Tech billionaire Bill Gates is one of the best-known figures on the planet, responsible for decades of philanthropy targeting poverty, disease, infant mortality and more recently COVID. Gates also invest in green technologies that he hopes will solve the climate crisis and the company behind the latest chatbot that's got us all talking about the future. Sarah Ferguson interviews Bill Gates." The Desk concluded that the video was of the original interview, which Australian Broadcasting Corporation journalist conducted, Sarah Ferguson on her current affairs show – 7.30, and released on Jan 31. The Desk watched the entire interview but could nowhere find any questions by Ferguson, or any such replies by Gates, as shown in the video received on WhatsApp. The interview ended with Ferguson thanking Gates and the latter nodding. In the original interview, whose video was shared by ABC News, Ferguson spoke to Gates on the following topics: 1. The rise of artificial intelligence 2. COVID-19 conspiracy theories 3. Elon Musk buying Twitter 4. Climate Change 5. His pledge to give away most of his wealth In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Sarah Ferguson interviews Bill Gates". The search results led us to an article on ABC News, which Ferguson and her colleague Myles Wearing wrote. "Bill Gates complained to tech companies about 'laughable' COVID-19 conspiracy theories," read the title of the article, dated Jan 31. Ferguson discussed everything from the interview and did not include any part of the discussion shown in the WhatsApp video. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the page: The Desk then watched the close video received on WhatsApp and noticed that the subtitles were played over the faces of the Ferguson and Gates, which made it challenging to observe the difference in lip-sync. Below is a combination of two screengrabs from the video received on WhatsApp showing how subtitles were played over the faces: The Desk then moved forward to find out about the origin of the viral video. A customised Google search led the Desk to a tweet by Dr Adrian Wong, a writer with Tech ARP - a Malaysian technology news and information website. Wong posted the same video and wrote in the post: "Did this journalist just destroy Bill Gates in an ABC News interview? Here are the facts: https://wp.me/p6DhDK-fWN #TechARP #BillGates #ABCNews #Interview #Viral #Microsoft #Windows #Computer #Vaccine #Vaccination #ArtificialIntelligence #DeepFake #TikTok #Facts #FactCheck". Here is the link to the Twitter post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The link mentioned in the tweet led us to an article by Tech ARP, according to which the video was created by a TikTok creator called bdti989, who posted it with the caption: "How dangerous AI can be #BillGates #billgates #microsoft #Microsoft #followformore #follow #msdos #uops #ups #ops #world #interview #interviews #artificialintelligence #ai". As per the report, the user mentioned using artificial intelligence to create a deep fake video in the comment section. To cross-check the same on our end, we asked a user in Dubai to check for the video on TikTok since the app is banned in India. Here is the archive link to the TikTok video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a deep fake video of Bill Gates' interview with ABC News journalist Sarah Ferguson was shared on social media. We contacted the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation for its comment on the fake video. The media department of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation refuted the claim in a reply mail to PTI. "We confirm that the audio in this altered video is fake", said the media department in the email.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of overcrowded train not from Tamil Nadu; Claim shared in social media post was false
content: New Delhi, Mar 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of an overcrowded passenger train claiming that migrants from Bihar were returning to their home state in large numbers from Tamil Nadu. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found that the train in the video posted on social media travels between Bihar's capital city Patna and Barka Kana in Jharkhand. It doesn't travel from Tamil Nadu to Bihar, as the social media post claims. The unrelated video was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a video which purportedly showed a train teeming with people. The text in the video reads 'Tamil Nadu to Bihar', which implied that they were migrant workers from Bihar leaving the southern state. "Tamil Nadu to Bihar #tamilnadu_to_bihar #तमिलनाडु_टू_बिहार," read the title of the Facebook video, dated Mar 8. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is the screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched for a tool named 'Watch Frame by Frame' to look closely at every frame of the 29-second video clip shared on Facebook. We noticed that at the 00:08-minute timestamp, the train's name appeared in the frame. We took a screenshot of the video from that specific timestamp and zoomed it in to find that the train was 'Palamu Express'. Below is a screenshot of the same: We then searched Google with the keyword 'Palamu Express schedule' and found that Train No. 13347/13348 plies between Barka Kana Junction in Jharkhand and Patna Junction in Bihar. Below is the screenshot of the train's route: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared in the Facebook post was unrelated to Tamil Nadu.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, woman with George Soros in this photo is not Manmohan Singh's daughter; False claim shared in social media post
content: New Delhi, March 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of a woman with Hungarian-American businessman George Soros, claiming the lady with him was the daughter of former prime minister Manmohan Singh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman in the photo was Soros' wife, Tamiko Bolton. The claim in the image shared in the social media post was false. Soros had recently grabbed the headlines after he said the Adani issue, in the wake of the Hindenburg report alleging the Adani Group's stock manipulation and improper use of tax havens, will 'weaken PM Modi's grip on power' and lead to a 'democratic revival' in the country. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo of a woman with Hungarian-American businessman George Soros and claimed her to be the daughter of former PM Manmohan Singh. The Hindi text on the photo roughly translated to English: "Congress people and Manmohan Singh Ji, what is your relationship with the American industrialist George Soros, who is against Narendra Modi? The daughter of Manmohan Singh, former prime minister of India, is in an objectionable state with George Soros, who is working against Narendra Modi in India. Has Manmohan Singh's daughter stooped so low in protesting against the country? It is a matter to be considered…. (Sic)". Here is the link to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the social media post. The search results led to an article by The Guardian on Aug 13, 2012, which carried the same image had been carried with the caption "Billionaire investor George Soros with his fiancée Tamiko Bolton". Here is a link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image of the viral photo and the one carried by the Guardian in 2012: The article read, "George Soros celebrated his 82nd birthday by announcing his engagement to Tamiko Bolton, 42 years his junior." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "George Soros, Tamiko Bolton, engagement". The search results led us to a report by China Daily published on Aug 12, 2012, which carried the same photo and another one. The headline of the article read: "Billionaire George Soros getting married for the third time". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: A further search on Google revealed that the couple married in Bedford, New York, on Sep 21, 2013. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search on "Manmohan Singh daughter" and found the former PM has three daughters - Upinder Singh, Daman Singh and Amrit Singh. Upinder is a professor of history at Delhi University, Daman is an author and novelist, and Amrit is an American human rights lawyer of Indian origin. Below is a photo of Singh's three daughters carried by The Indian Express in its September 2014 report titled: "Former PM Manmohan Singh releases 'Strictly Personal' book my daughter". The photo's caption read: "(L to R): Amrit Singh, Daman Singh and Upinder Singh, daughters of former PM Manmohan Singh". Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman in the viral photo was not Manmohan Singh's daughter.

title: PTI Fact Check: 3-year-old video of foreign tourist's sexual assault narration during 2020 Holi celebrations shared as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a female foreign tourist narrating her ordeal of 'being sexually assaulted' by a group of men while celebrating Holi. The video was posted in a tweet two days after Holi, celebrated on March 8 this year, indicating that the incident happened recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the Twitter video was part of an old video in which the tourist narrated an incident during her visit to the city (Varanasi) and how 'she was molested' during the Holi celebrations in Varanasi in 2020. Claim A Twitter user shared a video of a foreign tourist woman sharing how she was 'sexually assaulted' during Holi celebrations in Varanasi. "The videos of #Holi are appalling! Is this our famous Athithi Devobhava? Posting on this molestation will get you the tag of being anti-Hindu. That's how they normalise this predatory male behaviour (Sic)," read the post published on March 10, which garnered over 15K views, more than 300 likes and 150 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the 54-second video, which provided a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a YouTube video posted by a user named 'Under the Same Skye' on Sep 13, 2020. The Desk noticed that the video was uploaded by the same woman as seen in the video shared in a Twitter post. "Sexually Assaulted During Holi Festival In Varanasi, India • Safety For Solo Female Travellers," read the video title. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the 7:55-minute video and noticed it was an extended version of the video clip shared in the Twitter post. The video's description read: "For years and years, I'd wanted to come to India to experience Holi, the majestic, colourful, paint-throwing festival. And where better to experience Holi Festival than in Varanasi, India? The magical, religious town along the Ghats. You can imagine my disappointment when I arrived in Varanasi, and everyone told me women aren't allowed to go outside because it's too dangerous!" "In India, the pictures of foreigners enjoying the Holi festival are usually taken inside the hostel grounds, where they throw a party for their guests. I'd travelled for miles and miles and spent years looking forwards to this day, so with a big group (10+), I made the trip outside to experience the festival. After 2 minutes outside, I was sexually assaulted. Although I had a great day with my friends, please make sure you watch this video and stay safe throughout Holi! All my love, Skye! PS. I love love love India. Holi festival is just one day of the year when people seem crazy, and you experience issues you never would on any other day. Be clued up about Holi, but don't let this impact your whole perception of India!" it added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a three-year-old video of a foreign tourist narrating 'her ordeal of being sexually harassed' during Holi celebrations in Varanasi was shared as in a recent social media post. Meanwhile, when the Desk conducted a Google search to find whether about any such incident, we found a report by The New Indian Express reporting about a video of a woman from Japan being allegedly groped by a gang which forcefully applied colours on her face and body. While the police said they have taken cognisance of the matter and are verifying the veracity of the video, which was purportedly shot in Delhi's Paharganj, they said no complaint or call relating to any kind of misbehaviour with any foreigner has been received yet. The incident was reported by The New Indian Express on March 10. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same:

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated videos peddled as recent with false claims of attacks on migrant workers in Tamil Nadu; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video combining two separate clips -- one of a purported CCTV footage in which a gang of men brutally attacked two men and the other video of a person thrashed by a group of men with sticks -- claiming the clips were of Bihari migrants beaten up in Tamil Nadu's Tiruppur and Coimbatore recently.
