In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that both videos shared in the social media post were old and unrelated were not related to Tamil Nadu. Claim A Facebook user shared a post which included videos from two separate incidents. The first was purported CCTV footage showing a gang brutally attacking two men with rocks, and the second showed a youth being thrashed by some men with sticks. The user claimed the videos showed Bihari migrants being assaulted in Tamil Nadu's Tiruppur and Coimbatore. "Tamil Nadu Tirupur Coimbatore Bihari bhai ko Kaise mar raha hai (Tamil Nadu Tiruppur Coimbatore, how Bihari brother is being killed)," read the post dated Mar 5, which has garnered over 1100 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Since the Facebook post included videos from two incidents, the Desk investigated each separately. Video 1 The first video – 1:33 minutes long – was of a CCTV footage showing a group of men entering a street at night and then assaulting two men mercilessly with stones, kicks and punches, and later throwing them in a runnel. The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to an article published by NDTV on Dec 23, 2021. The news report, titled 'On CCTV, 2 Delhi Men Brutally Attacked With Rocks Over ₹ 3,000, One Dead', carried a screenshot of the same video shared in the social media post. According to the report, the incident related to the assault on two men in Delhi's Sangam Vihar. One of the victims died, while the other was critically injured in the incident. "The two men were returning from a friend's birthday party around 2 am and were stopped by some men who demanded that they hand over their valuables. When they refused, the attackers started attacking them. The accused did not take away from Pankaj, but they snatched ₹ 3,000 from Jatin's pocket," read the report. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Times of India also carried the same video in its report published on Dec 24, 2021. "On cam: 24-year-old man killed for resisting robbery bid in Delhi's Sangam Vihar," read the report title. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and found a Twitter post by Delhi Police, shared on Dec 24, 2021. In the video, Additional CP South Delhi mentioned that an FIR had been lodged in connection with the case, and one of the accused had been arrested while efforts were on to capture the remaining culprits. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the post: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of an incident from Delhi's Sangam Vihar, dating back to December 2021, was shared as recent with the false claim in social media post. Video 2 The second video – 1:20 minutes long – showed a group of men thrashing a person with a wooden stick and kicking him, purportedly at a farmland. The video carried the logo of TV9 Kannada and subtitled running along with the video. The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video but could not find anything relevant related to the video or the claim. In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk watched the video closely and took screenshots of various news tickers running above and below the video. Since the news tickers were in Kannada, we used the Google Translate tool to convert the text on the images to English. The Desk took a cue and conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords. The search results led us to a tweet by TV9 dated May 27, 2018. The Twitter post included the same video shared in the Facebook post and the caption: "#BIGNEWS: A ghastly video of rowdies thrashing a youth in #Bengaluru goes #viral. The youth was reportedly beaten up by rowdy sheeter Narothan Kumar & his aides." Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted several Google searches using different keywords but could not find anything more related to the incident. However, it was concluded that a five-year-old video was shared recently with a false claim on social media. Tamil Nadu and Bihar state governments have recently taken strict action against those sharing disinformation and old, unrelated videos to claim that Hindi-speaking migrants were being attacked in the southern state.

title: PTI Fact Check: HPV vaccine 'prevents most cases of cervical cancer only'; Poonawalla's last year's video shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of Serum Institute of India (SII) CEO Adar Poonawalla, claiming he talked about launching a 'cancer vaccine' in the 'next few months' at a price ranging between Rs 200 and Rs 400. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found it was an old and unrelated video from last year, in which Poonawalla spoke about the launch of India's first home-grown human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine. The HPV vaccine is aimed at preventing cervical cancer caused majorly by HPV. The vaccine would not cure any other type of cancer not caused by HPV. The video was shared with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a video of SII CEO Adar Poonawalla addressing the media about a vaccine set to be launched by his company. The user claimed that the SII was about to launch a 'cancer vaccine' in the next few months, priced between Rs 200 to Rs 400. "Great News ... India is going to launch Cancer Vaccine in next few months, that too in a very affordable price range of ₹200-400/- (भारत 200-400 रुपए के बीच कैंसर की दवाई लॉन्च कर रहा कुछ महीनों में, ग्रेट न्यूज, कैंसर मुक्त इंडिया) congrats," read the post, dated Mar 10. An English translation of the post read: "Great News ... India is going to launch a Cancer Vaccine in the next few months, that too at a very affordable price range of ₹ 200-400/- great news, cancer-free India) congrats." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which fetched us several keyframes of the 3:04-minute video. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to a Twitter post carrying the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk watched the video shared in the Facebook post; it started with Poonawalla saying that the company would first ensure that the vaccine is provided at affordable pricing across India. "In a few months, the vaccine will be launched, and I assure everyone it will be very affordable. It will be substantially lower than what is available today from manufacturers across the globe. First, we will give it to our country just like during COVID-19; we will provide the vaccine to the entire world. (The vaccine) maybe priced between Rs 200 and Rs 400. We can prepare 200 million doses in 2 years," Poonawalla said. Later, at the 1:28-minute timestamp, Poonawalla was heard saying, "the vaccine has been manufactured for women. It is an essential cause because women have to work and stay healthy, and it is crucial for their safety". At the 00:29-minute timestamp, the text running on the video read: "India developed its cervical cancer vaccine". It later read: "the quadrilateral qHPV vaccine for prevention of cervical cancer will hit the shelves over the next few months". Below is a screenshot of the video from the 00:39-second timestamp: We also noticed the English NewJ website logo on the video's top right corner. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and found the original video shared on English NewJ's Facebook page on Sep 2, 2022. "Good news: India develops its first indigenous vaccine for cervical cancer. It is expected to be available soon for 200-400 rupees according to Serum Institute of India's (SII) CEO Adar Poonawalla," read the post. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Searching for more details on the HPV vaccine, the Desk came across a PTI report from NDTV on Feb 9, 2023. The report headline read: "Serum Institute's Cervical Cancer Vaccine To Hit Market This Month: Report". According to the report, which quoted official sources, the vaccine named CERVAVAC "will be available in the market this month at an MRP of ₹ 2,000 per vial of two doses". "The first indigenous human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine was launched by Union Home Minister Amit Shah on January 24 in the presence of Serum Institute of India (SII) CEO Adar Poonawalla and its Director of Government and Regulatory Affairs Prakash Kumar Singh," it read further. The vaccine has been manufactured by the Pune-based Serum Institute of India (SII) in partnership with the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), the Ministry of Science and Technology, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched for more details about HPV. According to the World Health Organisation, Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common viral infection of the reproductive tract, responsible for most cervical cancer (more than 95%). "Cervical cancer is by far the most common HPV-related disease. Nearly all cases of cervical cancer can be attributed to HPV infection," read the WHO report on cervical cancer. According to the information on the National Cancer Institute (U.S. Department of Health and Human Services) website, "HPV is a group of more than 200 related viruses, some of which are spread through vaginal, anal, or oral sex". Other than cervical, HOV can also cause oropharyngeal, anal, penile, vaginal and vulvar cancers. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded two things – first, the SII did not launch a vaccine that could cure all types of cancer. Its vaccine, CERVAVAC, launched in January this year, was India's first indigenous human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine. Second, the vaccine will only prevent or cure types of cancer caused by HPV.

title: PTI Fact Check: Facebook post claiming Raghuram Rajan compared Indian economy with Sri Lankan economy is baseless
content: New Delhi, Mar 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a post claiming former Reserve Bank of India governor Raghuram Rajan advised people to save money because the Indian economy would fall like Sri Lanka's. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the former RBI governor never made any such statement comparing the Indian economy with Sri Lanka's economy. The social media post was shared with a false claim. The claim comes amid the neighbouring country facing many crises, including food insecurity, threatened livelihoods and increasing protection concerns. This is the worst economic crisis faced by Sri Lanka since its independence in 1948. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo of former RBI governor Raghuram Rajan claiming that he advised people to save money as India's economy was becoming like Sri Lanka. "People should save money as conditions are becoming like Sri Lanka," read an English translation of the Hindi text on the photo shared in the March 2 Facebook post. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Raghuram Rajan on the Indian economy, Sri Lanka" and found a report by The Indian Express. "Raghuram Rajan lauds RBI, says India not facing economic problems like Sri Lanka, Pakistan," read the headline of the news article dated Aug 1, 2022. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted Rajan saying India had sufficient foreign exchange reserves and would not experience economic problems like Sri Lanka and Pakistan. On further scanning the search results, we found that Rajan, in a recent interview with PTI, said that with subdued private sector investment, high-interest rates and slowing global growth, India was "dangerously close" to the Hindu rate of growth. Rajan said the sequential slowdown in the quarterly growth, as revealed by the latest estimate of national income released by the National Statistical Office (NSO) last month, was worrying. Hindu rate of growth is a term describing low Indian economic growth rates from the 1950s to the 1980s, which averaged 3.5 per cent. The term was coined by Raj Krishna, an Indian economist, in 1978 to describe slow growth. The Hindu carried the PTI report on Mar 5. "India is 'dangerously close' to Hindu growth rate, says Raghuram Rajan," read the report's headline. However, a report from SBI economists rejected these claims, arguing that such statements are 'ill-conceived, biased, and premature.' Here is the link to the Hindu report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk reviewed the report but found no remark comparing India's economy to Sri Lanka's. In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted Raghuram Rajan, who vehemently refuted the claim made in the social media post. "It is fake, and I don't know who does this, though I can guess. I have a LinkedIn account where I post my comments and articles. The plethora of Twitter and Facebook accounts purporting to be me are all fakes. These are cleverly exploited by those who oppose my arguments to send messages that I would never send. Worse than the clear fakes are the deliberate distortions of my concerns by otherwise sensible people who have their own personal agenda. Unfortunately, that is the world we live in, and people should be on their guard. Any new technology, in this case social media, can be used for the good and the bad. It has always been thus!" Rajan told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a false claim of Raghuram Rajan likening India's economy to Sri Lanka's crisis was shared in social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of electric bus outside charging station in London from early 1900s is genuine; Details inside
content: New Delhi, March 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A black-and-white photo of a vintage bus was received on the PTI Fact Check WhatsApp number requesting to verify the claim that the image of an electric bus at a charging station was from the 1900s. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found it was a genuine photo from London. showed a bus charging station operated by the London Electrobus Company during that company's short existence between 1907 and 1909. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759, a black-and-white photo which purportedly showed an electric bus outside a charging station in London in the early 1900s. The image was received with the request to verify whether the picture was genuine. Here is a screenshot of the photo received by the Desk: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found an Instagram post shared on Jan 22, which carried the same picture. "Imagine the surprise once you realise that around the same time Rockefeller used his connections to make cities rely on oil, he also did the same in the medical field, which is why everything is petroleum based now with loads of side effects to ensure future profits," the user wrote in the post, which has garnered over 2700 likes to date. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the Getty Images website carried the same photo. Here is the link to the Getty Images post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption read: "A photograph of an early battery-operated bus. Dated the 20th century." The 'Date Created' was mentioned as Jan 2, 1907. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and came across a blog post published on Nov 1, 2021, on the London Transport Museum's website. The article headline read: "How are engineers creating a greener future?" The article carried the same viral image and wrote: "Incredibly, London first experimented with operating electric buses in the early 20th century. Fast forward to the 21st century; today, more than 550 electric buses are in service." Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The photo's caption read: "Battery driven double deck bus operated by The London Electrobus Company Limited, Jul 1907." On further scanning the search results, the Desk found an article published by The Earthbound Report on Apr 23, 2018, with the headline "Your bus is running approximately 100 years late". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot. The Earthbound Report's article read, "The London Electrobus Company ran a bus service between Victoria and Kilburn from 1907 to 1910, the world's first fully operational electric bus route." We then conducted a Google search with the keyword "The London Electrobus Company" and found an article published by The Economist on Sep 8, 2007, with the headline "What is this that roareth thus?." Here is a link to the article , and below is a screenshot for the same. According to the article, the company started operating electric buses in London on July 15th, 1907, and its services collapsed in 1909. Also, according to the article, these charging stations were not plug-in stations as seen today but were facilities where old batteries were swapped for fresh ones. The Desk subsequently concluded that the photo shared over WhatsApp and in the Instagram post was genuine. The London Electrobus Company ran a fleet of 20 electric buses in London briefly between 1907 and 1909.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Elon Musk never endorsed 'Shilajit'; Doctored video with cloned voice shared in Facebook Reel with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of Elon Musk was shared in a Facebook reel, claiming the Twitter CEO endorsed 'Shilajit' – an alleged anti-ageing and revitalising remedy. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was an old video digitally altered with a cloned voice to make it appear that Musk endorsed the remedy. The claim in the Facebook post was false. Claim A Facebook page shared a video showing Elon Musk allegedly endorsing Shilajit, a natural remedy. "You need shilajit in your life. #shilajit #shilajitbenefits #healthfood #elonmusk #healthylifestyle," read the Facebook post shared by a page named Avonent Health on Mar 7. Here is the link and archive link to the post, which garnered over 700 likes and 300 shares, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the 10-second video clip and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Search on one of the keyframes led us to a YouTube video of the TED 2022 conference, where Musk spoke about "Twitter, Tesla and how his brain works". Here is the link to the YouTube video shared by TED's official channel on Apr 14, 2022, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that Musk's outfit and the background colour were the same as in the video clip shared in the Facebook post. The Desk watched the 54:45-minute video but could nowhere find Musk mentioning anything about 'Shilajit'. The Desk also noticed that Musk's visuals used in the clip were taken from the 13:20-minute timestamp of the YouTube video. Here is the link to the video of that particular timestamp, and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is the combined image of the screenshots of the videos – one shared in the viral social media post and the other uploaded by TED in April last year. Taking a cue from the video, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for the transcript of the video. The search results led us to an article by The Street, published on Apr 15, 2022 – a day after Musk appeared in TED Talks 2022. The article's title read: "Everything Elon Musk Said at His TED Talk. The full transcript of his interview with Chris Anderson." We went through the entire interview transcript but did not find any mention of Shilajit by Musk. Here is the link to the article . Also, the video clip shared in the Facebook post showed Musk only for a few seconds, during which a text ran over their face, thus making it difficult to ascertain his lip movement. The rest of the video only had his voiceover rather than his visuals. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned Avonent Health's Facebook page and found another similar video of Musk, which showed him endorsing Shilajit. Notably, the visuals in this video were also taken from Musk's appearance at the TED 2022 conference in April last year. It was dubbed with a different script, with a cloned voice audio track that sounded like Musk. Here is the link and archive link to the video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video with a cloned voice was shared in the Facebook post to make it look like Elon Musk was endorsing 'Shilajit'.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of TTE misbehaving with train passenger shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a Train Ticket Examiner (TTE) misbehaving with a passenger with a claim that he was a Bihari migrant worker fleeing from Tamil Nadu. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the person in the video was not a migrant worker travelling from Tamil Nadu to Bihar, and the incident didn't happen on a Tamil Nadu-bound train. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a video of a TTE manhandling a man on the train, allegedly for not possessing a ticket. The user claimed the man was a Bihari migrant trying to flee Tamil Nadu. "तमिलनाडु से भाग कर आ रहे बिहारियों को कुछ इस प्रकार से टीटी टिकट दे रहे हैं, क्या टीटी के द्वारा ऐसा बर्ताव सही है और इसने अपनी वर्दी भी नहीं पहन रखी है," the user wrote in the post, dated Mar 8, tagging Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and the Railway Ministry. An English translation of the post read: "The TT is giving Biharis who are running away from Tamil Nadu tickets in this way. Is this behaviour by the TT correct, and he is not even wearing his uniform." The Twitter post has garnered over 570K views, more than 5700 likes, and 3300 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk went through the comments in the Twitter post and found a user stating that a YouTuber shot the video in Sampoorna Kranti Express (Train No. 12393/12394). He also said in the comment that the man was travelling from Delhi to Patna without a ticket. Here is the link and archive link to the comment, and below is a screenshot of the same: Replying to his comment, a user questioned if the TTE's behaviour was justified, to which he shared a YouTube link of what he said was the complete video shot by the YouTuber. The link led us to a 16:52-minute video posted by a user named 'Travel India with Rishi' – a verified channel with over 800K followers. The title of the video , posted on Mar 3, read: "Sampoorn Kranti Express Delhi to Patna *फिलहाल Family के साथ travel न करे* (Sampoorn Kranti Express Delhi to Patna Avoid travelling with family as of now)". The Desk went through the entire video and noticed that the incident between the TTE and the man occurred at 13:51 minutes in the footage. The Desk also saw that this video was shot from a different angle than the 26-second clip shared in the viral social media post, purportedly shot by a passenger sitting on an upper berth. Below is the combination photo of the screenshots from the two videos – the one shared in the Twitter post and the other uploaded on YouTube. On closely watching the video shared in the Twitter post, the Desk noticed that at 00:14 seconds timestamp, a passenger could be heard saying, "Sampoorna Kranti Superfast". In the YouTube video, the passenger commented at 14:00 minutes. At 15:45 minutes, the man shooting the video talked about the train arriving at Patna Junction at 9 am, delayed by 3-4 hours. The Desk noticed a reply by Railway authorities on the viral tweet, stating that the TTE was suspended. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the information gathered from the video, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Delhi to Patna Sampoorna Kranti" and found that the train ran between Delhi and Patna. The route was nowhere connected to Tamil Nadu. Below is the train route for Delhi-Patna Sampoorna Kranti Express: The Desk conducted another customised Google search to check if any Sampoorna Kranti train ran between Tamil Nadu and Bihar but could not find any. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was shared on social media with a false claim. The Tamil Nadu and Bihar governments have repeatedly refuted rumours and unconfirmed reports alleging attacks on Hindi-speaking migrants in the southern state.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2014 photo from Imran Khan-led rally in Pakistan edited and shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a man waving a gun from vehicle, claiming he was a supporter of former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan's party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image of a 2014 election rally led by Khan was digitally altered to add a gun in the man's hand and shared in social media post with a false claim. Claim Mubasher Lucman, a known Pakistani journalist, shared on Twitter a photo of a man brandishing a gun from a vehicle and claimed that he was a supporter of former Pakistan PM Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). "PTI is a law abiding party," read the post, dated Mar 8, which has garnered 1.5 million views, along with more than 4500 likes and 1700 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Twitter post. The search results led to another Twitter post carrying the same photo with a similar claim. "RAW trained terrorists in Lahore," read an English translation of the Mar 8 post in Urdu. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The search results further led the Desk to a report by ENEWS Channel Africa, dated Aug 15, 2014, which carried a similar image, but the man in it did not hold any gun. "Imran Khan's PTI attacked on Islamabad march," read the headline of the article. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the news article: "Police and witnesses said activists from Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaaf (PTI) party clashed with supporters of Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-N (PML-N) in the town of Gujranwala, around 200 kilometres (120 miles) southeast of Islamabad," read a portion of the article. Below is a combination image, comparing the two photos – one shared in the viral Twitter post and the other published in Aug 2014 by a news website. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and found that the same photo was uploaded on Getty Images – a website that provides stock images – on Aug 15, 2014. "Supporters of Pakistani cricketer-turned politician Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) or Movement for Justice arrive in Islamabad to take part in Azadi (Freedom) march on August 15, 2014. Thousands of Pakistanis rallied behind Khan toward the capital Islamabad for a protest to demand the resignation of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif. (Photo by Muhammad Reza/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)," read the description of the image. Here is the link to the webpage and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that photo of a supporter of Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) dating back to August 2014 was digitally altered to add a gun in the man's hand.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated photos shared as recovery items from March 11 ED searches in land-for-jobs scam case; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared four photos of gold jewellery, gold biscuits and cash, claiming they were the items recovered from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) searches at former Bihar chief minister Lalu Prasad Yadav's residential properties on March 11 this year. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that two of the four photos shared in the social media post were old and unrelated to the ED searches conducted on March 11. The authenticity of the other two photos couldn't be established as the ED didn't release any pics in its press release on the ED searches conducted in the 'land-for-jobs case' on March 11. The claim shared in the social media post was misleading. The photos emerged on social media amid the ED's claim that it seized "unaccounted-for cash" of Rs 1 crore and detected Rs 600 crore as "proceeds of crime" after it searched 24 places linked to Yadav's family in connection with its probe into the Railways' land-for-jobs scam. Claim A Twitter user shared four photos of gold jewellery, gold biscuits and cash, claiming they were items recovered in ED searches at properties linked to Lalu Prasad Yadav and his family members during the investigation into the alleged Railways' land-for-jobs scam. "Few items that were recovered by ED from "Gareebon ka Masiha" Lalu Prasad Yadav's," read the Mar 13 post, which has garnered over 47K views, along with 1800 likes and more than 600 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted separate Google Reverse Image Searches on all four photos shared in the Twitter post. The search results led us to a Facebook post which shared the same photos with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Google Reverse Image Search results on the third and fourth photos – jewellery items in boxes and plates – combined with relevant keywords led the Desk to a Twitter post by the Twitter handle of the Enforcement Directorate on Mar 6. The tweet, carrying the same photos, read: "ED has conducted searches and survey at 15 locations in Nagpur & Mumbai about the investment fraud by Pankaj Mehadia, Lokesh & Karthik Jain. Unaccounted jewellery worth Rs 5.51 Crore and cash of 1.21 Crore have been seized. Further investigation is going on." Here is the link to the tweet by ED , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photos shared in the viral post and the tweet posted by ED. The Twitter post did not mention the land-for-jobs scam, Lalu Yadav or his family members. Taking a cue from the Twitter post, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to get more details about the case and came across an article by India Today, which carried the same photos as shared by the ED. "Crores in cash, jewellery seized by ED during searches in Nagpur, Mumbai," read the article's headline dated Mar 6. "The ED had conducted searches on March 3 at 15 places in Nagpur and Mumbai in connection with a money laundering case related to the investment fraud of Pankaj Mehadia and others," read the article. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then reviewed the Google Reverse Image Search results for the first two images shared in the Twitter post – a briefcase with stacks of notes and gold coins from different banks and jewellery brands. The search results led us to a news report by News Nine, which carried one of the two photos. Here is the link to the article titled "Rs 1 crore cash, Rs 600 crore in proceeds of crime detected in searches against Lalu Prasad's family: ED". Below is a screenshot of the report: The Desk noticed the photo's caption mentioned image credits to a news agency. The Desk took a cue and conducted another Google search with relevant keywords. On scanning the search results, we found that a news agency shared the same photos from its Twitter handle with the text claiming the items were seized in the ED searches at 24 locations in the Railways' land-for-jobs-scam on Mar 11. (Check the archive post here) Below is a combination image comparing the photos shared in the viral Twitter post and the news agency. The Desk conducted another search on Twitter and scanned the ED's Twitter handle. We found two tweets in a thread of tweets about the details of the ED searches on 24 locations in the 'land-for-jobs case' on March 11. The tweet read: "ED conducted searches at 24 locations in the Railways Land for Job Scam, resulting in the recovery of unaccounted cash of Rs 1 Crore, foreign currency including US$ 1900, 540 gms gold bullion and more than 1.5 kg of gold jewellery". "Searches resulted in detection of Proceeds of Crime amounting to Rs 600 Crore approximately at this point of time," it added in a threaded tweet. Here is the link to the Twitter post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that no photos were attached to both tweets by the ED's Twitter handle. We found its press release on the March 11 searches on the agency's official website. We couldn't see any photos of the release of the attacks on its website. Here is the link to the ED press release , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted the media cell of ED for its comment on the veracity of the photos shared in the social media posts. We will update the copy as soon as we get a reply on the mail. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that at least two of the four photos shared in the viral social media post were old and unrelated to the searches by the ED in the land-for-jobs scam case on Mar 11. The veracity of the remaining two photos could not be verified yet as ED has not shared any images in its tweets and press release on the searches.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Shahi Imam of Delhi's Jama Masjid did not join BJP; Video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of Shahi Imam of Delhi's Jama Masjid, Syed Ahmed Bukhari, with BJP MP Dr Harsh Vardhan, claiming the Imam joined the Bharatiya Janta Party (BJP). In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Bukhari shared the dais with the BJP MP at an event related to laying the foundation stone of a washroom in the mosque. The video was shared in the social media post with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a 1:03-minute video of Shahi Imam of Delhi's Jama Masjid, Syed Ahmed Bukhari, sharing the stage with BJP MP Dr Harsh Vardhan. The user claimed that Bukhari had joined the BJP. "गुरू, शाही इमाम भी सनातनी हो गया? जामा मस्जिद के शाही इमाम ने भारतीय जनता पार्टी ज्वाइन करी ! मोदी है तो मुमकिन है । सबका साथ, सबका विकास," read the Mar 15 post, which has garnered nearly 10K views and over 200 likes. An English translation of the post read: "Guru, Shahi Imam has also become Sanatani? The Shahi Imam of Jama Masjid has joined the Bharatiya Janata Party! If Modi is there, then it is possible. Everyone's support, everyone's development." Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned the comments on the Twitter post and found a user terming the claim false. He also mentioned that Dr Harsh Vardhan was present there to attend an inaugural event. Here is the link to the comment , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and found a report by ETV Bharat, published on Mar 15. The headline of the news report read: "Shahi Imam Bukhari: BJP ज्वाइन करने के कथित वायरल वीडियो पर भड़के जामा मस्जिद के शाही इमाम बुखारी (Shahi Imam Bukhari: Shahi Imam Bukhari of Jama Masjid furious over alleged viral video of joining BJP)." Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report stated that Bukhari and Harsh Vardhan were at the stone laying foundation for a toilet at Jama Masjid, along with several others. During the event, the Shahi Imam was greeted with a garland, and people started clapping and raising slogans of 'Shahi Imam Zindabad'. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to the Jama Masjid management board, who vehemently refuted the claim of Bukhari joining the BJP. It also said that the clip was intentionally used as it showed a poster used at the event (which can be seen in the video) with photos of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Harsh Vardhan and Bukhari. "A baseless news is viral on social media concerning Shahi Imam Mohd Syed Ahmed Bukhari claiming that he has joined the BJP. This news is completely false. The washrooms of Delhi's Maja Masjid were in deplorable condition, and we had sent the request to the MCD to approve its plan. However, it was not approved in the last 1.5 years. We requested MP Dr Harsh Vardhan to construct the washroom from his funds. This programme was of laying the washroom's foundation stone," Mohd Ansarul Haque, Assistant PRO at Jama Masjid Delhi, told PTI. Haque also shared a video of Shahi Imam's speech at the event with the Desk. He called for an end to the growing enmity between Hindus and Muslims and said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi should intervene and take a step in this direction. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the video, Harsh Vardhan sits beside Bukhari as he speaks on the mic, addressing the area's people. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Bukhari did not join the BJP and the video was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of a group of men thrashing a person peddled as recent with a false claim on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a group of men thrashing a person on the road, claiming the incident captured on camera was a case of 'lynching' of a Christian person by a 'Hindu mob'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found an old video of an incident in December 2022 when a Dalit youth was beaten allegedly by a group of upper caste men in Gujarat's Vadodara. The old video was recently shared in social media posts with a false claim. Claim A verified Twitter user shared a 41-second video clip of a group of men assaulting a person with belts and sticks on the road and claimed that the victim was a Christian attacked by a "Hindu mob". "Brutal attack on a Christian by a Hindu mob in India, A country where mob lynchings are on the rise," read the Twitter post dated Mar 17. The tweet has garnered over 82K views, more than 2500 likes and 1500 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image Search a couple of them led the Desk to another Twitter post, which carried the same video with a similar claim. "Rising trend of mob lynching in India captured on camera as a Hindu mob brutally attacks a Christian. Concerns over communal violence and religious intolerance escalate, the international community must take notice of this situation #MobLynching #India #ReligiousIntolerance," read the Twitter post by 'South Asian Human Rights Watch', shared on Mar 16. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet with over 88K views and 1400 likes. Below is a screenshot of the post: On further scanning the search results with relevant keywords, the Desk came across a tweet by Gujarat MLA Jignesh Mevani, dated Dec 22, 2022, which carried the same video. Mevani claimed that the video was on an incident in Gujarat's Vadodara on Dec 21, 2022, and the man assaulted was a Dalit. "गुजरात में गुंडाराज ! ऊना कांड के वक्त मोदी जी ने कहा था- "मारना है तो मुझे मारो, मेरे दलित भाईयो को नहीं" लेकिन प्रशासन द्वारा यह सुनिश्चित ही नहीं किया गया की दुबारा इस प्रकार की घटनाएं न घटे। नतीजा-कल वडोदरा जिले में दलित युवक की सरेआम लिंचिंग करने की कोशिश हुई। @dgpgujarat," read the Twitter post with over 387K views and 8900 likes. An English translation of the tweet read: "Gundaraj in Gujarat! At the time of the Una incident, Modi ji had said - "If you want to kill, kill me, not my Dalit brothers", but the administration did not ensure that such incidents do not happen again. Result- yesterday, there was an attempt to lynch a Dalit youth publicly in the Vadodara district. @dgpgujarat." Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Dalit man attacked by a mob in Vadodara, December 2021". The search results led the Desk to a report by The Indian Express, published on Dec 23 last year. The article's headline read: "Five detained for 'assaulting' Dalit youth in Vadodara". The article gave picture credit to Mevani, whose Twitter post was used in the news report. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the Twitter video and the photo in the news article: According to the report, five persons were detained for allegedly assaulting a Dalit youth by a group of seven persons belonging to an upper caste in Vadodara. "The accused told the police that they were allegedly summoned for help by a female social-media influencer, who was allegedly intimidated by the Dalit youth." "A video of the incident had surfaced on social media, showing seven men assaulting 24-year-old Alpesh Parmar (Vankar) with a leather belt and sticks while sitting with a friend. The police have identified five of the men seen in the video as Parampir Madansinh Rathod, Pratap Prakash Makwan, Tushar Bharat Solanki, Ajay Aarsinh Ninama and Mahipal Ronak Chavda — all residents of Vadodara city," read the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man assaulted in the video was a Dalit, not a Christian, as claimed in the social media post.

title: PTI Fact Check: 'Funny' video of woman refusing to vacate bus driver's seat shared as accurate on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a woman occupying the driver's seat of a public bus and refusing to vacate on the driver's request. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was part of a comedy video and posted on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a 2:20-minute video where a woman was seen occupying the driver's seat of a public bus and arguing with the driver on being asked to vacate it. The driver was eventually seen trying to pull the woman out of the seat. The post read, "A lady and her bahu get into a crowded bus somewhere in Rajasthan. The MIL got a seat. The bahu, too, searched for one, saw the driver's seat vacant, and occupied it. When the driver came and asked her to vacate his seat, she told him to sit elsewhere. She asked him to drive from any other seat when he tried saying that he needed to drive the bus. Her MIL, too, supports her! Modi has to settle these issues also. (sic)" Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes led us to a Twitter post from March 14, which has 500 views so far, where a shorter version of the same video had been posted. Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. The Desk then conducted a customised Google Search with the keyword "woman arguing with bus driver viral video Rajasthan" which led us to a YouTube video posted on Dec 29, 2020. "गांव की लुगाई मचायो शहर में रोलोव !! Hema Prajapat || Marwadi Comedy," read the title of the video. Scenes from the video, with over 2,800 views, looked visually similar to the clip posted on social media. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot. Below is a combination image of visuals from the two videos – the one shared in the Facebook post and the other posted on YouTube. According to the YouTube video, the actor seen in the clip was Hema Prajapati. We conducted a Google search on Prajapat and found a similar video on Facebook from Sept 23, 2020, titled "मारवाड़ी औरत बस में किया हंगामा", which has 35 reactions. In this video, too, Prajapat is seen getting on the driver's seat of a bus after being unable to find a seat and refusing to get off. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that a comedy sketch video was posted as a real-life incident on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, TV animation show The Simpsons did not predict collapse of Silicon Valley Bank; Edited video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a 33-second video from the popular TV animation show The Simpsons, claiming one of its episodes predicted the Silicon Valley Bank's collapse in 1994. The Silicon Valley Bank collapsed unprecedently on March 10 this year, leading to the second-biggest bank failure in US history. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video clip was digitally altered and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a 33-second video from the popular TV animation show The Simpsons, which showed an angry mob protesting being unable to withdraw money from the Silicon Valley Bank. The user claimed that the show had predicted the bank's collapse in 1994. The post, which has so far garnered over 1.2 lakh views and 270 likes, read, "#BankCrash Update: Die Simpsons in 1994 - Silicon Valley Bank #Crash The #withdrawals at SVB's Silicon Valley Bank have come from startups and technology firms, many of which also ran into new trouble once the Fed began raising rates. (sic)" Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video clip, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one keyframe led us to a Facebook post from March 14, where the same clip had been shared with a similar claim. The post, which garnered 25 likes, read, "The Simpsons - On the Collapse of the Silicon Valley Bank. They never predicted anything… I just told you the truth in advance. (sic)" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same- The search also led us to an article by The Cutting Room Floor website . The page titled "Proto talk: The Simpsons Game (PlayStation 2, PlayStation Portable, Wii)" carried an image with a banner of "First Bank of SpringField", which looked similar to that of the bank in the viral video clip. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the visuals from the viral video and the embodiment shown on the webpage: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Bank of Springfield Simpsons" and found a YouTube video uploaded on May 17, 2020. The Desk noticed it was the same clip as shared in the Twitter post, but instead of Silicon Valley Bank, the banner in the video read "First Bank of Springfield". Here is a link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: We again compared the visuals from the two videos – the one shared in the Twitter post and the YouTube video uploaded in 2021. According to the YouTube video description, the clip was from the episode "The PTA Disbands", the 21st episode of the sixth season and originally aired on April 16, 1995. On watching the episode, it was found that the clip had been taken from a scene where a character in the show, Bart Simpson, played a prank, leading to a protest at the First Bank of Springfield, a fictional entity within the series. The Desk subsequently concluded that a digitally altered video had been shared on social media to falsely claim that The Simpsons predicted the Silicon Valley Bank's collapse in 1994.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 chopper photo shared in tweet on March 16 Cheetah helicopter crash in Arunachal
content: New Delhi, Mar 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a helicopter in his post on the March 16 Army helicopter crash, indicating the same chopper crashed in Arunachal Pradesh. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image shared in the tweet was old and unrelated to Thursday's crash which killed both pilots. The social media post was shared with a misleading claim. Claim A Twitter user shared the photo of a helicopter in his post, which read in English: "Sad News. News of Indian Army helicopter crash reported in Arunachal Pradesh. Search operation is going on". Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the tweet. The search results led us to an article by APN News, which carried the same picture to report the incident of the Army helicopter crash in Arunachal Pradesh on Mar 16. Here is the link and archive link to the article, and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combined image of the two photos – one shared by a news outlet to report about the Mar 16 helicopter crash and the other shared in the 2020 news article: The Desk subsequently conducted a Google search with the keyword "Army helicopter crash-lands in Udhampur, Feb 2020". The search results led us to a report by Hindustan Times, carrying the same photo on the crash-landing of an Army helicopter in Jammu and Kashmir on Feb 3, 2020. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Reasi district is in the Jammu region, bordered by Udhampur and Ramban districts in the east. The Desk also noticed that the 2020 reports were on the crash-landing of a Chetak helicopter. In contrast, the news outlet and the social media user on the crash of a Cheetah helicopter on March 16 carried the same photo. The Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "difference between Cheetah and Chetak helicopters" and found a YouTube video by Defence Direct Education, a verified channel, which described the different features of both helicopters. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the page: "Compared to the older single-engine light utility Chetak helicopters, which have a bulkier body, Cheetahs are leaner and have skis as their landing gear. The Cheetahs also have fewer seating capacity and can land on the smallest helipads," according to an article by The Print . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media user shared an old and unrelated image in his post on the Army helicopter crash in Arunachal Pradesh on Mar 16.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of AIMIM leader Owaisi with BJP's Murli Manohar Joshi at a media event shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A photo of All India Majlis-E-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief and Lok Sabha MP Asaduddin Owaisi holding a trophy standing next to senior BJP leader Murli Manohar Joshi was shared in a social media post, claiming he was honoured by the BJP leader recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo shared in social media posts was edited to convey a false claim. Owaisi received an award in the category of outstanding Parliamentarian of 2022 at an annual event organised on March 14 by a media house in New Delhi. Owaisi received the award from former President Ram Nath Kovind. Claim On March 15, Rajasthan Youth Congress – a verified Twitter handle – shared a photo of AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi holding a trophy and claimed the Hyderabad MP was honoured by BJP leader Murli Manohar Joshi. "वरिष्ठ भाजपा नेता के हाथों असदुद्दीन ओवैसी को सम्मानित कराया जा रहा है। इतना काफ़ी है यह बताने के लिये कि...'ये रिश्ता क्या कहलाता है...?'," read the Twitter post, dated Mar 15, which has garnered over 7400 views, along with more than 500 likes and 140 retweets. An English translation of the post read: "Asaduddin Owaisi is being honoured by a senior BJP leader. This much is enough to tell that... 'What is this relationship called...?'" Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo. It led us to another Twitter post – by another verified handle named Bihar Youth Congress – which carried the same picture and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk found multiple other posts by organisations and leaders of the Congress who shared the same photo and claim on Twitter. Two can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk subsequently conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Murli Manohar Joshi Asaduddin Owaisi award" and found an article published by India Today on Mar 14, which featured a similar image. The headline read: "Asaduddini Owaisi Awarded Best Parliamentarian Award By Lokmat." Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image of the two photos – the one shared in social media posts and the other carried in the news article. The India Today website embedded a video in its article, where Owaisi was seen receiving an award from former Indian President Ram Nath Kovind and standing beside a group of people, including Joshi. Here is the link to the YouTube video : Below is a combination image of the photos shared in social media posts with the video's visuals from the 3:20 timestamp. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the YouTube channel of Lokmat Hindi, the media group which organised the event where Owaisi received the award. We found a video posted on March 15 titled "Asaduddin Owaisi को मिला लोकसभा के सर्वश्रेष्ठ सांसद का पुरस्कार | Lokmat Parliamentary Award (Asaduddin Owaisi received the Best Parliamentarian Award of Lok Sabha | Lokmat Parliamentary Award)." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same. At 1:02, Owaisi was seen receiving the award from Kovind. At 1:31, we can see all invitees to the event standing on the podium, and that is when Joshi is seen standing beside the AIMM chief. Below is the combined image of the photo shared in the social media post and a screenshot of visuals at the timestamp mentioned above in the video: The Desk subsequently concluded that Owaisi didn't receive the award from BJP's Murli Manohar Joshi as claimed in the social media posts. An edited photo was taken out of context and shared with a false claim on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: IEP 'wrongly' mentions CPI instead of CPI (Maoist) in its Global Terrorism Index report; Incorrect report's screenshot shared on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of the world's '20 deadliest terror groups of 2022' was shared on social media in which the Communist Party of India (CPI) was placed the twelfth position. The Institute of Economics and Peace released the report on March 16, headquartered in Sydney. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the name of the CPI was mistakenly mentioned in the report instead of CPI (Maoist). The information with the correct name was later updated on the official website of IEP. The claim shared in the social media posts was misleading. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo which showed the Communist Party of India ranked 12th in the list of the world's "20 deadliest terror groups". The user claimed that the CPI was mentioned in the Global Terrorism Index released by the Institute of Economics and Peace. "Institute for Economics and Peace, in its latest Global Terrorism Index, lists the 20 deadliest terror groups of 2022. At 12, is the Communist Party of India," read the post shared on Mar 17. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo and found a couple of Twitter posts carrying the same picture with similar claims. The tweets can be seen here and here , and the archived posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "world's 20 deadliest terror groups 2022". The search results led us to a report by Hindustan Times on March 16. Here is the link to the report titled "India among worst-hit but terror not a top concern to daily safety", and below is a screenshot of the same: "The report listed the Communist Party of India (Maoist) as the 12th deadliest terror group in 2022, ahead of al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula (13th) and Lashkar-e-Taiba (16th). The Maoists were responsible for 39 deaths and 30 injuries in 61 attacks last year," the report stated. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted another customised Google search with the keyword "Global Terror Index Report 2023, IEP". The search results led to the official website of the Institute of Economics and Peace, where we found the said report. Here is the link to the PDF report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk reviewed the 95-page PDF report titled 'Global Terrorism Index 2023' and found a similar list on the 13th page. "20 deadliest terror groups of 2022," read the listicle title, which mentioned CPI (Maoist) in the twelfth spot. Below is a comparison of the two lists – the one shared in social media posts and the other presented on the official report on the IEP website. Notably, the CPI (Maoist) and all its affiliated organisations have been included in the list of banned terrorist organisations under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act 1967. During its investigation, the Desk also found a report by Premium Times – a Nigerian media organisation – which hyperlinked a similar PDF report as there on the official website of the IEP. Here is the link to the report and the PDF file . The Desk clicked on the hyperlink, which led to the report mentioning the Communist Party of India on the list of "20 deadliest terror groups of 2022". Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a report by Times of India, dated Mar 18, which quoted a representative of IEP stating that the CPI (Maoist) was mistakenly labelled as CPI in the report, which was later rectified. Here is the link to the report titled "CPI in terror group list: IEP corrects report, uploads revised list". Below is a screenshot of the same: "The report utilised Dragonfly's Terrorism Tracker data and incorporated the terminology used in their database, which mislabelled the Communist Party of India as it did not include the correct (Maoist) addition. As soon as we were made aware, we immediately corrected the report to reflect the title of the Communist Party of India (Maoist)," read a part of the report. "Our data refers to a group called 'Communist Party of India – Maoist'. This is not the same entity as the 'Communist Party of India', which, as you note, is a legitimate political party and not a terrorist organisation. The confusion may have arisen by an omission or overlooking of the important 'Maoist' part of the name in material somewhere along the line," Dragonfly told the TOI. In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted the Institute for Economics & Peace (IEP), which acknowledged the error regarding the mislabelling of the party's name in the list. "The report utilises Dragonfly's Terrorism Tracker data, and incorporated the terminology used in their database which mislabelled the Communist Party of India as it did not include the correct (Maoist) addition. As soon as we were made aware, we took immediate action and corrected the report to accurately reflect the title of Communist Party of India (Maoist)," the IEP said in its response on the e-mail to PTI. It also shared with us the updated list, which can be viewed here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the IEP erroneously mentioned the Community Party of India's name instead of CPI (Maoist) in its list of "20 deadliest terror groups of 2022", which was part of its Global Terrorism Index report. The organisation, in its updated information, rectified the error.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated photos of collapsed buildings falsely linked to March 21 earthquake in Afghanistan and shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared four photos of collapsed buildings, claiming the destruction was caused by the 6.5 magnitude earthquake in SWAT and Gilgit Baltistan areas in Afghanistan. The user shared the photos in the tweet posted after Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region was hit by an earthquake late evening on March 21. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that all four photos shared in the tweet were old and unrelated to the March 21 earthquake. The claim in the social media post was false. The tremors of the massive earthquake in Afghanistan were also felt in several parts of north India and neighbouring Pakistan. Claim A Twitter user shared four photos, claiming they showed visuals of the destruction caused by the 6.5 magnitude earthquake that hit the Hindu Kush region in Afghanistan on Mar 21. "News coming from SWAT & Gilgit Baltistan is not good. Pray for the safety (Sic)," read the March 21 post, along with which the user put a hashtag of the earthquake. The Twitter post has garnered over 484K views, more than 1400 likes, and nearly 400 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on each of the four photos shared in the Twitter post. The search results led us to another Twitter post with the same images and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Going through the comment section of the Twitter post, we found a user claiming that none of the four photos was related to the Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. "None of these pictures are from today. The first one is 2019 - Kashmir, second is 2021 - Kashmir, third is 2021 - Kashmir, fourth is 2005 – Pakistan," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the comment, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a separate investigation on each of the four photos shared in the Twitter post. Below is the fact-check for each image: Photo 1 The first photo showed 3-4 men looking at the rubble of a house destroyed in what the user claimed was the Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. The Google Reverse Image Search results for the image led the Desk to a news report by Arab News, dated Sep 25, 2019. The information, which carried an image with visuals slightly matching the viral photo, was titled: "24 dead, more than 450 injured in Pakistan's devastating quake". The article reported the 5.8 magnitudes that caused massive destruction and loss of 24 lives, with more than 450 injured in Mirpur of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image highlighting the similarities in the visuals of the two photos – one shared in the Twitter post and the other carried in the news article – along with the same wall colour of both the dilapidated houses. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords, leading to a BBC article dated Sep 25, 2019. This article, which carried the same viral image, was also about the earthquake causing devastation in Mirpur. It attributed the photo to Getty Images. Here is the link to the article titled 'Mirpur: At least 25 people were killed and 452 injured in the earthquake' and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the first photo was of September 2019, relating to an earthquake that hit Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Photo 2 The second photo showed large cement slabs over the rubble of a building, destructed in an earthquake. The Google Reverse Image Search results led to a report by Evening Standard, which carried a similar image. The report, titled 'Turkiye earthquake death toll rises to 22 as rescuers hunt for survivors beneath collapsed buildings', was published on Jan 25, 2020. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two ideas – one shared in the viral social media post and the other shared in the news article. The Desk noticed that the photo shared in the Twitter post included the name of the AFP news agency at the bottom left corner. Taking a cue from this, we combined the Google Reverse Image Search results for the image with the keyword "AFP, Turkiye earthquake, Jan 2020". The search results led to an AFP Forum link of the same photo as shared in the social media post. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: The photo's description read: "Turkish officials and police work at the scene of a collapsed building following a 6.8 magnitude earthquake in Elazig, eastern Turkiye on January 24, 2020. A magnitude of 6.8 hits eastern Turkey, killing at least four people, causing buildings to collapse and sending panicked residents rushing into the street. Rescue teams were being sent to the scene of the quake, which had its epicentre in the small lakeside town of Sivrice in the eastern province of Elazig." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo was of the earthquake that struck eastern Turkey on Jan 24, 2020. Photo 3 The third photo showed two men looking at the rubble of a building, purportedly destroyed in an earthquake. The Desk went through the Google Reverse Image Search results and came across a news report by The Guardian. The headline of the article, dated Sep 25, 2019, read: "Pakistan earthquake leaves 19 dead and 300 injured in Kashmir region". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "At least 19 people have been killed and 300 injured after a shallow earthquake struck north-eastern Pakistan, tearing car-sized cracks into roads and heavily damaging infrastructure," read the report. The news report carried the same image as shared in the viral post, giving image credit to AFP and Getty Images. Below is a combination image comparing the two photos – one shared in the Twitter post and the other carried by the news article. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and found another news report by Daily Mail, dated Sep 24, 2019. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo dated back to September 2019, when a 5.8-magnitude earthquake struck Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Photo 4 The fourth photo in the Twitter post showed a boy standing near the rubble of a destroyed building. The Google Reverse Image Search results for the image led to the same article by The Guardian, as mentioned in the investigation for the third photo. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The photo's caption read: "A Pakistani man stands beside a collapsed building following an earthquake on the outskirts of Mirpur. Photograph: Aamir Qureshi/AFP/Getty Images". Below is a combination image comparing the two photos – one shared in the Twitter post and the other carried by the news article. Taking a cue from The Guardian report, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords, which led to a report by The Weather Channel, dated Sep 25, 2019. The article carried the same photo and reported the loss of 22 lives in the earthquake that hit Mirpur in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Hence, the Desk concluded that a photo from the September 2019 earthquake that hit Pakistan-occupied Kashmir was recently shared, relating it to the Mar 21 earthquake that hit Afghanistan. Subsequently, it was found that all four photos shared in the Twitter post were old and unrelated to the Mar 21 earthquake that struck Afghanistan

title: PTI Fact Check: Two old and unrelated videos falsely linked to Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan and shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Two videos were shared by social media users claiming both the video clips were related to the March 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. A 6.5-magnitude quake hit Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region on the evening of Mar 21, and strong tremors were felt across several parts of North India and neighbouring Pakistan. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that both the videos were old and unrelated to the Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. The claims in social media posts sharing the videos were false. The Desk conducted a separate investigation on the two videos shared on social media. Here's what we found in the investigation- Claim 1 A Twitter user shared a 10-second video clip showing the floor under a man's chair subsiding suddenly while he managed a close shave. The user claimed the video was related to the earthquake in Afghanistan on Mar 21. "Viral Video. Another #video showing the moment of yesterday's #earthquake that shook #Pakistan, #Afghanistan, recorded by CCTV. #भूकंप," read the tweet shared on Mar 22. Here is the link and archive link to the video. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation – Claim 1 Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to an Instagram post, which carried the same video. The March 9 post read: "Dude has advance conquers haki". Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combined image comparing the visuals from the two videos – one shared in the Twitter post and the other shared on Instagram. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Reddit post which included the same video shared on June 16, 2022. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk could last verify the origin of the video to June 2022, which made it clear that it was unrelated to the Mar 21 earthquake. Claim 2 A Twitter user shared a 45-second video of a building collapsing, purportedly due to an earthquake. "Allah Almighty, protect our brothers and sisters. Prayers for Pakistan Powerful 7.7," the user wrote in the post, using the hashtags #Earthquake #sialkot #Rawalpindi #lahore #Afghanistan #Turkey #Pakistan #astagfirullah". Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The tweet was posted after a 6.5-magnitude earthquake at 10:17 pm IST struck Afghanistan. The hashtags used in the Twitter post and its timing implicated that it showed visuals of the Afghanistan earthquake. Investigation – Claim 2 The Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A separate Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a tweet by NDTV posted on Feb 6, 2023, which carried the same video, mentioning it to be of the massive earthquakes that struck Turkiye and Syria on that day. "'Most Powerful In A Century' Earthquake In Turkiye, Syria, Over 1,400 Dead," read the Twitter post dated Feb 6. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords, which led to a YouTube video posted by CNBC-TV18 on Feb 6. This 14-second clip carried a smaller version of the video shared in the Twitter post. The video title read: "Turkey Earthquake: Building Collapses After The Earthquake Hits Turkey | #shorts | CNBC-TV18." Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination photo comparing images of the two videos – the one shared in the Twitter post and the other uploaded on YouTube by a news channel. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video related to the earthquakes in Turkiye and Syria on Feb 6 this year was recently shared, just after an earthquake struck Afghanistan on Mar 21. Hence, the Desk found that the two videos shared on social media were old and unrelated to the Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 couple kissing video at a railway platform peddled as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A Twitter user shared a video of a young couple kissing, purportedly, at a railway platform. It claimed it was a recent incident after being "inspired by Patna Junction" incident. The video emerged on social media after an incident where TV screens installed at platform number 10 at Patna railway station played a porn clip. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a one-year-old video from Dombivli Railway Station in Mumbai was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on March 21 a video clip of a couple kissing and claimed that it was a recent incident after being "inspired by Patna Junction". The post, which has over 1 million views and 7,300 likes so far, read, "After being inspired by #patnajunction, now trends have started coming from other stations as well. पटना रेलवे स्टेशन (Patna Railway Station) #23_मार्च_बिहार_बंद (23 March Bihar closed)". Here are links to the post and archive post , and below is the screenshot. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the 26-second video clip, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to an article published by Zee News on Jan 29, 2023, with the headline "Railway Station पर कपल का Kiss हुआ वायरल, यूजर्स ने कहा- शर्म करो". The English translation of the headline read, "Couple's kiss at railway station goes viral, users say – have shame". Here is the link to the article , and below is its screenshot: The article carried the same video as shared in the viral social media post. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals from the two videos: The summary of the article read, "मुंबई के डोंबिवली रेलवे स्टेशन का एक वीडियो तेजी से वायरल हो रहा है. इस वीडियो में आप एक कपल को सरेआम किस करते हुए देख सकते है. आपको बता दें की ये वीडियो पिछले साल डाला गया था लेकिन कई लोग इसे अब भी शेयर कर रहे हैं." An English summary translation read, "A video from Mumbai's Dombivli railway station is becoming increasingly viral. In this video, you can see a couple kissing in public. Let us tell you that this video was posted last year, but many people are still sharing it." Taking a cue from the information in the news article, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "couple kissing Dombivli railway station". The search results led to a report by Mid-Day from March 10, 2022. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The article carried a photo which looked similar to the visuals of the video shared in the Twitter post. Below is a combination image comparing the picture in the news article to the visuals of the viral video: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a one-year-old video was recently shared on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 photos of 'red glow' over Atlantic Ocean shared on social media with misleading claim after March 21 Afghanistan earthquake
content: New Delhi, Mar 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared photos of a 'mysterious red glow over the Atlantic Ocean, claiming a pilot clicked them in March 2023. The user also used the hashtag #earthquake in the post, suggesting that the rare occurrence was connected to the Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the pictures dated back to July 2022 and were shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. The Twitter post was shared shortly after a 6.5-magnitude earthquake struck Afghanistan on Mar 21 this year. Strong tremors of the quake were felt in several parts of North India and neighbouring Pakistan. Claim A Twitter user shared three photos of what he called a 'mysterious red glow' over the Atlantic Ocean, claiming they were claimed by a pilot this month. The user also used the hashtag #earthquake, suggesting a connection between the rare occurrence and the calamity that struck Afghanistan on Mar 21. "Something strange is happening around the globe. The mysterious red glow was seen over the Atlantic. The pilot that spotted the phenomenon said he's never seen anything like it. The photo was taken March 2023 Rs #earthquakes #زلزلہ (#earthquake)," read the tweet, posted on Mar 21. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, which has garnered over 30K views. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photos shared in the viral social media post. The search results led to an article by Interesting Engineering published on July 23, 2022. The title of the article, carrying the same photos as shared in the Twitter post, read: "A mysterious red glow over the Pacific Ocean leaves a pilot baffled". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the photos were shared by a Reddit user. The hyperlink on the article led the Desk to the Reddit post dated July 22, 2022. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photos shared in the Twitter post to those posted on Reddit. On further scanning the Google Reverse Image Search results, we found several other news reports carrying the same photos in their articles dating back to July 2022. Two such reports by Hindustan Times and The Sun can be viewed here and here . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photos, which dated back to July 2022, had nothing to do with any earthquake that occurred in March 2023, particularly the one that struck Afghanistan on Mar 21.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of two men marrying same woman peddled as real on social media, news websites; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared two photos of two men applying vermillion on a woman's forehead, claiming they married the same woman.
