In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the shared video clip was part of a scripted video, and the people in the video were actors. The photo was shared in social media posts with a false claim. As an actual incident, several news outlets also peddled the scripted video. Claim A Twitter user shared two photos, which showed a woman sitting and two men putting vermillion on her forehead one by one. The user claimed the two men married the same woman. "दो लड़कों ने एक लड़की की मांग में सिंदूर भरा, और बारी बारी से मंगलसूत्र भी बांधा। इस तरह दो लड़कों ने एक ही लड़की से शादी कर ली। इसकी पुष्टि @SureshChavhanke करेगा।" read the Twitter post, dated Mar 17. An English tweet translation read: "Two boys filled vermilion in the forehead of a girl and tied Mangalsutra one by one. This way, two boys married the same girl. @SureshChavhanke will confirm this." The Twitter post has garnered over 50K views, more than 1500 likes and 500 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on each of the two photos shared in the Twitter post. The search results led the Desk to an article by News18 Hindi, which carried the same images. "2 लड़कों ने बारी-बारी से भरी लड़की की मांग, मिल-बांट कर पहनाया मंगलसूत्र, Sharing Is Caring की जबरदस्त मिसाल," read the headline of the article, dated Mar 19. "2 boys filled a girl's forehead (vermillion) one by one, tied mangalsutra together, a tremendous example of Sharing Is Caring," read the headline when roughly translated to English. Here is the link and archive link to the news article. News18, however, later updated the article, stating it as a scripted video. The Desk found that DNA India and TV9 had also carried the same photos, reporting them as real in their news articles. The reports by DNA India and TV9 can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. Taking a cue from this, the Desk did a customised Google search with relevant keywords. The search results led us to a YouTube video uploaded on Nov 26, 2022. The title of the 2:20-minute video read: "एक लड़की ने की दो लड़कों से शादी (Girl marries two boys)." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The person shooting the video asked the woman and men if they were getting married willingly, to which they replied in affirmation. "I loved both and couldn't leave any of them; that's why I took this decision and married both of them," the woman says. At 1:00 minute, the two men said they were brothers and loved the same woman. They further said they were from Uttar Pradesh, while the woman claimed she was from Delhi. The 1:35 minute, the woman said she met them in college and fell in love. She further stated that her mother was unaware of her getting married to two men. The two men identify themselves as Ashish and Rohan, while the woman tells her name as Riya. Continuing our search, we found a Facebook post with an extended video version. The 6:33-minute video was uploaded by a Facebook page named 'Tukka' on Nov 10, 2022, which has garnered 1.9 million views. Here is the link to the Facebook video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and noticed that at 6:30 minutes, it displayed a disclaimer stating that it was "purely made for entertainment purpose". Below is a screenshot of the video from the specific timestamp when the disclaimer was displayed: The page 'Tukka (Content Creator India)' uploaded the video, which has 626K followers. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk went through other videos posted on the page and found that the female actor, as seen in the viral video, had appeared in another video. In this video, she played the role of a swindler who duped people of their money on the pretext of offering a job. Another character in the video can be seen hitting and slapping the girl to make her confess to the wrongdoing. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image from the two videos, showing that the female actor in both videos was the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a recent scripted video of two men marrying the same woman was shared by a Twitter user and several news outlets.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old videos unrelated to March 21 earthquake in Afghanistan shared as recent on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Mar 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Social media users shared two videos, claiming they were related to the 6.5-magnitude earthquake that hit Afghanistan's Hindu Kush region on Mar 21, leading to tremors in parts of North India and Pakistan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that both videos were old and unrelated to the Mar 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. The claim shared in the social media posts was false. The Desk separately investigated both videos, and here is what we found -- Claim 1 A Twitter user shared a six-second video clip on Mar 22 showing a man keeping liquor bottles from falling, purportedly due to the Mar 21 earthquake that led to solid tremors in the Delhi NCR region. "दिल्ली NCR में कल रात आए भूकंप के झटके से अपने कीमती सामान की रक्षा करता एक शख्स कैमरे में कैद हुआ है। मेरे ऐब तो जमाने मे उजागर हैं, फिक्र वो करे जिनके गुनाह पर्दे में है," read the post, which has over 1.95 lakh views and 1,300 likes. When translated to English, the post read, "A man has been caught on camera protecting his valuables from the tremors of last night's earthquake in Delhi NCR. My faults are exposed; only those whose sins are hidden should worry. (sic)" Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation – Claim 1 The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to a Twitter post from February 23, 2023, carrying the same video. "Earthquake in Afghanistan and Tajikistan Rt #Afghanistan #Earthquake #Tajikistan," read the post, which has over 214K views and 1500 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found an article published by Max Maharashtra on June 6, 2022, where screenshots from the same video were shared. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The article included a June 13 Twitter post, which carried the same video as shared in the viral social media post: Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: "Some guys r crystal clear about their priority #BREAKING 4.0 magnitude #Earthquake occurred at 6:32 am in Tura, Meghalaya (northeast). This champ is busy to save the state's economy, (sic)," read the one-year-old post with 37 likes. We could trace the origin of the video on the internet, from the latest to June 2022. While it was unclear when and where it was initially shot, the video had no connection to the May 21 earthquake in Afghanistan. Claim 2 A Twitter user shared a video on Mar 22 which showed massive cracks on the road and claimed it was related to the Mar 21 earthquake, whose impact was also experienced in Pakistan. "Earthquake in Pakistan," read the post with over 3,000 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation – Claim 2 The Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to an article published by India TV on Sep 25, 2019, with the headline "26 dead, over 300 injured as powerful earthquake jolts Pakistan; Mirpur worst-hit". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The photo in the news report looked visually similar to the visuals of the video shared in the Twitter post. Below is a combination image comparing the photo to the visuals of the viral video: The Desk then conducted a customised Google Search with the keyword "earthquake Pakistan 2019", which led us to a YouTube video posted by Guardian News three years ago titled "Earthquake in Pakistani Kashmir leaves dozens dead". Here is a link to the video , and below is the screenshot. We found that the 0:09-0:17 second portion of the video was the same as the 0:01-0:07 second portion of the video shared in the Twitter post. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos – one shared in the viral social media post and the other shared on YouTube. The YouTube video mentioned that the visuals had been taken from the Facebook page of Islamgarh Channel. Taking a cue from this, we scanned the Facebook page and found that the same video had been posted on Sep 24, 2019, titled "Earthquake in Jaatlan Azad Kashmir". Here is the link and archive post to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Hence, the Desk concluded that a recent four-year-old video had been posted on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photos of Donald Trump's 'imaginary arrest' peddled as real on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared photos which purportedly showed former US President Donald Trump arrested and taken away by the police. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found that the images were fake, created using AI-powered tools, and shared on social media with false claims. These photos of Trump's arrest have been widely shared across social media over the past few days. Notably, these photos emerged after Trump said on Mar 18 that he was expecting to be arrested on Mar 21 as New York prosecutors considered charges over a hush money payment to an alleged 'pornstar' and called on his supporters to protest. Claim An Instagram user shared a post on Mar 21 with several photos, which showed the purported arrest of former US President Donald Trump. The text on the photos read: "BREAKING: Donald Trump was just arrested by New York law enforcement." "Donald trump getting arrested today, what a time to be alive," read the post, which has been liked by over 79,000 people so far. Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted Google Reverse Image Search on the photos shared in the post and found a Twitter post carrying the same images with a similar claim. The Twitter post has received nearly 10 million views, more than 31000 likes and 2600 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk also came across a Twitter thread posted by a British journalist and director of Bellingcat Productions, Elliot Higgins. In his Twitter post, dated Mar 21, Higgins shared a long sequence of 52 photos and wrote: "Making pictures of Trump getting arrested while waiting for Trump's arrest." The photos narrated the sequence of Trump facing conviction in a court, followed by jostling with police officers and finally getting arrested. The images then show him in jail. In one of the tweets, Higgins stated that he created the images using Midjourney - an artificial intelligence program designed by a San Francisco-based independent research lab Midjourney, Inc. The tool uses generative AI to create images from user text prompts. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: Further, in reply to a user who asked which software he used to create the images, Higgins said: "Midjourney v5." Here is the link to the comment, and below is a screenshot of the same: Further, the user asked Higgins which prompt he used to create the images. To this, Higgins replied: "Donald Trump falling over while getting arrested. Fibonacci Spiral. News footage." gave me the following:" Here is the link to the comment , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked on Midjourney and found more images showing Trump getting arrested, created by other users. Below are a couple of screenshots: The Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Donald Trump gets arrested" but could not find any authentic news report regarding the claim made in viral social media posts. The Desk contacted Higgins, seeking his response on the photos and the viral claims via email, to which he replied: "It's been interesting to see the reaction to the thread as its moved through online communities, its now reached Infowars so I'm getting quite a few angry MAGA types responding, but generally the response has been positive. What really stood out for me is the number of people who don't seem to have been aware of Midjourney's existence, or what it's capable of, so I think it has had a positive impact in raising awareness of what kind of images can be faked now." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that photos showing Trump's arrest were created using a generative AI tool to create images from text prompts fed by users.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of 'Putin bowing to Jinping' peddled as real on social media with false claims
content: New Delhi, Mar 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo purportedly showing Russian President Vladimir Putin bowing to Chinese President Xi Jinping. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image was fake, created using advanced artificial intelligence technology. It was shared in social media posts with false claims. The photo went viral on social media amid Jinping's three-day state visit to Moscow from Mar 20-23. The meeting between Putin and Jinping grabbed the global eyeballs due to the current geopolitical scenario and the Russia-Ukraine War. Claim A Twitter user with a verified handle shared a photo that purportedly showed Russian President Vladimir Putin kneeling before Chinese President Xi Jinping. The user claimed it was from the recent meeting between the two leaders in Moscow on Mar 20. "PUTIN XI MEETING. Putin attempting to persuade Xi," read the post shared on Mar 20, which has garnered over 770K views, along with nearly 6000 likes and more than 1000 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Twitter post. The search results led to another Twitter post carrying the same picture with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk also came across a Twitter post by Next TV, which included a 24-second video clip of Putin and Jinping greeting each other ahead of the meeting. Here is the link to the Mar 20 Twitter post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk compared the viral photo with the video's visuals and found some contrast differences in chairs and the room where the meeting occurred. Also, Jinping can be seen wearing a blue suit in the viral photo, while the video shared by the news channel shows him wearing a black suit. Below is a combination image comparing the photo with the visuals of the video: On closely watching the viral photo, the Desk noticed the following irregularities that hinted towards the possibility of it being a fake image: The ears of both the persons in the photo – claimed by Putin and Jinping – look strangely deformed and not matching. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: The person standing behind was seen holding his hands, which look deformed. Below is a screenshot showing the same: The eyes and nose of the person standing (claimed to be Jinping) look deformed, and the head size does not match the proportion of the rest of the body. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: All these are considered strong indications of an image being fake or created through AI-powered tools. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the Google Reverse Image Search results for the viral photo and came across a Twitter post by Amanda Florian, a tech journalist. Florian posted the same photo on Mar 21, claiming an AI program generated it. In a thread of several tweets, Florian explained the entire investigation process to conclude that the image was created using an AI-powered tool. Check the Twitter thread here . Below are the key points she highlighted in her investigation: She first pointed out the genuine photos from the meeting, which showed a completely different background and set of chairs at the meeting between Putin and Jinping. Here is the link to the tweet and below is a screenshot: An AI image detector by Hugging Face, a French tech company, pointed out that the image was artificial. The blurriness and irregularity of the nose of the person standing, as discussed in the investigation above. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Putin Jinping Meeting March 2023". The search results led to a Mar 20 CNN article titled 'China's Xi stresses close ties with 'dear friend' Putin during his first visit to Russia since Ukraine invasion'. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The article included the same video as shared by Nexta TV in its tweet. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-created photo of Putin kneeling before Jinping was shared as accurate on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of US veteran confronting Joe Biden shared on social media as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of an Air Force veteran confronting US President Joe Biden over the latter's support of the 2002 invasion of Iraq by the American forces. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from a Presidential election campaign event in 2020 and that Biden had not been elected as the US president yet. The video was shared on social media as recently with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a 1:35-minute video on Mar 22 of a US Air Force veteran confronting Joe Biden regarding his support of the Iraq war. Comparing the state of democracy in the countries, the user questioned if a similar scenario was possible in India. "अमेरिका में अपने राष्ट्रपति से एक नागरिक कैसे आंखों में आंख डालकर सवाल कर रहा है। क्या "लोकतंत्र की मां" अर्थात भारत में ये संभव है ? अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति जो बाइडेन से अमेरिकी war veteran ने सवाल किया– "इराकी युद्व में लाखों बेगुनाह मारे गए, तुमने हमें मासूमों को मारने के लिए भेजा था? मेरे कई साथी मारे गए, तुम्हारे हाथ मासूमों के खू'न से रंगे है" अच्छा हुआ ये बन्दा अमेरिका में है! अपने देश मे होता तो अब तक कई देशों से तार जोड़ दिए जाते?" read the post. An English translation of the post read, "How is a citizen in America questioning his President eye to eye. Is this possible in "mother of democracy," i.e. India? American war veteran questions US President Joe Biden - "Millions of innocents killed in the Iraqi war, you sent us to kill innocents? Many of my companions were killed; your hands are painted with innocent blood." Good thing this guy is in America! How many countries would he have been linked to if it was in our country?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to an article published by The Independent on Mar 5, 2020, under the headline "'Their blood is on your hands': Veterans confront Joe Biden over support for Iraq war". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the article, the man seen confronting Biden was Air Force veteran Michael Thurman, a member of the group "About Face: Veterans Against the War", and the incident took place during a Presidential election campaign event in Oakland, California, on Mar 3, 2020. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keyword "Air Force veteran confronts Joe Biden". The search results led to a YouTube video posted by a verified user on March 4, 2020, titled "US veterans confront Joe Biden over his record of supporting war." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same. The video's description read, "Two veterans confronted US Presidential candidate Joe Biden over his record of supporting the war in Iraq and Afghanistan during a campaign stopover in California." The Desk subsequently concluded that an old video from 2020 of Biden, when he was not the President, being confronted by a US Air Force veteran was being shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim. The invasion of Iraq by the US forces began with the invasion of the country by a United States-led coalition that overthrew the Iraqi government of Saddam Hussein in 2002. The US claimed the intent was to "disarm Iraq of weapons of mass destruction, to end Saddam Hussein's support for terrorism, and to free the Iraqi people".

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and edited video of woman 'refusing' to accept LPG connection from PM Modi resurfaces and shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Mar 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video clip which purportedly showed a woman beneficiary refusing to accept an LPG gas connection from Prime Minister Narendra Modi at an event. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video dating back to 2016 was digitally altered to be played in reverse. The original video clearly showed the woman accepting and not returning or refusing to accept the LPG gas connection. The edited video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a 15-second video on Mar 12, which purportedly showed a woman refusing to accept a gas connection from PM Modi at an event. The post, which has over 470 views, read, "यें पकड़ो अपना सलेंडर हम को करो माफ़ इतना महँगा कहा से भरवाएँगे." "Hold on to your cylinder, forgive us, it is so expensive, from where will we get it filled?" an English translation of the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a YouTube video uploaded by the official account of the Bharatiya Janata Party on May 1, 2016. The video's title read: "PM Shri Narendra Modi at the launch of the Ujjwala Yojana in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk closely watched the video and found that the timestamp 26:23-26:34 showed the same woman – a beneficiary of the central government's flagship Ujjwala Yojana – accepting the gas connection from the prime minister. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral and original videos: Also, between 0:13 and 0:15 timestamps in the viral video, the woman is seen purportedly walking away from the stage while joining her hands. On the contrary, in the video posted by BJP's official handle on YouTube, the woman walks towards PM Modi on the stage to accept the free LPG connection. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from the viral and original videos: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk noticed the watermark of PowerEditor, a video editing programme, on the bottom right side of the viral video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the 2016 video was digitally altered to make it look like the woman was walking back after refusing to accept the LPG connection from PM Modi.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of China's railway bridge falsely shared on social media as Kashmir's Chenab Bridge on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a 28-second video clip showing a train passing through a railway bridge connecting two mountain areas, claiming it was a running train test video on the under-construction Chenab bridge of Jammu and Kashmir. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video shared in the tweet was of the Beipanjiang Railway Bridge in China. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a 28-second video claiming it showed a train passing through the Chenab bridge of Jammu and Kashmir, touted as the world's highest railway bridge. "Successful small train test run was conducted on 21st March on world's highest railway track under construction on Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla rail link on Chenab river in Reasi District (Jammu) of Jammu & Kashmir Union Territory Congratulations," read the Mar 24 post with nearly 200 views. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a page by Wikimedia Commons, which carried a similar photo under the title "Beipanjiang Railway Bridge". Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Beipanjiang Railway Bridge", which led to an article by Highest Bridges. The 'Beipanjiang Railway Bridge Shuibai' page included several photos of the bridge while detailing its features and construction. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the photo of the bridge shared in the article and the visuals in the video shared in the Twitter post. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: The Desk noticed that the website's founder Eric Sakowski took the photos for the Highest Bridges page website. Hence, we contacted him regarding the video shared in the Twitter post. A response from Sakowski shall be added to the article accordingly. Meanwhile, the Desk further scanned the search results for the keyword search on Google and came across an article on a website of the Chinese newspaper called DDCPC. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The article carried a video similar to the one shared in the Twitter post. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of both videos: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Chenab railway bridge, Jammu and Kashmir". The search results led to a Twitter post by the Railway Ministry, including a Chenab bridge video, touted as the "world's highest railway arch bridge". Whether the landscape behind the bridge or the pillars, the Chenab Bridge's visuals differed from the one shown in the Twitter post. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and noticed the bridge was still under construction. Below is a combination photo comparing the visuals of the two videos – the one shared in the viral Twitter post and the other shared by the Railway Ministry – showing that both the completely different. We also came across a Mar 27 report by The Hindu, which stated that the bridge was under construction and trains would ply on it by January-February 2024. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media post falsely labelled a railway in China as the Chenab Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, NYT never stated 'Rupee would soon replace Dollar'; Misleading claims on Indian Rupee shared in social media post
content: New Delhi, Mar 29 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A Twitter user posted a thread of tweets with several claims on the 'global acceptance of the Indian Rupee' and stated that as many as 30 countries are carrying out transactions in Rupee. The user attributed the statement to the New York Times. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral post was misleading and falsely attributed to the NYT. Claim A Twitter user shared a post on the expanding global acceptance of the Indian Rupee. Quoting the New York Times, the user claimed that the Rupee was set to replace Dollar globally. As many as 30 countries were already carrying out transactions in the Indian currency. "New York Times लिखता है की अब डॉलर का स्थान भारत का रुपया ले लेगा... भारत ने Rupee का आरंभ 13 जुलाई 22 को ग्लोबल करना शुरू किया था आज 8 महीने में अंतरराष्ट्रीय होने जा रहा है.. क्या आश्चर्य की बात नहीं? 30 देश आज Rupee में लेनदेन कर रहे है। सऊदी भारत को तेल Rupee में कर रहा है," the user wrote in the Mar 10 post. An English translation of the post read: "New York Times writes that now India's rupee will replace dollar... India started globalising the rupee on 13 July 22; today, it will be international in 8 months. Isn't it surprising? Today 30 countries are doing transactions in rupees. Saudi is selling oil to India in rupees (Sic)." The Twitter post has garnered over 3,000 views, along with more than 200 likes so far. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Indian Rupee to replace Dollar, New York Times" but could not find any such report by the NYT. However, the Desk came across a report by Firstpost, published on Mar 27. The headline read: "Rupee races to replace dollar: Egypt, the latest entrant to the club of countries wanting to trade in INR". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "If the deal to settle trade in Indian rupee between Cairo and New Delhi goes through, Egypt would join 18 countries — Russia, UK, Singapore, Germany etc. — that have agreed to trade in INR and give up dollar for cross-border transactions," read the report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "18 countries to trade in Rupee" and came across a report by Business Today, published on Mar 14. The report headline read: "RBI allows banks from UK, 17 other countries to open Vostro accounts for rupee trade". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, "The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has granted approvals to foreign banks in 18 countries to open Vostro accounts to settle international trade in rupees. In July last year, the Centre said it would set up a mechanism to settle international trade in rupees." "The RBI has allowed Botswana, Fiji, Germany, Guyana, Israel, Kenya, Malaysia, Mauritius, Myanmar, New Zealand, Oman, Russia, Seychelles, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Uganda, and the United Kingdom to open Vostro accounts as of now," it added. The Twitter user wrongly mentioned the name of Italy among the countries that use the Rupee to trade. What are vostro accounts? In July 2022, the RBI announced a new trade mechanism to settle international rupee trade. To fix these trade deals, authorised Indian banks must open and maintain Special Rupee Vostro Accounts of the partner trading country's banks. Simply put, Rupee Vostro Accounts keep the foreign entity's holdings in the Indian bank in Indian rupees. In another tweet in the same thread, the user claimed that as many as 64 countries had agreed to carry out trade in Indian Rupee. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords. It came across a report by Money Control , dated Mar 14, which quoted the data provided by the Ministry of Finance to the Rajya Sabha showing that 60 such vostro accounts were opened across 18 countries. "Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha on March 14, Minister of State for Finance Bhagwat Karad said the central bank had granted 60 approvals in total so far to domestic and authorised foreign banks to open so-called 'Special Rupee Vostro Accounts' of correspondent banks from 18 countries, including those from major nations such as the United Kingdom and Germany," it stated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk found the link to the PDF file of Karad's reply in the Parliament. Here is the PDF link , and below is a screenshot of the same: While the Desk could not find any report by the NYT on the increasing global acceptance of the Rupee, it found one in which the New York Times reported India opening up foreign transaction settlements in Indian rupees. Here is the link to the article . The user also claimed in the tweets in the thread that the Indian currency found a place in the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as soon as 50 countries started transacting in Rupee. Here is the link and archive link to the claim, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the information available on the official website of IMF , "The SDR is an international reserve asset. The SDR is not a currency, but its value is based on a basket of five currencies—the US dollar, the euro, the Chinese renminbi, the Japanese yen, and the British pound sterling." In 2016, Peter Zollner, the Head of Banking at the Bank of International Settlements, outlined the criteria for a currency eligible to enter the SDR. "The first "gateway" criterion affirms that only the currencies issued by (member) countries or monetary unions with the largest value of exports over a period of five years can be considered. This criterion responds to a need to ensure that only currencies that play a significant role in the global economy can be considered for inclusion in the SDR. The second criterion requires that the potential currency is "freely usable"." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that most of the claims made by the Twitter user regarding the global acceptance of the Indian Rupee were misleading.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, all UPI transactions will not attract 1.1 per cent surcharge; Claim shared in social media posts is misleading
content: New Delhi, Mar 29 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter post was shared claiming UPI payments like Google Pay, PhonePe and PayTM will attract 1.1 per cent tax from April 1 this year. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claim was misleading. The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has stated that the "interchange fee of up to 1.1 per cent will be applicable on merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2000 only". The claim shared in the social media post was misleading. Claim Delhi AAP leader Naresh Balyan shared a Twitter post claiming that UPI transactions like Google Pay, PhonePe and PayTM will attract a 1.1 per cent tax from April 1. "1 अप्रैल से UPI पेमेंट जैसे गूगल पे, फ़ोन पे, PayTM से पेमेंट करने पर 1.1% टैक्स लगेगा। मतलब 3 हजार का राशन खरीदा तो 32 रुपए टैक्स अलग से। याद कीजिए कैसे इन ठगो ने UPI पर अपना पीठ थपथपाया था। आखिर अब ये नया लूट किस लिए? लोग फिर लूट से बचने के लिए ऑनलाइन छोड़ कैश की तरफ भागेंगे ।" read the post, dated Mar 29. The English translation of the post read: "From April 1, UPI payments like Google Pay, PhonePe, and PayTM will attract 1.1% tax. This means if you bought a ration of 3 thousand, then tax of 32 rupees separately. Remember how these thugs patted their back on UPI? After all, what is this new loot for? People will again leave online and run towards cash to avoid loot." The tweet has garnered over 40K views, more than 1300 likes and 500 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media and came across another such tweet. The Twitter post, shared on Mar 29, carried a purported screenshot of a newspaper clipping, which claimed that UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 would attract a surcharge of 1.1 per cent. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with a specific set of keywords, which led to a Mar 29 report by NDTV. The report headline read: "UPI Merchant Transactions Over ₹ 2,000 To Carry Charge Of 1.1% From April 1". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the "interchange fee" of "up to 1.1 per cent" will be applicable on "merchant UPI transactions" from Apr 1. "In a notification issued today, NPCI said that the introduced fee only applies to merchant transactions made through prepaid payment instruments. The payments body clarified that no charges would be levied on regular UPI payments, which it termed "bank account- to-bank account-based UPI payments." the report read. Taking a cue, the Desk scanned the Google search results and came across a Twitter post by the NPCI, which was shared on Mar 29. The NPCI shared a press release in the post whose headline read: "NPCI Press Release: UPI is free, fast, secure and seamless. Every month, over 8 billion transactions are processed free for customers and merchants using bank accounts." Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: "The interchange charges introduced are only applicable for the PPI merchant transactions, and there is no customer charge. It is further clarified that there are no charges for the bank account to bank account-based UPI payments (i.e. normal UPI payments)," read the press release. Quoting the NPCI press release, PayTM also shared a Twitter post stating that "Paytm UPI is free, fast, secure, and seamless. No customer will pay any charges on making payments from UPI either from a bank account or PPI/Paytm Wallet." Here is the link to the Mar 29 tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that up to 1.1 per cent of interchange charges would only apply to merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, starting April 1.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi did not remove any tweets in recent past; Social media post claiming he deleted Savarkar tweets is false
content: New Delhi, Mar 30 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a post claiming Rahul Gandhi deleted his tweets on Savarkar after his grandson Ranjit Savarkar threatened to file an FIR against the Congress leader. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Gandhi did not recently delete posts on Savarkar on his Twitter handle. The claim shared in the social media post was false. The claim was made amid Gandhi facing a backlash from several political parties and leaders over his recent remarks against Savarkar. After being sentenced to two years in jail by a Surat court for his "Modi surname" remark, Rahul Gandhi had said: "My name is not Savarkar. My name is Gandhi. And Gandhis don't apologise." Savarkar's grandson Ranjit on Mar 27 lashed out at the Congress leader, saying that he would file an FIR against him for making baseless remarks and defaming his grandfather if he didn't apologise. Claim A Twitter user shared a post on March 28 claiming that Rahul Gandhi deleted tweets referring to late Indian politician Veer Savarkar following a backlash from his grandson Ranjit Savarkar. "#RahulGandhi has deleted all his tweets on #VeerSavarkar after Savarkar's grandson threatened to file an FIR against Rahul for his defamatory and baseless statements against Veer Savarkar," read the post with over 330K views and nearly 3000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media and came across a Twitter post shared on Mar 29. The user shared a screenshot of a Twitter search for a specific keyword related to Gandhi and Savarkar to back his claim that the former deleted his tweets referring to the late Indian politician. "डरो मत डरो मत चिल्लाकर राहुलजी थक गये। अब डर उनको लगने लगा है इस लिये राहुल जी ने सावरकर जी पर जितनी भी ट्वीट की है सब की सब हटा दी है। @RahulGandhi ये डर अच्छा लगा।" read the post. An English translation of the post read: "Don't be afraid, don't be afraid, Rahulji got tired of shouting. Now they feel scared; that's why Rahul ji has deleted all the tweets on Savarkar ji. @RahulGandhi This fear felt good." Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Rahul Gandhi deletes tweets on Savarkar" but found no such reports. The Desk then checked Rahul Gandhi's Twitter activities on a website named Social Blade. Social Blade gives all users access to our public database, which, using advanced technology, can provide you with global analytics for any content creator on a platform like Twitter. While scanning the website, the Desk found that Rahul Gandhi's total tweet count went up between Mar 27 (the day Ranjit Savarkar threatened to file an FIR) and Mar 30 (the day of publishing this article) three tweets. Here is the link to the Social Blade website, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the Twitter handle of Rahul Gandhi, which corroborated this. Gandhi shared one Twitter post on Mar 27 and two on Mar 30. Below are the screenshots of the three posts he made: Had Rahul Gandhi deleted any tweet on or after March 27, it would have reflected on the Social Blade statistics, i.e., the total number of tweets would have gone down. The Desk then searched Google Cache to see if Gandhi deleted any tweet referring to Savarkar in the past, but couldn't find any. Thus, the Desk concluded that while Gandhi referenced Savarkar in his speeches, there is a possibility that the Congress leader never posted Savarkar's name in the text in any of his tweets to date. Here is the link to one such tweet by Rahul Gandhi with a video of him referring to Savarkar during the Bharat Jodo Yatra. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Gandhi did not delete any tweet referring to Savarkar, following a backlash from the latter's grandson.

title: PTI Fact Check: Animated video of a car performing a high-octane stunt shared as real or movie scene on social media
content: New Delhi, Mar 30 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a car performing a high-octane stunt by bouncing off two buses across an underpass and landing on the other side of the road. Some other users believed the video was either original or a scene from any movie. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video shared on Twitter was not real footage. It was an animated video created using computer graphics and later shared on social media with false claims. Claim Noted businessman Harsh Goenka shared a video from his verified Twitter account on Mar 23 of a car performing a high-octane stunt by bouncing off two buses across an underpass and landing on the other side of the road. "Perfect timing….," read the post, which has garnered over 1 million views and over 1,300 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the same: Since Goenka nowhere mentioned in his tweet that it was a real video, many users believed it was either real or a scene from any movie. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed that Goenka shared the video posted by a Twitter user named 'No Context Brits', another verified handle. The handle shared the video on Dec 7 last year, writing: "Unbelievable". It has garnered over 5 million views and more than 11,000 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to a YouTube video uploaded one year ago titled "Car #jumps over a #truck#and #bus#crazy no #crash", where the duplicate footage had been shared. Here is the link to the video , which has over 4,000 views, and below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led us to an Instagram post by 2ncs. In this verified user, the same video had been shared on Apr 6, 2021, with hashtags such as #3D and #animation, indicating that the viral video was animated. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot: There were several animated videos of similar car stunts on the '2ncs' Instagram page. One such video was posted on Jul 18, 2019, where a car is seen moving under a truck, which had been shared with similar hashtags. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: We then searched the YouTube channel of "2NCS" and found a video posted three years ago titled "The truth | Ferrari under the truck". Here is the link to the video , which has over 90 lakh views, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the video, 2NCS explained how the animated video of the car moving under the truck was created. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk went through the comments section of the viral post and found that Harsh Goenka's reply to a comment confirmed that the video was not real. We also found many comments explaining that the video was created using computer graphics by Dionysis, a UK-based graphic designer, who shared it on his social media accounts and YouTube account named '2ncs'. Below is one of the screenshots of a comment- The Desk subsequently concluded that Goenka shared an animated video on Twitter which was further disseminated by many users thinking it was real or a movie scene.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered photo of Dubai's Burj Khalifa building shared on social media with the false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Dubai's iconic Burj Khalifa, claiming the skyscraper was lit up with Lord Ram's image on the occasion of Ram Navami. The photo was shared in a social media post on Mar 31, a day after Ram Navami, indicating that the picture was clicked recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo shared in the social media post was digitally altered, and an image of Lord Ram was placed on the picture of Burj Khalifa to share with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on Mar 31 a photo of Lord Ram being projected on the Burj Khalifa, indicating that it happened on the occasion of Ram Navami. "Jai Shree Ram." read the post, which has garnered over 480K views, more than 11,000 likes and 1,200 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo. It came across a Twitter post carrying the same picture with the claim that it happened on the occasion of Ram Navami. Here is the link and archive link to the Mar 31 post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found an iStock post carrying a similar image, uploaded on Feb 3, 2016. "Dubai, UAE - December 28, 2015: Night view of Burj Khalifa tower. Burj Khalifa is the tallest structure in the world (828 m)," read the photo's caption. Here is the link to the iStock page , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk compared the two photos and found them to be the same, except that Lord Ram's image was digitally included in the one shared in social media posts. Below is a combination image comparing the two photos: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords but could not find any relevant news reports. We also emailed Burj Khalifa's communications department, seeking a response on the viral image. The story will be updated as and when it is received. Subsequently, it was concluded that the photo shared on social media was digitally altered to add Lord Ram's image on the Burj Khalifa.

title: PTI Fact Check: Yes, Congress leader Pramod Tiwari said that 'law should be different for Gandhis' in a TV interview; Video shared on social media is true
content: New Delhi, Apr 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of Congress leader Pramod Tiwari saying 'there should be a separate law for the Gandhi family'. He said this while talking to a TV channel after the Surat court sentenced Rahul Gandhi to two years in jail in the 2019 criminal defamation case. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Pramod Tiwari's video was genuine. Claim A Twitter user shared a 47-second Hindi news channel report, which quoted senior Congress leader Pramod Tiwari saying that the law should differ for Gandhis regarding sentencing. "The law should be different for the Gandhis. Blunder after blunder by Congress leaders" read the Mar 25 post, which has garnered over 27K views, along with more than 1500 likes and 700 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the tweet: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a Twitter post by Amit Malviya, the head of BJP's IT cell, who shared an extended version of the same video. "कांग्रेस के नेता प्रमोद तिवारी का कहना है कि राहुल गांधी के परिवार के लिए कानून अलग होना चाहिए," Malviya wrote in his Mar 25 post. "Congress leader Pramod Tiwari says that the law should be different for Rahul Gandhi's family," read an English translation of the tweet, which has garnered over 110K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Pramod Tiwari on Rahul Gandhi sentencing". The search results led the Desk to a YouTube video uploaded by Aaj Tak on Mar 25. The title of the 1:40-minute video read: "Breaking News: Rahul Gandhi को लेकर Pramod Tiwari का बड़ा बयान, कहा- सजा होनी चाहिए कम| Congress" The title was roughly translated to English as: "Breaking News: Pramod Tiwari's big statement on Rahul Gandhi, says punishment should be less | Congress". Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk oversaw the video and found that Tiwari made the remarks at 00:20 minutes. "Law should be different for Rahul Gandhi's family, in terms of sentencing, not in conviction. When someone is convicted, the family or background is not considered; only the crime is considered. But when you decide on sentencing, the person's demeanour, stature, family background…," Tiwari is heard saying in the video. "For example, if someone is a teacher accused in (IPC Section) 302, you will give him a death sentence because he is not a habitual offender. So, in sentencing, the background of Rahul Gandhi and his family was to be analysed; it was not for maximum (sentencing) but minimum. Even after minimum (sentencing), you tell me, as far you memorise, have you ever heard of a case (of criminal defamation) with a sentencing of two years? This was not the case; this case was not at all for maximum sentencing. Because it is of Rahul Gandhi, one from the Gandhi family, there should not have been maximum sentencing; I can say this is thumping my chest. A person should understand that conviction is one thing; the sentence is different," the Congress MP added. The Desk also came across a news report by Hindustan Times, which quoted Tiwari making the same remarks as shared in the video in social media posts. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Pramod Tiwari for his comment on the social media post. Quoting the 1973 amendment in the Criminal Procedure Code, which introduced a change in the quantum of sentence that could be imposed on an offender, Tiwari said: "IPC and CrPC are two different things, conviction and sentencing is two different things. When a sentence is debated, then one talks about minimum. Who should be given the minimum, and who should be given the maximum? I said Rahul Gandhi is a normal person, a common citizen of India, and has been a member of Parliament." "He has never been convicted, has no criminal history, he is not a serial offender. So, he would have been given a minimum (sentence). If someone is a serial offender and has a criminal history, he will be given a maximum sentence. Rahul Gandhi was not a case of maximum, but minimum," added Tiwari while talking to PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video and claims shared in social media posts were genuine. Tiwari suggested considering Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and his family's background while sentencing a case. A Gujarat court found Rahul Gandhi guilty under Indian Penal Court (IPC) Section 500, which deals with punishment for defamation. The section states that whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with a fine, or with both. The maximum possible punishment under this section is two years.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, IMF World Economic Outlook report did not say 'India will become poorer than Bangladesh by 2025'; Claim shared on Twitter was false
content: New Delhi, Apr 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Cricketer-turned-politician Kirti Azad shared a photo tweet, claiming International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its latest World Economic Outlook report, has said that "India will become poorer than Bangladesh by 2025". The photo shared in the tweet showed the pictures of IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with the claim highlighted in bold-letter texts. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the IMF did not make such a statement in its recent World Economic Outlook reports. The claim shared in the social media post was false. Claim Trinamool Congress leader Kirti Azad on April 2 shared a photo tweet with pictures of IMF MD Kristalina Georgieva and India's PM Narendra Modi. The text in the photo attributed to IMF the claim that "India will become poorer than Bangladesh by 2025". "Another shocking report by IMF! The latest world economic outlook published by the International Monetary Fund reveals that India will become poorer than Bangladesh by 2025. This is very unprecedented. Modi has put India's future at stake. India is no more a "developing nation" now," read the text in the photo shared in the Twitter post. "भारत कंगाली के दौर से गुजरेगा? (Will India go through a phase of pauperism?)," read the post, which has garnered over 700K views, more than 5500 likes and 1800 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "India to become poorer than Bangladesh, IMF" but could not find any report validating the claim made in the photo shared in the social media post. Another customised Google search with the keyword "IMF on the Indian economy". The search results led to a Feb 22 report by Live Mint titled: "World Economic Outlook". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted Georgieva's interview with PTI in which she said that "the Indian economy will alone contribute 15 per cent of the global growth this year, as the country continues to remain a relative "bright spot" in the world economy." "The IMF MD said that India's performance has been quite impressive. For this year, the IMF expects India to retain a high growth rate, 6.8 per cent, for the year that ends in March," the report added. The relevant part of Georgieva's interview with PTI can be viewed here . Since the social media post by Azad quoted the IMF's "latest World Economic Outlook" report, the Desk scanned the IMF's official website and found the information that the IMF will release its latest (April) 'World Economic Outlook Update' on April 5. Here is the link to the page on the IMF website . Below is the screenshot of the page- Continuing the investigation, the Desk scanned the IMF website for the last report, released in January this year – as highlighted in the screenshot above. The Desk scanned the detailed information of the 'World Economic Outlook Update' released in January 2023 here and here on the IMF website but couldn't find any mention of the Indian economy compared with Bangladesh, as claimed in the tweet. Below are the screenshots of both pages- In the next part of the investigation, we searched for IMF's GDP growth projection for Bangladesh and found that the IMF has projected the neighbouring country's GDP growth at 6% for 2023. Here is the link to the IMF report , and below is a screenshot of the same: However, in the later part of the investigation, we found the IMF World Economic Outlook report released in October 2022, showing Bangladesh's real per capita GDP surpassed India's real per capita GDP. In nominal US dollar terms, India's per capita GDP was projected to be $1,876.53 in 2020, lower than the $1,887.97 projected for Bangladesh. However, the IMF didn't mention anything about 'India becoming poorer than Bangladesh by 2025', as claimed in the tweet. Here is the link to the report , and below is the screenshot of the page- Subsequently, the Desk concluded that IMF didn't compare Indian Economy with Bangladesh as claimed in the tweet. The Desk contacted IMF for its comment on the claim, and we will update the copy when we get a reply.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photo of Arvind Kejriwal with Nitin Gadkari peddled on social media as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 5 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A verified Twitter user shared a photo of Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, claiming that the former met the senior BJP leader to tender a written apology to him. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an unrelated photo dating back to 2014 was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A verified Twitter user shared a photo of Arvind Kejriwal and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, claiming that the Delhi CM met the senior BJP leader to tender a written apology to him. The Mar 26 tweet read: "इस फोटो में केजरीवाल जी के साथ "नितीन गडकरी " जी है ! अब आप ये ना सोचियेगा कि, केजरीवाल जी दिल्ली के लिए कोई " सड़क परियोजना " पर चर्चा करने गए है ! केजरीवाल जी नितीन गडकरी को लिखित में " माफी " मांगने गए है, गडकरी जी " माफ़ीनामा " पढ़ते हुए !" "In this photo, there is "Nitin Gadkari" ji with Kejriwal ji! Now don't think that Kejriwal has gone to Delhi to discuss some "road project"! Kejriwal ji has gone to Nitin Gadkari to apologise in writing, Gadkari ji reading out the "apology"!" read an English translation of the post with over 1700 views. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in social media posts. The search results led to another Twitter post carrying the same picture and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Desk noticed that the photo carried the watermark of Getty Images. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and the same picture on the stock image website. Here is the link to the Getty Images page , and below is a screenshot of the same: It mentioned that the photo was uploaded on Sep 16, 2014, and attributed the image to Hindustan Times. The photo's caption read: "AAP Leader Arvind Kejriwal Met Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari On Regularizing E-Rickshaws". "NEW DELHI, INDIA - SEPTEMBER 16: Aam Aadmi Party convener Arvind Kejriwal with Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari during a meeting on regularising e-rickshaws at Transport Bhawan on September 16, 2014, in New Delhi, India. The Delhi High Court last week said the ban on plying "illegal" e-rickshaws in Delhi would continue till the law is amended to bring them under the ambit of the Motor Vehicles Act, adding that "what is prohibited by law is not permitted in action (Photo by Arvind Yadav/Hindustan Times via Getty Images)." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Kejriwal meets Nitin Gadkari, e-rickshaws" and came across a video report by Aaj Tak, posted on YouTube on Sep 16, 2014. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: During our searches on Google, we also came across reports about Kejriwal apologising to Gadkari in 2018. This was about a defamation suit filed by Gadkari against the Aam Aadmi Party convenor, who had called him "one of the country's most corrupt politicians". Here is the link to an NDTV report titled "With Kapil Sibal And Nitin Gadkari, Arvind Kejriwal Hits 3 Of 33 "Sorry"." Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old photo of Kejriwal meeting Gadkari was recently shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's daughter appeared in UPSC exams; False claim on her 'IAS backdoor entry' shared on social media
content: New Delhi, Apr 5 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla with his daughter Anjali Birla, claiming the latter cleared the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) examination in the first attempt without even taking up any exam or interview. The user claimed that Anjali became an IAS officer through a "backdoor entry" facilitated by the UPSC. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Anjali appeared for the Civil Services Examination (CSE) examinations in 2019. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on Mar 30 a photo of Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla with his daughter Anjali Birla, which claimed that Anjali cleared the UPSC examination in the first attempt to become an IAS officer without giving any exam. The post claimed that Anjali became an IAS officer through "backdoor entry" using her father's position. The post, which has garnered over 110 reactions so far, read, "लोकसभा स्पीकर ओम बिरला की बेटी अंजली बिरला पहले ही प्रयास में बनीं IAS (वो भी बिना परीक्षा दिए). 90 seat जो बैकडोर इंट्री के लिये रखा गया था रुझान आने लगा है, देश के सबसे विश्वसनीय UPSC EXAM में बैक डोर इंटर्टी ने देश के कठिन परिश्रम करने वाले प्रतियोगी छात्रों, गरीबों एवं ग्रामीण लोगों के बच्चों के लिए यूपीएससी का प्रवेश द्वार बंद करने की तैयारी की शुरुआत हो चुकी है अब आप सिर्फ अपने बच्चों को नौकर बनाने के लिए तैयार रहिए, अधिकारी नहीं..." "Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's daughter Anjali Birla became IAS in the first attempt (that too without giving any exam). Ninety seats were kept for backdoor entry; the trend has started coming in the country's most reliable UPSC EXAM, back door entry has started to close the entrance of UPSC for hard-working competitive students, children of poor and rural people of the country. Preparation has started; now you just be ready to make your children servants, not officers, (sic)," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Anjali Birla UPSC exam result". The search results led to an article published by Mint on Jan 5, 2021, with the headline "Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla's daughter Anjali cracks UPSC in the first attempt." Here is the link to the article , and below is its screenshot: "Anjali, who studied political science (honours) from Ramjas College in New Delhi, was among the 89 candidates recommended by the UPSC this year. She cleared the competitive exam in her first attempt," read the article. The article added that the commission had recommended 89 candidates, including Anjali, for different civil services from its reserve list drawn based on the 2019 civil services examination. We then scanned the official website of the Union Public Service Commission. We found Anjali Birla's name among the 89 reserve list candidates who had been recommended to fill up the remaining vacancies based on the Civil Services Examination 2019. Here is the link to the list , and below is a screenshot of the same: The introduction of the list states that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) asked for more vacancies to be filled. "As sought by the Department of Personnel & Training, the Commission has recommended 89 candidates, including 73 General, 14 OBC, 01 EWS and 01 SC, to fill up the remaining posts based on the Civil Services Examination, 2019. Particulars of these candidates are included herewith. The recommended candidates will be intimated directly by the DOP&T," read the press note, whose screenshot has been shared below. Continuing its search on the UPSC website, the Desk came across the preliminary exam result list of CSE 2019 and found Anjali Birla's roll number (0851876). Here is the link to the result list , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched for the UPSC's Reserve List. The UPSC conducts the Civil Services Examination annually in three stages – Preliminary, Mains and Interview. After the interview, the commission decides on a general qualifying standard and releases the first list of candidates who have successfully cleared the cut-off marks without any relaxation. Apart from these, by Rule 16 (4) & (5) of the Civil Services Examination Rules, the Commission maintains a Consolidated Reserve List in order of merit below the last recommended candidate under the respective categories. The commission releases the reserve candidates list about six months after the main result of the respective CSE. Regarding the CSE 2019, the commission released a statement clarifying what a 'Reserve List' is in the Civil Services Examination and how it is applied, following misleading information on social media. "The Reserve list is necessitated in a multi-service examination to allow candidates of reserved categories to choose a service of higher preference who qualify at or above general qualifying standard without availing any concession/relaxation at any stage of the examination," read. Here is the link to the press release , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also contacted Anjali Birla for her comments on the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Similar claims regarding Anjali's UPSC selection surfaced on social media in 2021 after her selection. Back then, she refuted the rumours in an interview with NDTV. "I was taken aback that I had to explain after giving an exam that I did study for it. But I feel it made me stronger because I would face such unfounded criticism later in life. It made me mature," she said in the interview. Here is the link to the NDTV interview , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Anjali Birla did appear for both the Preliminary and Mains exams and cleared them to appear on the merit list.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, the women in photos are not Bangladeshi 'freedom fighters'; Social media posts shared with false claims
content: New Delhi, Apr 6 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a set of two photos – one monochrome and the other coloured – of four women carrying rifles on a jeep and claimed that they were "freedom fighters" from the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War who recreated the image after over 50 years. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the black-and-white photo was clicked in 1961, a decade before the Bangladesh Liberation War. Also, the women in the set of images were not freedom fighters. The collection of photos was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared a combination of two photos, both showing four women carrying rifles on a jeep. The user claimed that the women were Bangladeshi freedom fighters from 1971 (the period of the Bangladesh Liberation War) who recreated the same photo after over 50 years. "Four Bangladeshi freedom fighters recreate their 1971 photograph in the same Willy's Jeep," read the March 25 post with more than 2600 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo. The search results led to a Mar 28 Facebook post, which carried the same picture with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: One of the users commented on the post claiming that the women were forcefully converted to Islam. Below is a screenshot of the comment. The Desk also came across a similar Twitter post with the same photo and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post with over 300K views. We also found that the same photo had been shared on social media in March 2021, claiming that the women in the picture had been converted to Islam by the time they recreated the moment. Here is the link and archive link to one such Twitter post. The Desk then customised the Google Reverse Image Search with relevant keywords, which led us to a Pinterest post, which carried the black-and-white photo with the caption: "Women are posing with a gun in a village trip. Bangladesh (1965) Photo courtesy- Renan Ahmed." Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found the same black-and-white photo shared by a Facebook page named 'Bangladesh Old Photo Archive' on July 19, 2013. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that both Pinterest and the 'Bangladesh Old Photo Archive' attributed the photo to Renan Ahmed. Since the same person was tagged in the Facebook post, we scanned his profile and found the same black-and-white shared with the caption "1961". Here is the link to the August 2020 post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Further scanning the profile, we found that Renan had shared more photos of his grandmother Rokeya Ahmed. On Aug 26, 2020, Renan shared an obituary post for his grandmother, a day after she passed away. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the woman in the photos was the same as the one sitting next to the woman in the driver's seat in the coloured photo shared in viral social media posts. Below is a combination image comparing the two photos: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Tasmia Nehreen Ahmed, the granddaughter of Rokeya Ahmed, who outrightly rejected the claim that the women in the photos were "freedom fighters". Stating that the original monochrome photo was clicked in 1961, she left the share of them converting to Islam. "This family photo of the Ahmed family has caused quite a stir for two reasons, one of which was wrongly shared by an outsider to our family, who claimed the photograph was taken during Bangladesh's Liberation War. My grandfather, Mr Alauddin Ahmed, captured this image on one of his and our grandfathers' hunting trips — it was pure fun! The first snap was in 1961, and the next photo 50 years later saw us all recreating the same pose," Tasmia told PTI. "Sadly, two grandmothers in the pictures have since passed away. Recently, during my cousin's brother's wedding celebrations, we thought it would be a nice tribute to recreate this image again; however, it seems somebody outside of our family got wind of it and spread an inaccurate story that it was taken during wartime — this is not true! I'd also like to add that our family has always been Muslim — there's never been any change in religion. My grandfather captured this unique shot as a keepsake," she added. The Desk also reached out to Renan Ahmed for a response. The story will be updated as and when it is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the women in the viral photos were not "freedom fighters" from the Bangladesh Liberation Movement of 1971. Also, none of the women – all Muslims – ever converted their religion.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of former Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 6 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A verified Twitter user shared a collage of two photos – one of former Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor K S Shastri along with dates 22-08-1980 to 13-07-1981 written on the image and the other of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Masters' degree, signed by the former VC in 1983. The user claimed when Shastri passed away in 1981 and how his signature was on the degree issued two years later. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that Shastri was alive, and the dates mentioned along with his photo showed his tenure at another university, not his dates of birth and death years. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A verified Twitter user shared a collage of two photos – one of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Master's degree and the other of former Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor K S Shastri, along with the dates 22-08-1980 to 13-07-1981 in brackets. The user questioned how the degree was signed by Shastri in 1983 when he passed away in 1981. "प्रधानमंत्री की डिग्री पर हस्ताक्षर करनेवाले वाईस चांसलर K S शास्त्री का निधन 1981 में हो चुका था...तो उसके बाद डिग्री कैसे प्रिंट हुआ ?" the user wrote in the post, tagging PM Modi and Delhi Chief Minister Arvjind Kejriwal. An English translation of the post read: "Vice Chancellor KS Shastri, who signed the Prime Minister's degree, had passed away in 1981...so how was the degree printed after that?" The tweet, shared on April 5, has garnered over 1 million views, more than 8,000 likes and 3,000 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the tweet: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned the comment section of the Twitter post and found several users claiming that the dates mentioned with Shastri's photo were not of his birth and death but of his period of tenure at another varsity. Two such comments can be viewed here and here , and their screenshots can be seen below: Taking a cue from the comments, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Professor KS Shatri, Gujarat University". The search results led to a PDF file uploaded on the official website of Gujarat University. The PDF showed the tenure of all the 17 Vice-Chancellors who have served at Gujarat University. Here is the link to the PDF file , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo of Shastri shared in the viral Twitter post. The search results led to the Veer Narmad South Gujarat University website, where the exact picture was displayed, along with his tenure as the varsity Vice-Chancellor. Here is the link to the university page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Further, researching Shastri, the Desk found Professor Shastri listed on the advisory committees of the Som-Lalit Education and Research Foundation and the Som-Lalit Institute of Business Management . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Gujarat University and Som-Lalit Education and Research Foundation, seeking their responses on the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when they are received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim on Professor Shastri's death was false. The dates mentioned along with his photo in the viral post showed his tenure at a university, not his birth and death dates.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, these film stars, cricketers didn't visit Bageshwar Dham, edited photos, videos shared on social media with false claims
content: New Delhi, Apr 9 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyuash Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): At least four different videos posted on YouTube claimed that Bollywood celebrities Shah Rukh Khan, Akshay Kumar, Manushi Chhillar Shilpa Shetty, along with star couple Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma met Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, the head priest at Bageshwar Dham in Madhya Pradesh's Chhatarpur district. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claims false as none of these celebs visited Bageshwar Dham or met Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. Shastri, popularly known as Bageshwar Dham Sarkar/Maharaj, has been grabbing the limelight lately for his claims of resolving people's problems, including health and financial issues, with his Divya Shakti (magical powers). Below is a case-to-case fact check on the claims: Claim 1: Akshay Kumar A YouTube channel named 'Bhakti News Facts', with over 18,000 subscribers, posted a video titled "Bageshwar dham पहुंचे Aksay Kumar (Aksay Kumar reaches Bageshwar dham)" Feb 26. The visuals in the video purportedly showed actor Akshay Kumar, along with actress Manushi Chhillar, meeting Shastri at Bageshwar Dham to seek his blessings. "Bageshwar dham पहुंचे Aksay Kumar | Bageshwar dham sarkar को दिए 1 करोड़ रुपए (Aksay Kumar reached Bageshwar dham | 1 crore rupees given to Bageshwar dham sarkar)," read the description of the video, which has over 17,000 views and 500 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 1 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to another YouTube video posted by India TV on June 3, 2022. The title of the video read: "Akshay Kumar, Manushi Chhillar ने सोमनाथ मंदिर में की ज्योतिर्लिंग की पूजा (Akshay Kumar, Manushi Chillar worship Jyotirlinga at Somnath temple)." "फिल्म की रिलीज से पहले फिल्म के एक्टर अक्षय कुमार, एक्ट्रेस मानुषी छिल्लर और फिल्म के निर्देशक चंद्रप्रकाश द्विवेदी ने सोमनाथ मंदिर में भगवान भोलेनाथ के दर्शन किए। पूरी टीम ने सोमनाथ मंदिर में पूजा अर्चना की। इस दौरान फिल्म की टीम ने मंदिर में सम्राट पृथ्वीराज का झंडा रखा और हिंदू पूजाओं के लिए सभी जरूरी चीजें भगवान को अर्पित की," read the description of the video. "Before the film's release, actor Akshay Kumar, actress Manushi Chhillar and film's director Chandraprakash Dwivedi visited Lord Bholenath in Somnath temple. The entire team offered prayers at the Somnath temple. During this, the film team placed the flag of Emperor Prithviraj in the temple and offered all the necessary items for Hindu worship to the deity," read the English translation of the description. Here is the link to the video , which has over 17,000 views, and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that visuals from the video posted by IndiaTV were similar to the viral video. Below is a combined image comparing the visuals from the original and viral videos: Taking a cue from the information in the India TV video, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Akshay Kumar Manushi Chhillar Somnath Temple" and found several articles reporting the actor's visit to the Somnath Temple. One of them can be read here : The actor duo visited the Somnath Temple in Gujarat ahead of the release of their film Samrat Prithviraj, which was released on June 3, 2022. The Desk subsequently concluded that the video falsely claimed that Akshay Kumar was visiting Bageshwar Dham and meeting Dhirendra Krishna Shastri.
