Claim 2: Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma A YouTube channel, Trending News, with over 72K subscribers, posted a video on Jan 9, which purportedly showed cricketer Virat Kohli and his wife and actor Anushka Sharma, visiting Bageshwar Dham. "बागेश्वर धाम पहुंचे विराट कोहली, अनुष्का शर्मा (Virat Kohli, Anushka Sharma reach Bageshwar Dham)" read the title of the video, which has over 4,700 views and 60 likes so far. Here is the link and archive link to the video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 2 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to an article published by India Today on Jan 6, 2023, with the headline "Anushka Sharma and Virat Kohli seek blessings with daughter Vamika in unseen video from Vrindavan visit. Watch". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: We noticed that the photo carried in the article was visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combined image comparing the visuals from the viral video and the news article: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Virat Kohli Anushka Sharma Vrindavan visit" and found several news articles carrying the same visuals. One of them read here . The Desk, therefore, concluded that the claim made in the video was false. Claim 3: Shah Rukh Khan A YouTube channel named 'Dharam News' posted on Dec 11 last year a video titled "शाहरुख खान का गुरुदेव ने पर्चा बनाया बागेश्वर धाम लाइव न्यूज़ वीडियो". The video's visuals purportedly showed Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan visiting Bageshwar Dham and meeting Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. The video also showed Khan holding a 'parcha' (a prescription given by Shastri to his followers highlighting their issues and resolving them), claiming Shastri gave it. Here is the link and archive link to the video, which has so far garnered over 33,000 views, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 3 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to an article published by India Today on Feb 27, 2016, with the headline "28 years after graduation, Shah Rukh Khan receives his college degree". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the photo in the article was similar to the visuals in the viral video. Below is a combined image comparing the visuals from the viral video and India Today's theme: According to the India Today report, the photo was taken during a promotional event when the actor collected his degree from Hansraj College in Delhi after 28 years. We then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Shahrukh Khan college degree", finding several articles with similar visuals. Two such reports by the Times of India and NDTV can be read here and here . The Desk concluded that digitally altered visuals were used in the YouTube video to make it look like Khan received a paper from Shastri, which was his own college degree. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Shah Rukh Khan visits Bageshwar Dham" but could not find any report authenticating the claim made in the viral video. Claim 4: Shilpa Shetty A YouTube channel named 'Bhakti News Facts' posted a video on Mar 8 with visuals purportedly showing that Bollywood actor Shilpa Shetty, along with her husband Raj Kundra and other family members, visited Bageshwar Dham and met Shastri. It also claimed that Shilpa Shetty argued with Shastri during her visit. The title of the video read: "बागेश्वर धाम सरकार और बॉलीवुड अभिनेत्री शिल्पा शेट्टी के साथ बहस हो गई (Bageshwar Dham head and actress Shilpa Shetty got in to an argument). Here is the link and archive link to the video, which has garnered over 3.5 lakh views, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation 4 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a video posted on Facebook on Aug 30, 2021, titled "Happy Janmashtami Shilpa Shetty at Iskcon Temple in Juhu (it is very close to their bungalow) Throwback to Krishna Janmashtami celebrations with Raj Kundra, their son Viaan, Shamita and mumsy Sunanda Shetty". Here is a link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the visuals in the Facebook video were strikingly similar to those in the viral video. Below is a combined image comparing the visuals from the viral video and the Facebook video: The description of the Facebook video mentioned that it was shot pre-Corona (before 2020), but the same year was not mentioned. The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Shilpa Shetty visits Iskcon Temple" and found a YouTube video posted by Bollywood Insight on Aug 26, 2019, titled "Shilpa Shetty Family Visit Iskcon Temple Janmashtami Celebration 2019". Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the outfits Shilpa and her family wore and the background visuals in the YouTube video were strikingly similar to those shown in the viral one. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the original YouTube video to that of the viral one: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Shilpa Shetty visits Bageshwar Dham" but could not find any report authenticating the claim made in the viral YouTube video. The Desk subsequently concluded that the claim in the viral video was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Simulation gaming video of a truck passing through rough terrain shared as real on social media
content: New Delhi, Apr 9 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a truck carrying a rocket-like structure crossing a waterbody and then passing through a narrow, curvy road claiming it was an actual incident that happened in India. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the video was from a vehicle simulation game called "Spintires: MudRunner". The simulation video was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a 5:12-minute video which showed a truck carrying a rocket-like structure which crosses a waterbody and then passing through a narrow, curvy road. The video showed the vehicle travelling the waterbody with the help of another armoured vehicle-launched bridge. The user claimed the video was about an actual incident in India. "There is no perfect time or moment. Don't wait for the perfect conditions to dream. Great leaders deliver despite everything unfavourable. To give your best without caring for what you have and where you are in the real character. That's undying spirit. Never say never no. I could not admire the driver's dexterity in navigating such a difficult pass enough. Also, admiring India's infra progress in such a short time, capable of dreaming big things…. Don't wait for the right moment or time. Every moment can be the right moment," read the Apr 4 post, viewed by more than 800 people. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a Twitter post by the same Facebook user, carrying the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: The Google Reverse Image Search on another keyframe led to a Facebook post shared on Mar 22. The same video was shared in the post by Jim Natelo, a gaming video creator. The video's caption read: "Emergency bridge technology is beneficial in a situation like this." Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that Natelo tagged the video game Spintires: MudRunner in the video. On a Google search for "Spintires: MudRunner", the Desk found that it is an open-world driving simulation game. In this, gamers are given rugged terrains to drive their vehicles in different situations. We also reviewed the post's comment section, where Natelo stated it was a gaming video. The Desk then scanned their Facebook profile of Natelo and found similar videos of trucks, cars and planes. Here is the link to his Facebook profile , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Natelo via e-mail, seeking his response on the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when we receive the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a simulation driving game video was shared as an actual incident on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of armed guards wearing Swastika armbands not linked with former US President Trump; Claim shared in social media post is false
content: New Delhi, Apr 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A verified Twitter user shared a photo of armed guards wearing Swastika armbands, claiming he clicked the photo outside the New York courthouse where former United States President Donald Trump was held. Trump appeared in a Manhattan court on April 4 and surrendered to face criminal charges from 2016 hush money payments to adult movie star Stormy Daniels. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo was old and taken in 2017 while filming a fictional TV show in Vancouver in Canada. A six-year-old photo was shared on social media recently with a false claim. The Swastika (卐 or 卍) is a symbol widely associated with its appropriation by the Nazi Party and by neo-Nazis. Claim A verified Twitter user on April 5 shared a photo of armed guards wearing Swastika armbands and claimed he clicked the image outside the New York courthouse where former United States President Donald Trump was being held. "Wtf, I just snapped this pic outside the new york courthouse where Donald Trump is being held? Does anyone know what's going on?" read the post, which has garnered over 8.45 lakh views and 590 retweets. The Twitter post has garnered over 870K views and more than 11,000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed a comment on the viral post stating that the photo was misleading. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to an article published by Vancouver-based media house The Georgia Straight on Aug 18, 2017. "Uniformed Nazis in downtown Vancouver for filming The Man in the High Castle," read the article's headline. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: We found the article featured a visually similar image to the viral photo. Below is a combination image of two photos – the one shared on social media and the other carried in the article. According to the article, the image was taken while filming Amazon's speculative fiction TV show, The Man in the High Castle. "Based on the Philip K. Dick novel of the same name, the show—set in 1962—depicts what could have happened had the Axis powers won the Second World War and concentrates on events in the United States which have been carved up by Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan," read the article. We then conducted a customised Google Search with the keyword "The Man in The High Castle guards, " leading us to a YouTube video posted on January 9, 2020, titled "The Man in the High Castle - Season 4 RECAP.". Here is the link to the video , which has garnered over 5.8 lakh views, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that in several scenes, actors from the show wore the same Swastika armband as seen on the arms of guards in the viral photo. Below we have compared the viral photo to visuals from the YouTube video: The Desk subsequently concluded that the viral photo was taken while filming a TV show in Vancouver, Canada.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts on new Parliament building's cost and construction duration shared with false claims
content: New Delhi, Apr 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi from his recent visit to the new Parliament building, claiming the new Parliament House was built in just 17 months and Tata Group built it at the cost of one rupee. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that both the claims made in the social media post were false. The claim was made soon after PM Modi visited the new Parliament building on March 30 and spent over an hour inspecting the site and interacting with workers. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi from his recent visit to the new Parliament building and claimed that the new House was completed in 17 months. The user also claimed that the Tata Group charged just one rupee to the government for constructing the building. Here is the link and archive link to the April 4 tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media. It came across a Facebook post, which carried a different photo of PM Modi from his visit to the new Parliament building with the same claims. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk first took up the claim that the construction of the new Parliament took only 17 months. We conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords to start the investigation. We came across a press release by the Press Information Bureau stating that PM Modi laid the foundation stone of the new building on Dec 10, 2020. Here is the link to the press release , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also came across a report by The Indian Express published on Jan 23, which stated that the construction began in January 2021, and the government had announced a deadline of November 2022. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted officials saying that some portions of the building were still under construction and would take several months for completion. "Construction of the triangular-shaped new Parliament building in a plot adjacent to the existing Parliament House began in January 2021, with the deadline of November 2022 announced by the government," the report stated. Following the report's dates, the government stipulated 23 months to complete the construction. Since the recently concluded Budget Session took place in the old building, the timeline has already been overshot. Conducting another Google search with the keyword "new Parliament building construction timeline", the Desk came across a reply given to Lok Sabha by the government in December 2021. Here is the link to the reply , and below is a screenshot of the same: As stated in the document and given that the construction of the building started in January 2021, the government set a deadline of 22 months, which has already been overstepped. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim that the new Parliament building's construction was completed in 17 months was false. Some portions of the building are still under construction after 27 months after the start of the structure. The Desk then took up the second claim that the Tata Group charged only one rupee for the construction of the building. The reply given in the Lok Sabha, as mentioned above, shows that the estimated project cost was Rs 971 at the beginning. We also found that the government had shared the bid amount and tender details with the Lok Sabha in a reply in September 2020. According to the reply, the project's estimated cost was Rs 971 crore. Tata Projects Ltd. had emerged as the lowest tenderer in the open competitive bid, with a quoted amount of Rs. 861.91 crores. Here is the link to the reply given in the Lok Sabha , and below is a screenshot of the same: Further, we came across an NDTV report published on Jan 20, 2022, about the revised budget for the new Parliament building. It stated that the cost incurred in constructing the new building had increased by another Rs 282 crore. "The new parliament building, the highlight of the government's flagship Central Vista project, will cost another ₹ 282 crores, sources said. The 29 per cent hike over the budgeted cost of ₹ 977 crore comes more than a year after the groundbreaking ceremony, which took place in December 2020. Forty per cent of the work is completed by Tata Projects, which is executing the project," the report stated. Here is the link to the NDTV report , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk went through Tata Projects'42nd and 43rd annual reports for financial years 2020-21 and 2021-22, respectively. While both pieces mentioned the new Parliament building project, it was nowhere stated that the company charged just one rupee. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claims in the viral post regarding the new Parliament building were false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Five-year-old video of passports recovered from field shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Apr 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of some people collecting trashed passports from a field and claimed that it indicated the 'illegal influx of terrorists into the Indian territory through the border state of Gujarat'. The user also shared a hashtag about fugitive pro-Khalistani leader Amritpal Singh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2018, shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on Mar 26 this year a 14-second video of some men picking up trashed passports from a field and claimed that it indicated the massive terrorist influx in India. The post also included a hashtag related to fugitive pro-Khalistani leader Amritpal Singh and claimed that preparations were underway for any incident in the country. "#AmritpalSinghExposed जिस प्रकार गुजरात में बेट द्वारका के पास हजारों अवैध मुसलमान बसे थे उस आधार पर अंदाजा लगाया जा सकता है कि देश में सैकड़ों कसाब बसाए जा चुके हैं - @AchAnkurArya जी (23-03-2023) देश में बडे हमलों के एक साथ अंजाम देने की‌ कुछ तो बडी तैयारी चल रही है। सावधान रहे," read the post, which has garnered over 14,000 views and 1,000 retweets so far. "#AmritpalSinghExposed The way thousands of illegal Muslims were settled near Beyt Dwarka in Gujarat; it can be inferred that hundreds of Kasabs have been settled in the country @AchAnkurArya G (23-03-2023) Some big preparations are going on to carry out big attacks in the country simultaneously. Be careful," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, providing a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to a Facebook post from Mar 11, 2018, where the same footage had been posted with no relevant caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Since the Facebook video was posted in 2018, we conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "passports recovered India 2018", which led to an article published by Hindustan Times on Mar 11, 2018. "258 Punjab-bound passports found dumped in Sirsa village," read the headline. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the article, a photo has been carried which looks similar to visuals from the viral video. Below is a combination image of a screenshot from the viral video shared on social media posts and the other carried in the news article: "Haryana Police have taken into possession 258 passports and some other documents which were found dumped along a road in Chakerian village under Kalanwali police station in Sirsa district in Haryana on Saturday," read the article. We also found an article published by the Times of India on March 12, 2018, where the same photo had been carried. "Over 250 passports for Punjab found dumped in Haryana village," read the headline. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "The passports, scattered along a road in Chakerian village, were discovered on Saturday evening by locals, who then informed cops," read the Times of Indi article. The Desk also came across a video report by Punjab Kesari Haryana, which carried portions of the same video as shared in the viral social media posts. The headline of the video report, uploaded on YouTube on Mar 12, 2018, read: "खेतों से मिले 258 पासपोर्ट, वीजा कंपनी ने किया धोखा ? (258 passports recovered from farms, fraud by visa company?)." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination photo comparing the visuals of the two videos – one shared recently on social media and the other shared by a news channel in 2018. The video report also stated that the passports were found in the Chakerian village of Sirsa district. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a five-year-old photo had been shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Central govt did not lower employees' retirement age; Edited screenshot of 2019 newspaper report shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a screenshot of a Hindi newspaper report speculating that the central government was mulling changes regarding the retirement age of employees, in which one would retire after having served for 33 years, even if he hasn't reached the age of 60. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a four-year-old newspaper report was digitally edited to make it look recent. The claim made in the newspaper clip was false. Claim A Facebook user shared a purported newspaper clip, which claimed that the central government was mulling changes to the criteria for the retirement age of employees. It stated that the government could soon announce a new rule under which an employee would retire if he has completed 33 years of service, even if he has not turned 60. Here is the link and archive link to the April 5 post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the newspaper clip shared in the social media post. The search results led to an article by a website named 'Government Jobs UP', published on Sep 24, 2019. "अब 33 साल की हुई नौकरी तो 60 साल से पहले रिटायर हो जायेंगे केंद्रीय कर्मचारी , केंद्र सरकार करने जा रही सेवानिर्वृत्ति के नियमो में बदलाव , क्लिक करे और पढ़े पूरी पोस्ट," read the headline of the article, which carried the same newspaper clip as shared in the social media post. An English headline translation read: "Now, after 33 years of service, central employees will retire before 60 years; the central government is going to change the retirement rules; click and read the full post." Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: However, the Desk noticed that the newspaper clipping carried in the article did not mention any date, as in the one shared in the social media post. Below is a combination image comparing the two newspaper clippings: Further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the newspaper report carried by the article was genuine, which was taken by the online edition of Amar Ujala in September 2019. The Desk scanned the archived edition of Amar Ujala and found three such articles published online on Sep 17, 18 and 23, 2019. The articles can be viewed here , here and here , and below are their respective screenshots: The Desk found the three articles speculative about the government's decision to lower the retirement age. The news reports quoted sources without naming any government official or minister. Similar reports were carried out by Hindi news portals Patrika and ETV Bharat in September 2019. The reports can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Central Govt to reduce the age of retirement of employees". The search results led to the clarification given by the government in Rajya Sabha on Dec 5, 2019, where it refuted such claims, stating that there is no such proposal to reduce the retirement age below 60 years. We also came across a News18 Hindi report, published on Apr 27, 2020, which quoted BJP leader Dr Jitendra Singh refuting the claims that the government was mulling reducing the retirement age of central government employees. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results further led the Desk to another response by the government in the Rajya Sabha on Mar 17, 2022, in which it clarified that there was no such proposal under consideration of the government to increase the retirement age of central government employees. Here is the link to the government's response in Rajya Sabha , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted another Google search with the keyword "central government employees retirement age" but could not find any report supporting the claim made in the newspaper clipping shared in the social media claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old newspaper clipping, making unsubstantiated speculation on the retirement age of central government employees, was digitally altered to add a recent date to it and shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited screenshot of ABP News Opinion Poll Survey on Karnataka Assembly Elections shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a purported screenshot of an alleged poll survey by the ABP News channel on the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections 'predicting a majority' for the ruling BJP. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral screenshot of the survey was edited and shared on social media with a false claim. Karnataka is scheduled to go to polls next month and is crucial given the Lok Sabha elections, due next year. Claim A Twitter user shared a purported screenshot of a poll survey by the ABP News channel related to the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections. The survey showed a victory for the BJP, predicting 115-127 seats for the ruling party in the 224-seat state assembly. The tweet in Kannada roughly translated to English: "Effective leadership, Hard governance, Loyal workers, With the support of Hindutva, lotus will bloom again in the state.. #BJPYeBharavase." The March 29 Twitter post has garnered 319K views and more than 650 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the screenshot shared in the viral post. The search results revealed two Facebook posts with the same screenshot and claim. The posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed that the screenshot carried the logo of ABP News and mentioned the source as C-Voter. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "ABP survey on Karnataka elections 2023". The search results led to a YouTube video uploaded by ABP News on Mar 29. The title of the video read: "Abp News Karnataka Assembly Election Opinion Poll LIVE : कर्नाटक चुनाव पर सबसे पहला ओपिनियन पोल." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: At the 1:20:19 timestamp, the video showed a visual similar to the one shared in the viral social media posts. Below is a combination image comparing the two visuals: The opinion poll data in the video was precisely opposite to that in the screenshot shared in the viral social media posts. It predicted 115-127 seats for the Congress and 68-80 seats for the ruling BJP. The search results also led to a Twitter post by ABP News, shared on Mar 29. "#DeshKaMoodOnABP | abp न्यूज़ के सर्वे में कांग्रेस को मिला बहुमत, एक्सपर्ट की सुनिए राय (Congress gets a majority in ABP News survey, here is expert advice)," read the post, which carried a portion of the live telecast of the opinion poll survey from the same day. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digital screenshot of the opinion poll survey was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of Salman and Aishwarya posing together at Mumbai event shared on Instagram as real
content: New Delhi, Apr 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Two Instagram users shared separate videos purportedly showing Bollywood actors Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan posing together at the launch party of the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC), held recently in Mumbai. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that both videos were digitally altered and posted on social media with false claims. The Desk conducted a case-by-case investigation on the two videos, and here's what we found: Claim 1 An Instagram user shared on April 5 a video of actors 'Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan posing together', purportedly during the launch party of the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC), which was held recently in Mumbai. Here is the link and archive link to the post, which has garnered over 15.52 lakh likes. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation – Claim 1 Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led us to a YouTube video posted on April 1 by Tv Masala, a verified channel with 448K subscribers. "Celebs At Ambani NMACC Launch - Salman, Aishwarya, Priyanka, Deepika, Kareena, Alia, Kiara, Sid," read the video title, which has over 81,000 views so far. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the video, various celebrities can be seen posing for shutterbugs during the NMACC launch. On watching the YouTube video, we noticed Salman and Aishwarya striking similar poses as seen in the viral video, except that they didn't pose together. Between 3:30 to 4:30 minutes timestamps in the video, Salman is seen posing for the cameras, first with actor Shah Rukh Khan's family and then individually. Below is a combination image of screenshots from the viral video and YouTube video: Similarly, from 6:10 to 7:00 timestamps in the video, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan can be seen getting pictures clicked with her daughter Aaradhya. Below is a combination image of screenshots from the viral video and YouTube video: The search also led us to a YouTube video posted by Mirchi Plus, another verified channel with over 6 million subscribers. "#salmankhan and #aishwaryaraibachchan together? A fan-made video goes #viral | #salmankhanshorts," read the video title, which has over 13,000 views. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Mirchi Plus posted the same viral video with the description, "A fan cropped and edited a video in which it looks like Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan attended the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre Opening ceremony together". In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Salman and Aishwarya pose together at NMACC launch" but could not find any such report or actual video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that separate videos of the two actors had been digitally merged to make it look like they posed together. Claim 2 Another video of actors 'Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai posing together', purportedly during the launch of NMACC, was posted by an Instagram user on April 5. "Bhai and Aishwarya are looking so happy together," read the post description, which has garnered over 26,000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes of the footage. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led us to a YouTube video posted on Apr 2 by Bollywood Now, a verified account with 5.82 million subscribers. "Aishwarya Rai Denies Posing Solo For Paparazzi, Aaradhya Bachchan Sweet Gesture | NMACC Red Carpet," read the video title, which has over 2 700 views far. In the video, Aishwarya Rai can be seen posing for the cameras with her daughter Aaradhya in a way that looks visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image of screenshots from the viral video and YouTube video: The search also led us to another YouTube video posted by Bollywood Now on Apr 2, titled "Happy Salman Khan Poses For And With The Media Photographers On The Red Carpet of #NMACC". Here is the link to the video , which has over 580 views, and below is a screenshot of the same. In the video, Salman Khan can be seen posing for the shutterbugs in the same way as seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image of screenshots from the viral video and YouTube video: The Desk subsequently concluded that separate videos of the two actors posing had been digitally merged and shared as accurate on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Animated video of shark destroying ship in Canada shared on social media as real
content: New Delhi, Apr 12 (Abhinav Gupta/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video purportedly showing a shark attacking and destroying a ship with a claim that the incident occurred in Canada. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found it was an animated video, and social media users shared it as real with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on April 5 a video of a shark attacking a ship and claimed that the attack occurred in Canada. "Fish can be attacked? If yes.. it has happened in Canada..," read the post, which has garnered over 34,800 views and 93 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes of the footage. A Google Reverse Image Search on one led to a Twitter post from April 1 where the same video had been posted with a similar claim. "Fish attack from Canada #जिंदगी #lifeisstrange," read the post, which has over 19,800 views and 126 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search results also led the Desk to a Twitter post from March 10, 2023, where an extended version of the viral video had been shared by a user, "Aleksey__n", with hashtags such as #animation, #CGI and #3D. "I'm finally done!"#megalodon #meg #animation #digitalart #CGI #3D," read the post, which has garnered over 1.56 lakh views and 630 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then went through the video's comment section and found that the user mentioned he had made the video using animation tools '3Ds Max' and 'Unreal Engine'. Below is a screenshot of the comment: We also found that the user had mentioned 3D Artist or 3D Designer in his Twitter bio. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, we went through the other social media handles of Aleksey_n and found that he had shared the same video on Instagram and YouTube. The original Instagram post and YouTube video can be viewed here and here . The Desk subsequently concluded that an animated video had been shared as real on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old videos of Akanksha Dubey peddled as recent on social media with false claims
content: New Delhi, Apr 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Two Facebook users shared separate video clips claiming Bhojpuri actor Akanksha Dubey posted those videos on social media before her death last month. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the videos were at least a year old and were shared on social media after the actor's death with false claims. The 26-year-old actor allegedly committed suicide in a Varanasi hotel room. The Uttar Pradesh Police has registered a case for abetment to suicide against Dubey's rumoured boyfriend Samar Singh and his brother Sanjay Singh. Samar was arrested from Ghaziabad on April 8. The Desk conducted a separate investigation on each video shared on social media. Here's what we found – Claim 1 A Facebook user shared on March 27 a live-streamed video of now-deceased actor Akanksha Dubey and her rumoured boyfriend Samar Singh discussing during a live social media session and claimed that it was Dubey's last video appearance before her death. "समर सिंह और आकांक्षा दुबे जी का लास्ट वीडियो (Last video of Samar Singh and Akanksha Dubey)," read the description of the post, which has over 1,300 likes and 14 comments so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 1 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a YouTube video uploaded on Jan 24, 2022, by a verified user NEE Entertainment with over 10 lakh subscribers. "Samar Singh अपनी हीरोइन Akanksha Singh के साथ आएं Live," read the headline of the video. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that the 9:56-minute YouTube video was the same as part of the 33:14-minute video shared on social media. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: Also, Samar tells Akanksha in the video that he is in Banaras and has recently released his new song "Doodh Ke Factory". On scanning Samar's YouTube channel, it was found that the song's music video had been released on January 22, 2022. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that a one-year-old video was shared as recent, falsely linking it to the death of Akanksha Dubey. Claim 2 Another Facebook user posted on April 2 a video where Akanksha Dubey is seen in a park, apparently during the shooting of a film, and claimed that it was the actor's last video appearance before her death. In the video, the actor advises people not to harm themselves over differences with their better halves. "आकांक्षा दुबे का लास्ट वीडियो सुसाइड करने से जस्ट पहले (Last video of Akanksha Dubey just before committing suicide)," read the description of the video, which has over 44,600 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 2 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a YouTube video uploaded on June 26, 2022, by the channel "JKC MUSIC BHOJPURI", which has over 33,900 subscribers. Here is the link to the video , which has over 69,000 views and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that the video posted on YouTube was an extended version of the viral video shared on social media. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: The Desk subsequently concluded that a one-year-old had been posted on social media as recent, falsely linking it with the death of Akanksha Dubey. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the Instagram profile of the deceased actress and found that she shared several posts and reels before her death on March 26. The last post on her Instagram profile – a dance video – was shared on March 25. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Hence, it was established that the two videos shared on social media were not the last appearances of Akanksha on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post on Bathinda Military Station shooting incident shared with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Apr 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A verified Twitter handle shared a photo of an Army jawan parade, claiming the four Army personnel killed in the recent shooting incident at Bathinda Military Station were 'Hindu soldiers belonging to the 18 Horse Regiment'. The tweet further claimed that the 'attacker was a Sikh soldier'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that all the deceased soldiers belonged to the 80 Artillery Regiment. The '18 Horse Regiment' was part of the Pakistan Army, not the Indian Army. Also, the identity of the assailant/s has not been known so far. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Four soldiers at the Bathinda Military Station were killed in a shooting incident on April 12 this year. The FIR registered in the case has mentioned two unknown persons as assailants, and a massive hunt is underway to capture them. Claim A verified Twitter handle named "Saffron Diaries" shared a photo of the Army Jawan parade and claimed that the four soldiers killed in the April 12 shooting incident at Bathinda Military Station were Hindus who belonged to the "18 Horse Regiment". The user further claimed that the attacker was a Sikh soldier. "Sources within the #IndianArmy have reported that a Sikh soldier allegedly killed four Hindu soldiers belonging to the 18 Horse Regiment at the Bathinda Military Cantonment," read the April 12 Twitter post. The post has garnered over 780K views, more than 180 likes and 130 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media and found a Twitter post by another blue tick user named 'Khalsa'. Here is the link and archive link to the Apr 12 post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Bathinda Military shooting incident details" and came across a PTI report published on Apr 13. "Search on to nab assailants behind killing of four Army soldiers at Bathinda Military station," read the headline of the PTI report. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "The four Army jawans, in their mid-20s, were sleeping when the firing took place around 4:30 am on Wednesday in their barracks near the officers' mess in the artillery unit," the report stated. "According to an FIR, a jawan saw two unidentified men in white kurta-pyjama, their faces and heads covered with cloth, coming out of the barracks after the firing. One of them was carrying an INSAS rifle and the other an axe, the jawan said, according to the police FIR. The suspects, who were of medium height, went towards a forested area near the barracks on seeing the jawan, according to the police FIR," it added. The report further quoted the police saying that a massive manhunt was underway to capture the two assailants. The police also ruled out the possibility of any terror angle. The four soldiers killed in the incident have been identified as Sagar Banne (25), Yogesh Kumar J (24), Santosh M Nagaral (25) and Kamalesh R (24). However, no details have been disclosed so far regarding the identity of the assailants. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk accessed the FIR copy of the shooting incident at the Bathinda Military Station on the official website of Punjab Police. Below are a couple of screenshots of the FIR copy: The FIR was registered on April 12 based on the complaint lodged by Major Ashutosh Shukla, who has been posted as a Major in the 80 Medium Regiment since February 2022. According to Major Shukla's statement, Gunner Desai Mohan informed him about the firing incident inside the mess barrack at 4:30 am on April 12. He was also told that two unidentified men were seen coming out of the barrack. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted the Indian Army's Media Interaction Cell to clarify the viral claim. The story will be updated accordingly. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no official information was released on the identity of the assailant/s of the April 12 shooting incident at Bathinda Military Station. The Desk then cross-checked the following claim in the viral post that the four deceased belonged to the "18 Horse Regiment" of the Indian Army. We scanned the official website of the Indian Army but couldn't find any mention of any regiment named "18 Horse". On one page , we found the names of 1 Horse, 4 Horse and 14 Horse regiments. Similarly, on three other pages, we found the mention of 9 Horse , 17 Horse and Central India Horse regiments. On a Google search with the keyword "18 Horse Regiment", the Desk found a gazette notification issued by the Pakistan government in 2020. The notification listed the officers appointed as Colonels of the regiment/battalion. One of the regiments mentioned was "18 Horse". Here is the link to the gazette notification , and below is a screenshot of the same: Further details on this claim made in the viral post are awaited in the response sought from the Indian Army's Media Interaction Cell. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that there is no "18 Horse Regiment" in the Indian Army, but a regiment with the same name is in the Pakistani Army.

title: PTI Fact Check: Russian President Vladimir Putin has not embraced Buddhism; AI-generated photo peddled as real with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of Vladimir Putin in a monk's attire, claiming the Russian President has embraced Buddhism. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the image shared in the Facebook post was generated using the artificial intelligence (AI) powered tool 'Midjourney'. The edited photo was shared as real on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on March 20 a photo of Vladimir Putin in a monk's attire and claimed that the Russian President had embraced Buddhism. "Putin became a Buddhist monk," read the photo description. The post, originally in Khmer – the official language of Cambodia – roughly translated to English as: "Congratulations, the world is at peace now." Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to a Facebook post from Mar 15, where a collage including two shots each of Putin and US President Joe Biden had been shared, in which they were both seen donning traditional monk's attire. The four photos included Putin's viral image and were shared on a public group, AI Creatives Thailand. The post has garnered over 2,400 likes and 165 comments so far. "When two escape leaders come to ordain. All photos are not real. Created by AI Midjourney," read the English translation of the post, which is originally in Thai. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below are the screenshots of the same: The Desk translated the post and found that the user wrote: "All photos are not real. Created by AI Midjourney." We then scanned the user's profile who shared the photos and found him mentioned as a 'digital creator'. Below is a screenshot of the user's profile: On further scanning the profile, we found that the user had posted several AI-generated images on the page. Below is a screenshot of the page: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk went through the post's comment section carrying Putin and Biden's photos in monk's attire and noticed the user mentioning that he created them using Midjourney Discord V5. Below is a screenshot of one such comment where the user confirmed using the AI-powered tool. Taking a cue from this, the Desk searched for photos of Putin in monk's attire on the Discord channel of the AI-image generation tool of Midjourney and found images similar to the viral photo. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that an AI-generated image of Russian President Vladimir Putin in a monk's attire had been shared as real with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of foreign delegates eating on banana leaves with hands not from India; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Apr 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of officials in uniforms eating food on banana leaves with their hands instead of forks and spoons and claimed that they were foreign delegates visiting India for the ongoing G20 meetings. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was of Pongal celebrations in Waterloo, Canada. The footage from January this year was recently shared with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a video of officials in uniforms eating food using their hands instead of forks and spoons; and on banana leaves instead of plates. The user claimed they were foreign delegates in India for the ongoing G20 meetings. "यह मोदी जी है भाई जिन्होंने इन छुरी कांटे से खाने वालों को भी सीधे हाथ से भोजन करना सिखा दिया है। यह G20 के बैठक के लिए भारत आये विदेशी अतिथि भोजन करते हुए।," read the post, which has garnered over 270 views and 15 retweets so far. "Brother, this is Modi ji who taught those who eat with knives and forks to eat with their hands. These foreign guests came to India for the G20 meeting eating food," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link of the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes of the footage. A Google Reverse Image Search on one led us to another Twitter post where the same video had been posted with a similar claim. "भारतीय संस्कृति एवं स्वदेशी व्यंजनों का आनंद ही निराला है। मोदी जी को बहुत बहुत धन्यवाद 🙏जिन्होंने इन छुरी कांटे से खाने वालों को भी सीधे हाथ से भोजन करना सिखा दिया है। यह G20 के बैठक के लिए भारत आये विदेशी अतिथि भोजन करते हुए।," read the post, which has over 55 views. "The enjoyment of Indian culture and indigenous cuisine is unique. Many thanks to Modi ji, who taught those who eat with these knives and forks to eat with their hands. These foreign guests came to India for the G20 meeting having food," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link of the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led us to another Facebook post from Jan 15, where the same video had been posted. "TCA Tamil Thai Pongal Celebration (Tamil Thanksgiving) region of Waterloo politicians, Regional Chair City Mayors, councillors and Police Chief and staff," read the post's title, which has garnered over 2,900 views and 28 reactions so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The page description on which the photo was posted read, "This FB page promotes Tamil and events in the Region of Waterloo, Ontario, Canada. Also, News feeds around the globe." The Facebook page also shared an event of the celebrations, which was held at the address mentioned as: "1058 Spitzig Rd, Breslau, ON N0B 1M0". The event details were mentioned: "Tamil Cultural Association of Waterloo Region's annual Thai Pongal celebration. Tamil Thai Pongal is known as Tamil Thanksgiving: south Indian classical dance programs, Sri Lankan Tamil music, and Speech. Traditional Tamil pongal food be served on Banana leaf. It will be held at Woodland Christian High School, 1058 Spitzig Road, Breslau, Ontario. E-tickets are now open. Visit our website, www.tamilculturewaterloo.org". Taking a cue from this, we conducted a custom Google Search with the keyword "Pongal celebrations Waterloo 2023", which led us to a collage of four photos posted on Twitter from the verified account of Berry Vrbanovic, the mayor of Kitchener City in Canada. "Some more pictures from last night's #ThaiPongal celebration hosted by @waterlootamils. I was honoured to attend and participate! #ThaiPongalValthukkal," read Vrbanovic's post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We noticed that Vrbanovic is seen eating food from a banana leaf in one of the photos, and it looks similar to one of the officials caught in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the photo posted by Vrbanovic and a screenshot from the viral video: We also found another Twitter post comprising four photos posted on January 15 by Dorothy McCabe, the mayor of Waterloo, Ontario, Canada. "Thank you to the local @waterlootamils community for a wonderful evening of entertainment, enjoyment and delicious food! Celebrating Tamil Heritage Month and Thai Pongal with our vibrant and growing community is an honour. #tamilheritagemonth #ThaiPongal," read the post with over 1,970 views. Here is the link and archive link of the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: We found that in one of the photos posted by her, McCabe had worn the same attire as one of the officials in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the photo posted by McCabe and a screenshot from the viral video: The Desk subsequently concluded that a video from an unrelated event had been posted on social media with a false claim. The same video had gone viral in the past with another false claim in January this year. Here is the link to our fact check on the video.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of funeral procession shared after gangster Atiq's son Asad encounter with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of huge crowd at a funeral procession, claiming it was the video of the last rites of gangster-politician Atiq Ahmad's son Asad, who was killed in a police encounter in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi on April 13. In its investigation, the Desk found that the video showed the funeral procession of Maulana Rabey Hasani Nadwi, president of the All India Muslim Personal Law Board (AIMPLB), held in Lucknow on April 13 this year. The unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Asad, the prime accused in the high-profile Umesh Pal murder case, was killed in an encounter by the Special Task Force of UP Police, along with his aide Ghulam in Jhansi on April 13. He was buried at Kasari Masari village in Prayagraj in the presence of a few distant relatives amid heavy security deployment on April 15. Later on, the same day, Asad's father, Atiq, and his uncle Ashraf were killed in a shooting incident in Prayagraj. Claim On April 15, a Twitter user shared a 30-second video of a funeral procession and claimed that the huge crowd had gathered to attend the burial of gangster-politician Atiq Ahmad's son Asad, who was killed in a police encounter on April 13. "अतीक अहमद के बेटे #मरहूम_असद अहमद की मय्यत मे शामिल लोगो का हुजूम! या अल्लाह परिवार को सब्र दे अमीन," read the tweet. An English translation of the post read: "Crowd attending the funeral of #मरहूम_असद. May Allah give patience to the family, Ameen." The post has garnered 35K views, more than 780 likes and 190 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a YouTube video, uploaded on April 14. The video's caption was in Urdu, which translated to English as: "The scene of the funeral of Hazrat Maulana Syed Muhammad Rabi Hosni Nadwi, may God bless him and grant him peace #nadwa #dunul subscribe." Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the YouTube video was an extended version of the one shared in the viral social media post. Below is a combination photo comparing the visuals of the two videos – one shared on YouTube and the other on social media. The 30-second video shared on social media was taken from the 2:12-minute timestamp of the YouTube video. The Desk noticed another striking similarity in the videos, which has been highlighted in the combination image below: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Maulana Rabey Hasani Nadwi death" and found an April 14 report by The Hindu. The report headline read: "Muslim Personal Law Board president Rabey Hasani Nadwi passes away". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, we conducted a customised Google search on Asad's burial with relevant keywords. We came across a live-streamed video of Asad's last rites, shared by India Today's official YouTube channel on April 15. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video was falsely shared, claiming it showed visuals of a vast crowd participating in Asad's burial.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Putin's office does not have portrait of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar; Morphed photo shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 18 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of Vladimir Putin's office with a portrait of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar displayed on a wall in the room. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a digitally altered photo, which was shared on social media with a false claim. The edited photo was shared three days after India celebrated the 132nd birth anniversary of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar, a social reformer, economist, jurist and the architect of the country's Constitution. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 17 a photo which showed a portrait of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar on the wall of Vladimir Putin while the Russian President addressed a meeting. "Russian President Mr Vladimir Puttin has displayed Dr B.R. Ambedkar's photo in his office....a great honour for India.! (sic)," read the photo. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo. The search results led the Desk to a similar picture on Alamy, a stock image website. Alamy credited the image to the Russian news agency Sputnik, which was documented on February 15, 2007. Here is the link to the Alamy photo page , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Russian President Vladimir Putin holding a conference on economic issues in the Kremlin From left to right Sergei Ignatyev," read the image's caption. The Desk noticed this was the same photo as shared in the viral photo, except that it showed the National Emblem of the Russian Federation, the official government symbol inside the Security Council office, and not Dr Ambedkar's portrait. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two photos: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an article published on November 27, 2001, on the official website of the President of Russia. "Vladimir Putin chaired a Security Council session," read the article's headline. The photo of the meeting in the article also showed the National Emblem of the Russian Federation on the wall and not Dr Ambedkar's portrait. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo and the one carried in the article: The Desk subsequently concluded that a morphed photo had been shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Bigg Boss 16 winner MC Stan is alive; Claim about singer's death shared in YouTube video is fake
content: New Delhi, Apr 19 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A YouTube channel recently uploaded a video that showed stills of MC Stan with a voiceover claiming that the rapper-singer and Bigg Boss 16 winner passed away in a car accident. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that MC Stan is alive and doing well. The video was shared with a false claim. Claim A YouTube video was uploaded on April 10 by a channel named Bolly Dot that showed stills of rapper-singer and Bigg Boss 16 winner MC Stan. The voiceover in the video claimed that Stan passed away in a car accident. "OMG! Big News About Rapper Mc Stan | MC Stan Latest News | MC Stan Passed Away | MC Stan Death News," read the title of the video, which has over 6,350 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "MC Stan death news", but could not find any report backing the claim made in the YouTube video. Had such a mishap taken place, the news would have grabbed the headlines across the country's media. To further cross-check the claim, the Desk conducted another customised Google search with the keyword "MC Stan recent news" and found an article published by Times Now on April 16. "Baba Siddique Iftar Party: Bigg Boss 16 Winner MC Stan Hugs Former Maharashtra MLA At Grand Bash Ahead Of Eid," read the headline of the video report. Here is the link to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same: The report carried a 24-second video which showed Stan in black Pathani suit hugging Siddique, a former legislator. "Bigg Boss 16 winner and rapper MC Stan graced Baba Siddique's Iftar Party tonight at Mumbai's Taj Lands End," read the article, which had been published six days after the viral video was posted. The Google search results also led the Desk to an article published by News 18 on Apr 14 whose headline read, "MC Stan Gets Gifts Worth Rs 1.21 Lakh from Sania Mirza, Says 'Tera Ghar Jaayega Isme...'". Here is the link to the article . Below is a screenshot of the same: The article, which was published four days after the viral video was posted, read, "Recently, Sania Mirza gifted the rapper a special hamper, and MC Stan seems quite ecstatic about it." The Desk subsequently concluded that the claim made in the YouTube video was false as the singer was alive and doing well. We reached out to MC Stan for his comments on the viral video. The story will be updated as and when a response is received.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated clip of Russian President Vladimir Putin speaking in English peddled as real on social media
content: New Delhi, Apr 19 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video that showed a split screen where a man watches Russian President Vladimir Putin speaking in English and hitting out at Americans for accusing him of election interference. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was an AI-generated clip, created by a voting rights organisation for a 2020 ad campaign. Claim An Instagram user shared a video showing a split screen in which a man can be seen watching Russian President Vladimir Putin speaking in English and warning Americans for accusing him of election interference. "America, you blame me for interfering with your democracy, but I don't have to. You're doing it to yourselves. Polling stations are closing. You don't know who to trust. You are divided. There are strings we can pull, but we don't have to. You are pulling them for us," the video appears to show Putin stating. The user posted the video on April 16 with the caption "Truth". The post has garnered over 700 likes to date. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a YouTube video, posted on Sep 29, 2020. This was the same video as shared in the viral social media post. The video was posted by a channel named RepresentUs and the title of the video read: "Dictators - Vladimir Putin". Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: The channel used the hashtag #DeepFake in the description of the video. Also, the video towards the end displayed the text: "This footage isn't real but the threat is". This was also mentioned in the description of the video. Here is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the official website of RepresentUs. In its About section, the organization described itself as "America's leading nonpartisan anti-corruption organization fighting to fix our broken and ineffective government". On further scanning the website, we found another similar clip of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un making similar statements about division in the U.S. The organisation used the hashtag #DeepFake for this video too. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: The website also carried a press release issued on Sep 29, 2020, in which the organisation said it was launching the "first ever use of deepfake technology in a major ad campaign" to illustrate that "democracy will collapse" unless Americans take "immediate action to fix political corruption, voter suppression gerrymandering, and our broken election systems." The two AI-generated video clips were set to air following the first presidential debate between US President Joe Biden and his predecessor Donald Trump. But the videos were "so bold" that the clips were "pulled at the last minute" by Fox News, CNN and MSNBC, RepresentUs said. Instead, the organization posted the Putin deepfake on its YouTube channel that day. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated clip of Putin was shared as real on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Monk in video was not Swami Vivekananda; Social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a man in a monk's attire walking down the road, claiming it was a rare video of Swami Vivekananda. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the monk seen in the video was Paramhansa Yogananda, when he visited New York, most likely in 1923. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 13 a video of a man in a monk's attire walking on the road and claimed that it was a rare video of Swami Vivekananda. "Rare video of Swami Vivekananda," read the video description. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one led to a Facebook post from April 17, where the same video had been posted with a similar claim. "Rare video of Shree Swamy Vivekananda, Pride of India," read the video description, which has two likes and three shares so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led us to a YouTube video posted on March 6 by Ananda Sangha Worldwide, a channel with 1.05 lakh subscribers. "We are very happy to offer you (in collaboration with the University of South Carolina) this original video footage of Swami Yogananda visiting New York in 1923," read the description of the video, which has garnered over 5.74 lakh views and 22,000 likes so far. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The description also carried two links, including one to the website of Ananda. According to the website's about section, "Ananda is a global spiritual movement, based on the teachings of Paramhansa Yogananda, who showed how everyone can realise God in their daily lives as a tangible, loving reality." Here is the link to the website , and below is a screenshot of the same: On scanning the website, we found a video article, "Yogananda Visits New York", uploaded on July 9, 2020. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that stills from 0:32 to 0:42 looked visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots from the viral video and the video on Ananda's website: As both videos mentioned that the footage was offered in collaboration with the University of South Carolina, we conducted a Google search with the keywords "The University of South Carolina Swami Yogananda". The search led us to a video archived on the University of South Carolina's official website, whose headline read "Swami Yogananda of India—outtakes". Here is the link to the archived video . Below is a screenshot of the same: We found that stills from 0:33 to 0:44 in the University of South Carolina's video looked visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots from the viral video and the video on the University of South Carolina's website: The video's description on the University of South Carolina's website read, "The Swami and his party walking along Pershing Square in New York, possibly during a 1923 visit to the city." The Desk subsequently concluded that the video had been shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 1948 photo of lunch hosted by Sardar Patel shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Jawaharlal Nehru having a meal with several notable leaders from his cabinet, claiming this was the first Iftar party of Independent India which was organised by the former prime minister in 1947. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo was taken during a lunch organised by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to celebrate the appointment of Chakravarti Rajagopalachari as India's first governor-general. The image was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on March 31 a photo of Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India, having a meal with several notable leaders from his cabinet and claimed that this was the first Iftar party of independent India organised by Nehru in 1947. "स्वतंत्र भारत मे पहली इफ्तार पार्टी 1947 में जवाहर लाल नेहरू ने दी थी जिसमें उनका मंत्रीमंडल नजर आ रहा है. लेकिन सरदार पटेल ने इसका विरोध किया था कि यह गलत परंपरा शुरू करना देश के लिए खतरनाक है जबकि कुछ ही महीने पहले हमने होली, दिवाली पर किसी पार्टी का आयोजन नही किया था।,' read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "The first Iftar party of independent India was thrown by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1947, in which his cabinet ministers are visible. But Sardar Patel protested by stating that this wrong tradition is dangerous for the country. In contrast, a few months ago, a party had not been organised on Holi, Diwali," read the English translation of the post, which has 70 views and three likes so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, leading to an identical black and white image on Alamy, a stock image website. "मराठी: चक्रवर्ती राजगोपालचारी हे पहिले भारतीय जनरल गव्हर्नर बनण्याचा आनंदात वल्लभभाई पटेलांनी मंत्रीमंडळाला दिलेल्या सहभोजन निमंत्रणाला उपस्थित डॉ. बाबासाहेब आंबेडकर, जवाहरलाल नेहरू, मौलाना आझाद व इतर मंत्री. जून १९४८," read the caption of the photo on Alamy, which is originally in Marathi. "Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, Jawaharlal Nehru, Maulana Azad and other Ministers attending a dinner invitation extended by Vallabhbhai Patel to the Cabinet in celebration of Chakraborty Rajagopalchari becoming India's first Governor General. June 1948," read the English translation of the caption. Here is the link to the image on Alamy . Below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the image shared on Alamy: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google Search with the keyword "Chakraborty Rajagopalchari celebration Nehru", which led us to a collection of photos clicked by Homai Vyarawalla which had been shared in PDF format on a website "Zoroastrians.net". Here is the link to the PDF , and below is a screenshot of the same: "India's first woman press photographer Homai Vyarawalla, who passed away January 15, 2012, at the age of 98, captured the last days of the British Empire in India. Her work also traces the birth and growth of a new nation," read the PDF. On page 9 of the file, an image that looked visually similar to the viral photo but clicked from a different angle was shared. In this photo, all prominent leaders are seated in the same order as in the viral photo. "Nehru's Cabinet was seen at lunch hosted by Sardar Patel after C. Rajagopalachari became Governer-General in 1948. Seated here are: Rafi Ahmad Kidwai, Baldeve Singh, Maulana Azad, Jawaharlal Nehru, C. Rajagopalachari, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Raj Kumari Amrit Kaur, John Matthai, Jagjivan Ram, Mr Gadgil, Mr Neogi, Dr Ambedkar, Shyama Prasad Mookherji, Gopalaswamy Iyengar and Jayaramdas Daulatram," read the caption of the photo. Below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the picture clicked by Vyarawalla: The Desk subsequently concluded that the photo of Jawaharlal Nehru eating with prominent leaders from his cabinet had been shared on social media with a false claim. The Desk also conducted research on political Iftar parties in India and found a report an April 2022 report by The Indian Express, whose headline read: "From Vajpayee to Modi, Mulayam to Yogi: The changing politics of iftar parties". "Political iftars — a multi-partisan affair marked by competitive political outreach — are believed to have been started by India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, who hosted the sunset meal for his close Muslim friends at 7 Jantar Mantar Road, then the AICC headquarters," the report read. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Another report by India Today also reported about Nehru hosting Iftar party each year at the Congress office. The headline of the June 2015 report read: "Sonia Gandhi latest in long line of Indian politicians keeping Iftar tradition alive". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same:

title: PTI Fact Check: PTI Fact Check: No, two men with Akhilesh Yadav in this photo not linked to Atiq-Ashraf killings; False claim shared in social media post
content: New Delhi, Apr 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check Desk ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav swamped in a crowd and highlighted two persons standing behind him, claiming they were the "killers" of slain gangster Atiq Ahmad and his brother Ashraf. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the two persons highlighted in the picture are members of the Madhya Pradesh Congress. The photo was shared in a social media post with a false claim. Gangster brothers Atiq and Ashraf, arrested in connection with the killing of Umesh Pal in February this year, were gunned down in Prayagraj on the night of April 15 by three men posing as journalists while the siblings were being taken to a hospital under police escort. The three assailants were nabbed then and there and later identified as Lavlesh Tiwari (22), Mohit alias Sunny (23) and Arun Kumar Maurya (18). Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav swamped in a crowd of people and claimed that two persons seen with him were the assailants of gangster Atiq Ahmad and his brother. "Breaking news, both the killers have been identified and belong to the Samajwadi party. As per reports, #AtiqueAhmed and his brother know many black things about the Samajwadi party. Akhilesh Yadav, with the help of his party people killed him. Now we know who the real killer is," read the Twitter post on April 16. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the social media post. The search results led to an article published by Indus Scrolls. The headline of the April 16 article read: "Atique Ahmed's Murder: Is Akhilesh Yadav Behind the Crime? Crucial Evidence Out". Here is the link and archive link to the article, and below is a screenshot of the same: The article carried the same photo as shared in the viral social media post. It claimed links between Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and the assailants who killed Atiq and Ashraf. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and came across an April 13 Twitter post by Akhilesh Yadav. The post – a thread of three tweets – carried nine photos, including those shared in the social media post and the article mentioned above. "In Madhya Pradesh, Today," read the post in Hindi. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below are some other photos shared by Yadav from that day in an earlier tweet in the thread: Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Akhilesh Yadav, Madhya Pradesh, April 13". The investigation revealed several news articles about the former UP Chief Minister's visit to Madhya Pradesh. Here is the link to a report by ABP Live , published on April 13 and below is a screenshot of the same: The headline of the report read: "Asad Ahmed Encounter: मध्य प्रदेश के खरगोन पहुंचे अखिलेश यादव, कहा- 'फेक एनकाउंटर का उत्तम प्रदेश बन गया है यूपी' (Asad Ahmad Encounter: Akhilesh Yadav reaches Khargone in Madhya Pradesh, says - 'UP has become the best state of fake encounter')" According to the report, Yadav visited Khargone to pay floral tributes at the statue of the late Subhash Yadav, senior Congress leader and former Deputy CM of Madhya Pradesh. The Desk also found a video report by ABP News related to the same event. The Desk watched the video and noticed the same person highlighted in the social media post walking in the crowd behind Yadav. Here is the link to the video report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the man seen in the viral image and video news report: Since several Congress leaders attended the event, the Desk reached out to the Youth Congress wing of the state and found that the person in the photo was Rajkumar Yadav, a Youth Congress leader. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Rajkumar Yadav. "I am the president of Sehore Youth Congress, and this photo was taken on April 13 in Borawan village of Khargone district. The other person in the photo is Vikram Patel from Dewas," Yadav told PTI. Rajkumar Yadav also shared with us some more photos from the same event. The Desk then compared one of the photos shared by Yadav to the one shared in a social media post: The Desk also reached out Vikram Patel – the second person in the photo – who told us that he served as Dewas Mayor for several years. Patel also shared with us a photo of him. Below is a combination image, comparing the one shared in social media post to the one shared by Patel. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a separate Google search with the keyword "Atiq Ahmad, Ashraf attackers". The search results led to an April 17 report by The Indian Express.
