The report headline read: "Atiq Ahmed Murder Live Updates: Atiq Ahmed's killers transferred to Pratapgarh jail from Prayagraj". The report carried the photos of the three accused, accredited to the news agency PTI. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: None of the three accused matched the two men highlighted in the photo shared in social media post. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the men in the photo with Akhilesh Yadav were falsely labelled as Atiq-Ashraf assailants. A Prayagraj court granted a four-day remand of the three accused to the police this week. No official statement on the developments of interrogation or the involvement of anyone has been released so far.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Switzerland has not banned Covid vaccines; Claim shared in social media post is misleading
content: New Delhi, Apr 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a screenshot of a purported article published by American far-right political activist Pamela Geller with the headline, "Switzerland bans the Covid vaccines". The user hit out at the country's media houses, accusing them of keeping shut on the news. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk that the country did not ban the COVID-19 vaccine. The country is not recommending vaccination for the spring and summer of 2023 because of high vaccination and recovery rates. However, the vaccine is still available for high-risk individuals in the country. These vaccine recommendations made by Switzerland's Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) were taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user on April 11 shared a screenshot of a purported article published by American far-right political activist Pamela Geller. The article's headline read: "Switzerland bans the Covid vaccines". "Where's CBC, CTV & GLobal? Oh right paid to keep there traps shut and complicit with criminal negligence causing (skull, vomiting and illness emojis), (sic)" read the post, which has garnered at least nine reactions so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk noticed the screenshot shared in the viral post showed April 8 as the article's publishing date. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and found the original article. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the article featured a report attributed to Vanessa Renner from German media house Report 24, published on April 7. Below is a screenshot of the report, which was originally in German and translated into English: "Switzerland stops the Covid vaccinations: all vaccination recommendations have been withdrawn, doctors can only administer the controversial vaccines in individual cases under certain conditions – but then bear the risk of liability for vaccination damage," read Renner's report. The article provided a link to the original notice published by Switzerland's Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH) on its official website. According to FOPH's website, it is part of the Federal Department of Home Affairs and is responsible for the health of the population and developing Swiss health policy. Here is the link to the notice and below is a screenshot of the same: As it had been mentioned in Geller's article that "all vaccination recommendations have been withdrawn", we scrolled down to the "Vaccination recommendation for the Covid-19 vaccination in spring/summer 2023" portion of the notice. Below is a screenshot of the same: "Corona Immunitas seroprevalence data (June/July 2022) show that more than 98% of the Swiss population have antibodies against SARS-CoV-2. Due to the immunity situation, the currently predominant virus variants and the expected low virus circulation in spring/summer 2023, it can be assumed that people without risk factors have a shallow risk of becoming seriously ill with Covid-19 in spring/summer 2023. For this reason, no recommendation for vaccination against Covid-19 is formulated," read the notice. The note also stated that the policy would be re-evaluated and adjusted in case of a wave of infection. It also mentioned that doctors could recommend vaccination for high-risk individuals. The Desk went through the entire notice, but a ban on Covid vaccines was not mentioned in any section. The office predicts the virus will likely circulate less during this time, and those who contract the virus will experience mild symptoms. According to the office's website, high-risk individuals can still receive a vaccination if they have a consultation with a doctor. It also mentioned that the vaccination recommendation would be adjusted if a wave of infection emerged during spring or summer. We then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Switzerland Covid vaccine ban" but could not find any news report validating the claim made in the article. In the next part of the article, the Desk reached out to the Federal Office of Public Health of Switzerland, which vehemently denied the claim made in the social media post and the report. "There has been no change to evaluating the risks and dangers of authorised Covid-19 vaccinations in Switzerland. The conclusions drawn by voices online following the updated vaccination recommendation are incorrect. In principle, no COVID-19 vaccination is recommended for spring/summer 2023. Nearly everyone in Switzerland has been vaccinated and contracted and recovered from COVID-19. Therefore, their immune system has been exposed to the coronavirus," the FOPH Switzerland wrote in its email to PTI. "A few exceptions apply to persons at high risk (65+y of age, people with a chronic condition, pregnant women) who may still receive a recommended vaccination shot following an individual consultation with their medical practitioner. The vaccination recommendations have been updated several times based on the analysis of the epidemiological situation in Switzerland and the population's immune status, among other factors. The next update of the vaccine recommendation is scheduled ahead of the autumn/winter period 2023/24 unless unforeseen changes demand an earlier update," it added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the FOPH's recommendation had been misconstrued and shared with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Kamal Nath did not call Atiq-Ashraf killings a 'matter of great sadness'; Edited video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of Congress leader Kamal Nath responding to a media query on the killing of gangster-politician Atiq Ahmad and his brother Ashraf. The post claimed that the former Madhya Pradesh chief minister purportedly termed the killings "a matter of great sadness". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected part of the video of Nath's response to the media query was shared on social media with a false claim. Atiq and his brother Ashraf were shot dead at point-blank range in Prayagraj on April 15 by three men posing as journalists while police personnel were escorting them for a medical check-up. Claim A Twitter user shared on April 16 an 18-second video clip in which Congress leader and former Madhya Pradesh CM Kamal Nath responded to a media query on the killings of gangster Atiq Ahmad and his brother Ashraf, which can purportedly be heard terming it "a matter of great sadness". "अतीक अहमद मर गया बोहुत देख की बात है: कांग्रेस नेता कमल नाथ," read the text on the video. "Atiq Ahmad's death is an unfortunate matter: Congress leader Kamal Nath," read the English translation. "आतंकवादी और गैंगस्टर मरे और कांग्रेस समर्थन ना करे ऐसा हो सकता है?," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Terrorists and Gangsters die and don't get support from the Congress, can it happen?" read the English translation of the post, which has over 400 views and 20 likes so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a video posted on April 16 by the verified Facebook page of the Indian National Congress – Madhya Pradesh. "Live : प्रदेश कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष कमलनाथ जी प्रदेश कांग्रेस कार्यालय में पत्रकारों को संबोधित कर रहे हैं।," read the description of the video which is originally in Hindi. "State Congress President Kamal Nath is addressing the journalists at the state Congress office," read the English translation of the description. Here is the link and archive link to the video, which has over 390 reactions and 3,000 views. Below is a screenshot of the same: We found that stills from the video posted on the Facebook page of MP's Congress unit looked visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots of the viral video and the Facebook video: The video uploaded by Congress on April 16 had the extended version of Kamal Nath's response to the journalist's question on gangster Atiq Ahmad's killing. The entire exchange can be heard between 2:06 and 2:58 timestamps. "It is a matter of great sadness that these murders are being committed openly in Uttar Pradesh. This indicates the law, order, and political situation in UP and the country. Amid the spate of murders, the society must think about the direction this country and Uttar Pradesh are heading towards," Nath is heard saying. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Kamal Nath on Atiq Ahmad assassination", which led us to an article published by Times of India on April 17, carrying a PTI report. "Need SC-monitored probe into Atiq's killing, says Nath," read the article's headline, which was related to the same press conference where Nath made the remarks mentioned above. Here is the link to the article . Below is a screenshot of the same: "Madhya Pradesh Congress chief Kamal Nath on Sunday demanded a Supreme Court-monitored probe into the gunning down of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmad and his brother Ashraf in Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh a day earlier," read the report. The Desk subsequently concluded that Nath did not term the Atiq-Ashrad killings as a matter of "great sadness" but expressed concern over the law-and-order situation in UP. A selected portion of his response to a media query was taken out of context and shared with a false claim on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of scuffle between soldiers and civilians not from India; Video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of army personnel firing in the air to disperse some civilians following a heated argument and claimed they belonged to the Indian Army, indicating the incident happened in India. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the soldiers seen in the video were personnel of the Mexican Army. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 18 a video of army personnel firing in the air to disperse some civilians during a heated argument and claimed that they were officers of the Indian Army. "Indian army power," read the video description, which has garnered over 1.39 lakh reactions and 2,500 shares. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk initially noticed that one of the army officers seen in the viral video had the emblem of a green, white and red flag on his sleeve. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "countries with green, white and red flag", which led us to the Mexican government's official website, where we found an image of the country's flag. Here is the link to the website , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the emblem seen on the sleeve of the soldier in the viral video and the Mexican Flag: We also noticed that the vehicle of the army personnel said, "Ejército Mexicano". Below is a screenshot of the same: We entered the term on Google Translate and found that it translates to Mexican Army. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Mexican Army clash with civilians", leading us to a YouTube video posted on March 20 by "FDS FORCES", a channel with 255 subscribers. "do not mess with Mexican soldiers #shorts #army," read the video title, which has over 180 views. Here is the link to the video . Below is a screenshot of the same: We found that stills from the YouTube video are visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots from the YouTube video and viral video: We also found an article published by Al Jazeera on February 27, whose headline read, "Mexican soldiers kill five in a border town, sparking protests." Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "A shooting by Mexican army soldiers had left five people dead in the border city of Nuevo Laredo, Mexico, igniting a clash between the soldiers and residents who came to the scene to protest," read the article, which confirmed that clashes had taken place between the Mexican Army and locals in Nuevo Laredo, Mexico, around two months before the viral video was posted. The Desk subsequently concluded that the video had been shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Amitabh Bachchan's old photo shared in a recent report with false claim about his bad health
content: New Delhi, Apr 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A recent report on a website claimed that "Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's health deteriorated, and he was in a critical condition". The report also carried a set of two photos of Bachchan purportedly lying on a hospital bed, with his wife, Jaya Bachchan and daughter-in-law Aishwarya Rai Bachchan standing beside him. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Amitabh Bachchan is healthy and fit and was not hospitalised recently. The photo shared in the report was old and shared with a false claim. Claim A website named Dainik Kiran published a report on April 24 claiming that "Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's health deteriorated and he was on his deathbed". The report also carried a set of two photos showing Bachchan lying on a hospital bed and his wife, Jaya Bachchan and daughter-in-law Aishwarya Rai Bachchan standing beside him. "अमिताभ बच्चन की हालत हुई खराब, अस्पताल में ले रहे हैं अब अपनी अंतिम सांसे, जया बच्चन के आंखों से नही रुक रहे आंसू," read the headline of the article. "Amitabh Bachchan's condition worsened, now he is taking his last breath in the hospital, tears are not stopping from Jaya Bachchan's eyes," read the English translation of the headline. Here is the link and archive link to the article. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on both photos in the article. The search results for the first photo led to a BBC article published on Dec 17, 2005. "Bachchan leaves hospital after the op," read the report headline that carried the same photo as shared in the article. Here is the link to the BBC report , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the BBC report, Bachchan was admitted to the Lilavati Hospital and underwent surgery for a colonic condition on Nov 30, 2005. The Desk conducted Google Reverse Image Search on the second photo bur could not find its source. However, we came across a photo of Jaya Bachchan and Aishwarya in a similar attire attending Sri Devi's condolence meeting on Feb 28, 2018. Still, the Desk couldn't establish that the image shared in the report was from Sri Devi's condolence meeting. Below is the combination of the images – the one shared in the report and the other from Sri Devi's funeral in 2018. The Desk then scanned the social media handles of Bachchan and found that the actor had posted on Twitter the same day that the news article had been published (April 24). Here is the link and archive link to the Twitter post by Bachchan on April 24. Below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted a Google Search with the keyword "Amitabh Bachchan news", which led us to an article published by Hindustan Times on April 24. "Amitabh Bachchan has a hilarious response as he gets blue tick back on Twitter: 'Paise bharwa liye aur kehte ho free...'," read the article's headline. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "As Twitter restored the blue tick verification for accounts with over one million followers, veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan had a hilarious response. He wondered why he paid for the subscription, despite having 48.4 million followers," read the article, which does not mention Bachchan facing any health concerns. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keyword "Amitabh Bachchan hospitalised" but couldn't find any recent report. The most recent article regarding Amitabh Bachchan being hospitalised was published at least six months ago. One such report was published by Times Now on October 23, 2022, with the headline "Amitabh Bachchan reveals had cut a vein on his left calf, and was rushed to the hospital recently". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Amitabh Bachchan shared on his official blog that he was recently rushed to hospital after he cut a vein in his left calf. The megastar, who turned 80 a few days back, received stitches to control the bleeding due to a metal cut, Bachchan shared on his official blog," read the article. Taking a cue from this, we went through Amitabh Bachchan's official blog on microblogging and social networking website Tumblr and found that the most recent post was dated April 23/24, 2023. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: However, the post did not mention ill health or hospitalisation. We also contacted Amitabh Bachchan's PR team for his comments on the article. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. The Desk subsequently concluded that the claim made in the article relating to Bachchan's health was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of woman disrupting Eid prayers in Virginia mosque shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Apr 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video in which a woman was being escorted out of a mosque while Eid prayers were underway, purportedly in Virginia, USA, and claimed that she was a Hindu woman who had created a ruckus and allegedly used Islamophobic slurs. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman who disrupted the prayers was not a Hindu and reportedly suffering from mental health issues. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a 43-second video on April 23 where a woman was escorted out of a mosque while Eid prayers were underway, purportedly in Virginia, USA. The user claimed she was a Hindu woman who had created a ruckus and used Islamophobic slurs. "A Hindu woman in Virginia, USA, entered a mosque during Eid prayer, got on the mimbar, created a ruckus, and spewed Islamophobic slurs. She was later arrested. Modi and BJP have been poisoning Indian minds beyond borders. The RSS poison has spread far and wide (sic)," read the post, which has garnered over 1,500 views and five retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a video report published by Pipa News on April 24. "Watch: Woman disrupts Eid prayers in US mosque Pipa News," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Inside the article, a Tweet had been embedded where the same viral video was carried. Below is a screenshot of the same: "Woman gets removed from Masjid at Eid prayer. Where did this happen, and what happened? Anyone?" read the embedded tweet, which has garnered over 4.39 lakh views and 360 retweets. According to Pipa News' article, the video was from an incident at the All Dulles Area Muslim Society (ADAMS) Center in Northern Virginia, USA. "Later, the Adams Center issued a statement saying that the woman had mental health issues," the article further stated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk went through the social media handles of ADAMS and found a statement related to the incident, which had been posted on April 22. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Dear Community, Assalamu Alaykum, and Eid Mubarak, We want to clarify the recent incident at the mosque on Friday, April 21st, during the ADAMS Sterling, Virginia, Eid prayer involved an individual from the Muslim community struggling with mental health issues. ADAMS leadership and social services have met and are working with the family to provide additional resources and help," read the first paragraph of the post shared by ADAMS. The entire post can be read on the link provided above. In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to ADAMS, who clarified that the woman belonged to the Muslim community and was facing mental health issues. "We want to clarify that the recent incident at the mosque on Friday, April 21st, during the ADAMS Sterling, Virginia, Eid prayer involved an individual from the Muslim community struggling with mental health issues," the organisation said in its email response. "DAMS leadership and social services have met and are working with the family to provide additional resources and help. The family sincerely asks for forgiveness for the incident in the morning during Eid prayers. The family has requested that those who posted the video to please remove it from social media to protect the family's privacy since the video is causing additional stress to the family," it added. The Desk subsequently concluded that the video had been shared on social media with a false communal spin.

title: PTI Fact Check: Prank video of travel app Ixigo releasing AI-powered headset shared on social media as real
content: New Delhi, Apr 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video claiming Ixigo (Online travel portal) would launch "Ixigo bhAI", an AI-powered Bluetooth headset to provide real-time voice assistance to travellers. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a prank video released by Ixigo as an April Fool joke. The video was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 9 a video in which it was claimed that travel portal Ixigo would launch "Ixigo bhAI", an AI-powered Bluetooth headset that will provide travellers with real-time voice assistance. According to the video, the headset will be equipped with GPS tracking and real-time language translation features. "Bhai " AI " in your ear. You must listen to what it says about "Samosai Wala " Future will be different. Credit- Hassan Khanani . . #AI #artificialintelligence #chatgpt," Read the title and description of the post, which has over 30 reactions and ten comments so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk initially noticed a comment on the viral post which claimed that the video was part of an April Fool's joke. Below is a screenshot of the comment: The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation by conducting an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes of the footage. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a report published by the Times of India on April 1. #AprilFool: Ixigo announces new AI-powered headset named bhAI," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Ixigo has forayed into the wearables segment with its latest product -). The travel app has launched its new AI-powered headset named bhAI," read the opening lines of the report. However, the report further read, "But before you get carried away -Happy Fool's Day -). This is an April Fool's prank from the travel company shared a day earlier and the one they have been flooding social media accounts days ahead." The same viral video had also been embedded in the TOI article. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk went through the social media handles of Ixigo and found a tweet posted on April 3 from the company's verified account with the hashtag #happyaprilfoolsweek. "Maaf kar dena bhAI. But we're thrilled that you loved Ixigo bhAI & joined in on all the fun. A special discount code is on the way for everyone who signed up!" read the post, which has over 4,000 views and four retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The text in the video also read, "Happy April Fools' Week". The Desk subsequently concluded that the video was part of an April Fool's joke.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video from Telangana bypoll shared on social media with false claim relating it to Karnataka assembly elections
content: New Delhi, Apr 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video in which a woman was seen opening an envelope carrying five currency notes of Rs 2000, with a purported BJP leader's photo and a party symbol printed on it. The Facebook user shared the video to claim that BJP leaders used the highest value currency notes to buy votes and used a hashtag related to the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to October 2021 and was shared when the Huzurabad constituency of Telangana went to bypoll. The old video was shared on social media as recently with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 24 a video in which a woman was seen opening an envelope printed with a BJP leader's photo and party symbol and carrying five notes of Rs 2000. The Facebook user shared the video and tagged a notable Hindi news reporter, claiming that BJP leaders used 2000 Rs notes to buy votes ahead of the Karnataka Assembly elections. The post shared by the Facebook user has garnered 12 reactions and four shares so far. "Anjana Om Kashyap जी 2000की नोट यहां है आप का सेटेलाइट कहा गायब है पता नहीं चल पा रहा वैसे सब को पता है बाजार से 2 हजार की नोट गायब है पर चुनाव में #बीजेपी उम्मीदवारों के पास मिल ही जाती है #karnatakaelection2023," read the caption of the post in Hindi. "Anjana Om Kashyap, currency notes of Rs 200 are here, yet we cannot find your satellite's whereabouts. Everyone knows that 2000 notes have been discontinued in the market, yet they are found with #BJP candidates in elections #karnatakaelection2023," read the translation of the original post shared in Hindi. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an Invid Tool Search, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search of one of the keyframes led us to a Twitter post shared on Oct 28, 2021. The Twitter post carried the same video as the one shared on Facebook. "By election Bumper Offer! Door delivery of cash in packets with a party symbol on it. How much more brazen can this get? #BJP distributing cash for votes in the upcoming #HuzurabadByPoll," read the caption of the post shared on Twitter which dates back to 2021. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords and came across a report by India Today published on Nov 2, 2021. "Huzurabad by-poll: Videos claim TRS, BJP gave cash for votes during campaigning," read the report's Headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report included a Twitter post sharing the same video as the viral post. The tweet was shared by Congress leader Manickman Tagore, who accused the BJP of trying to buy voters. "How Democracy at Sale in #Huzurabad? @JPNadda is sending crores which they earn from Corrupt Sangi Sarkar, and @ECISVEEP watches the money distribution. ECI must show courage; they must countermand the election, will they? #MoneyDistribution," read the tweet shared by the Congress leader. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk researched the candidate fielded by the BJP in the Huzurabad by-polls held in 2021. We found that the leader whose photo was printed on the envelope was Etela Rajender. A customised Google search with specific keywords led the Desk to a poster shared by a Twitter user with a similar image to the one on the envelope. Here is the link to BJP's Huzurabad Etela Rajender poster on Twitter . Below is the screenshot of the same. Below is a combination of comparisons between the photo printed on the envelope and the photo of BJP leader Etela Rajender. It was subsequently concluded that an unrelated video dating back to 2021 was shared as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of NRI youths holding 'no vote for BJP' placards falsely linked to Karnataka assembly elections 2023; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Apr 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video showing several youths holding placards that read "No vote for BJP" and claimed that they warned people against voting for the saffron party in the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from the run-up to the 2021 West Bengal assembly polls. The two-year-old video was peddled as recent on social media with false claims. Claim A Twitter user shared a video of a montage of youths – purportedly Indians from across the world – holding placards which read "No vote for BJP". The user claimed the youths warned people against voting for the BJP in the upcoming Karnataka Assembly polls on May 10 and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The user had also tagged three prominent Congress leaders in the post. "Youths from across the Globe have understood BJP's devise & hateful politics, and they are warning us all ahead of Karnataka and the General Elections due in 2024. Watch it to believe it. Shri @Jairam_Ramesh Shri @Pawankhera Smt @SupriyaShrinate," read the post, which has garnered over 670 views and 55 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned the comment section of the viral post and found a user mentioning that the video was old from the run-up to the West Bengal Assembly polls. Below is a screenshot of the comment: The Desk then conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a Twitter post from April 23 where the same video had been shared with a similar claim by overseas Congress social media coordinator Vijay Thottathil. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: "Across the globe, everyone says "NO VOTE to BJP" #KarnatakaElections2023," read the post, which has garnered over 6.46 lakh views and 2,890 retweets so far. We noticed a comment on the video by Thottathil, which indicated that the video was old and had been posted as recent by relating it to the upcoming assembly polls in Karnataka. Below is a screenshot of the comment: The search also led to a Twitter post from April 24, 2021, where the same video had been posted by "No Vote to BJP", an account with over 2,460 followers. "Bengalis across the world saying "No Vote To BJP". #NoVoteToBJP," read the post, which has over 1.85 lakh views and 360 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: "বিভেদ নয় বাংলায় (There is no division in Bengal) #NoVoteToBJP in #BengalElection2021," read the description of No Vote to BJP's Twitter handle. Below is a screenshot of the same: This indicated that the video was from the run-up to the 2021 West Bengal assembly elections. We also noticed that the placards seen in the viral read: "বিভেদ নয় বাংলায়". An English translation meant – "There is no division in Bengal". Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keywords "no vote to BJP campaign Bengal elections 2021", which led us to a report published by Times of India on April 19, 2021. "Silent campaign for 'No Vote to BJP' now spreads to 20 Bengal districts," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Running parallel to that of political parties, the platform "No Vote to BJP" was set up by a group of political and civil rights activists in January," read the report. "Starting as a sideshow, playing in parallel to the high-decibel Trinamool and BJP pitch, the campaign has spread to 20 districts," it added. The Desk subsequently concluded that a two-year-old video had been falsely connected to the upcoming Karnataka assembly elections.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 photo of water leakage in dead train engine falsely shared in name of Kerala's first Vande Bharat Express flagged off in April this year
content: New Delhi, Apr 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off Kerala's first Vande Bharat Express from Thiruvananthapuram to Kasaragod, several social media users shared a photo of a loco pilot holding an umbrella in a train engine, claiming there was rainwater leakage in the engine of the semi-high-speed train before its debut journey on April 26. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that water leakage from the AC vent in one of its compartments was reported when it was parked at Kannur on April 25, and the railway officials repaired it on April 26. There was no water leakage in the engine of the train. The Desk subsequently found that the photo shared in the social media posts was a screenshot of a video shot in a dead engine in Jharkhand in 2017. The old and unrelated photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated India's 16th and Kerala's first Vande Bharat Express on April 25. There were reports of leakage through the AC vent in one of its compartments during the train's maiden journey, which the Railways' technical department staff fixed soon after. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of a loco pilot (train driver) sitting inside a train engine and holding an umbrella. The user claimed that he was the driver of the Kasargod-Thiruvananthapuram Vande Bharat Express in Kerala, recently inaugurated by PM Modi, who was trying to save himself from rainwater leakage during the train's maiden journey. "MODI's "VANDE BHARAT" is a disaster same, like Modi. On the 1st day of the inauguration, rainwater started leaking from the roof of VB in Kerala. Picture speaks for itself," read the April 26 Twitter post, which garnered over 66K views, along with more than 1700 likes and 800 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the social media post. The search results led to another Twitter post carrying the same image and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet, and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results also led to a video tweeted by journalist Sucheta Dalal on August 9, 2017. The video showed the same loco pilot holding an umbrella over his head. "Railway safety? @sureshpprabhu and @RailMinIndia need to take a serious look without victimising whistleblower," read the Twitter post. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the video, purportedly shot by another railway official, the loco pilot can be seen driving the train while saving himself from water leaking from the roof. The person recording the video also complained about the water leakage and urged viewers to share the video. Taking a cue from the date of the Twitter post shared by Dalal, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a report by The Indian Express, published on August 11, 2017. The report headline read: "Train driver holds an umbrella to save control panel from a leaky roof, video goes viral." Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Along with Sucheta Dalal's Twitter post, the report also included a response by the Railway Ministry on the incident. It stated that it was a dead engine, hauled by another machine in the front. "We r concerned, had enquired. The fact that it was a dead(non-working)engine hauled by another engine in the front can be seen in the video," read the reply by the Railways Ministry on August 9, 2017. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the Google search results, the Desk found an extended version of the same video uploaded on YouTube by a Bengali news outlet named Sangbad Pratidin on Aug 11, 2017. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: At the 00:16-minute timestamp, the person recording the video addresses the loco pilot as BK Mandal from Chandrapura, a town in Jharkhand's Bokaro district. Further watching the video closely, we noticed the station signage of "Bermo" at the 1:17-minute timestamp. A Google search found that Bermo Railway Station is in the Bokaro district of Jharkhand and falls under the Dhanbad railway division of the East-Central Railway zone. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Kerala Vande Bharat Express leakage reports". The search results led to an April 26 Times Now report with the headline: "New Kerala Vande Bharat Express 'Leaks' Amid Rain in Kannur; Repaired". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a six-year-old video of leakage in a train engine was falsely linked to the newly inaugurated Vande Bharat Express in Kerala. Notably, India's first Vande Bharat Express train, initially called Train 18, was flagged off by Prime Minister Modi on February 15, 2019. It runs between Delhi and Varanasi.

title: PTI Fact Check: Dancers performing Bharatnatyam in this video are not Chinese robots; Social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of two dancers performing on stage and claimed they were not humans but robots made in China. The user also claimed that the dancers performed at Disneyland in Shanghai. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the two women in the video were professional Bharatanatyam dancers. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 30 a 3:20-minute video of two Bharatnatyam dancers performing on stage and claimed they were not humans but robots made in China. The user also claimed that they performed at Disneyland in Shanghai. "*oversee this dance. I was dancing at Disneyland in Shanghai*. *These two are not human dancers, *But two robots made in China**. *The duration of the dance is only five minutes. But the waiting time to buy tickets to see this dance is 4 hours. Tickets to see this dance cost 499 yuan, equivalent to 75 dollars*. *Robots' facial expressions are so perfect that it's hard to distinguish them from real people.* (Sic)," read the post. Here is the link and archive link of the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a YouTube video from August 11, 2017, posted by IndianRaga, a channel with 5.5 lakh subscribers. "Vahana Alarippu: Bharatanatyam Dance | Best of Indian Classical Dance," read the video title, which has over 15.8 lakh views so far. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that stills from the YouTube video looked visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots from the viral video and YouTube video: The video's description read: "IndianRaga brings together the best musicians and dancers across 60 international cities to collaborate on high-quality music videos viewed by millions globally. The genres we work with are rooted in Indian classical performing arts and include Carnatic music (South Indian classical music), Hindustani music (North Indian classical music), semi-classical music, contemporary and fusion music, Indian classical dances including Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Mohiniattam, Kathak, and also ballet, tap, contemporary dance." It also mentioned that the performers seen in the video were Sophia Salingaros and Isha Parupudi. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the verified Instagram handle of "Indian raga", which has over 67,500 followers, and found a photo of Salingaros and Parupudi during a Bharatnatyam performance, which had been posted on September 17, 2019, Here is the link to the photo post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, we conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Sophia Salingaros Isha Parupudi Bharatnatyam dancers", which led us to the Instagram handle of Sophia Salingaros. Salingaros has posted photos of multiple Bharatnatyam performances on her profile, with over 53,000 followers. Here is the link to Salingaros' profile . Below is a screenshot of the same: On scanning Salingaros' profile, we found a photo posted on December 12, 2022, in which she looked similar to one of the dancers in the viral video. Here is the link to the photo , which has over 3,300 likes. Below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing a screenshot from the viral video to the photo posted by Salingaros: The Desk conducted a Google search for Isha Parupudi, the second dancer in the viral video. However, we could not find any authentic social media handle for Parupudi. But the Desk found an article posted by "The Aseemkala Initiative" in May 2021, which mentioned Isha Parupudi as a Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer from Houston, Texas, USA. Here is the link to the article . Below is a screenshot of the same: In one of the photos in the article, Parupudi looked similar to the other dancer in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing a screenshot from the viral video to the photo posted in the article: The Desk subsequently concluded that the two dancers in the viral video were humans, not robots. We also reached out to Sophia Salingaros and Isha Parupudi on social media for their comments on the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when their responses are received.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of abandoned Lockheed Martin L1011 TriStar airplane shared on social media in name of Malaysian Airlines Flight MH370 wreckage
content: New Delhi, May 3 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of underwater airplane wreckage and claimed that Malaysian Airlines Flight MH370 had gone missing in March 2014. The user also claimed that the wreckage was found without a human skeleton despite carrying 239 people on board. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo was of an abandoned Lockheed Martin L1011 TriStar airplane, which was intentionally sunk into Jordan's Gulf of Aqaba in 2019 to attract divers and create an artificial reef for marine life. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 2 a photo of airplane wreckage underwater and claimed that it was the Malaysian Airlines Flight MH370, which had gone missing in March 2014. The user also claimed that the wreckage was found without a human skeleton despite carrying 239 people on board. "Malaysia Airplane MH370 that disappeared nine years ago has been found under the ocean with no human skeleton. The plane had 239 passengers on board," read the Twitter post, which has garnered over 58,000 views and 350 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the viral social media post. The search results revealed a Twitter post with the same image and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet with more than 570K views and 2400 likes. Below is a screenshot of the post: The search results also led to a CNN report published on July 22, 2022, which carried a similar photo of underwater aeroplane wreckage. The report headline read: "Eerie abandoned passenger plane sits on the floor of Red Sea". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: "The venerable old Lockheed Martin L1011 Tristar airplane, with its three engines, mounted on wings and tail fin, would be a sight to behold in the air or on the ground, let alone deep beneath the surface of the Red Sea, among the fish and coral," the report read. "The abandoned jet, sunk in 2019 to create an artificial reef to encourage marine life, has been photographed by American underwater photographer Brett Hoelzer in a series of images that capture the eerie spectacle created by this aquatic airliner," it added. The report also mentioned a hyperlink to Hoelzer's Instagram page, where we found a video he posted whose visuals were strikingly similar to the photo shared in social media posts. "We had an epic dive at the Tristar wreck this week. I shot this footage and took many photos. The guests diving with @deepbluedivecenter had an awesome time at this site," read the May 2 post. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo with the visuals of the video posted by the underwater photographer: We found another post on Hoelzer's Instagram page, which showed the same wrecked airplane as in the abovementioned post. Here is the link to the Instagram post , and below is a screenshot of the same: We again compared the viral photo with the photo shared by the underwater photographer and noticed the same damage in the nose of the aircraft. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Lockheed Martin L1011 TriStar airplane". The search results led to a YouTube video posted by one Marinko Sanjković on August 31, 2022. Here is the link to the video titled "Lockheed L-1011 TriStar Wreck", and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results also led to the official website of Aqaba Tourism, where we found a page on the wrecked airplane titled "Dive a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar Wreck". "The Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority (ASEZA) scuttled A Lockheed L-1011 TriStar in the waters of the Red Sea next to King Abdullah Reef dive site and adjacent to Aqaba Container Terminal," it read. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Malaysian Airlines Flight MH370". The search results led to a video report by Al Jazeera, published on Mar 14, 2023. The report stated that the wreckage of the missing airplane is still missing. The search results also led to the Malaysian government's official website, which released its findings on the missing airplane on April 30, 2017. It stated that particular marine debris found in the western Indian Ocean had been established as parts of the missing aircraft. However, the airplane wreckage is yet to be found. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a Lockheed Martin L1011 TriStar airplane photo was falsely labelled as the wreckage of the missing Malaysian Airlines Flight MH370.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi did not support use of ballot papers over EVMs; Edited video of his speech shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 3 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a clip of Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaking at an event and claimed that the PM advocated the use of ballot papers instead of electronic voting machines (EVMs) in elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Modi's speech was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user on April 27 shared a 17-second clip of PM Modi speaking at an event and claimed that he advocated the use of ballot papers in elections instead of electronic voting machines (EVMs). "खुद ईवीएम हटवाना चाहते थे अब ईवीएम हटाकर बैलेट पेपर लागू कर दो सत्ता तुम्हारे हाथ में," read the text in the video, which has over 12,700 reactions and 500 comments so far. "You wanted to remove EVM, now remove EVM and apply ballot paper; the power is in your hands," read the English translation of the text. Here is the link and archive link of the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: "During elections, even educated countries of the world like America read names on the ballot paper and stamp them," PM Modi says in the viral video. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a YouTube video posted on December 3, 2016, by the verified channel of PM Narendra Modi, which has over 14 million subscribers. "PM Modi at Parivartan Rally in New Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh," read the video title, which has garnered over 13 million views. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that stills from the YouTube video looked visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots of the viral video and YouTube video: The Desk oversaw the video and found that the PM started the portion of the speech, as carried in the viral video, from the 55:20 timestamp. In the extended version of the video, PM Modi said, "During elections, even educated countries of the world like America read names on the ballot paper and stamp them. But, the people of India, called uneducated by some, vote by pressing a button." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "PM Modi Moradabad speech 2016", which led us to a report published by NDTV on December 3, 2016. "Your Phone Is Your Wallet, Says PM Narendra Modi In Moradabad: Highlights," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report . Below is a screenshot of the same: NDTV, in its report, highlighted key points from the PM's speech at the Parivartan Rally in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. One of the points read, "The people who say Indians are illiterate, Indians don't know anything. But around the world, people use paper ballots. India votes through a button." Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently that a selection portion of PM Modi's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Person seen slapping elderly woman in this video is not BJP leader; Footage from Bangladesh shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video clip of a man slapping an elderly woman purportedly with a set of clothes during what appeared to be a distribution drive. The user claimed that the former was a BJP spokesperson distributing clothes to people experiencing poverty in Karnataka ahead of the upcoming Assembly elections. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was originally from Bangladesh. An unrelated video from a neighbouring country was shared on social media with a false claim ahead of the Karnataka assembly elections. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 1 a 10-second video clip, which showed a man hitting an elderly woman purportedly with a set of clothes during what appeared to be a distribution drive. The user claimed that the man was a BJP spokesperson distributing clothes to the poor ahead of the Karnataka assembly elections scheduled on May 10. "#कर्नाटक चुनाव से पहले ये हाल है भाजपाइयों का असली रूम बीजेपी परवख्ता गरीबों को कपड़ा वितरण करते हुए। चुनाव जीतने के बाद आप समझ सकते हैं गरीबो के साथ इस तरह का व्यवहार दुःखद है,," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "#Karnataka This is the real face of BJP people before elections. BJP spokesperson distributing clothes to the poor. After winning the election, you can understand that this kind of behaviour with the poor is sad," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a Facebook post from April 29, where the same video and description had been posted with the hashtag "#karnatakelection2023". Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a YouTube video posted on March 21, 2023, by a channel named "Let's watch bd". The viral video is seen playing on a loop for 2 minutes and 32 seconds in the YouTube video. "আলীগ নেতার অত্যাচার। এমপির উপহার দিতে গিয়ে মানুষকে মারধোর করলো আ'লীগ নেতা," read the title of the video, which is originally in Bengali. "A-League leader beats up people while giving gifts," read the English translation of the title. Here is the link to the video , which has over 1,500 likes, and below is a screenshot of the same: "Desperate to rebuild the political parties keeping the next National Parliamentary election ahead. With his continuation, the general workers of Ward Awami League are disappointed as Habibur Rahman (Bitu) made a member secretary of the conference preparation committee of the two no. Ward Awami league under Satkhira municipality. If such a person stays in an important position in Trinamool, the party's image will be diminished, and the workers will become zero, says multiple leaders and workers of the Ward Awami League (Sic)," read the description of the video. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk noticed a text and logo 'SB Satkhira Bulletin' on the top left corner of the viral video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Habibur Rahman Satkhira Bulletin", which led to a Facebook post from March 20, where Satkhira Bulletin, a Bangladeshi news company, had posted the same viral video. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the video posted by Satkhira Bulletin had the same description as the YouTube video posted by "Let's watch bd". Also, at the bottom of the video posted by Satkhira Bulletin, we noticed a ticker in Bangla which read, "হাবিবুর রহমান (বিটু) সদস্য সচিব ২নং ওয়ার্ড আওয়ামী লীগ (Habibur Rahman (Bitu) member secretary 2nd ward Awami League)." The Desk subsequently concluded that a video from Bangladesh was falsely linked to the upcoming Karnataka elections and shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of 2017 CEAT tyre advertisement peddled on social media as real and recent; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A Twitter user shared a video of a man refusing to buy a carry bag from a shop after purchasing multiple items. Towards the end, the video showed messages not to vote for BJP and PM Modi. The user claimed that the video is being shared in Karnataka, the state which is going to polls on May 10. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a six-year-old advertisement was digitally altered and shared on social media as real and recent. Claim A Twitter user shared on April 27 a 35-second video of a man refusing to buy a carry bag from a shop after purchasing multiple items. It then shows him struggling to carry the items to his car, after which the following message flashes on the screen: "Paise bachane hain? Modi hatao paise bachao, naukari bachao, beti bachao, democracy bachao, desh bachao (Want to save money? Remove Modi. Save money. Save jobs. Save daughters. Save democracy. Save the country). The user also claimed the video was viral in Karnataka, where assembly elections are scheduled for May 10. "One Nation, One Solution. Watch this 'Modi hate video which is viral in Karnataka. (sic)," read the post, which has garnered over 1.87 lakh views and 1,800 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse image search on one of them led to another Twitter post from April 27, where the same video had been posted with the hashtag "#KarnatakaElection2023". "Modi Hatao Desh Bacho Best Ads #KarnatakaElection2023," read the post, which has over 32,000 views and 230 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a YouTube video posted on June 8, 2017, by the official YouTube channel of CEAT Tyres, which has over 40,700 subscribers. "Savings at Supermarket - CEAT Fuelsmarrt Tyres," read the video title, which has garnered over 1 million views so far. Here is the link to the video . Below is a screenshot for the same: The Desk found that the video posted by CEAT Tyres was the same as the one shared in social media posts till the 0:26 timestamp, after which the following text appears on screen - - "Paise Bachane Hai?". We noticed that the font of the text on the YouTube video was different from the viral video, along with a slight difference in the spelling. Also, the background of the viral video was blurry compared to the YouTube video. Below is a combination image comparing the text on the viral video to the YouTube video: Furthermore, the Desk found that an advertisement for CEAT Tyres followed the text appearing on the screen in the YouTube video. Below is a screenshot of the same: A voiceover in the video says, "CEAT Fuelsmart tyre lagao, ye bachaye teen saal mein Rs 15,000 tak ka fuel (Put CEAT Fuelsmart tyre, it saves fuel worth Rs 15,000 in three years)." However, there is no "Modi hatao, desh bachao…" message, as seen in the viral video. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keywords "CEAT Tyres ad 2016", which led us to a YouTube video posted on December 29, 2019. "Some interesting funny and creative ads| Funny ads |YouTube cinema hub," read the video title. Here is the link to the video . Below is a screenshot of the same: Between the 0:35 and 1:05 timestamps, the same CEAT Tyres advertisement video is played without the message "Modi hatao, desh bachao…". The Desk subsequently concluded that a selected portion of a six-year-old video was digitally altered and shared with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This 'NDTV Poll of Polls' graphics on Karnataka elections is fake; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, May 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared graphics, purportedly showing a 'poll of polls conducted by NDTV, which was seen "predicting a victory for the Congress in the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections". The graphics showed data from seven pre-poll surveys, all indicating a clear majority for the Congress. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the NDTV did not publish any such poll of polls. The fake graphic was shared on social media with a false claim. The Karnataka Assembly polls are scheduled for May 10, and the counting of votes will be taken up on May 13. Claim A Twitter user named Spirit of Congress shared on May 2 graphics of what was claimed as a 'poll of polls conducted by NDTV', which claimed a victory for the Congress in the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections. The graphic contained the purported data of seven opinion polls on Karnataka elections, all indicating a majority for the Congress in the 224-seat state Assembly. "BREAKING NOW - KARNATAKA ELECTIONS Most Opinion Polls are unanimously predicting that in Karnataka, BJP is staring at their biggest defeat due to huge anti-incumbency against 40% Commission govt. Today, the NDTV Poll of Polls Tracker predicts that," read the post. It garnered over 84,700 views and 530 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: According to the graphics, NDTV's 'poll of polls claimed that the BJP would win 55-62 seats, Congress 131-142 seats, JDS+ 16-25 seats and 0-4 seats for Others. Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the graph shared in the social media post. The search results led to a Twitter post from May 2, where the same photo had been shared. "Kannadigas are going to choose Congress govt. Congress 150+," read the post shared by a user named Ritu Choudhary, who mentioned herself as a member of the Congress party. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk further scanned the search results but could not find any NDTV report carrying any such 'poll of polls on the upcoming Karnataka elections, as claimed in the social media posts. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk went through the social media handles of NDTV to check if the media house had published any posts regarding the purported 'poll of polls. We found a tweet shared by NDTV on May 3 in which it posted the viral graphic, terming it "fake. NDTV also mentioned that it will release its authentic "poll of exit polls" on the evening of May 10. "Fake Tweet Alert | False posts on NDTV Poll of Poll tracker for Karnataka, being widely circulated, are misleading. Watch this space for the real #PollOfExitPolls on May 10th evening," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted specific Google searches for the purported seven surveys mentioned in the graphic. We found that data from three surveys – ABP C-Voter, TV9 Kannada and C Daily Tracker – was wrongly mentioned; two of them – RSS Internal Survey and State Intelligence Bureau – were non-existent, i.e. such surveys were never conducted at all. The data of the remaining two – Eedina and Lok Poll – was almost correct, as mentioned in the viral graphic. The ABP C-Voter opinion poll has predicted 110-122 seats for the Congress, 73-85 seats for the BJP, 21-29 seats for the JD(S) and 2-6 seats for Others. The viral graphic shows the ABP C-Voter survey predicting 120-131 seats for the Congress, 61-75 for the BJP, 16-25 for the JD(S) and 0-4 for Others. Here is the link to the ABP tweet on the survey conducted, and below is a screenshot of the same: The opinion poll conducted by TV9 Kannada gave an edge to the BJP, while the viral graphic showed it giving a majority to the Congress, giving 112-119 seats to it and 75-87 seats to the ruling BJP. Here is the link to the TV9 report on the opinion poll on Karnataka, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the third case of C-Daily Tracker, the pre-poll survey predicted 147 seats for the Congress and 46 for the BJP, while the viral graphic showed it giving 154 seats to the Congress and 43 seats to the BJP. Here is the link to the April 30 tweet by C-Daily Tracker, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that NDTV did not release a 'poll of polls' survey on the upcoming Karnataka elections. A fake graphic was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Man dancing in video is not former CJI's son Saurabh Kirpal; Claim shared in social media post is false
content: New Delhi, May 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a man dancing to a Bollywood song, claiming he was Saurabh Kirpal, a senior advocate and the son of former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Bhupinder Nath Kirpal. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man dancing in the video shared on social media was not former CJI's son Saurabh Kirpal. The man in the video was a co-founder of a fashion brand. The claim shared in the social media post was false. The video was shared when a five-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court was hearing the petitions seeking marriage equality. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 3 a 54-second video of a man dancing to a Bollywood song, whom he claimed was Saurabh Kirpal, a senior advocate and the son of former CJI Bhupinder Nath Kirpal. The user claimed that Kirpal, who openly identifies himself as a gay man, could become a Supreme Court judge, which was why the Supreme Court was treating the same-sex marriage case with importance. "ये हैं सौरव कृपाल SC के भावी न्यायाधीश. इनके पिता बी.एन. कृपाल 2002 में SC के मुख्य न्यायाधीश थे. इसलिए परिवारवाद परम्परा के तहत चीफ जस्टिस चंद्रचूड़ के लिए समलैंगिक विवाह को मान्यता अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है," read the post, which has garnered over 11,000 views, along with more than 1100 likes. "This is Sourav Kripal, future SC judge. His father, B.N. Kripal, Was the Chief Justice of SC in 2002. Hence under familyism tradition, for Chief Justice Chandrachud, recognition of gay marriage is crucial," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a video posted on an Instagram page named 'daman-diaries' on Jan 8, 2022. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The post's caption read: "Finally dancing to one of my favourite tracks of the season." The Desk noticed that the video was the same as the one shared on social media. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: The bio of the Instagram page mentioned "digital creator" and identified the user as Damandeep Singh Chaudhary, the co-founder of a fashion company called Runway Lifestyle. The bio also mentioned the link to the brand's website, where we found a page about Chaudhary. "Daman is a known name in the fashion industry. His keen eye, vast experience and presence at leading fashion events provide us with enviable scouting opportunities making us one of the leading model management agencies in the country. He heads our fashion division that nurtures fresh talent and services top publications to international brands," read the page. Here is the link to the website , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Daman Chaudhary dance video". The search results led to a May 4 Twitter post by advocate Saurabh Kirpal, in which he vehemently denied the claim made in the social media post. "There's a video of a man dancing, allegedly me, that's gone viral. a) it's not me; b) mocking anyone this way is disgusting homophobia. Bigots may cloak their hatred behind justifications, but it remains vile. Shame on them," Kirpal wrote in the Twitter post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to Saurabh Kirpal. "This is nothing but disgusting homophobia. Mocking someone in this manner is sheer contempt. The irony is that we can't do anything about it," Kirpal told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was shared poorly, falsely identifying the man in it as senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photo of a woman's body falsely linked to Manipur violence and peddled on social media with fake claim
content: New Delhi, May 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a bloodstained body of a woman wrapped in plastic bag and claimed that she was a nurse from Manipur who was raped and killed by members of a different community. The user linked the purported incident with the recent violence witnessed across several parts of the state. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo of an old and unrelated incident was shared on social media with a false claim, linking it to the recent violence in Manipur. Over the past week, Manipur witnessed violence following inter-community clashes. Curfew was imposed in several areas, and over 100 columns of the Army were deployed in the state after the violence broke out on May 3 (Wednesday). Claim A Twitter user shared on May 6 a photo of a woman's body lying in a plastic bag and claimed that she was a nurse who was raped and killed by members from another community. The user also used the hashtag '#ManipurViolence' in the post, linking it to the violence that broke out in several parts of the state over the past week. "What is this then? A Meitei nurse working in Ccpur was raped by Kuki inside the hospital and brutally killed! #ManipurViolence #letthismadnessend," read the Tweet shared by the user. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot highlighting the image being investigated: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the image carried in the Twitter post. The search results led to a report published by Amar Ujala on Nov 22, 2022. "Ayushi Murder Case: लव मैरिज के बाद छत्रपाल गुर्जर से छिप-छिपकर मिलती थी आयुषी, पिता का सनसनीखेज खुलासा," read the headline of the report published by Amar Ujala. "Ayushi Murder Case: Ayushi used to meet Chhatrapal Gurjar after love marriage secretly, father's sensational disclosure," read the English translation of the headline initially in Hindi. Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot of the same. "मथुरा में यमुना एक्सप्रेसवे की सर्विस रोड पर ट्रॉली बैग में युवती का शव मिलने के मामले में पुलिस ने सोमवार को माता-पिता को गिरफ्तार कर लिया। (Police arrested the parents on Monday in connection with the discovery of the girl's body in a trolley bag on the service road of Yamuna Expressway in Mathura)," read a portion of the news report. The Desk noticed that an image which is visually similar to the one shared on social media was carried by Amar Ujala in its report. Below is a combination image comparing the viral replication to the one carried by Amar Ujala in their report: The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Mathura girl body trolley bag", which led to a report published by India Today on Nov 22, 2022. "Father killed girl found in a bag in Mathura for 'leaving home unannounced'," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report . Below is the screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed that India Today's report carried a visually similar image clicked from a different angle to the one shared on social media. Below is a combination image comparing the viral replication to the one carried by India Today: The Desk subsequently concluded that the photo of an old and unrelated incident was shared on social media with falsely linking it to the recent violence in Manipur.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of men looting apparel shop in Philippines falsely linked to Manipur Violence; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, May 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video which showed dozens of people barging into an apparel shop and looting it. The user linked the video to Manipur amid the widespread violence in the Northeastern state. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from Lucena City, Philippines. The unrelated video was peddled on social media with a false claim. Over 50 people have been killed in violent clashes between the tribals living in the Manipur hills and the majority Meitei community residing in the Imphal Valley over the latter's demand for Scheduled Tribe (ST) status. Over 23,000 people have been rescued and sheltered in military garrisons and relief camps. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 3 a 30-second video clip – a CCTV footage – which showed dozens of men barging into an apparel shop and looting it. The user claimed that the video was from Manipur. The video's posting date and time implied it was related to the recent violence reported in the Northeastern state. "BJP is a failed govt in Manipur; its responsibility of govt to save property & lives of people? Shame on BJP," read the post, which has garnered over 1800 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. The search results led to an Instagram post shared on March 20. A user named SneakerGeeks Clothing shared the same video with the caption: "All that for t-shirts". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then went through the comment section of the Twitter post, which shared the video claiming it to be from Manipur. We noticed that one of the users mentioned that the video was from the Philippines. Here is the link to the comment , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk refined the Google Reverse Image searches, combining it with specific keywords and came across a website which embedded an Instagram post by VICE Japan. Here is the link to the webpage : The Desk clicked on the April 4 Instagram post mentioned on the webpage and found the same video as the one shared in the Twitter post. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: "At the end of February, as soon as Ukay Ukay in Lucena City, #Philippines opened, customers flocked to the store like an avalanche. When announcing new arrivals, many customers sometimes gather, but enthusiastic shoppers like this one surprised Bundiaran, the store owner; he said," read the English translation of a portion of the Instagram post. It further stated that the incident occurred on Feb 24 and explained the meaning of "Ukay Ukay" as 'to dig' or 'to look'. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the video shared in the Twitter post to the one posted by VICE Japan. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Lucena Philippines clothes shop loot video". The search results led to a YouTube video shared on Feb 27 by a verified channel named News5Everywhere, which has over 3 million subscribers. "Balyahan, agawan ng mga customer sa isang ukay-ukay sa Lucena, viral | Frontline Pilipinas," read the title of the video, which carried the same CCTV footage as shared in the social media post. An English title translation read: "Balyahan, customers fight over an ukay-ukay in Lucena, viral | Frontline Philippines". Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from the Philippines was shared on social media, falsely linking it to the recent violence in Manipur.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Mallikarjun Kharge with Sonia Gandhi at Congress rally in Karnataka shared with the false claim
content: New Delhi, May 9 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A Twitter user shared a video clip which purportedly showed Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge standing beside party leader Sonia Gandhi at an event. The user claimed that Gandhi had mistreated Kharge. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected part of a video from an election rally in Karnataka was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 8 an 18-second video clip and claimed that Sonia Gandhi had mistreated Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge at an event. In the video, Kharge is purportedly asked for Sonia's permission before taking a seat. "From Sonia Gandhi to Siddaramaiah, they all mistreat Kharge ji." The post has garnered over 38,000 views and 200 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a tweet by Amit Malviya, in charge of BJP's IT cell, who had on May 8 shared the same viral clip with a similar claim. "Reminds me of the famous dialogue from Zanjeer… जबतकबैठनेकोनहींकहाजाए, शराफ़तसेखड़ेरहो (keep standing till you are told to sit)… A vote for Congress means letting Sonia and Rahul Gandhi run Karnataka by proxy! Don't let that happen, Karnataka. You are too self-respecting for that… Vote wisely on the 10th.," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a Twitter post from May 7, where the same viral clip had been posted from the account of Karnataka BJP. "Three generations of the Gandhi family have consistently disrespected Karnataka and its leaders: Indira humiliated Nijalingappa, Rajiv demeaned Veerendra Patil, and now Sonia-Rahul belittles Mallikarjun Kharge. This cycle of unrelenting humiliation will end on 10th May," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk scanned the comment section of BJP Karnataka's post and found a video postedby a user, which showed Sonia Gandhi purportedly asking Kharge to sit before her. Below is a screenshot of the comment: The Desk noticed that stills from the video posted in the comments section looked identical to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing visuals from both videos: The search also led to a YouTube video posted on May 6 from the verified account of the Indian National Congress, which has 3.01 million subscribers. The Desk found that this was the original video, a portion of which was shared in social media posts. "LIVE: Joint mega rally | Hubballi, Karnataka |," read the video title, which has over 67,000 views. Here is the link to the video . Below is a screenshot of the same: At the 1:12 timestamp of the video, Sonia Gandhi can be seen asking Kharge to take his seat before her, as seen in the clip posted in the comments section. At the 22:34 timestamp of the video, when Sonia Gandhi finishes her speech and comes back to occupy her seat, everyone in attendance, including Kharge, stands up to applaud. This is the portion of the video being circulated on social media.
