However, in the extended version of the video, after Sonia Gandhi finishes her speech and takes her seat, Mallikarjun Kharge, standing nearby, walks to deliver his speech next. Also, the audio in the background indicates the host introducing Kharge to the crowd. The audio has been edited out in the viral clip. The Desk subsequently concluded that a selected video portionwas taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: PTI Fact Check: One year old unrelated video of crowd falsely linked to wrestlers' protest and shared on Twitter; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, May 9 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Wrestler Sakshi Malik shared on Twitter a video of huge crowd, which it claimed had gathered in support of the wrestlers protesting against Wrestling Federation of India President Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video at least a year old. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. The video was shared amid the ongoing protest by wrestlers against WFI President Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who has been accused of sexual harassment. The protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar has recently received support from some groups of farmers and political parties. Claim Wrestler Sakshi Malik shared on May 9 a video on Twitter which showed a huge crowd, which she claimed had gathered in support of the wrestlers protesting against WFI President Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. "Support from all over India #wrestlersprotest #istandwithmychampions," read the post, which has garnered over 194K views and 7500 likes so far. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a Twitter post, shared on September 30, 2022. "जयपुर में ओबीसी वर्ग का रैला... #OBC (OBC class rally in Jaipur...)," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the same: However, the Desk noticed that several users had commented on the video post, questioning the presence of BJP flags in the OBC rally. Here is the screenshot of one such comment: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Jaipur OBC rally September 2022" and found that such a rally was indeed taken out in the city on the same day when the Twitter user posted the video. Here is the link to a News18 Hindi's video report on the OBC rally held in Jaipur on Sep 30 last year and below is a screenshot of the same: While an OBC rally did take place in Jaipur, we could not establish if the visuals shown in the viral video were from that particular rally. The Desk then conducted Google Reverse Image Search on several other keyframes of the video, but could not trace the exact origin of the video. However, the latest origin of the video on social media, traced back to September 2022, proved that it was shared as recent with a false claim on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of cash recovery from a vehicle tyre falsely linked to Karnataka polls; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video showing stacks of cash recovered from a vehicle tyre and claimed the incident happened in poll-bound Karnataka. The state voted on May 10 to elect the next government. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2019 when cash was recovered from a vehicle during the run-up to the Lok Sabha polls in the southern state. The video was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to the upcoming Karnataka Assembly elections. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 6 a video of stacks of cash being recovered from a tyre and claimed that the incident happened in poll-bound Karnataka. "Forget RTGS, forget NEFT, Forget IMPS, forget mobile banking... here is THE method of funds transfer - tyre transfer, discovered during #KarnatakaElections! #bribes #KarnatakaAssemblyElection2023," read the post, which has garnered over 25,000 views and 200 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video shared in the social media post and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to another Twitter post carrying the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a report by NDTV published on April 21, 2019, which carried a photo visually similar to the video shared in social media posts. The report headline read: "Watch: ₹ 2.3 Crore Cash Seized From Car's Spare Tire In Karnataka". "The Income Tax department has had its hands full this election season, with various incidents of cash being seized across the country. In its latest haul, the department busted Rs 2.3 crore in cash from the spare tyre of a car travelling from Bengaluru to Shivamogga in Karnataka," read a portion of the news report. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photo shared in the news report to the visuals from the video: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "cash recovered from tyre in Karnataka, 2019 Lok Sabha elections". The search results led to a report by Deccan Herald, published on April 20, 2019. The report headline read: "I-T sleuths seize Rs 2.30 cr stuffed inside tyre". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report included a video tweeted by journalist Akram Mohammed. This was the same video as the one shared in the social media posts. "@IncomeTaxIndia officials seized Rs 2.3 cr stuffed inside a spare wheel of a bus, being transported from Bengaluru to Shivamogga," read the post, dated Apr 20, 2019. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a four-year-old video was shared as recent, falsely linking it to the Assembly polls in Karnataka.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, these photos don't show recent Northern Lights occurrences in Ladakh; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, May 10 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared four photos claiming that they showed the recent Aurora Borealis, also known as Northern Lights, in Ladakh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that all the photos were old and not from India. The photos were shared on social media with a misleading claim. While aurora-like lights were seen in Ladakh on the intervening night of April 22-23, the photos shared on social media predated the event. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 7 a set of four photos claiming that they showed the occurrence of Northern Lights – a rare event – in Ladakh. "A few days back, Ladakh's skies were illuminated by the Aurora Borealis, also known as the Northern Lights. A rare event" read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on each of the four photos shared in the Facebook post. The search results led to a Twitter post shared by Harsh Goenka, chairman of RPG Enterprise, on May 7. The post carried the same set of photos with the same claim. "A few days back, Ladakh's skies were illuminated by the Aurora Borealis, also known as the Northern Lights. A rare event!" read the post, which has garnered over 550K views and 6000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted Google Reverse Image Search on the four photos. Here's what we found: Investigation – Image 1 The Google Reverse Image Search results on the photo led to the website of Alamy, where the exact picture was uploaded on March 23, 2018. "Aurora borealis (Northern lights) over the mountain with one person at Skagsanden beach, Lofoten islands, Norway," read the photo's caption. Here is the link to the Alamy page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the two photos – one shared on social media and the other found on the Alamy website. Hence, the Desk concluded that a five-year-old photo of the occurrence of Northern Lights in Norway was shared as recent with a false claim. Investigation – Image 2 The Desk scanned the Google Reverse Image Search results on the photo and found that it was posted on iStock on March 27. The photo's caption read: "Norwegian fjord landscape with mountains, lake and clouds." Here is the link to the iStock page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photo shared on social media to the one uploaded on iStock. The Desk concluded that an old photo of the Northern Lights in Norway was recently shared, falsely linking it with the rare event in Ladakh. Investigation – Image 3 The Google Reverse Image Search results for the above image led the Desk to the Alamy website, where the same photo was uploaded on March 7, 2017, and the image's location was mentioned as Tromsø, a city in Norway. Below is a combination image comparing the two photos – one shared in social media posts and the other posted on the Alamy website. The Desk concluded that a six-year-old photo of Norther Lights occurrence in Norway was falsely linked to the rare event in Ladakh. Investigation – Image 4 The Google Reverse Image Search results for the above photo led to the same image posted on Getty Images website. "Spectacular Northern Lights over Kirkjufell Mountain Snæfellsnes peninsula, near Grundarfjörður Iceland," read the photo's caption. Here is the link to the page , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the two photos – the one shared on Instagram and the other shared on Getty Images. However, the Desk could not find the time and date when the photo was shot or uploaded on the stock images website. While scanning the search results, the Desk found the same photo in an article on the National Geographic website. Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The article mentioned that the photo was taken by Natthawat Jamnapa and submitted to Your Shot, National Geographic's photo community on Instagram. While it was confirmed that the photo was of the occurrence of Northern Lights in Iceland, we could not trace its exact origin. The National Geographic article was published on Sep 12, 2015. Hence, we concluded that the photo was at least eight years old. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Northern Lights Ladakh". The search results led to a Times of India report published on May 7. The report headline read: "Big buzz over aurora-like sighting in Ladakh skies". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a Twitter post shared by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics. "#Aurora from #Ladakh! This is a time-lapse of the sky taken by a 360 deg camera from #Hanle on 22/23 April night. You can see the aurora lights due to an intense geomagnetic storm that hit the Earth. It is extremely rare to see the aurora at such a low latitude! @dstindia" read the Twitter post dated Apr 29. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that all four photos shared with the claim that they showed the occurrence of Aurora Borealis in Ladakh were old and unrelated to India.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of Prakash Raj urging people 'not to vote for Congress' falsely linked to Karnataka elections; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video clip in which actor-politician Prakash Raj can be heard urging people not to vote for the Congress. The user also claimed that Raj's message was for voters of Karnataka, where assembly elections were held on May 10. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Raj's video message ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha elections was shared on social media as recent, falsely connecting it to the Karnataka polls. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 5 a 13-second clip in which actor-politician Prakash Raj can be heard urging people not to vote for the Congress party. The user claimed it was Raj's message for voters of Karnataka, where assembly elections were held on May 10. Raj can also be heard saying in the video that he has not joined any political party and is an independent. "A Message for Karnataka voters .....," read the post, which has garnered over 50 reactions and 20 comments. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: "Don't waste your vote on Congress. I have not joined any political party, and I'm an independent. I seriously take offence of this dirty politics and stooping down of Congress party…," Raj can be heard saying in the video. Investigation The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a Twitter post from April 17, 2019, where an extended version of the viral video had been posted from Prakash Raj's verified account. "FAKE NEWS by CONGRESS.. look at the dirty politics of this party. SHAME ON CONGRESS. HAVE SENT THE COMPLAINT TO ELECTION COMMISSION WITH PROOF ..please spread and share to counter DIRTY POLITICS (sic)," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The 0:21 to 0:35 portion of the video posted from Raj's verified account is the same as the viral video. However, in the extended version of the video, Raj says, "Look at the dirty politics Congress is doing in Bangalore central. A man who claims to be Rizwan's PA, Mazhar Ahmad… has taken a photograph of Rizwan and me attending a candidates' meeting and said that Prakash Raj is supporting the Congress. So, don't waste your vote on Congress. I have not joined any political party, and I'm an independent, and I seriously take offence to this dirty politics and stooping down of Congress party and Rizwan. I have given an election complaint; please don't believe in such rumours; thank you." This indicates that Raj's video message from 2019 has no connection to the elections in Karnataka. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Prakash Raj Rizwan Bangalore Central 2019", which led to a report published by The Indian Express on May 23, 2019. "Prakash Raj loses in Bangalore Central; calls it a solid slap on his face," read the headline of the report, while its summary read, "Actor-turned-politician Prakash Raj got only 28,906 odd votes while his rivals P C Mohan and Rizwan Arshad had gained more than 6 and 5 lakh votes respectively from Bangalore Central." Here is the link to the report . Below is a screenshot of the same: "During the elections, a photograph of a shake-hand between Prakash Raj and Rizwan had gone viral on social media platforms, which was captioned, 'Prakash Raj supports Congress. Don't waste your vote by giving it to Prakash Raj.' Later, Prakash Raj slammed these fake posts of him backing the Congress, but it could not stop the campaign," read a portion of the report. Below is a screenshot of the same: Rizwan Arshad was Congress' candidate from the Bangalore Central constituency in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, where he contested against Raj, who was an independent, and the BJP's PC Mohan, who eventually emerged as the winner. The Desk subsequently concluded that Raj's video message from 2019 was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the Assembly polls in Karnataka.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of PM Modi drinking tea at stall not from Karnataka; claim in social media posts is false
content: New Delhi, May 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video clip of Prime Minister Narendra Modi drinking tea at a tea stall and claimed the video was from Karnataka, where assembly elections were held on May 10. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a year-old video from Modi's visit to Varanasi was shared on social media, falsely linking it to the assembly polls in Karnataka. PM Modi was recently on a poll blitzkrieg in Karnataka, holding roadshows and rallies across the state as he led the BJP's election campaign. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 28 a 45-second video clip, which showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi drinking tea at a stall, and claimed that it was from Karnataka, where assembly elections are scheduled on May 10. In the video, the tea stall owner is also heard narrating the story of PM Modi's visit. "जय श्री राम जय हिन्दुत्व प्रधान सेवक तो सिर्फ़ मोदी जी है… बाक़ी आजतक सब प्रधानमंत्री हुए हैं। जब प्रधानमंत्री चाय की दुकान पर पहुंचे कर्नाटक में…।," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Hail Lord Ram Hail Hindutva. Only Modi Ji is the prime servant... Everyone else has only been Prime Minister to date. When the Prime Minister reached a tea shop in Karnataka...," read the English translation of the post, which has garnered eight reactions and six shares so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to an April 29 Facebook post, where the same viral video had been shared with the claim that it was from when Modi was campaigning in Karnataka ahead of the elections. The user also claimed that they owned the tea shop seen in the video. "*इतने बडे आदमी, देश के प्रधानमंत्री मेरी चाय की दुकान पर पहुंचे और दो कप चाय पिये..!!**यह घटना कर्नाटक में चुनाव प्रचार के दौरान की है....,* read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Such a big man, the country's Prime Minister, came to my tea shop and drank two cups. This incident occurred during the election campaign in Karnataka," read the English translation of the post, which has ten reactions so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a YouTube video from March 4, 2022, which had been posted from the verified account of Narendra Modi. "Unforgettable moments from Kashi as PM Modi enjoys a hot cup of 'chai' at a tea stall!" the video title has 1.2 million views so far. Here is the link to the video . Below is a screenshot of the same: We found that stills from the YouTube video looked visually identical to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing screenshots from the viral video and YouTube video: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "PM Modi tea stall Kashi", which led to a video report published by NDTV on March 4, 2022. "Watch: PM Modi's Tea Break, 'Damru' Session At Mega Varanasi Roadshow," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report . Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that stills from the video carried in the report are visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing a screenshot of the viral video to the video taken in the news: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi stopped for tea as he held a mega roadshow in Varanasi on Friday, drumming up support for BJP candidates ahead of the last phase of the assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh," read the report. The Desk subsequently concluded that a year-old video from PM Modi's visit to Varanasi had been falsely connected to the Karnataka elections.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of VVPAT slips removal shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of some people removing Voter VerifiedPaper Audit Trail (VVPAT) slips from machines kept inside a substantial room and alleged that the process was a violation of the conduct of elections rules, 1961. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found no issue in the video shared on social media. The workers were seen extracting the VVPAT slips from the machine and preserving them after counting as per the Election Commission of India's guidelines. The claim made in the social media post was found to be false. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 26 a 1:46-minute video, which purportedly showed some people removing VVPAT slips from EVM machines kept inside a substantial room, and alleged that the process violated the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961. The video shows a man removing all the slips (or votes) from the VVPAT machine and putting them in a black envelope. He then seals the envelope and places the machine inside a box. "Modi magic! VVPAT slips in any election... shall be retained for one year and shall after that be destroyed," says Rule 94 (b) of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961. Why are VVPAT slips removed from strongroom ?" read the post, which has over 4,800 reactions and 650 comments. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Search using the keyword "Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961". The search results led to the official website of the Chief Electoral Officer, Rajasthan, where we found a downloadable PDF file. Here is the link to the file . We downloaded the PDF document and scrolled down to Section 94 of the election rules regarding the disposal of election papers. Section 94(b) of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, states that subject to any direction to the contrary given by the Election Commission or by a competent court or tribunal, election-related papers such as used and unused ballot papers, counterfoils of used ballot papers, marked copies of electoral rolls, and registers of voters shall be retained for one year. However, this rule does not explicitly mention VVPAT slips. Below are the relevant screenshots: Nonetheless, the video in the viral post does not show the destruction of VVPAT slips or any other election-related papers. Instead, it offers the removal of VVPAT slips from respective machines (which is part of the process stated by the ECI, as mentioned in the article below). The Desk noticed that Section 94(c) of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, which addresses all other election papers not mentioned above (including VVPAT slips), states that they can be retained for a period as directed by the Election Commission unless the election petition/court case is Pending. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keyword "removal of VVPAT slips, ECI", which led to a page on the Election Commission of India's official website. A link to download a copy of the rules about removing VVPAT slips after completing the counting of votes has been provided on the page. Here is the link to the website , and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the ECI's rules, the VVPAT paper slips shall be removed from the drop box of VVPAT and kept in a paper envelope made of thick black paper polling station-wise. Also, the VVPAT slips taken out from each machine must be kept in a separate envelope. Below is a screenshot highlighting the ECI's rules: This was the same process followed by the person in the viral video, where he removed the VVPAT slips from the machine, preserved them in an envelope of thick black paper, and sealed it later. During its investigation, the Desk also found a Facebook post from December 12, 2022, where the viral video had been shared, claiming it was from the Bhavnagar district in Gujarat. It is pertinent to mention that this post is from around the same time the assembly elections were held in Gujarat. "BJP's contractors, see with your own eyes how BJP wins; this is from Bhavnagar district," read the post, originally in Gujarati. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Even though we could not trace the viral video to its source, the Desk concluded that it is at least five months old. Subsequently, the Desk that the process related to removing VVPAT slips from the EVM machine and its preservation, as shown in the viral video, was by the rules stated by the ECI.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Hrithik Roshan, Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar did not condemn arrest of ex-Pak PM Imran Khan; Edited video of Bollywood actors peddled as real on social media
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook video that purportedly showed Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar, Hrithik Roshan and Salman Khan separately condemning the arrest of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan and extending support to him was shared on WhatsApp recently. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that all three clips were digitally altered to add the actors' voices to them and was shared on social media with a false claim. Khan was arrested on May 9 as he arrived at a courthouse in Islamabad in connection with a corruption case. His arrest led to massive protests by his supporters and party workers across the country. Later, the country's Supreme Court termed his arrest illegal and ordered immediate release. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759, the link to a Facebook post with a request to verify the claims made in it. The post included a video combined three separate clips of Bollywood actors Akshay Kumar, Hrithik Roshan and Salman Khan, which showed them extending support to former Pakistan PM Imran Khan while condemning his arrest. "Indian actress hrithik roshan & akshay kumar & salman khan Support imran khan," read the May 12 Facebook post, which has garnered over 2,000 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk conducted separate investigations on the three video clips in the Facebook video. Here's what it found: Investigation – Hrithik Roshan In the first 38 seconds of the 1:11-minute clip, a voice similar to that of Hrithik Roshan can be heard saying: "I know who is Imran Khan. All my fans, irrespective of where you are from, I request you to raise voice for Imran Khan for the sake of humanity. Hi guys, this is Hrithik and all my fans, let's raise our voice for Imran Khan. Come on guys." The Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the clip and found a few keyframes showing Roshan. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a YouTube video, posted on January 10. The title of the video read: "EXCLUSIVE : Hrithik Roshan Birthday Special Fan Interaction FULL VIDEO | Krrish 4, Fighter, Jadoo". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the 42-minute-long YouTube video was an extended version of the clip shared in the Facebook post. We watched the entire video but nowhere did Hrithik mention anything about Imran Khan. Below is a combination image, comparing the two videos: We also came across a Twitter post that included visuals from the same video. "With One and Only Hrithik Roshan in Zoom Meet One of the best moments of my life @iHrithik. Thank you so much sir. Wishing you a very happy birthday again. Dream comes true. #HrithikRoshan #HappyBirthdayHrithikRoshan," read the January 9 post. Here is the link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Hrithik Roshan supports Imran Khan", but could not find any news report backing the claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Hrithik Roshan interacting with fans on his birthday was digitally altered to add a voice to it. Investigation – Salman Khan The same viral video also has a 13-second clip where Salman Khan is showing his support for Khan. "Hi guys, salaam to all my Pakistani fans. Did you think Pathan is weak? Imran Khan is weak? Now Salman Khan is supporting Imran Khan," Khan can be heard saying. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes with Salman in it led the Desk to a video on the actor's Instagram page. The video, which was uploaded on April 21, showed Khan talking about how he was travelling to Dubai to celebrate Eid. "See you on 24th April at Float Dubai! Exclusively for VKR Entertainment. You can't miss the biggest EID Celebration!" read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a dated video of Salman Khan was digitally altered to add a voice sounding similar to his. Investigation – Akshay Kumar The video then showed Bollywood actor Akshay Kumar condemning the arrest of Imran Khan and asking people raise their voice against it. A Google Reverse Image search on one of the keyframes showing Kumar led to a 13-second video clip shared on Twitter on May 13. "Akshay Kumar spoke against the illegal arrest of my captain and gave a message to Pakistanis," read the English translation of the post, which was originally in Urdu. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "I am supporting Imran Khan. This is the time to raise your voice. This is not how you arrest someone. Is this the way? Treating someone like animals. Akshay Kumar supporting Imran Khan. I love him," Kumar can be heard saying in the video. The Desk first noticed that the lip movement was not in sync with the audio, indicating that a voice sounding similar to Kumar's may have been added to the video. On scanning the search results, the Desk found a YouTube video, uploaded on the official channel of GOQii, a fitness company, on Nov 22, 2019. The title of the video read: "Akshay Kumar Talks About the GOQii Vital ECG and Heart Health". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the 1:03-minute video was an extended version of the same video as shared in the social media posts. In the YouTube video, Kumar can be heard saying that he is the brand ambassador of GOQii and endorses the company's wearable ECG device. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Akshay Kumar supports Imran Khan". However, we could not find any news report backing the claim. The search results only yielded a couple of fact-checks done on the viral video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Kumar was digitally altered to add his voice to it and make the false claim on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Screenshot of Pak PM's fake tweet on Karnataka elections peddled as real on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a screenshot of a tweet, claiming the post was published on the micro-blogging platform by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in which he 'thanked the people of Karnataka for voting for the Congress. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the Pakistan PM did not tweet this. A fake screenshot of his tweet was peddled on social media with a false claim. Karnataka went to polls on May 10, and the Congress emerged victorious by winning 135 seats in the 224-member Assembly. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp Number +91-8130503759 a purported screenshot of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif's tweet congratulating Karnataka on voting for the Congress. "I would like to heartily thank the people of Karnataka for electing Congress; I hope that Congress along with our SDPI will work for the strengthening of Islam in India and the sovereignty of Karnataka," read the English translation of the purported May 13 tweet, which was initially in Urdu. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the screenshot. The search results led us to a Twitter post with the same screenshot. Here is the link to the tweet , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned Shehbaz Sharif's Twitter handle but did not find that no such Tweet was made by him on May 13, as shown in the screenshot. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Shehbaz Sharif Congress Karnataka Elections" but found no reports related to the purported tweet shared on WhatsApp. In the next part of the Investigation, the Desk checked Shehbaz Sharif's Twitter activities on Social Blade. While scanning the website, the Desk found that the Total Tweet count went up on May 13 (the day Pakistan PM purportedly made the Tweet on Congress' win in Karnataka), whereas the Total Tweet count remained stagnant on May 14 as no tweets were made. Here is the link to the Social Blade website , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the Twitter handle of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, which corroborated this. Shehbaz shared three tweets on May 13, whereas no tweets were transferred on May 14. Below are the screenshots of his tweets from May 13. Had Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif tweeted and deleted the alleged tweet congratulating Karnataka for voting for Congress in Karnataka, it would have reflected on the Social Blade statistics, i.e., the total number of tweets would have gone down. The Desk searched for the archive page of Sharif's Twitter handle on Wayback Machine but couldn't find any such tweet on May 13, as shown in the screenshot. Here is the link to the archive page of his Twitter profile, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif did not share a tweet congratulating Karnataka for voting for Congress in the recently concluded Assembly polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of booth capturing in West Bengal falsely linked to Karnataka elections; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video that purportedly showed a person stopping people and casting votes on their behalf at a polling centre. User alleged that the incident took place in Karnataka's Gulbarga North constituency during the recently concluded assembly polls where one person individually cast 6,000 votes in favour of the Congress. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a one-year-old video from West Bengal had been falsely linked to the Karnataka elections and shared with a false claim. Results for the Karnataka assembly elections were announced on May 13, in which the Congress party registered a landslide victory, dethroning the BJP. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 15 a video that purportedly showed a man standing near an electronic voting machine (EVM) allegedly stopped voters and cast votes on their behalf. The user alleged a voting fraud in Karnataka's Gulbarga north constituency during the recent assembly elections and claimed that one person had individually cast 6,000 votes in favour of the Congress at the constituency. "Gulbarga North Fake voting done at one of the Muslim booth around 6000 votes by single person from Congress party. Now he is under capture by chandu patil and demanding for re-election or Disqualification of Congress MLA. @ceo_karnataka @ECISVEEP @BJP4Karnataka," read the post, which has garnered over 400 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk initially noticed a comment by the user who posted the viral video, in which he posted a photo of newly-elected Congress MLA Kaneez Fatima and alleged that she was the one who won through "fake" votes. Below is a screenshot of the comment: On cross-checking the Election Commission of India's official website, it was confirmed that Fatima was the winner from the Gulbarga north constituency by a margin of 2,712 votes, while BJP's Chandrakant B. Patil (Chandu Patil) was the runner-up. Below is a screenshot from the ECI's official website: The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search of the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a YouTube video posted on February 27, 2022, from the verified channel of TV9 Bangla, which has 1.9 million subscribers. "WB Municipal Election 2022 | দক্ষিণ দমদমের ৩৩ নং ওয়ার্ডের ১০৮ নং বুথে ভোটার না, ভোট দিলেন এজেন্ট (33rd Ward 108th Booth No Voter in South Dumdum, Voting Agent)," read the title of the video, which has over 8,900 views so far. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the video posted by TV9 Bangla was visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the one posted on YouTube: The search also led to a Twitter post from February 27, 2022, where the same video had been posted from the official account of West Bengal BJP. "TMC forces pressing the button before going to press the voting button. Stop the farce in the name of election! Democracy today is ashamed, looted by TMC supporters!," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "South Dumdum West Bengal MC elections", which led to an article published on February 27, 2022, by Bengali media house "Khabor 24x7". "দক্ষিণ দমদমের ৩৩ নম্বর ওয়ার্ডে চলছে ছাপ্পা ভোট, তৃণমূলের জমানায় উন্নয়নের ছবি ভোট বাংলায়," read the headline of the report, which is originally in Bengali. "Print voting is going on in Ward number 33 of South Dum Dum," read the English translation of the headline. Here is the link to the report . Below is a screenshot of the same: In the report, screenshots from the viral video had been carried. Below is a combination image comparing a photo carried in the report to the viral video: The Desk subsequently concluded that a one-year-old video from West Bengal was shared as recent, falsely linking to the recently concluded Karnataka assembly elections.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of a woman and her accomplices thrashing a man peddled as recent on social media with a false claim
content: New Delhi, May 16 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a woman and her accomplices thrashing a man for allegedly sending her lewd messages, claiming that the incident took place in Karnataka's Coorg and was an aftereffect of the recently released movie 'The Kerala Story'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a three-year-old video was posted as recent on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 9 a video of a woman and her accomplices thrashing a man for allegedly sending her lewd messages and claimed that this was an effect of the recently released movie, "The Kerala Story". The user claimed that the incident took place in Karnataka's Coorg. In the video, a man is seen talking to a woman sitting on a scooter, after which a group of men thrashes him. "द केरला स्टोरी के नतीजे आने शुरू! कर्नाटक के कुर्ग में एक शांतिदूत एक बहन को फोन करके अश्लील बातें करता था, बहन ने बड़े प्यार से मिलने के लिए बुलाया और बीच सड़क पर बक्कल सी उधेड दी गई!," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "The results of The Kerala Story have started pouring in! In Coorg, Karnataka, a peace ambassador used to talk obscenely on the phone to a sister. Sister called him to meet and thrashed him!" read the English translation of the post, which has garnered over 30,000 and 2,200 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a Twitter post from May 9, where the same viral video had been posted with a similar claim. The user also claimed that the man was a Muslim harassing the Hindu girl. "द केरला स्टोरी के नतीजे आने शुरू! कर्नाटक के कुर्ग में एक पंचरपुत्र हिन्दू बहन को फोन करके अश्लील बातें करता था। बहन ने बड़े प्यार से मिलने के लिए बुलाया और बीच सड़क पर बक्कल उधेडवा दी जय श्री राम," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "The Kerala Story results start coming! In Karnataka's Kurg, a punctured son used to call a Hindu sister and say nasty things. Sis called for a visit and broke the buckle in the middle of the street Hail Lord Rama," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk went through the comments section and noticed a few comments on the post mentioning that the video was old. Below is a screenshot of one such comment: The search also led to a Facebook video post published on September 25, 2020, by NEWJ English. "Man Thrashed And Then Arrested In Madikeri, Karnataka," read the video title. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the video "English NEWJ" posted was visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the Facebook video: The text in the Facebook video read: "This man was thrashed for sending offensive messages to a woman. The man, Muhammad Mudassir, works for a mobile shop in Madikeri, Karnataka. He allegedly sent lewd messages to a woman. The woman informed her relatives about the incident, after which they trapped and beat him up. A case has been registered at Madikeri police station. The video has created outrage on social media." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keyword "man thrashed in Madikeri 2020", which led to a Times of India report on the incident, published on Sep 18, 2020. "Woman thrashes man with footwear in viral video; five arrested," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "It was on Wednesday night that the video of a woman and her aides thrashing a man with slippers went viral on social media. Mohammed Mudasir, aka Sahil, allegedly sent the woman, a resident of Gowli Street, Madikeri, lewd messages. Following the incident, Mudasir was taken to Madikeri police after the woman complained," read the report. The Desk subsequently concluded that a three-year-old video had been falsely connected to the release of 'The Kerala Story' film and shared as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, the Central govt is not offering free mobile recharge of Rs 239; Viral WhatsApp message is a spam
content: New Delhi, May 19 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A message claiming that the BJP-led central government offered free recharge of Rs 239 to all mobile phone users so that they vote for the ruling party in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections was shared on WhatsApp recently. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the message was spam, and the government introduced no such offer. Such messages are often viral on WhatsApp and social media platforms, intended to gain users' personal information. Several scams are frequently reported in which people have been duped through such messages. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 a WhatsApp message from a user who requested to verify the claim made in it. The message claimed that the central government was offering a free recharge of Rs 239 for 28 days to all mobile phone users so that people vote for the ruling BJP in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi is offering all Indian users a free recharge of Rs 239 for 28 days so that more and more people vote for the BJP in the 2024 elections. I have received the free recharge; you can also receive the same free recharge for 28 days by clicking on the link mentioned below (Last Date – 20 May 2023)," read a rough translation of the message, which was in Hindi. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by clicking on the link mentioned in the WhatsApp message. It led to a webpage carrying a photo of PM Modi and the text: "Prime Minister Free Recharge Scheme. Your one vote is important to us. Keep BJP in mind again in 2024". The photo also carried the logo of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. Here is what the webpage looked like: It also featured a clickable hyperlink stating 'Get Free Recharge'. When we clicked it, the link further led us to another page, asking us to enter the mobile phone number and the telecom company name. On entering the details, we were led to another webpage stating that the free recharge had been activated. We were asked to forward the message to another ten people or groups on WhatsApp to confirm the recharge. Aware of the frequent financial frauds and scams through such messages, we did not move further, as it could expose personal information. In the subsequent investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Govt announces free Rs 239 recharge". We could not find any news report backing any such claim, except for a few fact-checks from last year and earlier this year, indicating that such messages have also gone viral. Since the webpage carried the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas logo, the Desk also went through its official website but could not find any mention of a free recharge scheme. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake message was shared on WhatsApp with the false claim that the BJP-led central government was offering free recharge of Rs 239 to all mobile phone users.

title: PTI Fact Check: Selected part of Rahul Gandhi's 2021 speech video peddled as recent on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 19 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a speech by Rahul Gandhi and claimed that the Congress leader urged people to throw both Hindus and 'Hindutvavadis' out of the country. The user also mentioned that the alleged remarks were related to the recently concluded Karnataka Assembly elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of an old public speech by Gandhi was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claims. The Assembly polls in Karnataka were held on May 10, in which the Congress made an impressive comeback to power, bagging 135 seats in the 224-member Assembly, thereby dethroning the BJP. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 14 an 18-second video of Rahul Gandhi's speech, claiming the Congress leader urged people to throw both Hindus and 'Hindutvavadis' out of the country. The user also mentioned 'Karnataka Assembly elections vote counting', relating it to the recent polls in the southern state. "इसकी ये क्लिप सुनने के बाद भी लाखों हिन्दू इस पार्टी को बोट देगे..इसलिए भारत सेंकड़ों साल गुलाम रहा..."कर्नाटक विधानसभा चुनाव" #VoteCounting" read the tweet orgingally in Hindi. "Lakhs of Hindus will vote for this party even after listening to this clip. That's why India remained a slave for hundreds of years. 'Karnataka Assembly Elections' #VoteCounting," read an English translation of the Tweet. The Twitter post has garnered over 33,000 views, more than 1,600 retweets, and 2,200 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the video clip, Gandhi was heard saying: "And we have ousted these Hindus… these Hindutvavadis out and once again…." Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the viral video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a Facebook post shared on September 14 last year. It carried the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: This made it clear that the video was old and unrelated to Karnataka's recently concluded Assembly polls. On further scanning the Google Reverse Image Search results, the Desk came across a news article published by India Today on December 13, 2021. The report carried a photo visually similar to the viral video. "Rajasthan | Congress and BJP engage in a war of words over Rahul Gandhi's Hindu, Hindutvavadi remark," read the headline of the news article. Here is the link to India Today's report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral image to the image carried by India Today's article. Taking a cue from the report, the Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Rahul Gandhi Jaipur speech", which led to a video of Rahul Gandhi's speech, uploaded on the Congress' YouTube channel on Dec 19, 2021. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the viral 18-second video clip was taken from the 12:21-minute timestamp of the YouTube video. In the original video, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said, "Yet again, we have to oust these Hindutvavaadi people and bring Hindus back to power." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Gandhi's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: These Twitter accounts in name of Imran Khan's sons Suleman, Kasim are fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared screenshots of two Twitter profiles and questioned whether they were genuine accounts of Suleman Isa Khan and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan and his ex-wife Jemima Goldsmith. The PTI Fact Check Desk found neither of the two Twitter accounts authentic. Khan was arrested on May 9 as he arrived at a courthouse in Islamabad concerning a corruption case. His arrest led to massive protests by his supporters and party workers nationwide. Later, the country's Supreme Court termed his detention illegal and ordered immediate release. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 18 screenshots of two Twitter profiles and questioned whether they were the genuine accounts of Suleman Isa Khan and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan and his ex-wife Jemima Goldsmith. The user also tagged Jemima Goldsmith in the post. In the profile pictures of both accounts whose screenshots were shared, Imran can be seen posing with a young man. "Are these real Accounts of your Kids? @Jemima_Khan," read the post, which has over 8.43 lakh views. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk initially noticed some comments on the viral post, which stated that Imran Khan's sons Suleman and Kasim didn't have social media accounts and that the profiles with shared screenshots were fake. Below is a screenshot of one such comment: The Desk then reviewed Jemima Goldsmith's profile to check whether she responded to the viral post query. On May 19, Goldsmith had, in reply to the viral post, confirmed that the accounts don't belong to her sons Suleman and Kasim. "Thanks, @elonmusk. Imposters created fake accounts pretending to be my children with a political agenda in Pakistan. This is exactly what I feared would happen when you took away Twitter's verification blue ticks. FYI my children are not on social media & have no plans to be," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: This confirmed that Goldsmith and Khan's sons don't have accounts on Twitter or any other social media platform. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Imran Khan sons social media" but could not find any authentic profiles of Suleman and Kasim. However, the search led to an IANS report published by Assam Tribune on May 19. "Imran's ex-wife complains about using her kids for 'political agenda in Pak'," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Directly addressing outgoing Twitter CEO Elon Musk, Jemima Goldsmith, the former wife of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) chief Imran Khan, complained of fake accounts on the micro-blogging site pretending to be her sons, which she claimed were created by "imposters with a political agenda in Pakistan"," read the report. "Goldsmith and Khan were married in May 1995 and divorced nine years later in June 2004. Goldsmith has two sons from her marriage to Khan -- Sulaiman Isa (born 1996) and Kasim (born 1999)," the report further read. The Desk scanned the two Twitter profiles, claiming to be of Imran Khan's sons – Suleman Isa Khan and Kasim Khan. We noticed both accounts were opened around Imran Khan's arrest on May 9. Also, most of the posts shared condemned the action against the former Pakistan PM. The Desk subsequently concluded that both the Twitter accounts claiming to be of Imran Khan's sons were fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post on winning margins of less than 2,000 votes and 1,000 votes in Karnataka elections is misleading; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user claimed that in the recently concluded Karnataka Assembly elections, the BJP lost as many as 58 seats by a margin of 2000 votes and 41 seats by a margin of 1000 votes. The user further claimed that while the BJP's vote share remained unchanged from the 2018 Assembly polls, the 5 per cent drop in the vote share of JD(S) led to the Congress' victory in the elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the winning candidates' margin was less than 2000 votes in only 12 constituencies of Karnataka. Among these 12 seats, the difference in the winning margins was less than 1000 seats on eight seats. However, the claims that the BJP vote share remained unchanged from 2018 and that the vote share of the JD(S) dropped by 5 per cent were almost correct. A misleading claim was shared on social media. Karnataka went to polls on May 10, and the counting of votes was taken up on May 13, in which the Congress registered a landslide victory, bagging 135 out of the 224 seats. Claim A Facebook user claimed on May 14 that the BJP lost 58 seats by a margin of 2000 votes and 41 seats by a margin of 1000 sets in the recently concluded Karnataka Assembly elections. The user also claimed that while the BJP's vote share remained unchanged at 36 per cent from the 2018 Assembly polls, the JD(S)' vote share dropped by 5 per cent, which went in Congress' favour. "Karnataka Results analysis - BJP lost 58 seats by a margin of 2000 votes. BJP lost 41 seats by a margin of 1000 votes.. 2018 BJP Vote Share 36% 2023 BJP vote share 36%, No change. 2018 JDS Vote Share 18% 2023 JDS vote share 13%. 5% lost. So 5% JDS vote share transfer to congress," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned the constituency-wise results of the Karnataka Assembly polls on the official website of the Election Commission of India. Here is the link to the Karnataka Assembly election results in 2023 on the ECI website. After scanning the results for all the 224 Assembly seats, the Desk found that there were 12 constituencies where the victory margin was less than 2000 votes. Of these, the margin of four was between 1000 and 2000 votes, while the remaining eight had margin of less than 1000 votes. Below is the list of eight seats where the winning candidate's margin was less than 1000 votes: Below is the list of four constituencies where the winning margin was between 1000 and 2000 votes: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk further scanned the Assembly polls results on the ECI website to find out the vote shares on the parties. As per the data on the EC website, the Congress garnered 42.9 per cent of the total votes polled, BJP received 36 per cent votes, and the JD(S) got 13.29 per cent votes. We then analysed the 2018 Karnataka Assembly poll results on the ECI website. The details mentioned in a downloadable PDF file showed that the BJP received 36.22 per cent votes, Congress 38.04 per cent, and JD(S) got 18.36 per cent votes. Here is the link to the file, and below is a screenshot of the same: This means that the BJP's vote share dropped minutely by 0.22 per cent, from 36.22 per cent in 2018 to 36.00 per cent this time. On the other hand, the JD(S)' vote share took a significant hit of 5.07 per cent, from 18.36 per cent in 2018 to 13.29 per cent. For the Congress, the vote share went up to 42.9 per cent from 38.04 per cent in the previous Assembly polls. This was an increase of 4.86 per cent. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in the Facebook post was partly false.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of Congress leader protesting against Hyderabad rape-murder case shared on social media as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of a man walking towards the Parliament with a girl child claiming she was his daughter, allegedly a rape survivor. The user also claimed that the 'man pinned blame on the BJP-led central government for the incident of rape'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it is a four-year-old video of a protest by a Congress leader against the incidents of sexual violence against women. The girl child with him was not a rape survivor. The social media post was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The man in the video was Sachin Chaudhary who was protesting against the rape-murder of a veterinary doctor in Hyderabad in 2019. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on May 2 and claimed that it showed a man walking towards the Parliament with his five-year-old daughter, who had been allegedly raped. The user also claimed that the man had pinned blame on the BJP-led central government. In the video, the man is seen raising slogans against the Modi government while holding a young girl in his arms, which is followed by police intervention. "दिल्ली में 5 साल की मासूम बच्ची का रेप हुआ... बच्ची के पिता बच्ची को लेकर संसद भवन की ओर चल दिया और आरोप लगाया की मोदी सरकार जिम्मेदार है!," "5 year old innocent girl raped in Delhi... The father of the girl walked towards the Parliament with the child and alleged that the Modi government is responsible!," read the English translation of the post, which has garnered 36 reactions so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk initially noticed a few comments on the viral post which claimed that the video was old. Below is a screenshot of one such comment: We then started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a video report which had been published by ABP Live on Dec 5, 2019. "दिल्ली में संसद के पास रेप कांड के खिलाफ प्रदर्शन, बेटी को साथ लेकर विरोध जताने पहुंचा युवक (Demonstration against rape case near Parliament in Delhi, man reaches along with his daughter to stage protest)," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that stills from the video carried in the report were visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the one carried by ABP Live: The search results also led to a report about the incident, published by Patrika on Dec 5, 2019. "Hyderabad Rape And Murder Case: बेटी के साथ संसद के बाहर धरना देने पहुंचे कांग्रेस नेता को पुलिस ने किया गिरफ्तार," read the headline of the report. "Hyderabad Rape And Murder Case: Police arrest Congress leader who came to protest outside Parliament with daughter," read the headline's English translation. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the man seen in the video is Congress leader Sachin Chaudhary, who came to protest outside Parliament with his daughter over the 2019 Hyderabad rape and murder case, following which he was arrested by the police. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Sachin Chaudhary protest Parliament", which led to a Twitter video post by Chaudhary from December 5, 2019. "बेटियों की सुरक्षा के लिए संसद के सामने अपनी बेटी को लेकर पहुंचा तो पुलिस वालों ने घसीटा, गिरफ्तार किया। मोदीराज में बेटियां सुरक्षित नहीं है मोदी सरकार मुर्दाबाद," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "For the safety of the daughters, when he reached in front of the Parliament with his daughter, the policemen dragged him and arrested him. daughters are not safe in modi raj Down with Modi government," read the post, in which prominent Congress leaders have been tagged. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the post, Choudhary had posted a clearer version of the same viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the video posted by Choudhary: The Desk subsequently concluded that a four-year-old video had been posted as recent on social media with a false claim. Chaudhary, a Congress leader, was protesting against the rape and murder of a 26-year-old veterinary doctor in Hyderabad that took place in 2019.

title: PTI Fact Check: Tweet claiming Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia removed 'BJP' from his Twitter bio is false
content: New Delhi, May 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter account affiliated to the Congress party shared a screenshot of BJP leader and Union Civil Aviation Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia's Twitter account, claiming that he recently removed 'BJP' from his bio. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Scindia never added 'BJP' in his Twitter bio since joining the party in 2020. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Claim A Twitter account affiliated with the Congress party shared on May 20 a screenshot of BJP leader and Union Civil Aviation Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia's Twitter account, claiming that he recently removed 'BJP' from his bio. "उसूलों पर आंच फिर आ रही है : केंद्रीय मंत्री ज्योतिरादित्य सिंधिया ने हटाया ट्विटर से भाजपा का नाम ...!" read the post, which has garnered over 200K views and 3,200 likes so far. An English translation of the post read: "The fire is coming again on the principles: Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia removed BJP's name from Twitter...!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the screenshot shared in the Twitter post. The search results led to another Twitter post carrying the same screenshot and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then looked for archived versions of Scindia's Twitter profile on Wayback Machine and found several versions from 2015 till now. Below is a screenshot of the archive page from August 22, 2015: Since Scindia joined the BJP on March 12, 2020, we next looked for the archived page of the profile as on July 15, 2020. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk next looked for the archive page of the profile on June 2, 2021, and July 11, 2022. Below are the screenshots of the same: The archive version of the profile from February 2023 also showed that Scindia did not mention 'BJP' in his Twitter bio. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found the only change made by Scindia in his Twitter bio since May 2023 was the addition of "Office Account: @Officejmscindia". In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google with the keyword "Jyotiraditya Scindia removes BJP from his Twitter bio". The search results led to a May 20 Twitter post by the BJP leader, where he refuted the viral claim and hit out at the Congress for spreading "lies and propaganda". "मध्यप्रदेश में कांग्रेस पार्टी के पास जनता का कोई मुद्दा नहीं है, इसलिए सुबह-शाम केवल झूठ और प्रोपेगैंडा फैलाना है। मेरे ट्विटर बायो से अच्छा अगर जनता की मन की बात पढ़ ली होती तो 15 महीनों में भ्रष्ट सरकार ना जाती।" read the post. An English translation of the post read: "In Madhya Pradesh, the Congress party does not have any issue of the public, so it only has to spread lies and propaganda in the morning and evening. If you had read people's minds better than my Twitter bio, the corrupt government would not have gone in 15 months". Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk found that Scindia never removed 'BJP' from his Twitter bio. He never added 'BJP' to his Twitter bio after joining the saffron party in March 2020.

title: PTI Fact Check: TV actress Devoleena Bhattacharjee did not play role of supporting actress in 'The Kerala Story'; social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of TV actress Devoleena Bhattacharjee with her husband, Shanwaz Shaikh, claiming that she acted in the film 'The Kerala Story' despite being married to a Muslim man. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Bhattacharjee was not part of 'The Kerala Story'. The post had been shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 17 a photo of TV actress Devoleena Bhattacharjee with her husband Shanwaz Shaikh and claimed that she acted in the film 'The Kerala Story' despite being married to a Muslim man. "मुसलमान अगर पैसे वाला है तो दामाद है मुसलमान अगर गरीब है तो लव जिहाद है !! उदाहरण फिल्म द केरला स्टोरी की सहायक अभिनेत्री देवालिना भट्टाचार्य के पति का नाम शहनवाज शेख है !!," read the post. "If a Muslim is rich, then he is a son-in-law; if a Muslim is poor, it is love jihad. For example, the name of the husband of Devalina Bhattacharya, the supporting actress of the film The Kerala Story, is Shahnawaz Shaikh." read the English translation of the post, which has garnered over 2.83 lakh views and 1,600 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by conducting a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to an Instagram post from April 22 where Bhattacharjee had posted the same viral photo from her verified account. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Devoleena Bhattacharjee Shanawaz Shaikh", which led to a report published by Hindustan Times on Dec 14, 2022. "It's official: Devoleena Bhattarjee gets married to her gym trainer Shanwaz Shaikh; reception soon," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: Through this report, it was confirmed that Bhattacharjee had been married to Shanwaz Shaikh since Dec 2022. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned Bhattacharjee's Twitter profile to check whether she had replied to the viral post. On May 19, Bhattacharjee wrote in reply to the viral post that she was financially and mentally independent and had gotten married without converting. Here is the link and archive link to the reply. Below is its screenshot: In a comment in the post thread, Bhattacharjee further wrote that she was not part of the movie "The Kerala Story". "And one more thing, I wish I could have been a part of the kerela story. But my bad, I wasn't there. And you call yourself PATRAKAAR? Fact check karna bhool gaye yaa attention paane ka naya tarika dhoondh nikaala hai.," she wrote. Below is a screenshot of the comment: The Desk then conducted a Google Search with the keyword "The Kerala Story actors", which led us to the IMDb page of the movie "The Kerala Story". IMDb is considered one of the world's most reliable online databases for information related to films, television series, podcasts etc. Here is the link to the page , and below is its screenshot: IMDb listed the movie's entire star cast, but Bhattacharjee's name could not be found anywhere. Below is a screenshot of the complete list of actors seen in "The Kerala Story": The Desk subsequently concluded that actor Devoleena Bhattacharjee was not part of "The Kerala Story". The claim in the post was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clock tower in Nepal's Birgunj falsely claimed as one in Srinagar; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 24 (Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of a clock tower, claiming the iconic clock tower in Srinagar was given a facelift for the G20 meeting held in the city recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo of the clock tower of Nepal's Birgunj was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo on May 22 and claimed that it was the iconic Clock Tower in Srinagar which had been given a facelift for the G20 meeting, which was held in the city recently. "The clock tower (Ghanta Ghar) is being restored and rebuilt by SMC to reflect our heritage and architecture – down to the finest details as a part of Srinagar's facelift for G20 meet... #NewJammuKashmir #peacefuljammukashmir #prosperousjammukashmir," read the post, which has garnered 39 reactions so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk initially noticed a logo at the bottom left-hand side of the photo shared in the viral post that read "Govind Photography". Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation by conducting a Google Search with the keywords "Govind Photography social media", which led to the Facebook page of Govind Photography. On scanning the page, the Desk found a post from March 17, where multiple photos had been shared with hashtags including #Birgunj and #birgunjnepal. "Today's raining after weather at Birgunj #Birgunj #birgunjnepal #birgunjphoto #ghantaghar #maisthan #photography!," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that one of the photos shared by Govind Photography was visually identical to the viral photo and also carried the logo. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one shared by Govind Photography: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo, which led to a Facebook post from March 26, 2021. In the post, multiple photos from a "Freedom Run" event had been shared from the page "Cgi Birgunj". "The Consulate General of India, Birgunj kick-started the celebrations of "Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav (India@75)" with a freedom run organised today by jointly flagging off by Shri Nitesh Kumar, Consul General/ Cgi Birgunj and Shri Ashman Tamang, Chief District Officer, Parsa. India in Nepal (Embassy of India Kathmandu) Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India ICCR in Nepal PMO India," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that in one of the photos, runners can be seen in front of a building that looks identical to the one seen in the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one shared from the Facebook page of Cgi Birgunj: The Desk then conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Clock Tower Srinagar", which led to a report published by Outlook on Jan 26. In the report, a PTI photo of the Clock Tower, or "Ghanta Ghar" in Srinagar had been carried. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the photo of Srinagar's Clock Tower which has been carried in the report does not look anything like the viral photo. The Desk subsequently concluded that the photo was from Nepal's Birgunj, and not Srinagar as claimed in the viral post.

title: PTI Fact Check: Man dictating terms to cop in shared video is not a Karnataka MLA; Unrelated video peddled on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video and claimed it showed a Karnataka Congress MLA dictating terms to a police officer and instructing him to do as he was told. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was from Telangana, and the man seen talking to the police officer in the video was AIMIM MLA Jaffar Hussain Meraj. An unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared a video on May 16, claiming that it showed a Congress MLA from Karnataka dictating terms to a police officer and instructing him to do as he was told. "कर्नाटक:<कांग्रेसी MLA"जफर हुसैन मेराज" (नामपल्ली विधायक) जाचटियाल ने एक पुलिस अधिकारी (एसबी) को घर बुलाकर.... शांति प्रिय' ढंग से समझाते हुए।कहां जैसा हम कहेंगे वैसा ही करना होगा" "Zafar Hussain Merajsh (MLA, Nampally) in Jagtial," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Karnataka:< Congress MLA "Zafar Hussain Meraj" (Nampally MLA) Jachtiyal calling a police officer (SB) home.... explaining in a 'peace loving' manner, said you have to do as we say. Zafar Hussain Merajsh (MLA, Nampally) in Jagtial," read the English translation of the post, which has garnered over 71,000 views and 2,500 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation by conducting an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a Facebook post from May 16, where the same video had been carried with an identical claim. "*जैसा हम कहेंगे वैसा करना पड़ेगा।कर्नाटक में निर्वाचित विधायक एक पुलिस अधिकारी को अपने घर बुलाकर शांति प्रिय ढंग से समझाते हुए।*,"read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "* We will have to do as we say. Elected MLA in Karnataka calling a police officer to his home and explaining peace lovingly. *," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed a logo on the top right-hand side of the Facebook video. A separate Google Reverse Image Search on the logo led to the Twitter profile of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM). We noticed that the profile picture of AIMIM's Twitter account looked visually identical to the logo seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing them: The search also led to a Facebook post from May 11, where an extended version of the viral video had been posted from the account "All India Majlis-E-ittehadul muslimeen Karimnagar". "AIMIM MLA and AIMIM team in Jagtiyal," read the text in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google Search with the keyword "AIMIM MLA meets cop in Jagtiyal", which led to a report published by Deccan Chronicle on May 11. "Jagtial rural SI who attacked woman & her mother suspended," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that the photo carried in the report is visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing a screenshot from the viral video to the picture carried in the news: "The inspector-general of police, multizone-1, suspended Jagtial Rural sub-inspector A. Anil on Thursday on the charges of attacking two women passengers in an RTC bus. On Wednesday night, police superintendent A. Bhaskar issued orders attaching Anil to the district headquarters on disciplinary grounds," read the report. "Earlier in the day, following the instructions of AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi, Nampally MLA Jaffar Hussain Meraj and the district unit president Younus Nadeem visited the house of the postgraduate student involved in the row," the report further added. During our investigation, we also discovered that Nampally is an Assembly constituency in Telangana and one among the 15 constituencies of Hyderabad. The Desk subsequently concluded that the man seen talking to the cop in the video was not a Congress MLA from Karnataka but an AIMIM MLA from Telangana's Nampally constituency.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi was not 'ignored' at G7 Summit; Clipped video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video showing several leaders at the G7 Summit in Hiroshima, Japan posing for a group photograph and interacting with each other. The user claimed that other leaders left PM Modi' isolated' after the group photo. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video was taken out of context and shared with a false claim on social media. The extended version of the video showed leaders interacting with PM Modi before and after taking the group picture at G7 Summit. The 49th G7 Summit was held from May 19-21 in Hiroshima, Japan. PM Modi attended three sessions at the G7 summit following an invitation by Japanese counterpart Fumio Kishida. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 21 a 12-second video clip which showed leaders at the G7 Summit in Hiroshima, Japan posing for a group photograph and interacting with each other while 'PM Modi stood alone'. The user claimed that other leaders isolated the prime minister at the event. "Looks like our PM is lonely and isolated at the G7 Summit in Hiroshima," read the post, which has garnered 2 million views and more than 5,000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video clip and found several keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a May 21 Facebook post carrying the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the official website of the G7 Summit, where several photos from the May 20 event had been posted. Here is the link to the photo on the webpage, and below is a screenshot of the same: In another photo shared on the G7 website, PM Modi can be seen sharing a light moment with other leaders. Below is the image: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Modi at G7 Summit". The search results led to more photos from the event shared on Getty Images. Two such photos can be seen here and here . Below are the screenshots of the same: The photos show PM Modi and Macron entering the stage while interacting with each other. The search results further led us to a video from the event shared on the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: This 2:45-minute video, shared on May 20, was an extended version of the video shared in social media posts.
