At the 2:38-minute timestamp, PM Modi and his Japanese counterpart Fumio Kishida can be seen holding hands while interacting as they get off stage after the picture has been taken. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of a video from the G7 Summit had been taken out of context to falsely claim that other world leaders had recently ignored PM Modi at the event in Hiroshima, Japan.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Telugu actress Sanjjanaa didn't convert to Islam after watching 'The Kerala Story'; Social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of Telugu actress Sanjjanaa Galrani with her family, along with a screenshot of a news report about her going to perform her first Umrah in Mecca. The user claimed that actress converted to Islam after watching the film 'The Kerala Story' and undertook the sacred Haj pilgrimage after getting married post-conversion. The user also claimed that television actress Devoleena Bhattacharjee worked as a supporting actress in 'The Kerala Story'. The claim has been debunked by PTI Fact Check separately. The fact-check story can be read here . In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Sanjjanaa converted to Islam in 2018, whereas 'The Kerala Story' was released earlier this year. The social media post was shared with false claims. 'The Kerala Story', released on May 5, has courted controversy for claiming that thousands of women from Kerala were converted to Islam by force or deceit and later joined the Islamic State. Claim A Facebook user on May 24 shared a photo of Telugu actress Sanjjanaa Galrani with her family and a screenshot of a news report about her going to perform her first Umrah in Mecca. The user claimed that Sanjjanaa converted to Islam after watching the film 'The Kerala Story' and undertook the Haj pilgrimage after getting a married post-religious conversion. "#TheKeralaStory के सुखद परिणाम। फिल्म देखने के बाद साउथ फिल्मों की एक्ट्रेस संजना गलरानी ने #इस्लाम कुबूल करके #अजीज पाशा ने निकाह किया और सऊदी अरब हज यात्रा पर गई। संजना ने कहा की वो अब सुखी जीवन जी रही है और दिल को सुकून है। B - मंडलीय में शोक की लहर (Happy results from TheKeralaStory. After watching the film, South films actress Sanjana Galrani accepted Islam and married Aziz Pasha and went on Haj pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia. Sanjana said that she is living a happy life now and her heart is at peace)," the user wrote. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media. It came across a Twitter post, which carried the same photos and claims as shared in the Facebook post mentioned above. Here is the link and archive link to the tweet shared by Dr Shoaib Jamai, chairperson and spokesperson of India Muslim Foundation. Below is a screenshot of the post: The post shared on May 23 has garnered over 200K views and more than 3,600 likes. Jamai also made the same claim about Devolina Bhattacharjee in the Facebook post. Here is the link to the PTI Fact Check on the false claim. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and found The Indian Express report , whose screenshot was shared in the social media posts. The headline of the May 17 report read: "Sanjjanaa Galrani set to perform her first Umrah in Mecca: 'I don't want to be judged by people who are not secular'." "Sanjjanaa, born into a Hindu family, converted to Islam a few years back and married a doctor named Aziz Pasha. This received much flak from certain sections of people back then. Now, for the first time, Sanjjanaa has publicly spoken at length about her new-found faith," read a paragraph in the report. The Desk then conducted a Google search with the keyword "Sanjjanaa Galrani covers to Islam". The search results led to an Asianet News report published on Sep 18, 2020. The report headline read: "Sandalwood actress Sanjjanaa converted to Islam, changed the name to Mahira". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report carried an affidavit issued by Darul Uloom Shah Valiullah on Oct 9, 2018. Below is a screenshot of the same: "Miss Archana Manohar Galrani shall now be known by her new Muslim name Miss Mahira," the affidavit read. Miss Mahria "embraced Islam on her own will and accord without any pressure or hindrance from any source whatsoever", it added. The Desk then went through Sanjjanaa's Instagram account and found the same photo as shared in the viral social posts, which shows the actress with her husband, Aziz Pasha, a physician, and their child. Here is the link to the May 23 Instagram post , and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that the actress had shared several other posts with her child on her Instagram page. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Sanjjanaa Gilrani had converted to Islam in 2018, whereas 'The Kerala Story' was released earlier this year.

title: PTI Fact Check: Man dancing in viral video is not Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah; Edited video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 29 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of two clips claiming the newly-elected Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah consuming champagne and dancing purportedly in an inebriated state. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the first clip appeared to be authentic. However, the man dancing was not Siddaramaiah but a farmer from Mysuru in the second video. The claim in the second video shared on social media was false. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 19 a video – a combination of two clips – where the first one showed Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah consuming champagne, followed by the second one where he is allegedly seen dancing in an inebriated state. The two parts were conjoined by a slide that read "a few moments later…", which implied that the second event was followed by the first. "Real face of #Siddaramaiah," read the post, which has garnered 666 reactions. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk separately investigated both clips, and here is what we found: Investigation - Clip 1 In the first part of the video, Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah is allegedly seen taking a sip of champagne, seemingly at a party. The Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the clip, providing keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a YouTube video uploaded on August 3, 2022, from the channel of NewsFirst Kannada, which has over 2.81 million subscribers. "Siddaramaiah Birthday : ಶಾಂಪೇನ್ ಕುಡಿದು Siddaramaiah ಬರ್ತ್ಡೇ ಸೆಲಬ್ರೇಟ್ | Siddaramotsava | NewsFirst," read the title of the YouTube video, which has over 19,000 views. Here is the link to a video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that stills from the video uploaded by NewsFirst Kannada were visually similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing them: Taking a cue from the YouTube video's title, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Siddaramaiah Birthday 2022", which led to another YouTube video uploaded on August 3, 2022, from the channel National TV, which has 6.58 lakh subscribers. "Siddaramaiah drinking beer : ಖುಷಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕುಡಿದು ತೇಲಾಡಿದ ಸಿದ್ದು | party cheers | NationalTV," read the title of the video. Here is the link to the video , and below is its screenshot: In the video uploaded by National TV, the same video of Siddaramaiah appeared to take a sip of champagne was seen playing on a loop. It was also confirmed through a Google search that the Karnataka CM's birthday falls on Aug 3, the same day that both YouTube videos were uploaded. The Desk subsequently concluded that the first clip appeared to be true. Clip 2 In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the second clip, which allegedly shows Siddaramaiah dancing in an inebriated state. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a video report published by Bangalore Mirror on March 14, 2018. "'Dancing CM' is a farmer from Mysuru," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that the steps of the dancer seen in the video carried in the news report are identical to the viral video, and their attire is also the same. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the one carried in the report: "A video of a person resembling Chief Minister Siddaramaiah dancing to the tunes of 'Alladsu Alladsu' from the movie 'Chowka' had gone viral recently," read the report, while adding, "While social media attributed this video to the Chief Minister, the fact remains that it was not the CM but a 55-year-old far Chanmaayi Gowda from Mysuru, who was dancing at a cultural programme." The search also led to a report published by Deccan Chronicle on March 15, 2018, with the headline "Is it Siddaramaiah dancing in this video? No, it's a farmer from T Narsipur!." Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that the photo carried in Deccan Chronicle's report is identical to stills from the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing them: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keyword "Siddharamaiah lookalike dancing, " leading to multiple other news reports about the viral video. One such report by the Times of India can be read here. The Desk subsequently concluded that the man seen dancing in the second part of the video was not Siddaramaiah but a farmer from Mysuru.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of students preparing for cultural programme in UP's Baghpat shared with false communal spin; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, May 31 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A Facebook user shared a video which showed a group of girl students kneeling and bowing their heads in front of their teacher inside a classroom. The user claimed Hindu girls were taught to offer namaz at Uttar Pradesh's Baghpat school. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the students were rehearsing for a school play. The video shared on social media posts was false. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 28 a video which showed a group of girl students kneeling and bowing their heads in front of their teacher inside a classroom. The user claimed the footage was from a school in UP's Baghpat, where Hindu girls were taught how to offer namaz. The user also tagged UP CM Yogi Adityanath and the state police in the post. "विडीओ उत्तर प्रदेश के बागपत के एक स्कूल की बताई जा रही है ॥ स्कूल में हिंदू लड़कियों को नमाज़ की ट्रेनिंग देती यह महिला शिक्षिका ॥ इस मामले को बिल्कुल भी हल्के में ना लें बागपत के हिंदू परिवार ॥ आपकी हिंदू बेटी को भविष्य की आयशा ॥ सानिया बनाने की तैयारी है ॥ हिंदुओं से अनुरोध इस मुद्दे को हल्के में ना लेते हुए बड़े स्तर शेयर करें ॥ बागपत पुलिस कृपया बताएँ मामला के बारे में ॥ Pro SP Baghpat Baghpat Police MYogiAdityanath UP Police," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "It is being said that the video is from a school in Baghpat in Uttar Pradesh. This lady teacher trained Hindu girls to do Namaz in school. Baghpat's Hindu family do not take this matter lightly. They are preparing to make your Hindu daughter future Aisha ॥ Sania ॥ Request to Hindus not to take this issue lightly and share it largely. Baghpat police, please tell about the case ॥ Pro SP Baghpat Baghpat Police MYogiAdityanath UP Police," read the English translation of the post, which has garnered five likes so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a news report published by ABP Live on May 28. "Baghpat News: छात्राओं को नमाज पढ़ाती मुस्लिम टीचर का वीडियो वायरल, हिंदू संगठनों ने की कार्रवाई की मांग," read the headline of the report, which is originally in Hindi. "Video of Muslim teacher teaching Namaz to girl students goes viral, Hindu organisations demand action," read the English translation of the headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that the photo carried in the news report was visually identical to stills from the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the photo taken in the information: According to the report, the video was shot in October last year at Hoshiyari Devi Girls Inter College, Rathore, under the Chhaprauli Police Station area of Baghpat district. "The school management says that this video is from the rehearsal of a play during October last year in which Salma, a teacher, was making the students practice namaz, which was part of the play," read the English translation of the report's summary. The search also led to a news report published by Amar Ujala on May 29. "Baghpat News: छात्राओं को नमाज पढ़ाते हुए वीडियो सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल, जांच के बाद सामने आई सच्चाई," read the headline of the report, which is originally in Hindi. "Baghpat News: Video of Namaz being taught to girl students goes viral on social media, the truth came out after investigation," read the English translation of the headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The report quoted the principal of Hoshiyari Devi Girls Inter College confirming that the video was from the rehearsal of a school play while adding that the portion in which the students offered namaz was not shown in the final stretch. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keywords "Baghpat School namaz incident", which led to a Twitter post from May 28, where the photo of a press note had been shared from the verified account of Baghpat Police. "थाना छपरौली क्षेत्रान्तर्गत विद्यालय की मीडिया पर वायरल वीडियो के संबंध में- #UPPolice @uppolice @UPPViralCheck," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "About the viral video of the school under Chhaprauli police station," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: "अवगत कराना है कि थाना छपरौली क्षेत्रान्तर्गत गांव रठौडा स्थित होश्यारी देवी गर्ल्स इण्टर कॉलेज की सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल वीडियो की जांच थाना छपरौली पुलिस द्वारा की गई तो पाया कि पूर्व में विद्यालय में सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रम की तैयारी चल रही थी," read a portion of the press note shared by Baghpat Police. "We want to pass on the information that Chhaprauli police investigated the viral video from Hoshiyari Devi Girls Inter College, Rathore, and found that preparations for a cultural programme were underway," read the English translation of the text above. The Desk subsequently concluded that a video from preparations for a school play had been shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photos falsely connected to PM Modi's May 31 rally in Ajmer
content: New Delhi, May 31 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared two photos – one of a signboard that read "Modi no entry" and another of graffiti on a road that read "Go Back, Modi". They claimed that these photos were recent and from Rajasthan. Both images were shared on May 31, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a rally in Rajasthan's Ajmer. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that old and unrelated photos from Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal were falsely connected to PM Modi's rally in the state, scheduled to go to polls later this year. The Desk investigated both photos separately, and here's what we found: Claim 1 A Twitter user shared on May 31 a photo of a signboard that read "Modi No Entry", along with a picture of PM Modi. The signboard also carried hashtags such as #ModiIsAMistake and #NoMoreModi. "ये राजस्थान है, गुजरात समझें थे क्या #modi_Go_back #मोदी_वापस_भागो," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "This is Rajasthan. Did you think it was Gujarat? #modi_Go_back Modi #Modi run back," read the English translation of the post, which has garnered over 1.88 lakh views and 2,230 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 1 The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo, which led to a report published by News18 on February 10, 2019. "Security Tightened in Andhra as Assam-Style Protests Threaten Modi's Visit Today," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: "As PM Narendra Modi gears up to visit Andhra Pradesh for the first visit after the ruling TDP severed its ties with the BJP, posters slamming the prime minister have come up on streets," read the report. In News18's report, the photo of the same signboard shared in the viral post was carried. Below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one carried in the report: The search also led to a report published by the Economic Times on Feb 10, 2019, where the same viral photo of the signboard had been carried. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk subsequently concluded that a four-year-old photo from Andhra Pradesh had been falsely connected to PM Modi's rally in Rajasthan and shared recently on social media. Claim 2 A Twitter user shared on May 31 a photo of graffiti on a road which read "Go back Modi" and claimed that it was from Rajasthan's Ajmer, where PM Modi addressed a rally on the same day. "अजमेर की धरा पे कुछ इस तरह स्वागत की झलकियां - धन्यवाद अजमेर 🇮🇳 #modi_Go_back #मोदी_वापस_भागो," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Glimpses of welcome on the land of Ajmer like this - Thank you Ajmer #modi_Go_back #Modi run back," read the English translation of the post, which has over 1.56 lakh views and 1,500 retweets so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation 2 The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to a Twitter post from May 31, where the same photo had been shared with a similar claim. "ओ राजस्थान है प्रधान अटे जुमला कोनी चाले #modi_Go_back #मोदी_वापस_भागो," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "This is Rajasthan Prime (Minister), jumlas won't work here #modi_Go_back #Modi run back", read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a news report from the Bengali media house Ei Samay on January 12, 2020. "শহরে মিছিলে অসমিয়া পড়ুয়া, লন্ডনের গবেষক," read the headline of the report, which is originally in Bengali. "Assamese students marching in the city, researchers from London," read the headline's English translation. Here is the link to the report , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that the photo carried by Ei Somoy in its report is visually identical to the viral photo. "Go-back Modi slogan written in front of Metro channel," read the English translation of the photo's caption. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one carried in the news report: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Kolkata Modi go back", which led to a Twitter post from January 11, 2020, where four photos were carried. "Esplanade now. Students are painting on the road—a loud and clear message from Kolkata. #GoBackModiFromBengal Coward Modi is afraid of the students & youth. Avoids road. Protest continuing all over the city," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that one of the four photos in the post was visually identical to the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one carried in the Twitter post: The Desk also noticed that the board on the building in the viral photo read "Metro Channel Control Post Hare Street Police Station". By conducting a Google search, we found that Hare Street Police Station is part of Kolkata's Central Division. The Desk subsequently concluded that a three-year-old photo from West Bengal had been recently shared on social media with the false claim that it was connected to PM Modi's rally in Rajasthan's Ajmer on May 31.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Afghanistan cricketer Naveen-Ul-Haq didn't issue apology to Virat Kohli after IPL spat; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 1 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of Afghanistan cricketer Naveen-Ul-Haq addressing a press conference and claimed that he had apologised to Virat Kohli following a spat in the recently concluded Indian Premier League tournament. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim false, as Haq did not offer any apology to the Indian cricketer. Naveen-Ul- Haq, who played for Lucknow Super Giants', and Royal Challengers Bangalore's Virat Kohli, were involved in a heated argument when the two teams faced each other on May 1 in the tournament. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 25 a photo of cricketer Naveen-Ul-Haq addressing a press conference and claimed that he had apologised to Virat Kohli following a spat in the IPL clash between Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) and Royal Challengers Bangalore (RCB) on May 1. "Naveen-ul-Haq said, 'My sincere apologies to Virat Kohli, Sir. He's the Brand of Cricket, and I'm not even dust off his Foot'," read the post, which has garnered over 50 reactions. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to a May 25 tweet sharing the same image with an identical claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a video posted on IPL's official website on May 24, which showed Haq addressing a press conference. "It was a good season for me; I have learnt quite a few things from this IPL: Naveen-ul-Haq," read the video title. Here is the link to the video , and below is its screenshot: The Desk noticed that stills from the video posted on IPL's official website were visually identical to the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing them: The Desk went through the two-minute six-second video but found that Haq had not apologised to Kohli at the press conference. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Naveen-ul-Haq Virat Kohli apology", which led to a news report published by News 18 on May 27. "Naveen-ul-Haq Reacts to Viral 'Sorry Virat Kohli' Tweet, Urges Fans to Report 'Fake Account'," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the report published by News18. Below is the screenshot of the same. "More recently, a tweet from a 'fake account' went viral from the account named '@naveenulhaq66'. The tweet read, "I'm sorry Virat Kohli, sir," and the tweet went crazy viral in no time, garnering more than 25000 likes," read a portion of the report published by News18. The report carried a screenshot of a purported Tweet shared by a fake account, "Naveen Ul Haq", which read ", I'm sorry @imVkohli sir". Below is a screenshot of the same: In the same report, a screenshot of an Instagram story posted from Haq's verified account was carried out, out of which Haq confirmed that the statement mentioned above was fake. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk concluded that Haq did not apologise to Kohli following a verbal spat during an IPL match. The claim made in the social media post was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Post claiming Arvind Kejriwal his decision to resign as Delhi CM to support wrestlers' protest is false; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, June 1 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of Arvind Kejriwal alongside women wrestlers Sakshi Malik, Vinesh Phogat and Sangeeta Phogat and claimed that he decided to resign as Delhi CM in solidarity with the protesting wrestlers. The user further claimed that Kejriwal had said he would leave the country if the government didn't accept the demands of the wrestlers. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that Kejriwal did not make any such statement. The statement was tweeted by a parody Twitter handle of the Aam Aadmi Party Rajasthan. The social media post was shared with a false claim. Several top wrestlers of the country have been protesting against WFI President Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, demanding his arrest on charges of sexual harassment of some women athletes. Several political leaders, including Kejriwal, supported the wrestlers and visited Jantar Mantar, where the protesters camped from April 23 till May 28, when Delhi Police cleared the site. Claim Delhi BJP leader Krishnan Gahlot shared a photo of Arvind Kejriwal standing alongside women wrestlers Sakshi Malik, Vinesh Phogat and Sangeeta Phogat and claimed that he had announced to resign as Delhi CM in solidarity with the protesting wrestlers. The user further claimed that Kejriwal had announced they to leave the country if the government didn't accept the demands of the protesting wrestlers. "Breaking पहलवानों के समर्थन में केजरीवाल देंगे दिल्ली के CM पद से इस्तीफा। फिर भी अगर सरकार नहीं मानी तो देश छोड़ कर भी जा सकते है। #BREAKING #AAP," read the May 30 post, which has garnered over 1 million views and 24,000 likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by conducting a Google search to check whether Kejriwal had made any such statement announcing his resignation in support of the protesting wrestlers. However, we could not find any news report backing the claim made in the social media post. The search, however, led the Desk to a report by PTI News published on April 29. "They must get justice: Kejriwal extends support to protesting wrestlers," read the report's headline. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Extending support to the protesting wrestlers, Kejriwal said those who commit such wrongs against women "should be hanged"," read a portion of the report. It also mentioned Kejriwal urging people from all over the country to join Jantar Mantar to support the wrestlers. However, nowhere in the entire report could we find any mention of Kejriwal making any such announcement as claimed in the social media posts. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search on the keyword "Arvind Kejriwal announces resignation to support wrestlers' protest". The search results led to a Twitter post carrying the same photo with an identical claim. Here is the link and archive link to the May 30 post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed the handle's name read: "AAP Rajasthan | Mission 2023 | Seats 150 - Parody". The bio of the Twitter account read: "Parody Account of AAP Rajasthan | Not affiliated with any Political Party | All tweets are Satire | Just for Fun | Fan of Arvind Kejariwal". In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk scanned their Twitter handle of Kejriwal to look for any posts from the day he visited Jantar Mantar. We found a live broadcast post from the event where Kejriwal delivered a speech supporting the wrestlers at Jantar Mantar. The Desk went through the entire 8:40-minute address, in which the Delhi CM targeted the central government for turning a blind eye towards the protesting wrestlers and charged that the accused – WFI President Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh – was being shielded. However, we did not find Kejriwal mentioning his resignation as the Delhi CM. Here is the link to the broadcasted video post , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a couple of other tweets by Kejriwal on the same day, supporting the protesting wrestlers. They can be seen here and here . Here too, Kejriwal did not make any announcement of him stepping down from the post of Delhi CM or leaving the country in solidarity with the wrestlers. The also Desk reached out to the social media cell of the Aam Aadmi Party via email to cross-check the veracity of the viral claim. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Kejriwal did announce to step down as Delhi CM in solidarity with the protesting wrestlers. Also, the false claims seemed to have been amplified by a post made by a parody Twitter account of AAP Rajasthan.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 photo of massive crowd in Ethiopian event falsely linked to 2023 IPL finals; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, June 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a massive crowd, claiming that it showed Chennai Super Kings fans at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad during the Indian Premier League finals. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a six-year-old photo from an event held in Ethiopia had been falsely linked to the 2023 IPL finals and shared on social media with a false claim. Chennai Super Kings faced Gujarat Titans in the finals of IPL 2023 on May 29, where the former won by five wickets, thereby bagging the title for a record fifth time. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo on May 28 of a massive crowd, claiming that it showed Chennai Super Kings fans at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad during the Indian Premier League finals. "Chennai Super Kings fans are crazy on a whole new level at Ahmedabad. #CSKvGT #IPL2023Final," read the post, which has garnered over 1.8 million views and 1,800 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to a tweet from May 28 where the same photo had been shared with an identical claim. "Believe me, This isn't chepauk,This is out Narendra Modi (Stadium sign) We are massive #CSKvGT | #IPLFinals," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a report published by CNN Travel on August 4, 2017. "Ethiopia is the hot new place in Africa – here's why," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Multiple photos had been carried in the report and the Desk noticed that one of them is visually identical to the viral photo. Below is a screenshot of the same: "The annual Great Ethiopian Run in Addis Ababa is popular among tourists," read the caption of the photo in the report. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one carried in the report: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Great Ethiopian Run Addis Ababa", which led to the United Nation's MDG Achievement Fund website where the same photo had been posted. "Haile Gebreselassie kicks off the Great Ethiopian Run under the slogan "We Can End Poverty by 2015," read the title of the photo. Here is the link to the photo shared on the website and below is its screenshot: The Desk subsequently concluded that a six-year-old photo from an unrelated event had been falsely connected to IPL 2023 finals.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, the protestor in this photo is not Sakshi Malik; 2021 photo from farmers' protest falsely linked to wrestlers' protest
content: New Delhi, June 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo purportedly showing a cop pinning down a protester by stepping on his face and linked the photo with the recent protests of the wrestlers against WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. The post claimed that the protester in the photo was wrestler Sakshi Malik. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a two-year-old photo from the farmers' protest against the Farmers Bill 2020. The photo from two-year-old protests was shared on social media with a false claim. Wrestlers Sakshi Malik, Vinesh Phogat, Sangeeta Phogat and Bajrang Punia, who are protesting against WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, were booked for rioting on May 29, a day after an alleged scuffle with the Delhi Police over the wrestlers' march to the new Parliament building. Thousands of farmers had convened to carry out a year-long agitation against the central government's now-repealed farm laws in 2020. Claim A Twitter user shared on May 29 a photo that purportedly showed the police pinning down wrestler Sakshi Malik by stepping on her face. "This is @SakshiMalik who won the first Olympic medal in women's wrestling for the country. Such a picture was not seen even in Taliban Is the country's land alive or dead or has it been sold!! #WrestlersProtest @BhimArmyChief @VinayRatanSingh," read the post, which has garnered over 2,300 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to a tweet from May 29, where the same viral photo and claim had been shared. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a report published by the Times of India on February 1, 2021. "Farmers' protest: Man under boot now image of cop aggression," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the photo carried by Times of India is visually identical to the viral photo. "Delhi Police accused Ranjit of attacking a SHO with his sword," read the caption of the photo carried by TOI. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one carried in the news report: "Photograph of 22-year-old Ranjit Singh's face crushed under a cop's boot has become the face of mob attack on the farmers' protest at Singhu border," stated the report, while adding, "Videos and the image of a cop crushing his face showing Ranjit being dragged by police and then police personnel thrashing him with lathis have also gone viral". In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a cutomised Google search with the keyword "Farmers' protest Ranjit Singh", which led to a daily blog published by Deccan Herald on Jan 29, 2021. "Farmers' protest news updates: Delhi Police asks nine farmer leaders to join investigation over R-day violence," read the blog's headline. Here is the link to the blog and below is a screenshot: In the blog, the same viral photo had been carried and credited to PTI. Below is a screenshot of the same: "Police pin down a farmer, who allegedly attacked Police SHO (Alipur) Pradeep Paliwal, during clashes between people claiming to be local villagers and farmers at the Singhu Border. Credit: PTI Photo," read the description of the photo. The Desk subsequently concluded that a two-year-old PTI photo related to farmers' protest had been falsely linked to the ongoing wrestlers' protest.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally-altered photo of Yogi Adityanath bowing before Tipu Sultan's portrait shared as real on social media
content: New Delhi, June 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath bowing his head before a portrait of Tipu Sultan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally-altered image had been shared as real on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 26 a photo of Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath bowing down before a portrait of Tipu Sultan. "जिनको आज के मुसलमानों से नफरत है वो भी हमारे बुजुर्गों के आगे सर झुकाते है," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Those who hate today's Muslims also bow their heads before our elders," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation by conducting a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral photo, which led to a photo posted from the verified Facebook account of UP CM Yogi Adityanath on June 29, 2021, where he can be seen bowing before a portrait of Dr BR Ambedkar. Former President of India Ram Nath Kovind can also be seen in the photo. "आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी की प्रेरणा व मार्गदर्शन में बाबा साहेब की स्मृतियों को जीवंत बनाए रखने के लिए पंचतीर्थ की स्थापना हुई। भारत के अलावा इंग्लैंड में बना बाबा साहेब का भव्य स्मारक उनकी स्मृतियों व भारत की आवाज को वैश्विक स्तर पर पहुंचाने का एक माध्यम है। आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री Narendra Modi जी की प्रेरणा से आकार ले रहा 'भारत रत्न डॉ. भीमराव आंबेडकर स्मारक एवं सांस्कृतिक केंद्र' बाबा साहेब डॉ. भीमराव आंबेडकर जी की स्मृतियों को संरक्षित करेगा।," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "Panchtirth was established to keep the memories of Baba Saheb alive under the inspiration and guidance of respected Prime Minister. Apart from India, the grand monument of Baba Saheb made in England is a means to bring his memories and the voice of India globally. Bharat Ratna Dr. taking shape with the inspiration of respected Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial and Cultural Center Baba Saheb Dr. Bhimrao will preserve the memories of Ambedkar," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the setting of the viral photo was visually identical to the one posted on Facebook by UP CM Yogi Adityanath. Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one posted on Facebook: The search also led to an almost identical photo on stock image website Alamy in which Yogi Adityanath can be seen bowing before a portrait of Dr BR Ambedkar. Former President Ram Nath Kovind can be seen in this photo as well. "Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath pays floral tribute to Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar during the foundation stone for Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial and Cultural Centre in the presence of Governor of Uttar Pradesh Anandi Ben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, at Lok Bhawan, on June 29, 2021 in Lucknow, India," read the caption of the photo. Here is the link to the photo and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keywords "Yogi Adityanath Ram Nath Kovind BR Ambedkar portrait", which led to a YouTube video posted on June 29, 2021, from the President of India's verified account, which has 2.57 million subscribers. "President Kovind lays foundation stone of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial & Cultural Centre at Lucknow," read the title of the video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: At the 1:44 timestamp of the video, Yogi Adityanath can be seen bowing before the portrait of Dr BR Ambedkar. Below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral photo to the one posted on YouTube: The Desk subsequently concluded that a digitally-altered image had been shared as real on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: ISKCON Temple near Odisha train crash site falsely labelled as mosque; Social media posts shares with false communal spin
content: New Delhi, June 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of the aerial view of the accident site where the recent triple train crash occurred in Odisha's Balasore on June 2. The user pointed to a structure near the railway tracks, claiming it was a mosque, insinuating that a particular community was responsible for the tragedy. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the structure in the photo was an ISKCON temple and not a mosque. The social media post was shared with a false communal spin. The crash involving Bengaluru-Howrah Superfast Express and Shalimar-Chennai Central Coromandel Express, carrying around 2,500 passengers, and goods train in Odisha's Balasore on Friday left 275 people dead and over 1,100 injured. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 3 an aerial view image of the accident site where the recent train crash took place in Odisha's Balasore and pointed out at a nearby structure, claiming it was a mosque. "ट्रेन हादसा शुक्रवार को हुआ है और हादसे की जगह एक बड़ी मस्जिद है. बाकी आप समझदार हैं #उड़ीसा_ट्रेन_हादसा," read the post. An English translation of the post read: "The train accident happened on Friday, and there is a big mosque at the accident site. Rest you are sensible #Orissa_train_accident." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the viral social media post. The search results led the Desk to another Facebook post, carrying the same picture with an identical claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted one of the PTI correspondents in Odisha, who covered the tragic train crash. He confirmed that the structure highlighted in the photo was the Bahanaga ISKCON temple, not a mosque. "The under-construction structure seen in the photo is the ISKCON temple and not a mosque," said Mohammed Sufian, Special Correspondent at PTI. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "ISKCON Temple Bahanaga Odisha". The search results led to a five-month-old YouTube video which showed that the structure was white and under construction. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a separate Google search with the keyword "ISKCON Temple Bahanaga". It came across another long-shot image of the accident site carried by Reuters in its report. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: This image showed a structure similar to the one shared in the social media post. Below is a combination image comparing both photos: A closer look at the photo shared by Reuters showed that the structure looked more like a temple than the traditional shikhara and not a mosque. The Desk then looked up the temple on Google Maps and found it near the railway tracks of Bahanaga Bazar, where the accident occurred on June 2. Google Maps confirmed that the temple was located near the railway tracks, as seen in the viral photo and the one carried by Reuters in its report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned through the latest news reports on the triple train crash to learn about the developments related to the cause of the accident. As per a June 5 PTI report by Times of India, the CBI took over the probe into the triple train crash and visited the accident site. The Railway Board recommended the CBI probe on Sunday. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across another PTI report on the incident published on June 5. The report headline read: "CBI all set to take over the probe into Balasore train accident case". "Railway officials have indicated that possible "sabotage" and tampering with the electronic interlocking system, which detects the presence of trains, led to the Friday accident," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media posts were shared with false claims as neither the structure seen in the photo was a mosque, nor there have been any established findings by the investigative agencies on any conspiracy behind the accident, as insinuated in the social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: ISKCON Temple near Odisha train crash site falsely labelled as mosque; Social media posts shares with false communal spin
