The user pointed to a structure near the railway tracks, claiming it was a mosque, insinuating that a particular community was responsible for the tragedy. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the structure in the photo was an ISKCON temple and not a mosque. The social media post was shared with a false communal spin. The crash involving Bengaluru-Howrah Superfast Express and Shalimar-Chennai Central Coromandel Express, carrying around 2,500 passengers, and goods train in Odisha's Balasore on Friday left 275 people dead and over 1,100 injured. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 3 an aerial view image of the accident site where the recent train crash took place in Odisha's Balasore and pointed out at a nearby structure, claiming it was a mosque. "ट्रेन हादसा शुक्रवार को हुआ है और हादसे की जगह एक बड़ी मस्जिद है. बाकी आप समझदार हैं #उड़ीसा_ट्रेन_हादसा," read the post. An English translation of the post read: "The train accident happened on Friday, and there is a big mosque at the accident site. Rest you are sensible #Orissa_train_accident." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the viral social media post. The search results led the Desk to another Facebook post, carrying the same picture with an identical claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted one of the PTI correspondents in Odisha, who covered the tragic train crash. He confirmed that the structure highlighted in the photo was the Bahanaga ISKCON temple, not a mosque. "The under-construction structure seen in the photo is the ISKCON temple and not a mosque," said Mohammed Sufian, Special Correspondent at PTI. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "ISKCON Temple Bahanaga Odisha". The search results led to a five-month-old YouTube video which showed that the structure was white and under construction. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a separate Google search with the keyword "ISKCON Temple Bahanaga". It came across another long-shot image of the accident site carried by Reuters in its report. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: This image showed a structure similar to the one shared in the social media post. Below is a combination image comparing both photos: A closer look at the photo shared by Reuters showed that the structure looked more like a temple than the traditional shikhara and not a mosque. The Desk then looked up the temple on Google Maps and found it near the railway tracks of Bahanaga Bazar, where the accident occurred on June 2. Google Maps confirmed that the temple was located near the railway tracks, as seen in the viral photo and the one carried by Reuters in its report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned through the latest news reports on the triple train crash to learn about the developments related to the cause of the accident. As per a June 5 PTI report by Times of India, the CBI took over the probe into the triple train crash and visited the accident site. The Railway Board recommended the CBI probe on Sunday. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across another PTI report on the incident published on June 5. The report headline read: "CBI all set to take over the probe into Balasore train accident case". "Railway officials have indicated that possible "sabotage" and tampering with the electronic interlocking system, which detects the presence of trains, led to the Friday accident," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media posts were shared with false claims as neither the structure seen in the photo was a mosque, nor there have been any established findings by the investigative agencies on any conspiracy behind the accident, as insinuated in the social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson didn't choose to follow Sanatana Dharma, AI-generated photo shared with false claims
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of renowned Hollywood actor Dwayne Johnson, also known as 'The Rock', donning a Hindu priest attire along with the text on the photo, which claimed that the Hollywood actor had chosen to follow and embrace Sanatana Dharma. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the images shared on social media of Dwayne Johnson donning a Hindu priest attire were AI generated. The claim shared by the users was false. Claim A Twitter user on May 28 shared a photo of Hollywood actor Dwayne Johnson, also known as 'The Rock', seen donning a Hindu priest attire along with the text on the photo claiming that the Hollywood actor has accepted Sanatana Dharma. "Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, the iconic WWE legend and beloved Hollywood actor, has chosen to follow and embrace Sanatana Dharma," read the text on the photo which has garnered 69 thousand views and 12 retweets. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo, which led to a Facebook post shared by a user on April 22. The Facebook post carried three other photos of Johnson donning a Hindu priest attire. While sharing the post, the user had mentioned in the caption that it was an 'AI Concept Art'. "dwayne johnson as a Sadhu worshipping in mandir @therock how is it ? AI concept Art," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the Facebook post and below is the screenshot of the same. On scanning through the comment section of the post, the Desk also noticed that the user confirmed the use of AI while replying to one of the comments. Below is the screenshot of the user confirming the use of the AI tool: On further scanning through the user's profile, we found that the user had posted more such AI-generated photos on the page. Below is a screenshot of the page: The user on May 28 also shared screenshots of a few posts by other users that carried images of Dwayne Johnson donning in Hindu attire and wrote, "My artwork becoming viral on social media... yeah," Here is the link to the post and below is the screenshot of his post. Taking cue from the caption on the Facebook post, the Desk searched for photos of Dwayne Johnson in priest attire on the Discord channel of the AI-image generation tool of MidJourney. Though the Desk did not find the identical photos of Hollywood actor Dwayne Johnson in Hindu Priest attire, we were able to find images similar to the viral photo. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk further scanned the viral photo using the 'Hugging Face' website (a website that scans images to determine if they are AI Generated). The results of the viral photo confirmed that the viral photo is AI generated by giving a score of 94%. Below is the screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the images shared by the Twitter user were AI-generated.

title: PTI Fact Check: Claim of Bahanaga Bazar station master belonging to minority community and absconding after triple train crash is false and baseless
content: New Delhi, June 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo claiming that he was station master at Bahanaga Bazar Railway Station in Odisha's Balasore, where the triple train crash took place on June 2, who was a Muslim and absconding since the accident happened. The user also claimed that also claimed that the train crash had claimed over 300 lives. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the station master at Bahanaga Bazar railway station was neither a Muslim, nor he was absconding. The social media post was shared with a false communal spin. At least 289 people died in the triple train crash involving three trains – two passenger and a goods train – at the Bahanaga Bazar railway station in Odisha's Balasore on June 2. Claim A Twitter user shared a photo of a man inside a railway station control room and claimed he was the station master at Bahanaga Bazar railway station in Odisha's Balasore, where the triple train crash took place on June 2. The user claimed he was a Muslim who was absconding after the accident. It was also claimed that the crash involving two passenger and a goods trains had claimed over 300 lives. "अभी तक 300 से ज्यादा को मौत की नींद सुलाने वाला और 900 से ज्यादा को गंभीर घायल करने वाला उड़ीसा का ट्रेन एक्सीडेंट जिस स्टेशन पर हुआ उसका नाम है बहानागा स्टेशन*इस स्टेशन के स्टेशन मास्टर का नाम है *मोहम्मद शरीफ अहमद*एक्सीडेंट की जाँच के आदेश के बाद फ़रार है," read the June 5 post, which has garnered 1.2 million views so far. An English translation of the post read: "The name of the station master at the railway station, where the Odisha train accident took place – in which over 300 people were killed and more 900 were injured – is Mohammad Sharif Ahmad. He is absconding since an investigation was ordered into the accident." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Twitter post. The search results led to a Facebook post, carrying the same photo with an identical claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk the conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Bahanaga Station Master, Odish train accident". The search results led us to a video news report by India Today, which identified the station master as one SB Mohanty. According to the report, Mohanty had been shunted following the train crash. It further quoted the current station master saying that Mohanty was not guilty for the crash that happened on June 2. Here is the link to the June 5 video report and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results further led to another report by Odisha Bhaskar, published on June 5. The headline of the report read: "Odisha Train Tragedy: Bahanaga Station Master Grilled By Railway Safety Commissioner Team". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The Railway Safety Commissioner team is currently interrogating the Bahanga Bazar Station Master SB Mohanty over the Coromandel train accident near the Bahanaga station of Balasore district. According to reports, the Station Master SB Mohanty is being interrogated about the status of the signal," read a portion of the report. In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted South-Eastern CPRO Aditya Kumar Choudhary, who confirmed that neither the station master at Bahanaga Bazar Railway Station, at the time of the accident, was a Muslim, nor he was absconding. "The station master's name is PS Mohanty, and not Mohammad Sharif Ahmad. No one in the region's railway division goes by this name. Also, Mohanty is not absconding, he joined the investigation as it started," Choudhary told PTI. The Desk then conducted a Google search to get the latest death toll figures on the Odisha train accident and came across a tweet shared by PTI on June 13. "Toll in Odisha triple train accident increases to 289 after an injured passenger succumbs to injuries: Officials," read the tweet. Here is the link to the Twitter post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that neither the station master, deputed at Bahanaga Bazar railway station at the time of Odisha train crash on June 2, was a Muslim nor he was absconding. The social media post also exaggerated the death figures in the mishap. The Desk tried to find more on the man in the photo shared in the social media posts. The earliest origin could be traced back to a blog titled "Kottavalasa Kirandul KK Line". In the blog, the author detailed about his visit to the Kottavalasa Kirandul KK line in March 2004. However, we could not find any more information on the photo.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photos falsely linked to recent police action on protesting farmers in Haryana; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, June 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Wrestler Sakshi Malik shared on Twitter three photos of injuries suffered by men and claimed that they were farmers beaten up by the police for protesting for minimum support price (MSP) for their crops. She also claimed that a farmer had died in the police action on the protesters. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that two of the photos dated back to 2019 and 2021 from unrelated incidents. Furthermore, the claim of a protesting farmer's death was also false. A large number of farmers led by Bharatiya Kisan Union (Charuni) chief Gurnam Singh Charuni blocked the Delhi-Chandigarh national highway near Kurukshetra on Tuesday (June 6) demanding that the government procure sunflower seeds at the MSP. Police used water cannons and resorted to lathicharge to disperse the protesters. Nine BKU (Charuni) leaders, including Charuni, were arrested. Claim Wrestlers Sakshi Malik on June 7 tweeted three photos claiming they showed farmers injured in police action against their protest demanding MSP for their crops in Haryana. She also claimed that a farmer died in the police action against protesters. "किसानों ने सिर्फ़ अपनी फसलों की एमएसपी माँगी थी. लेकिन क्रूर तंत्र ने उन्हें लाठियाँ और गिरफ़्तारियाँ दीं. किसान नेता गुरनाम सिंह चढूनी की गिरफ़्तारी की हम निंदा करते हैं, उनकी जल्द रिहाई हो. आंदोलन में शहीद हुए किसान की खबर ने आँखें नम कर दी हैं," read the June 7 post, which has garnered 2 million views and 31,000 likes so far. An English translation of the post read: "The farmers only asked for MSP for their crops. But the cruel system gave them lathis and arrests. We condemn the arrest of farmer leader Gurnam Singh Chadhuni, he should be released soon. The news of the martyred farmer in the movement has brought tears to his eyes." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media and came across a Twitter post by Aam Aadmi Party leader Sanjay Singh, who tweeted same two of the three photos which were shared by Sakshi Malik in her Twitter post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the first image that showed injuries, purportedly of lathicharge, on the back of a Sikh man. The search results led us to a Facebook post, shared by a page named Haryana Times on June 17, 2019, which carried the same photo as shared in the post by Sakshi Malik and Sanjay Singh. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the two photos – one shared on social media recently and the other dating back to 2019. Taking a cue from the Facebook post, the Desk conducted a Google search with the keyword "Sikh man beaten by Delhi Police, June 2019". The search results further led to a Twitter post by one Ankit Lal, shared on June 17, 2019. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "These injury marks on the body of Gramin Seva driver beaten by @DelhiPolice clearly show how the lawmakers broke laws in broad daylight in the National capital. @JarnailSinghAAP visited the victims in hospital and also went to Mukherjee Nagar P.S. to talk to the police officers," read the post. The search results further led to a PTI report on the incident, carried by NDTV on July 25, 2019. The headline of the report read: "2 Cops Dismissed After Probe In Delhi's Mukherjee Nagar Incident". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The incident was related to a scuffle that broke out between a commercial vehicle driver and cops of Delhi after the latter grazed past a police van. The cops reportedly thrashed the driver and his son, who had threatened them with a sword. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old photo from an unrelated incident was falsely linked to the recent farmers' protest in Haryana. In the next stage of investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the second photo of a man with a bleeding head shared by Sakshi Malik in her Twitter post. The search results led the Desk to a Twitter post shared by a user on August 29, 2021. The post carried four photos, of which one was visually similar to the photo shared on social media recently. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "#groundreport सिर्फ फ़ोटो गलत शेयर हुई है, लेकिन बाकी जानकारियां सारी सही हैं. यह रविंदर हैं जिनके सर में 7 सेंटीमीटर लंबे घाव को टांको से सिला गया है. 3 किसानों का सर पुलिस ने फोड़ा है," read the post. An English translation of the post read: "#groundreport only the photo has been wrongly shared, but the rest of the information is correct. This is Ravinder whose 7 cm long wound on his head has been stitched. Police attacked three farmers on their heads." Below is a combination image, comparing the two photos – one shared on social media recently and the other shared in 2021 in the Twitter post mentioned above. The Twitter post also carried images of the medical examination report of the injured person who was named as "Mr Ravinder". According to the report, the person with head injury was treated at the Civil Hospital, Karnal on August 28. Below is a combination of images of the alleged medical report: The Desk could not trace the origin of the photo any further, but it was clear that an old and unrelated photo was falsely linked to the recent scuffle between protesting farmers and police in Haryana. The Desk also tried to get details of the third photo – a collage with four photos of men showing their injury marks – but couldn't verify its authenticity or trace its presence elsewhere. In the next part of investigation, the Desk moved to the claim made by Sakshi Malik that a farmer died in the protest in Haryana. On conducting a Google search with relevant keywords, we could not find any report verifying the claim. We came across several media reports on lathicharge on protesting farmers on June 6, but no casualty was reported. Here is the link to a report by India Today on the incident and below is a screenshot of the same: "Farmers blocked the Delhi-Amritsar National Highway in Kurukshetra on Tuesday as they protested against the Haryana government's decision to not buy sunflower seeds at the minimum support price (MSP). The police resorted to using water cannons and lathi-charge to disperse the agitating farmers," read a section of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a false claim of farmer's death during the June 6 scuffle between protesting farmers and police in Haryana was shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Newspaper clipping questioning Rahul Gandhi's lineage is fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo of a newspaper clipping which quoted an American DNA expert Martin Sizo claiming that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was not the son of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the newspaper clipping shared in the post was fake. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo on June 5 of a purported newspaper clipping which read that an American DNA expert Martin Sizo has claimed that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was not the son of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. "अमेरिकी डीएनए विशेषज्ञ का दावा राजीव गांधी के बेटे नही है राहुल," read the headline of the newspaper clipping, which is originally in Hindu, while its body read, "न्यूज़ डेस्क, दिल्ली : अमेरिका में रहने वाले डीएनए विशेषज्ञ डॉक्टर मार्टिन सिज़ो ने एक प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस करके चौंकाने वाला दावा किया है, डॉ मार्टिन का कहना है कि उनके पास राजीव गांधी और राहुल गांधी का DNA है, और दोनों आपस मे मैच नही होता है डॉ मार्टिन ने कहा कि वो भारत आकर सारे सबूत भी देने को तैयार है जिस से साबित भी हो जाएगा कि राहुल राजीव गांधी के बेटे नही है कांग्रेस पार्टी ने डॉ मार्टिन के दावे पर फिलहाल चुप्पी साध ली है कोई भी कांग्रेस नेता इस मामले पर कुछ बोलने को तैयार नही है." "American DNA expert claims Rahul is not Rajiv Gandhi's son," read the English translation of the headline. "America-based DNA expert Dr. Martin Sizo has made a shocking claim in a press conference, Dr. Martin says that he has DNA of Rajiv Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, and both do not match. Dr. Martin said that He is ready to come to India and give all the proofs which will prove that Rahul is not Rajiv Gandhi's son. Congress party has kept silence on Dr. Martin's claim for the time being. No Congress leader is ready to speak anything on this matter," read the English translation of the body. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation by conducting a Google Reverse Image Search on the newspaper clipping, which did not lead to a credible news report to corroborate the claim made in the viral post. Had there been any questions raised on the lineage of a prominent leader like Rahul Gandhi, it would have certainly been reported by all major news organisations. The Desk also conducted a Google search using the keywords "DNA expert Martin Sizo", but there was no mention of a DNA expert Martin Sizo in any credible article or report. The Desk also noticed some glaring punctuation and grammatical errors in the newspaper clipping. Had the report been published by a genuine media organisation, there wouldn't have been such errors in the copy. The same has been highlighted below: The Desk subsequently concluded that the viral newspaper clipping is fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from an Iftar party showing Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah and Deputy CM DK Shivakumar shared as recent with false claims
content: New Delhi, June 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video showing newly elected Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah and Deputy CM DK Shivakumar donning a Muslim attire and having food at an Iftaar party and claimed that they were celebrating their victory in the recently held Karnataka Assembly polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2022 and was being shared as recent with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user on June 7 shared a video showing newly-elected Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah and Deputy CM DK Shivakumar donning a Muslim attire and having food at an Iftaar party and claimed that they were celebrating their victory in the recently held Karnataka Assembly polls. "The CM and Deputy CM of Karnataka are celebrating by wearing new uniforms ...you cannot recognize them …god save Karnataka *Muslims are enjoying the Fruits Of Unity & Solidarity*," read the caption of the post shared by the Facebook user which has garnered over 9 reactions. Here is the link and archive link of the viral post, below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video clip and found several keyframes. A Google Reverse Google Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a Facebook post shared by a user on April 16, 2022 that carrying visuals similar to the viral video. "DAWAT E IFTAR by Former CM Siddaramaiah for peace and prosperity. Zameer Ahmed Khan and team attends. #Siddaramaiah #ZameerAhmedKhan," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post shared by the Facebook user and below is the screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image comparing the viral image to the Facebook post: Taking cue from the Facebook post, the Desk conducted a Custom Google search using the keywords "Siddaramaiah Dawat-e-Iftaar Party 2022", which led to another video shared by New18 Urdu on their YouTube Channel on Apr 16, 2022. The News18 Urdu video also carried similar visuals to the viral video. Here is the link to the video posted on News18 Urdu's YouTube channel. "Karnataka New: Sabiq CM Siddaramaiah Ki Janib Se Iftar Party Ka Ehtemam | News18 Urdu," read the title of the YouTube video posted on News18 Urdu channel. "Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah hosted an Iftar party this year as every year. The party was attended by leaders of all religions and at the same time expressed concern over the current situation in the state," read the description of the video posted on News18 Urdu's YouTube Channel. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared by the Facebook user showing Karnataka newly-elected CM Siddaramaiah and Deputy CM DK Shivakumar was not of them celebrating the Congress' recent poll victory in the state. It dates back to an Iftar party hosted by the then Congress leader Siddaramaiah in 2022.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of shipwreck from USA falsely linked to Cyclone Biparjoy; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a tidal wave capsizing a boat at sea and claimed that it was struck by Cyclone Biparjoy at the Arabian Sea. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of a shipwreck from the USA had been falsely connected to Cyclone Biparjoy. Cyclone Biparjoy's landfall near Jakhau Port in Gujarat's Kutch district took place on the evening of June 15 after churning across the Arabian Sea for over 10 days. Claim A Twitter user shared a video on June 13 of a tidal wave capsizing a boat at sea and claimed that it was struck by Cyclone Biparjoy at the Arabian Sea. "Cyclone #Biparjoy somewhere in #Arabian_sea. #CycloneBiporjoy #Cyclone," read the post, which has garnered over 1.55 lakh views. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search of the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a Twitter post from June 13, where the same viral video had again been linked to Cyclone Biparjoy. "#CycloneBiparjoy | Over 12,000 to be evacuated in Kutch & Dwarka; Western Railway short terminates 56 trains heading to coastal #Gujarat #WATCH | Horrible shipwreck scenes," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The search also led to a BBC video report from February 4, where an extended version of the viral video had been posted. "Giant wave overturns yacht during dramatic US rescue," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the one carried in the report: "A wave overturned a boat in rough seas off the Pacific coast of the US, as the coastguard was attempting to rescue a person on board. The boat was about six miles (10km) from land, at the mouth of the Columbia River in the north-west of the country," read the report. It was also mentioned in the report that the one man on board the ship had been rescued and taken to a hospital. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keywords "shipwreck USA Pacific Coast", which led to a report published by The Guardian on Feb 5 where the same viral video had been carried. "US Coast Guard rescues man after yacht flipped over by huge wave – video," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The US Coast Guard shared footage of a rescue involving a rescue swimmer saving a man from a 35ft yacht that was rolled over by a huge wave. The rescue swimmer was lowered into the water from a helicopter and swam towards the vessel, before the man was thrown into the water in the mouth of the Columbia River," read the report. The Desk then conducted another Google search with the keyword "Cyclone Biparjoy hits Gujarat". The search results led to a PTI report published on June 15, whose headline read: "Biparjoy starts making landfall near Jakhau Port in Gujarat's Kutch". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that a video from the USA had been falsely connected to Cyclone Biparjoy and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of tree falling on scooter falsely linked to Cyclone Biparjoy; shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 19 ( PTI Fact Check Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan): A Twitter user shared a video of a tree falling on three people riding a scooter and claimed it was related to the recent Cyclone Biparjoy in Gujarat. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from Rajasthan had been falsely linked to Cyclone Biparjoy and was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared on June 16 a video of a tree falling on three people riding a scooter and used hashtags linking the incident to the recent Cyclone Biparjoy in Gujarat. "હજુ 24 કલાક ઘરમાં રહો, સુરક્ષિત રહો," read the post, which is originally in Gujarati and carried hashtags including #CycloneBiparjoyUpdate #CycloneAlert and #BiparjoyUpdate. "Stay home for 24 more hours, stay safe," read the English translation of the post, which has garnered over 730 views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search of the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a video report published by NDTV on May 30, 2023, in which an extended version of the viral video had been carried. "Video: Tree Falls On 3 Men Riding Scooter In Rajasthan," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The short clip has been gaining traction on social media and shows part of a tree falling on the two-wheeler almost crushing the riders," read the report. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video to the video carried in the report: The search also led to a video report published by Time Now on May 30, 2023, in which an extended version of the viral video had been carried. "Video: Tree Falls On Moving Scooter in Rajasthan's Jodhpur Amid Gusty Winds, Three Injured," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "In a tragic incident reported from Jodhpur district of Rajasthan, a tree fell on a scooter rider injuring three persons. The incident took place amid gusty winds and rains alert in the city on Monday," read the report. The Desk subsequently concluded that an old video from Rajasthan had been falsely connected to Cyclone Biparjoy.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Bangladesh shared with false claim of Muslims obstructing Army vehicle in West Bengal; Details
content: New Delhi, June 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video claiming that it showed an Army vehicle being surrounded by some people as it carried an injured Lashkar terrorist in West Bengal. The user insinuated that the vehicle was obstructed by members of a particular community. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a two-year-old video from Bangladesh had been posted on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 8 a video claiming that it showed an Army vehicle being surrounded by some people as it carried an injured Lashkar terrorist in West Bengal. In the video, some people who were wielding sticks can be seen surrounding the Army vehicle. A person who looks injured can also be seen lying inside the vehicle. "बंगाल में लश्कर के घायल जवान को ले जाते समय कुछ एक से दिखने वाले लोगों ने घेर कर सैनिकों की गाड़ियाँ रोक लीं एक सैनिक के जीवन की इनकी नज़र में ये क़ीमत ….????," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "While carrying an injured Lashkar jawan in Bengal, some people who looked alike surrounded and stopped the vehicles of the soldiers," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of them led to a Twitter post from March 20 where the same video had been shared with a similar claim. "बंगाल में लश्कर के घायल जवान को ले जाते समय मुसलमानों ने घेर कर गाड़ियाँ रोक लीं, तादाद बढ़ने पर लश्कर का ये हाल है ?? Pls dnt ignore," read the post, which is originally in Hindi. "While taking the injured Lashkar jawan in Bengal, Muslims surrounded and stopped the vehicles, this is the condition of Lashkar when the number increased?? Pls don't ignore," read the English translation of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also noticed a red insignia on the sleeve of two soldiers seen in the video. Below is a screenshot of the same: By conducting a Google Search with the keywords "army red insignia", the Desk found a photo on stock image website Getty Images, where two soldiers were seen with the same insignia on their sleeves. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing a screenshot from the viral video to the Getty Images photo: The Desk also noticed that the number plate of the Army vehicle seen in the viral video was in Bengali. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk subsequently concluded that an old video from Bangladesh had been shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to India.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 incident from Karnataka's Udupi falsely linked to Odisha triple train tragedy; shared on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, June 28 (abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a man claiming that he averted a major train tragedy by running 6 km, despite a leg ailment, to inform the officials about cracks in railway tracks. The user used hashtags to link the claim with the Balasore train tragedy in Odisha that happened on June 2. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old incident from Karnataka's Udupi, dating back to 2018, was shared on social media with a misleading claim. At least 289 people died in the triple train crash involving three trains – two passenger and a goods train – at the Bahanaga Bazar railway station in Odisha's Balasore on June 2. Claim A Twitter user shared on June 2 shared a photo of a man and claimed he was a 53-year-old labourer, Krishna Poojari, who ran 6 km to avert a major train accident despite having a leg ailment. The post related Krishna Poojari to the recent triple-train accident in Odisha and was circulated with hashtags denoting the Odisha train accident. "This person helped prevent a major train accident. Krishna Pujari is a true hero. #odisha #TrainAccident #coromandel'," read the caption of the June 2 post, which garnered 21.3K views so far. "Meet Krishna Poojari, a 53-year-old labourer ran for 6 km to inform the officials about crack in railway tracks. He had a problem in his leg but he did not care. This helped them save the train from a major tragedy. He deserves huge respect," read the text within the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the Twitter post. The search results led to an October 2018 news article by Bangalore Mirror. "Poojari has been unwell for 3 months, but that did not stop him taking immediate action when he observed a dangerous crack in a railway track in Udupi," read a portion of the Bangalore Mirror article. Here is the link to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results further led the Desk to a report by The Hindu, dating back October 31, 2018. The headline of the report read: "Udipi man runs 3 km to alert about crack in track". Here is the link to The Hindu article and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an incident of averting a possible train tragedy by Poojari did happen, but in October 2018 at Udupi Railway Station in Karnataka. Despite being physically challenged, Poojari ran 3 km and not 6 km to inform railway officials about a broken track. His timely action averted a major tragedy.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of billboard opposing PM Modi's Hyderabad visit falsely linked to his recent US visit; Shared on social media with a false claim
content: New Delhi, June 29 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a photo of a billboard poster of Netflix crime series 'Money Heist' with text against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent visit to the US. The use claimed that the billboard was put up in America to oppose the prime minister's state visit. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old image from Hyderabad was falsely linked to PM Modi's state visit to the US and shared on social media with a false claim. PM Modi was on a state to the US from June 21 to June 24, during which he met President Joe Biden along with several other top dignitaries of the country and also addressed the US Congress. Claim A Twitter user on June 20 shared a photo of a billboard poster of Netflix series 'Money Heist' with a text printed on it that read, "Mr N Modi we only rob banks you rob the whole nation," and claimed that the billboard was put up in USA ahead of PM Modi's State Visit to the US. "Posters in USA, loud and clear message from money heist Mr modi we only rob bank you rob the whole nation #ModiNotWelcome #ModiNotWelcome #Voice_For_Indian_Muslim #Stand_With_indian_Muslims #IndianMuslims," read the caption of the post shared on Twitter which has garnered over 7,000 views. Here is the link and archive link of the Twitter post, below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral post which led to a Twitter post shared by Bhartiya Rashtriya Samiti (BRS) leader Y Sathish Reddy on July 1, 2022. "Such creativity! #Hyderabad #MoneyHeist," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the post. The Reverse Google Image Search also led to a news report by The Telegraph that carried the same image as the one shared by the Twitter user. "Hyderabad welcomes Narendra Modi with 'sarcastic' billboard," read the headline of the report published on September 3, 2022. Here is the link of the news report and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the PTI Fact Check concluded that the viral photo shared by the user was from Hyderabad and was put up last year when PM Modi was scheduled to visit the state for BJP executive national meeting.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake press release claiming France suspended Internet services shared on social media amid violence, unrest in European country
content: New Delhi, July 3 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid violent unrest in France, a Twitter user shared an alleged press release by the country's Ministry of the Interior and Overseas stating that internet service was suspended in some parts amid the violence. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that screenshot of a fake press release was shared on social media to make the false claim. Claim A Twitter user shared an alleged screenshot of a press release by French government, claiming that internet service had been suspended in some areas amid violent unrest in the country. "Unrest in France is a reminder that mistreatment of minorities and institutionalized racial discrimination are endemic in self-proclaimed liberal democracies that lecture non-Western democracies on civil rights. After mass arrests, France suspends internet service in some areas," read the July 3 Twitter post, which included the alleged press release in French language. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the screenshot of the alleged press release shared in the social media post. However, we couldn't find any relevant information, backing the claim. The Desk the conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "internet service suspended in parts of France", but could not find any news report, reporting about any such decision announced by the country's government or any ministry or official. However, on further scanning the search results, we came across a July 3 Twitter post shared by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, which shared the same screenshot of the press release, terming it fake. "#UrbanViolence | Beware of #FakeNews A "press release" from the French national police force @PoliceNationale has claimed that temporary restrictions have been imposed on Internet access in certain neighbourhoods. This document is FALSE: no such decision has been taken," read the Twitter post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the Twitter handle of France's Ministère de l'Intérieur et des Outre-mer (Ministry of the Interior and Overseas), to check if the ministry had shared any post, regarding the claim. We came across a July 2 tweet in which it refuted the claim that internet services had been suspended in some parts of the country. "#ViolencesUrbaines | Attention aux #FakeNews Un communiqué de presse de la @PoliceNationale annoncerait des restrictions temporaires à l'accès internet dans certains quartiers. Ce document est un FAUX : aucune décision n'a été prise en ce sens," read the tweet in French. An English translation of the tweet read: "#UrbanViolence | Beware of #FakeNews A press release from the @PoliceNationale would announce temporary restrictions on internet access in certain neighborhoods. This document is a FALSE: no decision has been taken in this regard." Here is the link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the post: We also went through the official website of the ministry. However, it was found to be under maintenance. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to the French Embassy, seeking its response on the viral claim. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake screenshot of a press release by the French government had been shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video with old and unrelated clips shared on social media to falsely claim that Tiger Shroff died of cardiac arrest
content: New Delhi, July 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video, received by the Desk on WhatsApp with a request for fact check, claimed that Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff died due to heart attack. The video included clips of Tiger's father and actor Jacky Shroff and a still of Hrithik Roshan, purportedly from the last rite ceremonies. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found that a false claim was made on social media with visuals from old and unrelated videos, and edited photos used in the post. Claim The PTI Fact Check Desk received a video on its WhatsApp number +91-8130503759, claiming that Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff died due to a heart attack and the visuals were from the last rites. The video included a clip of Jacky Shroff along with stills of several actors, including Hrithik Roshan, insinuating that they attended the last rites ceremony. Here is the link and archive link of the post shared by the Twitter user. Below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the video clip which provided us with several keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes, which showed Jacky Shroff, led to a YouTube video posted by 'Manoranjan Katta' channel on July 13, 2013. "Jackie Shroff gets angry on Public during Pran's," read the title of the video posted on the Youtube page, which has garnered over 5,700,000 views. Here is the link to YouTube video , below is the screenshot of the same. "Jackie Shroff gets angry on Public during Pran funeral," read a portion of the bio posted on Youtube. The Desk noticed that the visuals in the YouTube video were similar to those seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the two videos: The Desk then conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on another keyframe, which led to a post shared on Voompla's Facebook page that carried a video showing Hrithik Roshan at the last rites ceremony of his grandfather, J Om Prakash. Here is the link to the Facebook post , below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the August 2019 video had visuals similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: In the next part of the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keyword "Tiger Shroff heart attack", but could not find any news report backing the claim. Had such an unfortunate event taken place, it would have grabbed the national headlines. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a false claim on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff was made on social media, using a video made from old and unrelated clips.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi did not say that he and his ancestors are Muslims; fake news bulletin screenshots shared on social media
content: New Delhi, July 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a screenshot of a purported news bulletin, which quoted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, during his foreign visit, stating that he and his ancestors were Muslims, and that after winning the elections (2024 Lok Sabha), his party would hand out a loan of Rs 5,000 crore to Pakistan as financial aid. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that digitally altered images of news bulletin flash were shared on social media. Claim A Facebook user on June 5 shared a screenshot of a news bulletin purportedly run by ABP News, which quoted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi saying that he and his ancestors were Muslims, and that the Congress party was a party of Muslims. The alleged bulletin further quoted Gandhi saying that after winning (2024 Lok Sabha) elections, his party will give Rs 5,000 crore as financial aid to Pakistan. The text at the bottom of the viral photo also claimed that these statements were made by the Congress leader during his recent visit to America. "Very good Rahul Khan," read the caption of the post shared by the Facebook user. Here is the link and archive link of the post shared by the Facebook user. Below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with a Google Reverse Image Search on the viral image, which led to a Facebook post shared on July 2, 2021. The Facebook post carried a similar photo carrying the same claims. Here is the link of the post shared by the Facebook user, and below is a screenshot of the same. The search results further led to another post shared by ABP News' Twitter handle on November 12, 2018. The ABP News tweet carried a photo similar to the viral one, but with different text. The news channel stated that they did not run any such bulletin as shown in the viral social media posts. Here is the link to the Twitter post shared by ABP News, below is the screenshot of the same: "#Urgent: This is to notify that the attached media which is being circulated online has been doctored with our channel's template. The information about Sh. Rahul Gandhi's statements, which these images carry have not been reported by ABP & have no relation with ABP News Network," read the caption of the post shared by ABP News on their Twitter handle. In the next part of the investigation the Desk conducted a Google Search using the keywords "Rahul Gandhi Muslim remark in US", but were unable to find any report of any such comments made by the Congress leader. Had Rahul Gandhi made such statements, various news media outlets would have reported about the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that digitally altered images of bulletin by a Hindi news channel were shared on social media.
