The bulletin further quoted him saying that after winning the (next general) elections, his party will hand out a financial aid of Rs 5,000 crore to Pakistan. In its investigation, the Desk found that fake news bulletin screenshots were shar
content: New Delhi, July 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid incessant rainfall leading to flood-like situation in several parts of North India, two videos of crocodiles wading through waterlogged residential areas have gone viral, with social media users claiming that they were from Punjab's Kharar and Haryana's Ambala. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that old videos – one from Gujarat's Vadodara and the other from Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri – were shared on social media with false claims. The Desk conducted separate fact-checks to debunk the two claims. Here's what we found: Claim - 1 A Twitter user shared a video of a crocodile in a waterlogged residential area, claiming that the incident happened recently in Punjab's Kharar. "Crocodile now found in residential area of Kharar. SCARY #CHANDIGARH #CROCODILE #KHARAR," read the July 10 post. Here is the link and the archive link of the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation – Claim 1 The Desk started its investigation with an InVid Tool Search on the viral video and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a YouTube video, which was uploaded on August 7, 2019. The title of the video read: "2019 mini sunami... Surat". Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that it was the same video as the one shared on social media. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: On further scanning the search results, we found a tweet by DPRO Mohali, refuting the claims on social media that the crocodile was spotted in Kharar. Here is the link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a four-year-old video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the recent flood-like situation in Punjab. Claim 2 A Twitter user shared on July 10 a video of a crocodile wading through a waterlogged residential area, claiming the reptile was spotted recently in flood-hit Ambala, Haryana. "In the streets of Ambala #Ambala #Flood," read the post, which has garnered over 345K views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation – Claim 2 Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on video shared in the social media and found a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led the Desk to a July 11 YouTube video shared by Zee News. The video, same as the viral one, was shared by the news channel with the title: "Crocodile in Punjab Rain: Ambala की गलियों में दिखा मगरमच्छ, लोगों ने बनाया वीडियो | Viral Video (Crocodile in Punjab Rain: Crocodile spotted in the lanes of Ambala, people record video | Viral Video)." Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results further led the Desk to a Twitter post, shared on August 14, 2022, which carried an extended version of the same video as shared in the viral social media post. The user stated that the reptile was spotted in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh. Here is the link to the tweet and below is a screenshot of the post: Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos – the one shared on social media recently and the other shared last year. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with relevant keywords, that led to a news report, published by ABP News on August 15, 2022. The headline of the report read: "Video: भारी बारिश के बीच आवासीय कॉलोनी में घुस आया मगरमच्छ, वीडियो देखकर उड़ जायेंगे होश (Video: Crocodile entered the residential colony amid heavy rains, you will be shocked to see the video)." Here is the link to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same: The report stated that the crocodile was spotted in a residential colony in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri. The Desk also came across a PTI report carried by NDTV on August 14, 2022. The headline of the report read: "Video: Crocodile Enters Madhya Pradesh Colony Amid Heavy Rain." "A crocodile wandered into a residential colony in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district amid heavy rainfall on Sunday and was captured after an hour-long operation, an official said. The reptile was spotted in a colony near the old bus stand in the early hours of the day, following which the authorities were informed, sub divisional officer of police (SDOP) Ajay Bhargava said," read a portion of the news report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a year-old video from Madhya Pradesh was falsely shared with the claim of the crocodile being spotted in Haryana's Ambala.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fabricated quote in name of CJI Chandrachud shared on social media with fake claim
content: New Delhi, Aug 14 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A Facebook user shared a photo of Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud with a text, purported to be a quote from him, urging people to go out on the streets and protest against the government. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a fabricated statement was shared on social media in the name of CJI. The post shared by a social media user was fake. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 10 a photo of CJI DY Chandrachud with a text that quoted him urging people to protest against the government on the streets, adding that he was standing in their support. "We are trying our best to save the Constitution of India, the democracy of India. But your cooperation is also very important for this; all the people should unite and come out on the streets and ask the government for their rights, this dictatorial government will scare people and threaten them, but you don't have to be afraid. Keep courage and ask the government to account; I am with you," read an English translation of the Hindi text in the photo. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the photo shared in the social media post. The search results led us to a Facebook post by boxer-politician Vijender Singh, who shared the same picture. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with a specific set of keywords, which led to an X post by Live Law, shared on August 14, which carried a statement issued by the Public Relations Office (PRO) of the Supreme Court, refuting the viral claim as "fake, ill-intended and mischievous". Here is the link to the Twitter post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also came across a PTI report, published on August 14, on the Supreme Court refuting the viral claim. Here is the link to the report . "A press note issued by the apex court said the CJI has issued no such post nor has he authorised any such post," read a portion of the report. In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk contacted the CJI office for its comment on the viral claim. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a false and fabricated statement was shared on social media in the name of CJI DY Chandrachud.

title: PTI Fact Check: Pakistani flag was displayed on Burj Khalifa on August 14; the Claim made in social media posts is misleading
content: New Delhi, Aug 18 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X user shared a video of the iconic skyscraper Burj Khalifa in Dubai, in which a woman can be heard narrating how Pakistanis there were left disappointed after their national flag was not displayed on the iconic building. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the Pakistani national flag was displayed on Burj Khalifa on August 14 – the country's Independence Day. The social media post was shared with a misleading claim. Burj Khalifa is known for hosting daily light shows and special displays on occasions such as New Year's and Independence/National Days of other countries on one side of its facade (facing Burj Lake in Downtown Dubai). Claim An X (formerly known as Twitter) user shared a 38-second video of a Pakistani national gathering near Dubai's iconic on August 14 at midnight. The woman in the footage narrates how they were disappointed after their national flag was not displayed on the building. "The time is 12:01 am now, and the Dubai officials have informed us that Pakistan's national flag won't be displayed on Burj Khalifa. This has become our status now. Pakistanis are raising slogans here, but Pakistan's flag won't be displayed on Burj Khalifa. So sad, a prank has been played on Pakistanis," a woman can be heard saying in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with the keywords "Pakistani flag displayed on Burj Khalifa, August 14, 2023". The search results led us to an X (formerly known as Twitter) post by the Times of Karachi, a Pakistan-based digital media outlet. The August 14 post included a video showing Pakistan's national flag displayed on Burj Khalifa. "Dubai's Burj Khalifa lit up in green to mark the 76th Independence Day of #Pakistan. #IndependenceDaypakistan #burjkhalifa," read the X post. Here is the link to the X post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The search results further led to an Instagram post by the official handle of Burj Khalifa, which showed the Pakistani flag being displayed on the iconic building. "#BurjKhalifa lights up to celebrate The Islamic Republic of Pakistan's Independence Day. Wishing the people of Pakistan a day filled with pride, unity and prosperity as you celebrate your great nation's rich heritage and achievements. May the future hold even greater success and happiness for all Pakistanis. Happy Independence Day!" read the Instagram post. Here is the link to the Instagram post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk went through the comment section and found that the handle responded to a comment, confirming that the flag was displayed at 7:50 pm on August 14. Below is a screenshot of the comment: The Desk then conducted another Google search with specific keywords, which led to news reports by several reputed media outlets about the Pakistani flag being displayed on the Burj Khalifa on its Independence Day. "Burj Khalifa displays the Tricolour on India's Independence Day, Pak flag flashed a day earlier," read the headline of an August 17 report by The Indian Express. Here is the link to the news report : A report by Gulf Times also reported about the display of Pakistan's national flag on Burj Khalifa. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Pakistan's national flag was displayed on Burj Khalifa on August 14. The social media post was shared with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Lady in viral video is not Manipur Governor; Claim shared in social media post is false
content: New Delhi, Aug 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Twitter user shared a video of a man addressing a meeting purportedly about the Kuki community in Manipur. The user claimed that the woman beside him was state Governor Anusuiya Uikey. The user claimed that the meeting was an event organised by the RSS), and the banner behind the man showed words like "Save Manipur", "terrorism", and "Bhagat Singh Kranti Dal", and "Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman seated in the event organised on August 8 was not the Governor of Manipur. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. The video comes amid the long-prevailing ethnic strife between the Kuki and Meitei communities in Manipur, which has claimed over hundred lives since May 3, when violence first broke out in the northeastern state. Claim A Twitter user shared on August 19 video of a man addressing a meeting purportedly organised against the minority Kuki community in Manipur. The user claimed that the woman in the video, seated beside the man speaking at an RSS event, was Manipur Governor Anusuiya Uikey. "Why is the Manipur Governor attending an RSS-sponsored meeting spreading hate against the minority Kukis," read the caption of the X (formerly known as Twitter) post that has garnered over 50,000 views. Here is the link and archive link to the X post. Below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to a post shared on August 10 by a Facebook user that carried several photos similar to the visuals seen in the viral video. Here is the link to the Facebook post , and below is the screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing the keyframes of the viral video to one of the photos shared by the Facebook user: On scanning through the profile of the Facebook user who shared these photos, the Desk noticed that the man seen addressed in the viral video was the same who posted the pictures from the event on Facebook. Below is a screenshot of the Facebook profile of the man named 'Sohan Giri'. Giri described himself as the founding president at Rashtrahit Sarvopari Sangathan (RSS). He also mentioned his contact number in the About section of his profile. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk reached out to Giri, who clarified that the event organised by Rashtrahit Sarvopari Sangathan on August 8 was not attended by Manipur Governor. "8 August को राष्ट्रहित सर्वोपरि संगठन द्वारा आयोजित कार्यक्रम में ना तो आरएसएस (Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh) द्वारा किसी प्रकार का सहयोग योगदान था ओर ना ही हमारे इस कार्यक्रम में मणिपुर की राज्यपाल शामिल हुई GeetV द्वारा किये गये ट्व्वीट बिल्कुल झूठे हैं ओर उनका वास्तविकता से कोई लेना देना नहीं है," Giri wrote in his text response to PTI. "The program organised by Rashtrahit Sarvopari Sangathan on August 8 was neither supported by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) nor did the Governor of Manipur participate in our programme," read the English translation of the response. The Google Reverse Image Search results also led to a post shared by Manipur Police on August 19, which carried a screenshot of the viral tweet claiming that Manipur Governor attended a meeting against the Kuki community. "The lady seated is not the Governor of Manipur as has been posted. 1. FIR will be taken up at cyber crime PS, 2. Twitter has been requested to take down the post," read the post's caption. Here is the link to the Twitter post ; below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing a woman at the meeting organised on August 8 was not Manipur Governor. The video had been shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts, YouTube Videos about American actor Clint Eastwood's death not confirmed
content: New Delhi, Aug 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a screenshot of a post claiming that legendary Hollywood actor-director Clint Eastwood was dead. The user shared the screenshot with PTI Fact Check to verify the claim. The PTI Fact Check, in its investigation, found that the social media posts of the American actor's death are not confirmed. Claim PTI Fact Check received on its Fact Check WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 a request from a user to verify the claim in a screenshot of a social media post that Clinton Eastwood Jr. is dead. Below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The PTI Fact Check Desk started the investigation with a Google search with the keywords "Clint Eastwood Death". The search results showed no reports about the death of the famous Hollywood actor and director. The Desk scanned X (Formerly known as Twitter) with the exact keywords and found no such reports from authentic news portals' handles. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched YouTube with the exact keywords and found two videos which claimed that 'Clint Eastwood' was dead. Here is the link and archive link to the first YouTube video published on June 22, 2023. Here is the link and archive link to the Second YouTube Video published on March 2, 2023. Below are the screenshots of the pages- The Desk scanned the comment section of one of the YouTube videos and noticed many users' comments called this 'fake news'. Below are the screenshots of the comments: Continuing the investigation, the Desk did a customised search on Google and found an article on East Clintwood by the website fandomwire.com. The article's first paragraph, published on August 20 (Sunday), reads: "Clint Eastwood is among the few artists in Hollywood who have successfully solidified their status as the best in all their artistic ventures. As an excellent actor and an even impeccable director, Eastwood has starred in and created multiple critically acclaimed movies and TV series. Not only has he crafted a separate niche for his craft, many look up to him as an inspiration now." This shows that the actor is alive. Here is the link to the story , and below is the screenshot of the page- In the subsequent search, the Desk found another article filed by the Yahoo entertainment website. The report's headline filed on August 10 reads: "Clint Eastwood's Reaction to His Former Mistress' Death Shows How Strong Their Connection Was." The report's two paragraphs about Eastwood's former mistress's death read: Per the source, Eastwood's grief over Tunis has extended far beyond their relationship and made him question his whole life too. "Her loss not only gutted him but also made him think more about his mortality, which he never does," the source said of the 93-year-old actor. "Clint loves living life," the source continued. "He loves being around, but when Roxanne passed, he started feeling things he wasn't used to. Clint is a storyteller, and that is how he lives his life. With Roxanne's passing, it taught Clint many things he never thought were possible." Here is the link to the story , and below is the screenshot of the page- Both reports filed in August (August 10 and August 20) confirm that the American actor is not dead. The Desk also found that multiple X accounts are active in the actor's name but still need to be confirmed or authenticated. The report can be read here . Clint Eastwood is no stranger to death hoaxes. In 2019 and 2022, there were false reports that he had died at 89. This was not the first time such a rumour had circulated, as there was a similar hoax about him in 2017. Politifact : Clint Eastwood is still not dead (Oct 1, 2019) Snopes : Clint Eastwood Is Not Dead, Despite 'Sad News' Facebook Death Hoax (Dec 6, 2022) AAP Fact Check : Stories of his demise are greatly exaggerated: Clint Eastwood is not dead (Nov 13, 2019) There is no doubt that if the veteran Hollywood actor had passed away, reputable news outlets would be the first to report it, not random YouTube videos.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show Russia's Luna-25 crashing on the Moon's surface; Animated video shared as real on social media
content: New Delhi, Aug 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): An X (formerly known as Twitter) user shared a video that showed a cylindrical object crashing on what looked like a lunar surface and claimed that this was footage of Russia's Luna-25, which crashed into the Moon after it spun into an uncontrolled orbit on August 20. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old animated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Russia's Luna-25 was scheduled to land on the lunar surface on August 23 but suffered an unfortunate failure on August 20. Chandrayaan-3, on the other hand, created history as it landed successfully on the Moon's south pole on August 23. Claim An X user shared on August 22 a 15-second video clip, which showed a cylindrical object crashing on what looked like a lunar surface. The user claimed that it showed the crashing of Russia's Luna-25 on the surface of the Moon. "LIVE Footage, How Russia's Luna-25 has crashed into the Moon. #Luna25 #Russia #MoonLanding #Chandrayaan3Mission #Chandrayaan3 #Luna25Crash #Kashmir #VikramLander #Chandrayaan_3 #NASA #ISRO," read the post, which has garnered over 25,000 views till date. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the viral video, which provided a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to the same video, uploaded on YouTube on August 21. The video title read: "How Russia Luna-25 crashed into the moon|#luna25 #Chandryaanmission #russia." Here is the link and archive link to the YouTube video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Upon further scanning the Google Reverse Image Search results, the Desk came across a March 2022 article published on SciTech Daily. The headline read: "A Rocket Is Going To Crash Into the Moon Friday – NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Will Get an Up-Close View of the Smoldering Crater". Here is the link to the article , and below is a screenshot of the same: The article carried the same video, whose caption read: "Artist's animation of a rocket booster crashing into the moon". An Indian TV news channel, WION also carried the same video in its video report, uploaded on YouTube on June 29, 2022. The report's title read: "Gravitas: Mysterious rocket crash on moon baffles scientists." Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the video carried by WION in its report was the same as the one shared by SciTech Daily, as the video had the logo of the website. The same video was found shared on Instagram in a March 15, 2022 post. The post's caption read: "Artist's animation of a rocket booster crashing into the moon." Here is the link to the Instagram post , and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across an article by Daily Star, published on July 23, 2018. The headline of the article read: "Aliens might have lived on the MOON scientists discover in bombshell find". The article carried a video which included visuals of the Moon's surface by NASA. The Desk noticed that one of the visuals showed the lunar surface, similar to what was established in the viral video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Here is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos – the one shared in the Daily Star article and the other shared in the viral video: The same lunar surface footage was carried in a YouTube video by Smithsonian Channel Aviation Nation, uploaded in October 2022. Here is the link and a screenshot of the video: None of the above two videos showed the cylindrical object falling on the lunar surface, as shown in the viral video. This suggests that it was digitally added to the clip of the lunar surface to create an animation video.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi did not raise slogan in support of opposition's INDIA bloc; 10-year-old video shared as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, Sep 18 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressing a public rally, claiming that he raised 'Vote for India' slogan to extend his support to the opposition's INDIA alliance. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a 10-year-old video was shared on social media with misleading claim. The video dates back to 2013 when Narendra Modi was the then Gujarat CM whereas the INDIA (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance) alliance – a bloc of 26 opposition parties – has been formed only recently in view of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. Claim An Instagram user shared on September 10 a video of PM Modi where he can be seen raising 'vote for India' slogan at a public rally. The user shared the video, insinuating that the PM extended support to the opposition's INDIA alliance. The super on the caption read: "Did Narendra Modi change his party? Raised slogans, Vote for India". Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk took screengrabs of the video and conducted Google Lens search on them. The search results led us to an X (formerly known as Twitter) post, which carried the same video with a similar claim. "THANK YOU MODI JI FOR SUPPORTING "#VOTE_FOR_INDIA" FOR UPCOMING 2024 ELECTION COMPAIN," read the September 9 post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search and came across a YouTube video, uploaded by Aaj Tak on December 22, 2013. The title of the video read: "'Vote for India' is the slogan for 2014 elections: Modi". "Addressing the Maha Garjana rally in Mumbai, BJP leader Narendra Modi urges the people of India to vote for the nation and not for any party," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the same video that was being shared on social media recently. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos – one shared in social media posts and the other uploaded on YouTube in 2013. From 1:53 timestamp, Narendra Modi can be heard raising the 'Vote for India' slogan, before which he asked the people to vote for the country, and not any political party in the 2014 Lok Sabha polls. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another customised Google search with a specific set of keywords, which led to the same video on the official website of PM Modi, along with the full text of the speech that he delivered back then. Here is the link to the page on the official website and below is a screenshot of the text of relevant portion of the speech, which is being shared on social media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 10-year-old video was being shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, it's not Joe Biden's aircraft as claimed in viral video; Footage of video game shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Sep 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): An X (formerly known as Twitter) user shared a video of a USA aircraft flying with a few fighter planes and claimed that it was the airplane of US President Joe Biden when he was returning to the US in his Air Force One – the official aircraft of the US President – escorted by fighter jets, after attending the G20 Summit in Delhi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a simulation video game footage was shared on social media as real with a false claim. The claim in the social media post was false. Claim An X user shared on September 16 a video claiming that it showed US President Joe Biden returning to America in Air Force One – the official aircraft of the US President – escorted by fighter jets after attending the recently concluded G20 Summit in Delhi on September 9-10. "_President Joe Biden returning to the USA after attending the G-20 summit in New Delhi ..... What a Security! #BjpAndhrapradesh_," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the video and received a few keyframes. A Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes led to another X post carrying the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Another post on Facebook, dated September 18, carried the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a September 4 Instagram post, which carried the same video with the caption "Real or Fake". Here is the link and archive link to the Instagram post, and below is a screenshot of the same: This video was posted on September 4, days before the G20 Summit in Delhi. The US President arrived in India on September 8 and attended the two-day mega event before leaving for Vietnam on September 10. The Desk went through the comments section on the Instagram post and noticed several users stating the video was not real. Below is a screenshot of one such comment: Another user indicated that the video footage was from the video game DCS World. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google with specific keywords. The search results led to a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named 'Digital Combat Simulator Air Force One Escort'. The video, uploaded in April 2022, carried different visuals showing Air Force One aircraft. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to look for details on Air Force One, the official aircraft of the US President. The search results led us to the official website of Boeing, where we found the original photo of Air Force One. (https://www.boeing.com/defense/air-force-one/) On comparing the visuals of aircraft in the video shared on social media with the one on the Boeing website, we found that the former had additional widgets which were not present in the latter. Below is a combination image comparing the aircraft visuals to the photo on the Boeing website: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a simulation video game footage was shared as real on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming Punjabi-Canadian singer Shubhneet's Instagram followers took a hit after his controversial Instagram post is false; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Sep 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing diplomatic row between India and Canada and the social media outrage against Punjabi-Canadian singer Shubhneet Singh (aka Shubh) over his controversial social media post, an X (formerly known as Twitter) user shared a screenshot, allegedly showing that the singer's Instagram following dipped from 4 million to 1.1 million. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a fabricated screenshot was shared to make the false claim, as Shubh's Instagram following didn't see any dip. Instead, it rose amid the ongoing controversy. The artist was under scrutiny for his purportedly pro-Khalistan views and social media posts. The announcement came soon after boAt decided to withdraw sponsorship from his upcoming tour, and cricketer Virat Kohli reportedly unfollowed the singer on Instagram. Meanwhile, BookMyShow cancelled ticket sales for Shubhneet Singh's 'Still Rollin Tour for India' after the ticket-booking app faced a boycott call on social media for hosting a singer allegedly a Khalistani sympathiser. Claim An X user shared a screenshot, allegedly showing a comparison of how Punjabi-Canadian singer Shubh's Instagram following saw a massive dip from 4 million to 1.1 million after the artist faced backlash over his purported pro-Khalistani views amid the diplomatic row between India and Canada and the subsequent cancellation of his India tour. "well-done #Bharat, we all have shown that if we unite no one can downplay us. #BharatMataKiJai #BookMyShow #Khalistan #Canada," read the September 23 X post, which has garnered over 450K and over 10,000 views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Reverse Image Search on the screenshot shared in the viral X post. The search results led the Desk to a September 22 Facebook post, which carried the same photo. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with specified keywords to check whether the singer's Instagram following took a hit amid the ongoing controversy. However, we couldn't find any such report backing the claim. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked the Instagram account of the singer, which showed that he had 1.5 million followers. Here is the link to Shubh's Instagram handle , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then checked the details of the handle on InsTrack, an app that offers in-depth Instagram analytics and actionable insights for brands, influencers and agencies. We found that in the last 30 days, the artist's Instagram following increased by 54.9 per cent. Below is a screenshot showing the same on InsTrack: The Desk then checked the growth/fall in followers over the past 90 days, again showing an upward trend of 88.8 per cent. Below is a screenshot of the same: On Aug 26, he had one million followers on his Instagram account, which went up to 1.5 million on Sept 22. However, there was a dip in number of followers and it went down to 1.3 on Sept 23. But, the number again increased and touched 1.6 million on Sept 24. Below are the screenshots of the change in his followers count: August 26: 1 million Sept 22: 1.5 million Sept 23: 1.3 million Sept 24: 1.6 million However, another website socialblade.com showed his followers count was slightly down on Sept 16. But, it clearly shows that his followers count on Instagram went up from one million to 1.5 million in the last few days. Subsequently, the Desk led to two crucial conclusions in its investigation: firstly, the singer's Instagram following witnessed a jump, and not a dip, amid the ongoing controversy; secondly, he never had 4 million followers on Instagram, which proves that a digitally altered screenshot was shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of mob attacking security forces is not from Manipur; old video from Kenya shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Sep 30 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid the recent incidents of violence in ethnic strife-hit Manipur, a video has been doing the rounds on social media, particularly WhatsApp, with the claim that it showed a mob of a particular community attacking security personnel with teargas shells as they tried to escape in their vehicle. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an unrelated video from Kenya was falsely linked to Manipur and shared on social media. A fresh bout of violence broke out in Manipur's capital Imphal earlier this week, after photos of the bodies of the two youths, who went missing in July, went viral on social media. Claim The Desk received on its Fact Check WhatsApp No. +91-8130503759 a request to verify the authenticity of a video, which was being widely shared on the platform with the claim that it showed a mob belonging to a particular community in ethnic strife-hit attacking security personnel with teargas shells as they tried to escape in their vehicle. Below is a screenshot of the video received by the Desk: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted an InVid Tool Search on the viral video and found a few keyframes. A Google Lens search on one of the keyframes led us to the same video, shared on X (formerly known as Twitter) on September 29. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk found the same video in an Instagram post, which was shared on July 27. The caption of the post read: "Maandamano". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk searched for the term "maandamano" used in the caption and found that Swahili word meant protest/demonstration, which was used in Kenya. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with a set of specific keywords and came across the same video, posted by a verified X user on July 10. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: "Wednesday's #maandamano might be worse as Raila Odinga and Azimio supporter are set hold demonstrations," read the caption of the post. On conducting Google searches for the terms "Raila Odinga" and "Azimio", we found that the former was a leader of the opposition coalition Azimio la Umoja (Declaration of Unity) in Kenya. The opposition alliance held a number of protests in July, causing widespread disruption and in some cases violent confrontations with police in which more than two dozen people were killed and scores injured. Here is the link to a Reuters report on the violent protests. Another video report on the violence by a local channel named NTV Kenya can be seen here . The Desk then closely watched the viral video and found that at 00:18 seconds, a shop named "Tiengo Auto Paints" could be seen. Below is a screenshot of the same: On conducting a Google search for the shop name, we found that it was in Nairobi. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from Kenya was falsely linked to the recent incident of violence in Manipur on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Post by X handle impersonating Kohli claiming 'he will host party for Pak cricket team' shared as real; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Oct 3 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly known as Twitter) post, allegedly of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli welcoming Pakistan cricket contingent, which arrived in India for the ICC World Cup on September 27, has been doing the rounds on social media. The post further talked about the Indian star batsman hosting a party for the Pakistan team at his residence. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the X post was shared by a parody account impersonating Kohli. The X post shared on the social media platform was false. Claim An X post, allegedly shared by Indian cricketer Virat Kohli, welcomed the Pakistani cricket contingent in India as they arrived for the ICC Men's World Cup. The post also mentioned Kohli hosting a party for the Pakistani team at his house. "I warmly welcome Pakistan Cricket Team on their arrival in my country after a long time period of 7 years, I will host a party for my friends specially for Shadab at my house. Love you all, always spread love and joy #Hyderabad #PakistanCricketTeam #BabarAzam #CWC23," read the September 27 post, which has garnered over 1.3 million views so far. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by looking for similar claims on social media and came across a Facebook post that shared a screenshot of the same X post mentioned above. Here is the link and archive link to the Facebook post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the official X handle of Virat Kohli and found that he did not share any such post on September 27, as shown in the viral post. The only post shared by Kohli on September 27 was a photo of the India Women's Cricket Team, congratulating them on winning the Asian Games Gold. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the activity of Kohli's X handle on Social Blade to check whether any other post was shared on September 27, which might have been deleted later. The stats clearly showed that the post mentioned above was the only one shared by Kohli on the given date. The Desk then scanned the X handle, which shared the viral post and found that it was a parody account impersonating Kohli. It mentioned "Parody Account" in the handle's bio. Below is a screenshot of the same: It also showed that the account was created in August 2023 and had 951 followers. On the other hand, Kohli's official X account has a verified blue tick with a whopping 58.2 million followers. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an X post was shared by a parody account, impersonating Virat Kohli, with a false claim. Claim

title: PTI Fact Check: No, the woman with Dawood Ibrahim in this photo is not Congress leader Supriya Shrinate; 1987 photo shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X user shared a photo of a woman sitting in front of India's most wanted terrorist Dawood Ibrahim and claimed that it dated back to 1987, and the woman was Congress leader Supriya Shrinate, a journalist-turned-politician. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman in the photo was senior crime journalist Sheela Bhatt, who interviewed the fugitive designated terrorist in 1987. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user shared on December 15 a photo of India's most wanted terrorist, Dawood Ibrahim, and claimed that the woman sitting opposite him was Congress leader Supriya Shrinate. "@SupriyaShrinate एक महिला पत्रकार दाऊद इब्राहिम के साथ बैठी हुई है यह फोटो 1987 का है और जो महिला पत्रकार बैठी है वह आज की *कांग्रेस* की प्रवक्ता *सुप्रिया श्रीनेत* है अब समझ में आया खानग्रेस क्या चीज है?" read the post. An English translation of the post read: "@SupriyaShrinate A female journalist is sitting with Dawood Ibrahim. This photo is from 1987, and the female journalist sitting in it is today's *Congress* spokesperson *Supriya Shrinate*. Now, do you understand what Congress is?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the photo shared on social media through Google Lens. It came across another X post, where the user questioned Congress' Supriya Shrinate about the woman in the photo. Here is the link and archive link to the post with over 240K views, and below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, a Facebook user shared the photo, claiming that the woman in the photo was Supriya Shrinate. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: While scanning the search results, the Desk also came across an X post by a renowned crime journalist shared in June this year, wherein she shared the same photo. The photo's caption read: "Interviewing Dawood Ibrahim in Pearl Building, Dubai. 1987". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In a thread post, Bhatt stated that the interview with Dawood was carried out by two weekly – Abhiyaan and The Illustrated Weekly. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In another thread post, the senior journalist clarified that the interview was done in 1987 but published in 1988. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Journalist Amrita Shah tweeted Bhatt's X post and stated that the latter's interview was run with her cover story in the Illustrated Weekly of India in December 1988. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk researched Supriya Shrinate's journalistic career and found that she started her career with India Today in October 2001 and finally joined the Congress in 2019. Here is a screenshot of Shrinate's LinkedIn profile detailing the same: The Desk then contacted Shrinate for her comments on the viral claim and photo. "This is a lie; this photo was taken in 1987, and the woman seen in the photo is journalist Sheela Bhatt. I was ten years old when this interview was conducted. I was born on 27 October 1977. Such personal lies inspire me to fight hatred with double strength," Shrinate told PTI. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman in the photo was not Supriya Shrinate but senior crime journalist Sheela Bhatt.
